commit.message:
src: add a flag to keep the embedder's wasm streaming callback

`SetIsolateMiscHandlers()` always installs Node.js's
`WebAssembly.compileStreaming()` implementation, which is backed by the
Environment's fetch-based handler. An embedder that provides its own
streaming callback (for example one wired to its own network stack) has
to re-install it after every `SetIsolateUpForNode()` or `NewIsolate()`
call. Add `SHOULD_NOT_SET_WASM_STREAMING_CALLBACK` next to the existing
`SHOULD_NOT_SET_PROMISE_REJECTION_CALLBACK` and
`SHOULD_NOT_SET_PREPARE_STACK_TRACE_CALLBACK` flags so it can opt out
the same way.

commit.message:
vfs: support recursive readdir in ZipProvider

ZipProvider threw ERR_METHOD_NOT_IMPLEMENTED for readdir() with
`{ recursive: true }`, although an archive already stores every member
under its full path, so a recursive listing is the same scan of the
entry names as a flat one, keeping the whole path below the directory
instead of only its first segment.

List every member below the directory, and every directory their paths
pass through, whether the archive holds an entry for it or only implies
it. Names are relative to the listed directory and joined with `/`, as
MemoryProvider returns them, so VirtualFileSystem reports the right
parentPath for each Dirent. A name that is both a member and a
directory is listed once, as a directory, as a flat listing already
did.

The entries are now collected in a map rather than looked up in an
array, so listing a directory no longer takes time quadratic in the
number of its children.

commit.message:
stream: trim per-pipe and per-tee costs in webstreams

An object literal with computed symbol keys is rebuilt through the
runtime every time it is evaluated, close to a microsecond each. pipeTo,
tee and the byte tee materialized their internal read request as such
a literal once per pipe or tee, and the byte tee's BYOB path did so on
every read. The requests are now instances of one small class holding
the three step functions.

A source without pull() ran the pull bookkeeping anyway: two reaction
closures and a microtask per read whose only effect was to clear the
pulling flag. Push-style sources now skip it.

The default tee's pull algorithm was an async function and the byte
tee's returned a fresh resolved promise; both now return nothing, which
reaches the controller's pull-fulfilled step at the same microtask
position without the promise.

ReadableStreamBYOBReader.prototype.read() was an async method, so the
read request's promise was adopted through a wrapper (an extra promise
and two microtask hops per read). It now returns the request's promise
directly, as the spec does; argument errors still become rejections.

A TransformStream without start() no longer allocates the start promise
record: the sides adopt a promise that is already resolved either way.

test_runner: do not reuse a worker ID held by a running file

Worker IDs were handed out round-robin and never released, so a file
that started after another finished could get an ID still held by a

commit.message:
util: show SuppressedError's error/suppressed properties on inspect

util.inspect() (and console.log()) silently dropped a SuppressedError's
`error` and `suppressed` properties, the two pieces of information
needed to actually debug a disposal failure. Both properties are
non-enumerable, so they never showed up without this.

formatError() already special-cases two other non-enumerable
"container" properties for the same reason: Error's `cause` (#41002)
and AggregateError's `errors` (#43646). Handle SuppressedError's
`error` and `suppressed` the same way; nested SuppressedErrors (from
multiple failed disposals) are shown recursively since inspect()
already recurses into any Error-valued property.

commit.message:
src: free placeholder nodes for cppgc wrappers in MemoryTracker

`MemoryTracker::AddNode(const CppgcMixin*)` allocates a
`MemoryRetainerNode` that only stands in for the wrapper's JS node while
its `MemoryInfo()` runs; unlike the other node kinds it is not handed
to the `EmbedderGraph`, and nothing freed it. Every heap snapshot (or
other `BuildEmbedderGraph` call) leaked one node per live `vm.Script`
or `vm` context.

Keep the placeholders in the tracker and free them with it, and make
the already-seen path in `Track(const CppgcMixin*)` add its edge to the
wrapper's JS node like the first visit does, so the graph never refers
to a placeholder.

commit.message:
sqlite: add virtual table support via createModule()

Expose SQLite's virtual table API through a new
`database.createModule(name, options)` method, wrapping
`sqlite3_create_module_v2()`. This enables read-only virtual tables
backed by JavaScript data sources, usable either as an eponymous table
(`SELECT * FROM module_name`) or via `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t USING
module_name`. Hidden columns pass parameters using table-valued
function syntax (`SELECT * FROM module_name(param1, param2)`).

`options` accepts `columns`, `rows`, `directOnly`, and
`useBigIntArguments`. Column types are validated against INTEGER,
TEXT, REAL, BLOB, and ANY, and column names are quoted when building
the `sqlite3_declare_vtab()` schema.

Rebased from https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/61544, which was
opened by byteforge38 and became inactive. Changes on top of that
work:

- xColumn reports the value each hidden column was constrained to,
  rather than NULL. SQLite treats xBestIndex's `omit` as a hint, so it
  may recheck a constraint it already handed to xFilter; against NULL
  that recheck rejected every row, and `gs(1, 3) WHERE start = 1`
  returned no rows.
- xBestIndex lowers estimatedCost as it consumes constraints. With a
  constant cost the planner was free to pick the unconstrained plan and
  recheck afterwards, so a correlated parameter such as
  `FROM t, gs(t.a, t.a + 1)` also returned no rows.
- Violations of the iteration protocol report a SQLite error instead of
  calling PropagateJSError with no JavaScript exception pending. That
  left `.all()` returning undefined and `exec()` reporting success.
- xBestIndex passes the constrained hidden-column indices to xFilter
  through idxStr rather than an int bitmask, which previously aliased
  for parameter indices at or above the width of an int.
- xFilter, xNext, and xColumn take a CallbackDepthGuard. Without it
  close() from inside rows(), an iterator's next(), or a row getter
  finalized the statement that SQLite was still stepping, crashing the
  process.
- xClose calls the iterator's return() method so generator `finally`
  blocks run when SQLite stops stepping early, as it does for LIMIT or
  a `break` out of a for...of loop. It is skipped while tearing down
  from ~StatementSync or ~DatabaseSync, which run from garbage
  collection callbacks where JavaScript cannot be executed; an
  abandoned generator does not run `finally` in JavaScript either. It
  is also skipped when an error is already pending, so that error still
  reaches the caller.
- VirtualTableModule holds a BaseObjectWeakPtr<DatabaseSync> to match
  UserDefinedFunction instead of a raw pointer.
- createModule() rejects being called from an authorizer callback.
- Documents that values yielded by rows() follow the usual conversion
  rules, so a number is stored as REAL and a BigInt as INTEGER even
  when a column declares INTEGER, since virtual tables do not apply
  column affinity to the values they return.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/61544
Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/63826
Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/61539

node-api: do not crash on module version mismatch

`node_napi_env__::New()` returns nullptr after throwing when an add-on
declares a Node-API version this binary does not support, but
`napi_module_register_by_symbol()` dereferenced the result without
checking it. Loading such an add-on segfaulted instead of surfacing the
error the version check had already produced, so `require()` could not
catch it.

Reproduced on v20.x, v22.x, v24.x and v26.8.2 with a ten-line add-on
whose only distinguishing content is a NAPI_VERSION above
NODE_API_SUPPORTED_VERSION_MAX. `main`, `v22.x-staging` and
`v24.x-staging` all lack the check.

The error path had no test coverage: the message text appears in exactly
one file in the repository, `src/node_api.cc`. A test is added next to
`test_null_init`, which covers the sibling early return in the same
function.

Prepared with assistance from a closed-source coding agent, named in the
pull request description. The design, review and validation are my own:
I verified the fix and the test against a local build, including
removing the four added lines and relinking to confirm the test fails
without them.

commit.message:
fs: close fd 0 on discarded FileHandle transfer

`FileHandle::TransferData` uses `-1` to indicate that it no longer owns
a file descriptor. However, its destructor only closes descriptors
greater than 0.

If a transferred `FileHandle` owns fd 0 and the message is discarded,
the descriptor is left open.

Treat fd 0 like any other valid descriptor and only skip `-1`.

commit.message:
https: handle invalid TLS options in proxied requests

tls.connect() can throw while validating TLS options. For proxied HTTPS
requests, it is called after the CONNECT response has been received, so
the throw happens asynchronously from the original https.request() call
and ends the process as an uncaught exception.

Catch the error, close the tunnel socket, and propagate it to the
request.

commit.message:
perf_hooks: restore GC tracking after snapshot deserialization

V8 GC callbacks do not survive a snapshot, so a `'gc'`
PerformanceObserver that was active while building a user-land
snapshot received no entries after deserialization, unless another
`'gc'` observer was created.

When `'gc'` is observed while building a snapshot, add a deserialize
callback that registers the GC callbacks again if `'gc'` observers are
still active.

Assisted-by: OpenCode
Signed-off-by: James M Snell <jasnell@gmail.com>
PR-URL: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/66097
Reviewed-By: Xuguang Mei <meixuguang@gmail.com>
Reviewed-By: Matteo Collina <matteo.collina@gmail.com>

perf_hooks: track GC callback installation natively

Whether the V8 GC callbacks used for `'gc'` performance entries were
installed was tracked by a boolean in JavaScript, separately from the
native state, and the two could get out of sync. After deserializing a
user-land snapshot built while a `'gc'` PerformanceObserver was active,
the boolean claimed the callbacks were installed, although V8 GC
callbacks do not survive a snapshot. Observing `'gc'` again did not
install them, and disconnecting removed callbacks that had never been
registered, crashing the process.

Track the installation state in `PerformanceState` instead, and replace
the install and remove bindings with a single idempotent
`updateGarbageCollectionTracking()` binding, which registers the
callbacks if and only if there are `'gc'` observers.

Assisted-by: OpenCode
Signed-off-by: James M Snell <jasnell@gmail.com>
PR-URL: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/66097
Reviewed-By: Xuguang Mei <meixuguang@gmail.com>
Reviewed-By: Matteo Collina <matteo.collina@gmail.com>

perf_hooks: fix PerformanceObserver observer count leaks

Observing the same entry type more than once on a PerformanceObserver,
through repeated `observe({ type })` calls or duplicates in
`entryTypes`, incremented the internal observer count each time, while
`disconnect()` decremented it only once per observed type. The counts
never returned to zero, so GC tracking stayed installed, and entries
for types such as `'http'` and `'dns'` kept being created after all
observers had disconnected.

Count each entry type at most once per observer.

Assisted-by: OpenCode
Signed-off-by: James M Snell <jasnell@gmail.com>

Reviewed-By: Xuguang Mei <meixuguang@gmail.com>

commit.message:
src: let Environments on one isolate share a cleanup hook

The registry behind `AddEnvironmentCleanupHook()` is keyed on
{isolate, fun, arg} and asserts that every insertion is unique. Two
Environments on one isolate that register the same hook, which the
Node-API documentation allows per environment, abort the process on
the second `napi_add_env_cleanup_hook()`.

Key the registry on `arg` only and tell entries apart by Environment:
adding the same hook to one Environment twice still aborts as
documented, and removal prefers the current Environment's registration,
falling back to a matching one from another Environment when there is
no current context. Because the entry to remove after a hook has run can
no longer be found by {isolate, fun, arg} alone, `CleanupHookThunkRun()`
marks its entry as running and erases exactly that entry afterwards; a
removal of a running entry (a hook removing itself, as `~ObjectWrap()`
does) is a no-op, which keeps the use-after-free fixed by #65630 fixed.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/63985

commit.message:
src: fix task queue deadlock when built as C++23

Since #65353, FlushForegroundTasksInternal() and the
DelayedTaskScheduler drain their queues with
`for (auto& task : queue.Lock().PopAll())`. In C++20 the Locked
temporary is destroyed at the end of the range initializer, before the
loop body runs. C++23 (P2718R0) extends the lifetime of every temporary
in a range-for initializer to the end of the loop, so the queue's mutex
stays held while the tasks run, and the first task that posts to the
same queue - any V8 foreground task that schedules another one -
deadlocks on the non-recursive mutex. Node.js itself builds with
-std=gnu++20, but an embedder that compiles it as C++23 hangs in the
first foreground task flush.

Store the drained tasks in a local before iterating so the lock is
released independent of the language version.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/65353
Signed-off-by: Shelley Vohr <shelley.vohr@gmail.com>

commit.message:
stream: trim per-stream costs in webstreams

Short-lived streams (create, a few chunks, close) pay a fixed cost per
stream that dominates once the per-chunk path is lean.

Streams created internally (transform stream sides, tee branches,
ReadableStream.from, transferred streams) were built by wrapper
constructors that swapped the prototype of every instance and then
assigned an own, enumerable `constructor` property to look like a
public stream. Each internal stream therefore had its own hidden class
and `Object.keys(stream)` reported `['constructor']`. The public
constructors now accept the internal construction sentinel and leave
controller setup to the caller, so every ReadableStream and
WritableStream shares one hidden class and no per-instance prototype
swap or own property is needed.

The queue ring buffer grew after a push filled it, so the initial 8-slot
ring held only three (value, size) pairs and a four-chunk stream
reallocated every time. Growing before the push lets the ring hold four
pairs.

pipeTo observed the source's closed promise with two reactions and, on
teardown, let the reader and writer release paths probe and reject
promise records that only the pipe could have observed. One reaction
pair now watches the source, and finalize drops the records before
release.

commit.message:
perf_hooks: add performanceNodeTiming.uvMetricsInfoBigInt

`performance.nodeTiming.uvMetricsInfo` returns the libuv event loop
metrics as numbers, which are only exact up to
`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. Add `uvMetricsInfoBigInt`, which returns
the same metrics as bigints backed by `uint64_t` storage, carrying the
full 64-bit range reported by libuv.

A single native call fills both a `Float64Array` and a
`BigUint64Array`, so `uvMetricsInfo` does not pay for bigint
allocation and conversion. The new property is omitted from
`toJSON()`, as `JSON.stringify()` cannot serialize bigints.

using `v8::Integer::New()`), so they wrapped around after 2^31 on

commit.message:
sea: add vfsArchive to serve the assets from a ZIP archive

When "vfsArchive" names a ZIP archive in the SEA configuration (with
"useVfs": true), --build-sea embeds the archive verbatim as one
reserved asset, and at runtime the SEA virtual file system mounts the
existing ZipProvider over a zero-copy view of the embedded archive
instead of the SEAProvider. The main script is injected into the
in-memory archive index as a stored entry, so the mounted tree looks
the same as with "assets".

The archive can be produced with any ZIP tool or with the ZIP support
in node:zlib; no ZIP serialization logic is added to the build side.
This trades asset read speed (entries are inflated when opened) for a
substantially smaller executable when the assets are compressible.

Also make FindSingleExecutableResource() return the deserialized
SeaResource by reference instead of by value: the copy included the
whole assets map, and getAsset() calls it once per asset read, so
every fs operation served by the SEA virtual file system paid a cost
linear in the number of bundled assets - with 8192 assets, reading
each of them took seconds instead of milliseconds.

Signed-off-by: Matteo Collina <hello@matteocollina.com>

commit.message:
doc: document the node:ffi call paths

`node:ffi` dispatches native calls through one of three call paths: the
V8 Fast API with a generated trampoline, a per-function shared buffer,
or the generic libffi invoker. The public documentation only describes
the Fast API path and a "generic" fallback, never mentions the shared
buffer path, and leaves the selection order implicit.

Add a "Call paths" section to doc/api/ffi.md that explains the selection
order, what each path does, and when a signature qualifies for it, and
point the existing per-architecture limits table at it. Add a call path
overview table to the FFI Fast API internals contributor guide and
cross-link the two documents.

`node:ffi` dispatches native calls through one of three call paths: the
V8 Fast API with a generated trampoline, a per-function shared buffer,
or the generic libffi invoker. The public documentation only describes
the Fast API path and a "generic" fallback, never mentions the shared
buffer path, and leaves the selection order implicit.

order, what each path does, and when a signature qualifies for it, and
point the existing per-architecture limits table at it. Add a call path
overview table to the FFI Fast API internals contributor guide and
cross-link the two documents.

commit.message:
http: reduce per-request allocations in the server

Remove allocations and repeated work performed for every request:

- reuse a per-connection updateOutgoingData closure and a shared
  'finish' listener instead of binding two functions per request,
  reaching resOnFinish through the connection state stored on the
  response
- cache the ServerResponse options object per server (custom response
  classes keep receiving a fresh object)
- check for Host, Expect, Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding by
  scanning rawHeaders instead of materializing req.headers, which was
  built (with per-name toLowerCase calls) for every request even when
  the application never reads it
- cache the rendered status line per status code when the reason
  phrase is the default, skipping its character validation
- cache the complete 'Date: ...' header line in the utcDate cache and
  the keep-alive header pair for the current server settings
- compute the lenient-validation option chain once per message

commit.message:
buffer: add Buffer.stringLength()

Add `Buffer.stringLength(input[, encoding])`, the counterpart of
`Buffer.byteLength()`: it returns the number of UTF-16 code units that
`buf.toString(encoding)` would produce, without decoding.

For UTF-8 the count is computed with simdutf. Invalid input is counted
with the same maximal-subpart replacement that the decoder applies, so
the result always matches `toString().length`. The other encodings are
computed from `byteLength` alone.

This lets code that accumulates streamed input check the result against
`buffer.constants.MAX_STRING_LENGTH` and size its memory budget before
decoding.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/66062

the process, and `getEnabledCategories()` dereferenced a null pointer,

`ERR_TRACE_EVENTS_UNAVAILABLE` when it does not, as for a

commit.message:
sessions: Make sessions list component fixtures data-driven (#337926)

* sessions: Make sessions list component fixtures data-driven

Sessions list fixtures now declare state (sessions, custom groups, view options, and which rows are selected, focused, hovered or being renamed) and render it through the real list services and menus, replacing per-fixture mocks and DOM tweaks. Adds fixtures for custom groups, group rename and row interaction states, and moves the fixtures next to the sessions list.

The list widget and sessions list CSS pair row :hover rules with a .hovered class, so hover-only actions can be rendered without a pointer. Row operations that only tests need live in a TestSessionsList subclass under test/, keeping them out of the production API.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Keep archive wording per fixture when fixtures mount together

The explorer UI mounts all fixtures of a folder at once, and they share the archive action registrations. Switching those registrations to a fixture's wording changed the toolbars and onboarding targets of every mounted fixture, so they depended on mount order. Register the actions once in the Archive wording and let each fixture's menu service swap in its own wording's titles and icons.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Port nested chat archive fixtures to the list harness

Ports SessionsList_ArchivedNestedChat and SessionsList_ArchivedNestedChatSessionMenu from the old fixture file. Chats can now be archived in the test session builder, and the harness gains an interaction.contextMenu state that opens a row's production context menu. The fixture context menu service renders it with the product menu widget; the shared fixture services had stubbed context menus, so the session menu fixture never showed its menu.

Archive actions now take each fixture's wording from the production action descriptors by command id, which also covers wording-specific titles outside the shared presentation, such as Show Done Chats.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: Update sessions list screenshot hashes

Takes the Linux hashes CI rendered for the sessions list fixtures whose screenshots change: rows now show their production toolbar actions, and the two ported nested chat archive fixtures render the real Restore action and session context menu.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Pair the sticky row hover rule with .hovered

Keeps the new sticky row hover background from #337935 renderable in fixtures, like the other sessions list row hover rules.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: mark external sessions in ~/.copilot/chats as workspace-less (#337950)

agentHost: Mark external sessions in ~/.copilot/chats as workspace-less

The GitHub Copilot app keeps workspace-less chats in nested folders under ~/.copilot/chats (e.g. <date>/<name>). External discovery reported that folder as a regular working directory, so these sessions showed a workspace in the Agents window.

Copilot discovery and chat metadata now mark a chat workspace-less when its working directory is inside ~/.copilot/chats, unless the host already recorded its own marker. The catalog no longer backfills the persisted agentHost.workspaceless marker for external sessions: that marker also identifies host-created sessions, so persisting it would reclassify a rediscovered external session as internal.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

test: wait for MCP readiness in Copilot restart replay (#337934)

* test: wait for MCP readiness in Copilot restart replay

The recorded first tool call can run before the plugin MCP server starts, producing a nonexistent-tool result. Materialize an empty chat and wait for the plugin server's ready action before the default chat's first recorded turn.

A peer chat's MCP readiness does not establish readiness for the default chat that runs the probe and owns the restart target. Record a no-tool warm-up turn on that chat, await its server state, and replay the probe turns with the refreshed fixture.

commit.message:
agentHost: gate create_session chat folders on the provider's multi-root setting (#337920)

* agentHost: gate create_session chat folders on the provider's multi-root setting

`create_session` lets a current-session chat work in its own folder or
worktree, which needs a provider with multiple working directories.
Without it the tool advertised the capability anyway and failed with
"Provider does not support chat working directories".

Follow each provider's own `chat.agentHost.{copilot,claude,codex}Agent.multiRootEnabled`
setting, via the provider's `multipleWorkingDirectories` capability:

- Enabled: unchanged. `relationship` is optional (defaults to
  `currentSession`), and a current-session chat may take `workspace` and
  `worktree` to work in its own folder.
- Disabled: the session is offered the earlier shared-workspace
  `create_session`. `relationship` is required, current-session chats
  share the session's workspace, and `workspace`/`worktree` are rejected
  for `currentSession` and valid only for `independent` sessions.

The Copilot prompt snapshots go back to the shared-workspace definition
because the E2E suite runs Copilot with multi-root disabled.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: say "new chat or session" in the shared-workspace create_session prompt

A `currentSession` relationship creates a chat in the existing session,
not a new session, so the `prompt` description names both.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: keep the pre-feature create_session schema verbatim

Revert the `prompt` wording change so the shared-workspace
`create_session` definition is exactly the one used before chats could
work in their own folder.

This reverts commit 85ffafe36aa.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Fix response selection menu during pointer drag (#337921)

* sessions: fix: settle response selection after pointer release

Keep response-selection affordances hidden while a primary pointer drag is active, then reconcile the final selection on the next animation frame. This prevents the menu from flickering or intercepting upward selections while preserving synchronous keyboard selection behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: fix: preserve response selection drafts on pointer press

Track primary presses across the transcript without dismissing immediately. Dismiss only after a real selection change so drags begun between response parts stay gated while response controls cannot erase a focused question draft.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: fix: scope response selection to initiating pointer

Only finish selection reconciliation for the pointer that started the transaction, and cancel a pending release frame when a new selection begins. Update regression expectations for the current side-chat action label.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Stop chat progress signals once the request settles (#337883)

* Stop chat progress signals once the request settles

ChatAccessibilityService only removed a pending progress signal scheduler when a caller reported the response. Widgets that attach to an in-progress request (e.g. the Agents window new-session flow) never do, so every such session left a scheduler and its 5s signal loop alive. The map was also keyed by URI identity, so equal session URIs never matched.

Related to #146841

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Pause chat progress signals while a request waits for input

requestInProgress is false while a response waits for a confirmation or elicitation, so keep the pending entry until hasActiveRequest settles and restart the scheduler when processing resumes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Keep progress signals for reruns and unregistered chat models

Reruns cancel the active request right before sending its replacement, so only stop once the model settles as idle. Let ChatWidget pass the model it displays so unregistered models (the Agents window preparation transcript) still clean up on disposal.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: leave peer-discovered recorded pull requests to their folder (#337913)

* sessions: leave peer-discovered recorded pull requests to their folder

Recorded pull requests carry no folder, so #337694 adopted all of them
into the session folder's GitHub info. A pull request that a peer chat
created from its own worktree and recorded therefore still drove the
session row and every session-folder chat's PR status icon.

The session folder now skips a recorded pull request that another
folder of the session discovered for its own working directory, unless
the session folder discovered it too. Recorded pull requests no folder
discovered still belong to the session folder.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: keep recorded pull request exception out of the provider spec

The exception is concrete bug-fix behavior, so the regression test and
the comment beside the filter represent it; the specification keeps
its existing contract.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Enhance peer chat display in classic editor window (#337902)

* chat: Show session chats as independent items

Use the lightweight AHP session chat catalog so the classic Agent Sessions sidebar can expose every chat without eagerly subscribing to each session. Give peer chats distinct editor resources and route removals and deletion to the selected chat.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: Validate catalog chat origins

Reuse the catalog origin decoder at the list boundary and import the generated session-chat type from its protocol module.

commit.message:
sessions: fix renderer OOM from workspace file count telemetry (#337889)

SessionsTelemetryContribution computed workspaceFileCount with an unbounded
file search and restarted it on every send, because the prewarm bypassed the
per-session cache. When a session's workspace is a very large folder such as
the home directory, every file URI was materialized in the renderer until the
V8 heap ran out, and the next send after reopening crashed it again.

- Cap the count at 20,000 files, searching one folder at a time with the
  remaining budget so the cap holds across folders and schemes.
- Cache the pending or completed count per workspace URI and folder roots so
  each set of folders is scanned once per window.
- Skip the scan when usage telemetry is off, since the event is not sent.

Fixes #325919

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: show live HydraFusion phase work in its phase chat (#337635)

* agentHost: show live HydraFusion phase work in its phase chat

Runtime #21218 sends a provisional copy of each phase message and tool call
as it happens, then replays the committed phase with a commitId. Show the
copies live in the phase chat when the phase is known, and skip the
committed replay of anything already shown. A phase's answer still waits
for its commit, so a rejected draft never becomes the response.

Requires an SDK built on a runtime that contains #21218.

* agentHost: route every HydraFusion phase message to its phase chat

A phase's text is routed by its model call, not by whether each message
carries tool requests. Live, everything a phase says goes to its chat,
including its answer, so a rejected draft's answer is visible there. On
commit, a model call that ends in tool requests is phase work and one
that ends without them is the answer; earlier chunks wait for the last
one, so text before a reasoning boundary no longer leaks into the
response and displaces the real answer. Review phases still show their
critique on completion.

Also define renderMessage before the handler that uses it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: preserve Fusion phase chunks and completion routing

Share whole-call classification between live events and history, retain every complete Fusion chunk, and keep phase completion summaries out of the root response. Cover missing call IDs and non-Fusion rendering regressions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Release accessible view listeners per show instead of on dispose (#337857)

* Release accessible view listeners per show instead of on dispose

AccessibleView registered provider listeners (content changes, clear last provider, code block context) into its own store on every show and dropped the listeners of content refreshes. Every provider ever shown was retained for the lifetime of the window, e.g. every terminal whose accessible view was opened, including its TerminalInstance, xterm and DOM.

Related to #146841

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Honor clear requests of directly implemented providers

The clear-last-provider listener was only installed for AccessibleContentProvider instances, which excludes TerminalAccessibleBufferProvider. The terminal provider also lost its clear notification when the accessible view disposed it on hide, so tie it to the terminal instance lifetime.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address review: own render cleanup once and keep clear requests on help copies

- Create the context view cleanup once in render instead of returning a new tracked disposable from every _render call; refreshes discarded it.
- Copies of the current provider made for accessibility help use the structural provider check and forward onDidRequestClearLastProvider, so a terminal restored after the help view can still be cleared.
- Drop the unused _updateLastProvider() call in onHide that created an untracked provider copy on every hide.
- Tests render through a context view mock that behaves like the real one.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Don't restore a provider that was cleared while accessibility help was open

Closing accessibility help restored its copy of the last provider unconditionally. If the provider requested to be cleared while help was open (e.g. its terminal was killed), the copy was remembered again after the clear notification was gone, retaining the killed terminal.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Make render listener test independent of model attach timing

Editor contributions register their own key listeners when the accessible view's text model gets attached, which happens asynchronously and, on macOS, added listeners after the baseline was taken. Take the baseline once the model is attached.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Release canceled Delayer tasks to avoid retaining detached DOM (#337864)

* Release canceled Delayer tasks

Delayer.cancel() (and dispose()) rejected the pending promise but kept the last task closure until the next trigger(). QuickInputList's hover ThrottledDelayer therefore retained the tree mouse event, and through its relatedTarget a detached editor view.

Clear the task on cancel, reject with CancellationError when cancel lands after the delay elapsed but before the task runs, and drop the queued factory when a Throttler is disposed.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Ignore stale Delayer rounds after a late cancel

A cancel() after the delay elapsed, immediately followed by trigger(), let the stale round's continuation run the new task as the result of the canceled promise and clear the new round's promise and resolver, so the new promise never settled. Bind the continuation to its own completion promise and reject with CancellationError when it is stale.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Delayer.cancel() (and dispose()) rejected the pending promise but kept the last task closure until the next trigger(). QuickInputList's hover ThrottledDelayer therefore retained the tree mouse event, and through its relatedTarget a detached editor view.

Clear the task on cancel, reject with CancellationError when cancel lands after the delay elapsed but before the task runs, and drop the queued factory when a Throttler is disposed.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Ignore stale Delayer rounds after a late cancel

A cancel() after the delay elapsed, immediately followed by trigger(), let the stale round's continuation run the new task as the result of the canceled promise and clear the new round's promise and resolver, so the new promise never settled. Bind the continuation to its own completion promise and reject with CancellationError when it is stale.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: keep new-session controls opaque over dark chat backgrounds (#337832)

* sessions: keep new-session controls opaque over dark chat backgrounds

With a chat background, the new-session composer's bottom-row controls,
including the combined Mode + Permissions picker, were transparent in
the default dark themes. chatView.css repeated the chatWidget.css
surface rule at a higher specificity but fell back to
button.secondaryBackground, which 2026 Dark and Dark Modern make
transparent. The new-session view has no chat list to set
--vscode-chat-list-background, so that fallback always applied.
Removing the duplicate lets the chatWidget.css rule and its opaque
session-view fallback apply.

The opaque-surface test now uses the full new-session ancestry and a
transparent secondary background, so it catches this regression.

Fixes #337721

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: Update new-session chat background screenshot baseline

The new-session status controls now paint an opaque surface over the
chat background, which hides the part of a wallpaper icon that showed
through the Status control. The hash comes from the CI screenshot job.

commit.message:
sessions: add remote session delegation tools (#336690)

* sessions: add remote session delegation tools

Add host discovery, resource-aware remote creation, exact-chat messaging, and read-only session inspection in the Agents window.

Refs #336682

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: harden remote delegation after review

Handle background reference lifetimes and connection replacement, isolate message queues by destination, revalidate origins before creation, and bound response assembly. Preserve remote origin metadata in the upstream session catalog.

Validate unsupported callers from their invocation context without depending on visible-widget context keys.

Refs #336682

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: register remote-session translations

Add the remote sessions contribution to the localization resource registry so the CI translation reminder check passes.

Refs #336682

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: validate remote targets and queued message trust

Reuse authoritative workspace trust and model-availability checks, guard target replacement, retain uncertain deliveries until idle, and distinguish acknowledgement timeouts from cancellation.

Refs #336682

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: default remote tools off with an experiment setting

Gate remote delegation, messaging, discovery and inspection with chat.remoteSessions.tools.enabled. Respect experiment defaults and explicit user settings without abandoning running sessions. Also rename the host resource adapter to totalMemory.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: isolate remote tools configuration tests

Configuration registry suites clear module-load registrations. Restore the actual contributed configuration for each test when needed and clean up that registration afterward.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: localize remote session tool errors

Localize validation and host-selection diagnostics surfaced in chat while preserving protocol identifiers and model instructions.

Refs #336682

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: fix remote session tool test compatibility

Supply the required preparation context field and use a browser-compatible matcher while preserving complete validation-message checks.

Refs #336682

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: reduce remote delegation tool context

Shorten reply guidance, tool descriptions and schemas, and emit compact JSON without changing result fields. Cover deferred client-tool loading and its eager fallback.

Refs #336682

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: check added quick chat folders for trust

Chat-specific workspaces can add folders while the session retains its workspace-less marker. Exclude only the immutable scratch primary from workspace trust checks, rather than skipping all roots. Cover trusted and untrusted additions using host-qualified resources and keep scratch-only sessions unchanged.

Refs #336682.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: raise remote session limits

Raise creation requests per window to 500 and maximum depth to 10.
Cover both boundaries and retries at the creation limit.

Ref #336690.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: handle relay publish acknowledgement failures (#337819)

Track relay acknowledgements per published chunk and fail the transport on rejection or after 30 seconds without acceptance. Share the handshake timeout constant and use one scheduler without extending older publish deadlines.

Cover successful, Duplicate, rejected, missing, and out-of-order acknowledgements, including chunked sends and handshake and cleanup behavior. Do not automatically replay publishes.

commit.message:
[Experiment] Show a pip and popup when a Copilot sale is ongoing and the chat is closed (#331588)

* Add command-driven chat model picker onboarding tour

Arm via Chat: Start Model Picker Tour (F1), show an activity badge on Chat,
then open chat and spotlight the model picker when the view is revealed.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Show a sale card instead of the chat promo banner

When a model has a live discount, skip the chat-input banner and
open the post-update card with one Try CTA. The CTA opens chat and
switches the model the same way the banner does. Close and CTA share
the banner dismissal store. Remove the out-of-scope model picker tour.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Drop leftover model-picker tour wiring

Keep TOGGLE_CHAT_ACTION_ID file-local and remove the onboarding
spotlight target from the model picker. Neither is needed for the
sale card.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Gate sale card vs banner with chat.promo.saleNotification

Add a banner|popup setting (default banner) with an ExP auto override.
Keep the post-update sale card on-screen when the window is narrow:
size to the viewport, drop the fixed 80px gutter, and re-place on layout.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Strip sale promo sprawl from shared update widget

Drop the copied post-update widget changes, preview command, and unused
sale-card extras. Keep the collapsed-chat Copilot-icon pip and popup after
hasPromoBanner. Codex and Claude sales stay on their input banners.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: slim sale promo popup to collapsed-chat treatment

Keep the Copilot-icon popup only while Chat is collapsed so expanded Chat still uses the input banner. Drop extra SKU, entitlement, and unselectable gates, slim the card payload, and activate the pip via click, keyboard, and touch. Recover the pip class if the status entry rebuilds.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: simplify promo popup and refresh its state

Use typed card data and the shared Button, refresh changed promo payloads, recover replaced status entries and restore icons on disposal. Complete the Sale-to-Promo naming cleanup within the feature and cover refresh, dismissal and lifecycle regressions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: defer promo experiment until the final eligibility gate

Honor explicit closed-promo settings without reading ExP. Resolve the configured treatment only for eligible collapsed-chat promos with a visible status icon, preserve control banners, and reject stale responses. Remove eager experimental-default enrollment and cover override, visibility, refetch, failure and disposal behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: offer a sale once, in chat or as a pip

The collapsed-chat pip could re-offer a sale the user had already met as a
banner in an open chat. Record a promo as seen the first time a chat input
actually renders it, and stand the pip down for that promo id. The record is
application-scoped, so it holds across windows and reloads, and a later sale
still gets its own pip. The experiment stays the last gate.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: resolve the Chat session before the promo CTA picks a harness

Opening Chat from a collapsed state resolves its session asynchronously, so the
promo CTA read an undefined session and assumed the Local harness. A user who
met the sale as a pip therefore landed on whichever session Chat restored, and
the promoted model was never applied.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: restore the model vendor icon on the promo card

The collapsed-chat promo card fell back to a generic sparkle after the
payload lost its provider icon. Pass the model provider icon through the
card input again and cover it with a rendering test.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Keep the promo card vendor icon at its 24px design size

The hover host styles every codicon under .hover-contents with
font-size: inherit, which outranked the card's own rule and shrank the
model vendor mark to the card body font size. Scope the rule to the
promo hover so it wins, and pin the size in the widget test.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Load the hover stylesheet in the promo icon size test

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: log promo card shown, dismissed, and CTA analytics

Move closed-chat pip eligibility into the promo widget, hide the pip only
when Local chat is already showing the sale, and emit chatPromoWidgetShown,
chatPromoWidgetDismissed, and chatPromoWidgetAction telemetry with tests.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: address closed-promo review feedback

Keep the status-bar pip discoverable, avoid permanent dismiss when the
hover cannot open, use high-contrast borders, and defer input-notification
onDidShow until the Chat host is actually visible.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: soften closed-promo card gradient stop

Use a fixed 110px left wash at 33% button tint so every sale card gets
the same leading-edge gradient regardless of width.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: fix promo gradient property indentation

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: extract closed-promo eligibility from widget

Split opportunity detection (closed Local Chat + eligible sale) and treatment
selection (config/policy/TAS) out of ChatPromoWidgetContribution so future
closed-Chat treatments can branch independently of the Copilot icon popup.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: merge closed-promo eligibility into ChatClosedPromo

Combine opportunity detection and treatment selection into one feature-local
helper owned by the promo contribution, matching tip-style non-Service naming.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: drop host-visibility gate on input notifications

Remove setHostVisible / deferred onDidShow for hidden Chat hosts. That path
only covered collapsed-but-still-mounted Chat and is not a product case we want
to engineer for.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: invert closed-promo ownership to contribution

ChatClosedPromoContribution owns eligibility, treatment, and background
listeners, and drives ChatPromoIconPopup as presentation-only.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: fix closed-promo test type errors

Sinon withArgs is arity-typed to store(); count matching store calls by args instead. Type the hover mock options parameter.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: format closed-promo notification test

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: fix closed-promo eslint for multi-window DOM rules

Use DOM.isHTMLElement and dataset dot notation, track labeled nodes without querySelectorAll, and scope status-bar lookups with no-restricted-syntax disables.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: refresh closed promo when model message changes

Always forward the current opportunity model to the icon popup so title and payload updates apply even when the promo id is unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci: retrigger after unrelated linux electron flake

Agent Host Provider Integration idle-release timeout is unrelated to the closed-chat promo changes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: integrate model promos with the native status bar

Replace the custom popup and DOM interception with the standard status-bar tooltip and action. Preserve status priority, seen-promo state, keyboard focus, and restored chat sessions, with focused regression coverage.

Refactors #331588.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Ralph Feltis <ralphfeltis@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Logan Ramos <loganramos@microsoft.com>

commit.message:
automations: move Agent/Model pickers into the automation dialog composer (#337590)

* automations: move agent and model pickers into the prompt composer

Relocate the Agent mode and Model pickers from the standalone Session configuration toolbar into the chat input composer, matching how the New Chat composer surfaces the same controls. Execution mode and permissions remain below the prompt, and the now-redundant Session configuration header is removed.

- utomationDialog.ts reuses ChatInputPart.inputToolbarElement as the embedded Agent/Model lane and keeps execution/permission controls in a separate labelled group below the prompt.
- chatInputPart.ts exposes the existing input toolbar element as a narrow, reusable getter.
- modelPicker.ts and gentHostAgentPicker.ts contribute Agent/Model actions to the new Menus.AutomationsDialogInputToolbar menu, with responsive/compact support for the embedded layout.
- mobileChatInputConfigPicker.ts registers the combined phone picker against the same menu so phone layout stays equivalent.
- utomationsAccessibility.ts documents the new control layout in the dialog's accessibility help.
- Tests updated/extended to cover embedded vs. below-input placement, accessible grouping, and menu gating on desktop vs. phone.

* sessions: rename Copilot Cloud session type label to Copilot

The New Session and Automation dialog pickers showed the cloud-hosted agent as \Cloud\, which reads as an infrastructure detail rather than the product name users pick. Rename the label to \Copilot\ to match how it's presented elsewhere.

* sessions: add component fixture for the New automation dialog

Adds a component-explorer fixture for the automation dialog's Default
and Populated states, exercising the real `renderForm` export and a
real `Dialog` instance (matching `externalSessionBanner.fixture.ts`'s
precedent) rather than hand-built dialog chrome.

Follows existing fixture conventions:
- Agent-mode and execution/permission chips use plain synthetic
  `FixtureMenuService` entries (matching `newChatWidget.fixture.ts` /
  `renderChatInput.ts`), avoiding a non-provider fixture importing
  provider-specific picker contribution classes across the layer
  boundary.
- The Model picker keeps its real `AutomationModelPickerContribution`
  (a legitimate same-layer, non-provider import), preserving the real
  thinking-effort/context config-summary chip (e.g. "GPT-5.4 · High ·
  872K").

`modelPicker.ts`'s `AutomationModelPickerContribution` stays exported
so the fixture can instantiate it directly.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: fix automation dialog fixture against upstream ISession/IChat changes

Merging main brought in an upstream refactor that moved 'changes'/'changesets' from ISession to IChat. The fixture's mock ISession still overrode them, and its mock ISession.modelId/mode were derived from another mocked class's same-named properties (chat.modelId/chat.mode) rather than independent literals like every other override in that class - both trigger TS4113 (override modifier target not found) under tsgo/tsc on the merged tree even though the interfaces do declare those members. Fixed by giving session.modelId/session.mode their own constObservable(...) literals (matching the rest of the class) and moving the changes/changesets mocks onto the chat object, which is what production code (readSessionChangesStats) actually reads from.

* automations: keep picker layout changes narrowly scoped

Defer the new Automation dialog fixture and its export-only adaptation to follow-up work because its shared-bundle CSS ordering changes unrelated screenshots. Restore the existing Cloud provider label. Keep this PR focused on picker placement, required wiring, accessibility, and tests without changing global chat backgrounds or screenshot baselines.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* automations: label the actual picker toolbars

Forward the prompt toolbar label through ChatInputPart to the existing ActionBar API and remove redundant wrapper group roles. Assert the names on real nested toolbars and ensure each label appears only once.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Use VS Code GitHub auth for private plugin marketplaces (#337586)

* Use VS Code GitHub auth for private plugin marketplaces

* Git: Normalize trace environment variable names

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337586#discussion_r4088416670.\n\nAuthenticated Git retries now remove trace variables case-insensitively so lowercase Windows variants cannot expose authorization headers.

* Git: Scope marketplace auth to the actual remote

Addresses review threads https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337586#discussion_r4088416703 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337586#discussion_r4088416730.\n\nAuthenticated retries now resolve pull and fetch from the repository's actual origin, remove inherited extra-header configuration, and scope the reset and editor credential to the exact remote URL.

* Git: Recognize HTTP authentication failures

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337586#discussion_r4088416763.\n\nNative Git 401 and 403 status errors now trigger the existing VS Code GitHub authentication retry.

* Git: Preserve updates without an origin remote

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337586#discussion_r4096049729.\n\nPull and fetch now continue through the native path when an origin URL cannot be resolved.

* Git: Keep cancellation out of error logs

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337586#discussion_r4096049744.\n\nCancellation now propagates before authentication classification or error logging.

* Git: Defer editor auth lookup until fallback

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337586#discussion_r4096049757.\n\nCanonical Git operations now start with native Git immediately and look up the VS Code session only after a classified authentication failure.

* Git: Cover unsupported authentication retries

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337586#discussion_r4096049767.\n\nNegative tests now require unsupported origins and non-authentication failures to stop after the native attempt without cleanup or editor credentials.

* Git: Cover bare credential redaction

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337586#discussion_r4096049776.\n\nThe redaction test now exercises stderr containing only the encoded credential value rather than the complete authorization header.

* Git: Reduce marketplace authentication log noise

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Fix chat conversation context in Create PR for VS Code Agents Window (#337766)

* agentHost: generate pull request details from the originating chat

Chats sharing a folder share its Branch Changes changeset, whose
representative chat is the first chat working in the folder (the default
chat first). Prepare PR and Create PR built the title, description and
generated branch name from that representative chat's conversation, so
opening Create PR from a peer chat described another chat's work.

The Create PR form now names the chat it was opened from, mapped to its
backend chat URI, in a new `vscode.pullRequestConversation` operation
meta slot, kept apart from `vscode.pullRequest` so older hosts still
accept preparation requests. The host uses that chat's conversation only
when it is a chat channel of the same session whose first effective
working directory is the changeset's folder; otherwise, and when no chat
is sent, it falls back to the representative chat. Working directory,
branches and Git operations stay folder-scoped.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: list pull request files relative to the repository

The change summary fed to the model when generating a pull request
title and description listed each file by its absolute path and is
capped at 4,000 characters. In a worktree the repeated absolute prefix
made each line long enough that only about half of a 46-file change
fit; since the list is sorted, every `src/vs/sessions` file was cut off
and the model titled a Sessions change as Agent Host work.

Files inside the changeset's working directory are now listed relative
to it; files elsewhere keep their absolute path.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
chat: stabilize collapse scrolling and simplify tool errors (#337759)

* chat: stabilize collapse scrolling and simplify tool errors

- Prevent completed and stopped responses from retaining empty scroll space by limiting compensation to automatic collapses and bounding it to the viewport.
- Keep readers oriented by anchoring below pinned prompts, waiting for deferred collapse content before cleanup, and consuming existing space during manual expansion instead of briefly clamping the scroll position.
- Avoid adding padding for manual collapses, while preserving scroll-up intent and selection holds.
- Keep failed tool calls visually consistent with normal tool rows: restore the pre-card content renderer and change only the associated neutral error icon.
- Add regression coverage and interactive fixtures for animation-frame stability, lifecycle cleanup, sticky prompts, and live/restored tool errors.

Validation: 678 tests passed with one pre-existing skip; client type-check, targeted ESLint, Stylelint, and whitespace checks passed. Live component checks verified zero header movement during expansion and neutral error icons across dark, light, and high-contrast themes.

Follow-up to #337425.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: preserve tool failure accessibility and align diff headers

- Preserve denial indicators when suppressing duplicate failure icons, without changing the neutral failed-tool presentation.
- Keep failures distinguishable to screen-reader users by including error reasons and terminal exit codes in response labels and the Accessible View.
- Keep diff totals centered with their disclosure title and use compact chevrons after they move outside the title button.
- Cover live and restored tool states, header geometry at multiple font sizes, and interactive failed/denied examples.

Validation: affected renderer, tool progress, accessibility, response-model, thinking, and chat-list suites passed; client type-check, targeted ESLint, Stylelint, and whitespace checks passed. Live dark/light and narrow-layout checks confirmed aligned counts and 12px compact chevrons.

Refs #337759.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: make collapse tests use a reachable offscreen position

- Derive the offscreen header target from the preview's measured height instead of assuming the transcript can scroll 600px past it.
- Preserve the exact positioning, visibility, bounded-padding, and anchoring checks while covering both initially visible and offscreen headers.

The full CI stylesheet set makes the 48-tool preview shorter than in a focused run, clamping the old setup to -541px and failing the same two tests in Electron, Chromium, and WebKit.

Validation: reproduced both failures before the change; all 41 collapse-anchoring tests now pass with the full module/stylesheet set in Electron, Chromium, and WebKit, and in the focused Electron runner. Targeted ESLint and git diff --check pass.

Refs #337759.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: fix background subagent lifecycle and recipient labels (#337620)

* agentHost: fix background subagent reuse and inline progress

Preserve reusable child routing on cancellation and settle unroutable approval requests instead of buffering indefinitely. Restore live inline subagent observations across history hydration, including reused turns and new tool approvals.

Fixes #337339. Refs #335292.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: address subagent lifecycle review feedback

Retire cancelled child execution state through the existing completion cleanup so reuse cannot inherit usage or Auto routing. Bound failed routing suppression separately and release disposed signal buffers immediately.

Add regression coverage for cancelled usage, late completion, failed-route eviction, scoped cleanup, and reentrant permission denial.

Addresses review feedback on #337620.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: refresh MCP provenance screenshot baseline

Accept the CI-generated light-theme baseline for the MCP provenance fixture. The recorded difference is limited to insignificant border antialiasing.

Refs #337620.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: tolerate skipped pet teleport animation frames

The sprite player advances from elapsed time, so busy CI runners can legitimately skip intermediate frames. Verify both phase endpoints and reverse/forward ordering while retaining geometry, visibility, landing and focus assertions.

Refs #337620.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: stabilize MCP provenance fixture painting

Defer painting until the fixture is ready to avoid intermediate-paint antialiasing noise, and restore the latest CI baseline. Repeated targeted captures were stable in both themes.

Refs #337620.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: show readable write-agent recipients

Resolve agent names from lifecycle events, completion notifications and runtime task metadata in live and restored chats. Name each recipient for multi-agent writes while preserving raw routing IDs and the existing unknown-ID fallback.

Validated with 880 focused tests and a live Code OSS/AHP scenario covering single-recipient writes, broadcasts and renderer reload.

Refs #337620.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
chat: add user-perceived time to first progress telemetry (#337625)

* chat: add user-perceived time to first progress telemetry

Measure submissions and forks from UI interaction entry through first meaningful rendered progress, with explicit no-progress outcomes and telemetry-safe session context.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: harden first-progress telemetry and remove debug UI

Replace visual measurement helpers with trace-level start/end logs. Release interaction listeners and animation callbacks promptly, wait for visible fork navigation, and cover cancellation, hidden views, auxiliary windows, and repeated submissions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: make chat pet teleport frame assertions deterministic

Drive sprite timing with a controlled clock while retaining real browser layout, image loading, and the fall animation. Preserve the complete frame sequence and landing assertions under CI load.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: keep unrelated CI quarantine in a separate PR

Remove the Chat Pet timing-test adjustment from this telemetry change. The one-test quarantine is tracked independently in #337639.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: measure continuously visible progress across composer sends

End hidden observations without affecting requests, preserve gesture timing through Agents new-session and new-chat handoff, and correlate only the exact created response. Add visibility, lifetime, handoff, and provider forwarding regressions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: simplify submission timing and consolidate regression fixtures

Scope first-progress measurement to submissions, share response observation in one per-interaction handle, and remove fork navigation timing and startup reporting plumbing. Retain continuous visibility, Agents composer handoff, metadata, diagnostics, and lifecycle coverage.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: correct first-progress classification and attribution

Count visible serialized tool invocations, sample participant and session context at measurement completion, and preserve remote peer-chat fragments without leaking connection authorities. Cover the three Copilot review findings with focused regression tests.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: align first-progress timing cohorts across harnesses

Exclude queued sends without changing dispatch behavior, share a two-minute observation limit, and classify successful observations by request phase and first-progress kind. Preserve absent latency for excluded outcomes and keep the original submission clock.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: remove the first-progress observation timeout

Measure until progress or a real lifecycle outcome instead of imposing a telemetry-only duration cap. Leave provider/request timeouts unchanged and remove obsolete timeout test cases without adding a new regression test.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* build: preserve private npm staging directories during retries

Clear staged entries without recreating the mkdtemp directory, preserving its private permissions. Cover permissions and nested partial-file cleanup for both package materialization helpers.

* test: await queued server exit after termination failure

Keep Agent Host cleanup tied to the owned ChildProcess exit event when taskkill reports failure before Node delivers that event. commit.message:
agents: preserve session identity on first send (#337571)

The first-send path could replace a new remote session with an unrelated archived session.
A catalogue refresh could discover that old session before the requested session appeared.
The novelty fallback then selected the old session as the committed draft. The message still
ran in the requested session, but the visible conversation switched to the wrong session.

- Require the requested raw session ID and resource scheme in both the cache and session-added
  notification paths. Do not select a session only because it was absent from the earlier cache.
- Remove the novelty snapshot, in-flight own-ID set, and committed-ID claim set. Keep cancellation
  and connection-loss handling.
- Add tests for newly discovered archived and unarchived sessions in both matching paths.
- Update first-send test mocks to materialize the requested session ID.

Why the fallback and in-flight bookkeeping can be removed safely:

- The original novelty matcher came from #307732, when drafts used temporary untitled URIs.
  #313622 later made the client create the session URI and added a guard that rejects a backend
  URI different from the requested URI. First-send commitment therefore preserves identity.
- Commit 87d66b3a18fecc3f134f57467466203abee4e704 (#324792) preferred the own ID but retained a
  novelty fallback "for backends that assign a fresh id." That rationale does not match the
  first-send creation contract now enforced by the handler.
- The in-flight own-ID set protected the fallback from selecting another concurrent draft's
  session. Exact matching removes that possibility: send A accepts only A, even when B appears
  first. The claim set is also unnecessary for distinct drafts because their matches cannot
  overlap. Backend identity remapping would require an explicit mapping, not a novelty guess.
- The existing concurrent-send regression remains and passes: B materializes before A, and
  each send commits to its own session. Cached own-session and delayed-materialization tests
  also pass.

Validation:

- Client transpilation passed.
- Complete local and remote provider suites: 392 passing, 11 pending.
- ESLint passed for all three changed files.
- git diff --check passed.
- No live remote UI end-to-end validation was performed.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337322

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
test: fix Windows Agent Host descendant cleanup flake (#337657)

* test: avoid taskkill tree traversal for Agent Host descendants

Terminate individually captured descendants after server shutdown instead of asking taskkill to traverse a potentially stale Windows process tree. Restore the Windows-only coverage and use single-PID cleanup for the detached test process.\n\nFixes #337636\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: wait for Windows Agent Host descendants to exit

A successful process.kill does not mean Windows has released the process's working directory. Wait for the captured process identity to disappear before cleanup returns, and verify the delayed-exit case.

Fixes #337636

commit.message:
sessions: scope recorded pull requests to the session folder (#337694)

Recorded pull requests and issues carry no chat, folder or branch, yet
toGitHubInfo promoted them into the GitHub info of every folder of the
same repository. In a multi-folder session, a peer chat on its own
worktree therefore showed the session folder's recorded pull requests
as its PR status icon in the sessions list.

Promote recorded entries only into the session folder's GitHub info;
other folders report only the pull requests discovered for their own
working directory. Single-folder sessions and session-wide artifact
surfaces are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

agentHost: fix account-scoped Copilot SKU telemetry for Codex (#337258)

* agentHost: fix account-scoped Copilot SKU telemetry for Codex

Read entitlement metadata from the CAPI account cache instead of a Copilot-owned global property. Carry guarded account contexts through turn and tool telemetry, preserve valid refreshes, and isolate credential replay and endpoint-cache races. commit.message:
customEditor: forget failed documents so they can be opened again (#337607)

When creating a custom editor document failed (an extension's openCustomDocument threw, or the text model of a custom text editor could not be loaded), CustomEditorModelManager kept the rejected model promise. Every later attempt to open the resource got the same error back without asking the extension again, until the window was reloaded (#250622, #268301).

- CustomEditorModelManager forgets models that fail to resolve, skips them in getAllModels, and only lets an entry remove itself from the map so that stale references no longer dispose or drop a newer model.
- The custom editor resolver rethrows document creation failures so the editor shows the error, and reuses the webview handle when the same editor is resolved again.
- LazilyResolvedWebviewEditorInput resolves again after a failed resolve instead of memoizing the failure, so Try Again and the file-not-found placeholder reload work in place. Only the cancellation caused by disposing the input is ignored.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
chat: check nested subagent calls against the caller's allowlist (#337611)

* chat: check nested subagent calls against the caller's allowlist

RunSubagentTool resolved the current agent from the session's last
request, which is always the top-level agent because subagent requests
are not added to the chat model. A subagent's calls were therefore
checked against the top-level agent's `agents:` allowlist, so calls
two or more levels deep were rejected (regressed by #331442).

Tool invocation tokens now carry the id of the request they were issued
for. RunSubagentTool tracks running subagents by request id, and uses
the calling subagent's instructions and allowlist for nested calls. A
subagent that runs the tool without agentName now gets a copy of
itself, with its model, tools and hooks, instead of a copy of the
top-level agent.

Fixes #335257

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: model real tool enablement in the nested subagent copy test

The fake tools service only returned the tools an agent lists, while the
real service also returns every other known tool as disabled. Because
RunSubagentTool keeps an explicit `runSubagent: false`, the copy test
exercised a subagent calling runSubagent without having the tool, which
production does not allow. Mirror the real enablement map and list
runSubagent in the calling subagent's tools.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: surface staged Fusion client tools and give HydraFusion phases their own chats (#337621)

* agentHost: surface staged Fusion client tools and give HydraFusion phases their own chats

Client tools invoked during a provisional HydraFusion phase never ran: the SDK
handler waited on the client, the client waited for a tool start the runtime
was holding back until commit. Surface the start (or a synthesized one) when
the handler is invoked so skip-permission / auto-approved client tools and
tool search complete instead of hanging the response.

Also nest each phase's committed conversation (intermediate text, tool calls)
and review critiques under the phase tile as a child chat, both live and on
restore, and make the phase pill open that chat when one exists.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Guard Fusion phase chat closes against reopen during drain

A close that waits on file-edit completions cleared the open set immediately,
so a phase reopened on the error/resume path was closed by the stale callback.
Track the latest pending close per phase and only fire that one.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Bump golang.org/x modules and mdlayher/socket

golang.org/x/net v0.59.0, crypto v0.57.0, sys v0.48.0, term v0.46.0,
text v0.42.0, sync v0.23.0, tools v0.50.0, mod v0.41.0, time v0.16.0,
oauth2 v0.37.0, exp 85c1c2202aba, and github.com/mdlayher/socket v0.7.0.

x/mod v0.40.0 fixed CVE-2026-56865 and CVE-2026-56864 in sumdb; the
package is not vendored but module scanners flag the requirement. The
floors move together: x/net v0.59.0 requires the crypto, sys, term and
text versions above, x/crypto v0.57.0 and mdlayher/socket v0.7.0
