Invalid TLS options can cause an uncaught exception when an HTTPS request uses a proxy.

After the proxy responds to CONNECT, `tls.connect()` is called from the socket read handler. If TLS option validation throws at that point, the exception is outside the original `https.request()` call.

issues.body:
A discarded `FileHandle` transfer can leak fd 0.

`FileHandle::TransferData::~TransferData()` only closes descriptors greater than 0, but `-1` is the sentinel used when the descriptor is no longer owned. This means fd 0 is skipped even though it is valid.

This changes the check from `fd_ > 0` to `fd_ >= 0`.

The new test closes stdin, opens a file as fd 0, discards the transferred `FileHandle` through a `MessagePort` context mismatch, and verifies that fd 0 is closed

issues.body:
libuv reports the event loop metrics exposed through
`performance.nodeTiming.uvMetricsInfo` as `uint64_t` counters, but
they were copied into an `Int32Array` (and, before that, converted
using `v8::Integer::New()`), so they wrapped around after 2^31 on
long-running processes. While such large numbers aren't typical,
they are possible, making the current implementation flawed.

This PR stores the metrics in a `Float64Array` instead. Values are
now exact up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.

We also introduce a parallel `uvMetricsInfoBigInt` whose values are
represented as `bigint` to represent the fully correct value.

Note that the corrected handling using `Float64Array` vs. `Int32Array`
adds roughly 1-6ns per call overhead due to the fact that v8 must create
a `HeapNumber` from the `Float64Array` element while the `Int32Array`
allows it to use SMI. Given the typical usage pattern here, however,
6ns is unlikely to be noticed but it will show up in the unrealistic
microbenchmark.

issues.title: zlib: reject reset while a zstd frame is incomplete

labels.name: c++
labels.description: Issues and PRs that require attention from people who are familiar with C++.

labels.name: zlib
labels.description: Issues and PRs related to the zlib module and its compression dependencies.

labels.name: author ready
labels.description: PRs with CI started, the required approvals, and no outstanding review comments.

labels.name: needs-ci
labels.description: PRs that need a full CI run.

issues.body:
Calling `reset()` on a zstd compressor while a frame is still in progress left
the stream in a state where it produced output that could not be decompressed,
without reporting anything. This makes `reset()` throw instead.

Fixes #66087.

### The problem

`reset()` drops the state of the frame currently being compressed. Any bytes
that were already written out — by `flush()`, or by an earlier `write()` that
filled the output buffer — cannot be taken back, so they stay at the start of
the output stream. The next frame is then appended to that fragment, and the
result decodes as corruption.

```js
stream.write(Buffer.from('hello'));
await new Promise((r) => stream.flush(r));  // emits 14 bytes, frame unfinished
stream.reset();                             // frame state dropped here
stream.end(Buffer.from('world'));           // emits another 14 bytes, new frame
// 28 bytes total: fragment + complete frame -> ZSTD_error_corruption_detected
```

Without the `reset()` the same input produces 22 bytes and decodes to
`helloworld`, because `end()` continues the existing frame (8 bytes) instead of
starting a new one (14 bytes).

zstd requires buffers to be fully flushed before a new compression job starts —
see `ZSTD_compressStream2` in `deps/zstd/lib/zstd.h`:

> Before starting a new compression job, or changing compression parameters, it
> is required to fully flush internal buffers.

`ZSTD_compressStream2` returns non-zero while a frame is unfinished, which is
how a caller is meant to detect this. The compressor context was not keeping
track of that.

### The fix

`ZstdCompressContext` now records whether the current frame has completed. A
frame is complete once `ZSTD_compressStream2` has been called with `ZSTD_e_end`
and returned 0. `ResetStream()` refuses with `ERR_ZLIB_INCOMPLETE_FRAME`
otherwise:

```text
Error [ERR_ZLIB_INCOMPLETE_FRAME]: Cannot reset a zstd stream with an incomplete
frame; end the frame or discard the output produced so far
```

This follows the existing behaviour for the other invalid reset case, where
`reset()` during a write already throws.

After the change the repro above reports the error instead of emitting a
corrupt stream.

### What is not changed

- `reset()` before any write still works.
- `flush()` followed by `end()` still works and still produces a valid stream.
- `reset()` on a finished frame is unaffected.

### Tests

`test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-reset-incomplete-frame.js` covers the reset
mid-frame case, the valid `flush()` + `end()` sequence, and the valid
`reset()` before writing.

Ran against a `--debug-node --debug-symbols` build on Linux x86_64:

```text
$ ./out/Release/node --test test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-reset-incomplete-frame.js
✔ ZstdCompress reset throws when a frame is incomplete
✔ ZstdCompress flush followed by end still produces a valid stream
✔ ZstdCompress reset before any write still works
ℹ pass 3
ℹ fail 0
```

Existing zlib tests:

```text
$ ./out/Release/node --test test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd.js \
    test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-reset.js \
    test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-flush.js \
    test/parallel/test-zlib-reject-garbage-after-end.js \
    test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-pledged-src-size.js \
    test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-dictionary.js
ℹ pass 19
ℹ fail 0
```

### Notes

gzip and brotli hit the same class of problem for the same call sequence (their
output is undecodable too). I kept this PR to zstd because that is where the
failure is completely silent, but I am happy to look at the other two codecs
separately if that is wanted.

issues.title: zlib: reset() after flush() silently produces an undecodable zstd stream
issues.body:
### Version

v27.0.0-pre (built from `main` at `99f0ddef`)

### Platform

```text
Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 22.04, built with clang 20)
Reproduced identically on macOS arm64 with v26.8.1
```

### Subsystem

zlib

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

Call `.flush()` on a zstd compressor and then `.reset()` it. The stream keeps
producing output, but that output can no longer be decompressed, and **nothing
throws**.

```js
import * as zlib from 'node:zlib';

const stream = zlib.createZstdCompress();
const chunks = [];
stream.on('data', (chunk) => chunks.push(chunk));
stream.on('error', (err) => console.log('compress error:', err.code)); // never fires

stream.write(Buffer.from('hello'));
await new Promise((resolve) => stream.flush(resolve));  // <-- produces 14 bytes
stream.reset();                                          // <-- drops the frame state
stream.end(Buffer.from('world'));
await new Promise((resolve) => stream.on('end', resolve));

const output = Buffer.concat(chunks);
console.log('compressed bytes:', output.length);          // 28
console.log(zlib.zstdDecompressSync(output).toString());  // throws
```

Result:

```text
compressed bytes: 28
Error: Data corruption detected (code: ZSTD_error_corruption_detected)
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Always, as long as `reset()` is called after some bytes have already been
written out but before the frame is finished. A plain `flush()` (without
`reset()`) is fine, and so is `reset()` before any write — you need both calls
in that order.

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

The compressor should either produce a stream that decompresses correctly, or
report an error. It currently does neither — it silently emits a stream that no
zstd decoder can read.

`reset()` is documented as "cancel the current frame and start a new session".
Cancelling a frame would be fine on its own, but the bytes that `flush()`
already handed to the output stream cannot be taken back, so the next frame gets
appended to a fragment of the cancelled one.

zstd itself is explicit that this is not allowed. From `deps/zstd/lib/zstd.h`
(`ZSTD_compressStream2`):

> Before starting a new compression job, or changing compression parameters, it
> is required to fully flush internal buffers.

`flush()` leaves the frame unfinished: `ZSTD_compressStream2` returns non-zero
in that case, which is how a caller is supposed to know there is still work
pending.

### What do you see instead?

`flush()` emits a **fragment** of the frame (14 bytes in the example above).
`reset()` throws that frame away, but the 14 bytes stay in the output. `end()`
then starts a brand-new frame on the reset session and emits 14 more bytes. The
result is a 28-byte stream made of `fragment + complete frame`, which decodes as
corruption.

The same amount of data without the `reset()` produces 22 bytes and decodes to
`helloworld` — because `end()` continues the existing frame (8 bytes) instead of
starting a new one (14 bytes).

### Additional information

This is a source code level debugging observation

**1. write("hello") → `SetFlush`, `flush = 0` (`ZSTD_e_continue`)**

The data goes into the compressor but nothing comes out yet.

![breakpoint on SetFlush](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/node-bug-assets/main/f018/01-breakpoint-setflush.png)

**2. `DoThreadPoolWork` with `flush_ = ZSTD_e_continue`**

`input_` holds the 5 bytes, `output_.pos` is still 0.

![continue state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/node-bug-assets/main/f018/02-write-continue.png)

**3. flush() → `SetFlush`, `flush = 1` (`ZSTD_e_flush`)**

Same breakpoint, now with the value that forces output.

![flush triggered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/node-bug-assets/main/f018/03-flush-triggered.png)

**4. `DoThreadPoolWork` with `flush_ = ZSTD_e_flush`, before the call**

![before output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/node-bug-assets/main/f018/04-flush-before-output.png)

**5. After stepping over the call: `output_.pos = 14`**

`input_` is empty, but 14 bytes were flushed out — an unfinished frame.

![14 bytes fragment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/node-bug-assets/main/f018/05-fragment-14-bytes.png)

**6. reset() → `ResetStream` runs `ZSTD_CCtx_reset(session_only)`**

The 14 bytes are already out, but the frame state is about to be dropped.

![reset drops frame](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/node-bug-assets/main/f018/06-resetstream-drops-frame.png)

**7. end() → `DoThreadPoolWork` with `flush_ = ZSTD_e_end` produces another 14 bytes**

A fresh frame, not a continuation of the previous one. 14 + 14 = the 28 bytes
above.

![end new frame](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/node-bug-assets/main/f018/07-end-new-frame-14.png)

**Other codecs are affected the same way.** gzip and brotli both produce
undecodable output for the same `flush()` + `reset()` sequence, so this is not
specific to the zstd backend:

| codec | result of `flush()` + `reset()` |
| --- | --- |
| gzip | `Z_DATA_ERROR` |
| brotli | `ERR__ERROR_FORMAT_PADDING_2` |
| zstd | `ZSTD_error_corruption_detected` |

The zstd case is arguably the worst of the three because the compressor itself
reports nothing at all — with gzip/brotli the failure at least surfaces on the
same stream.

issues.body:
`node:ffi` dispatches native calls through one of three call paths: the V8 Fast API with a generated trampoline, a per-function shared buffer, or the generic libffi invoker. The public documentation only describes the Fast API path and a "generic" fallback, never mentions the shared buffer path, and leaves the selection order implicit.

This PR:

- Adds a "Call paths" section to `doc/api/ffi.md` that explains the selection order, what each path does, and when a signature qualifies for it. The existing per-architecture limits table now points at it.
- Adds a call path overview table to `doc/contributing/ffi-fast-api-internals.md` and cross-links the two documents.

The described behaviour matches `DynamicLibrary::CreateFunction()` in `src/node_ffi.cc`, `IsFastCallEligible()` / `IsSBEligibleSignature()` in `src/ffi/types.cc`, and the wrapper in `lib/internal/ffi-shared-buffer.js`.

Docs only, no code changes. `tools/lint-md/lint-md.mjs` passes on both files.

agentHost: discover a peer chat's pull request in its own folder
issues.body:
When a peer chat works in its own worktree and creates a pull request outside the Agents Window's Create PR operation (for example with `gh pr create`), the pull request showed on the session's main chat instead of on the peer chat.

## Why

At turn end the host looks up the pull request of the current branch. `GitHubReferencesContribution` passed the owning session (`turn.session`) for every turn, so a peer chat's turn only looked up the session folder's branch. The peer worktree's folder was never looked up, so its GitHub state never got the pull request. The client only knew about it from the recorded artifact, and recorded artifacts carry no folder, so they attach to the session folder.

The other lookup triggers don't cover this case:
- Session restore looks up the session folder only.
- A peer chat's Git refresh looks up its folder only when the branch changes.
- Agent Merge looks up per folder, but only while it is on.
- The Create PR operation records the pull request on its folder directly, but `gh` bypasses it.

## Change

A turn that ends in a peer chat whose folder isn't the session folder now looks up that chat's folder, which runs the existing per-folder lookup (`_attachFolderGitHubPullRequest`). The default chat, peer chats in the session folder, and sessions without a folder keep looking up the session folder. Once the peer folder has the pull request, the client already moves the recorded artifact from the session folder to that folder, so no client change is needed.

## Notes for reviewers

- Session restore still looks up only the session folder, so an existing session's pull request moves to the peer chat after that chat's next turn, not on restart. That could be a follow-up.
- Test: `chatContributions.test.ts` covers turn ends from the session, the default chat, a peer chat in the session folder, and a peer chat in its own folder. Without the fix it fails on the last case.
- Validated with `typecheck-client`, the Agent Host node tests (8,303 passing), the sessions unit tests (4,794 passing), and eslint.

issues.title: Build/Package fails at prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim due to .moduleignore stripping @github/copilot/sdk

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?:
 N/A (This is a local build/packaging failure from source, occurring before the application or extensions are loaded)

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version:  1.139.0 / 1.139.1 (Building from source, `main` branch)
- OS Version: Linux x64

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Clone the `microsoft/vscode` repository and checkout release `1.139.0` (or `1.139.1` / `main`).
2. Run `npm install` strictly following the "How to Contribute" guide.
3. Run a packaging gulp task, for example: `npm run gulp vscode-linux-x64`.
4. The build fails during the `prepareCopilotRipgrepShimTask` phase.

Expected Behavior:
The build should successfully package the VS Code binaries without missing dependencies.

Actual Behavior:
The build fails with the following error:
```text
Error: [prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim] Copilot SDK directory not found at <path>/resources/app/extensions/copilot/node_modules/@github/copilot/sdk
    at prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim (file:///<path>/build/lib/copilot.ts:273:9)
```

Root Cause Analysis:
There is a conflict between the `.moduleignore` configuration and the Copilot packaging script introduced in the 1.139.x releases.

1. `build/.moduleignore` contains the rule `@github/copilot/**` which strips the `@github/copilot` directory from the local `extensions/copilot` build.
2. However, `build/lib/copilot.ts` (specifically `prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim`) explicitly expects this directory to exist in order to copy target-platform `ripgrep` binaries into it:
```typescript
const copilotSdkBase = path.join(copilotBase, 'sdk');
if (!fs.existsSync(copilotSdkBase)) {
    throw new Error(`[prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim] Copilot SDK directory not found at ${copilotSdkBase}`);
}
```

Workaround:
Adding an exception for the `sdk` directory in `build/.moduleignore` allows the local packaging step to succeed:
```text
@github/copilot/**
!@github/copilot/sdk/**
```

issues.title: compareIgnoreCase sorts ASCII punctuation [\]^_` after letters, contradicting its own ordering contract
issues.body:
`compareSubstringIgnoreCase` (which backs `compareIgnoreCase`) normalizes case by mapping lowercase ASCII letters *up* to uppercase (`code -= 32`, `src/vs/base/common/strings.ts:404-409`). That moves `a-z` (97-122) down to `A-Z` (65-90), i.e. below the punctuation block 91-96 (`[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `_`, backtick).

But the function's own test oracle (`src/vs/base/test/common/strings.test.ts:95`) defines the intended order as `compare(a.toLowerCase(), b.toLowerCase())`, which keeps letters at 97-122, above 91-96. So for any letter-vs-punctuation pair in that range, the sign of the result is inverted relative to the documented contract:

```
compareIgnoreCase("[", "a")  // +26, oracle says negative
compareIgnoreCase("_", "b")  // +29, oracle says negative
```

This is user-visible: `compareIgnoreCase` is used as a real sort comparator, e.g. language-name sorting in `src/vs/editor/common/services/languagesRegistry.ts:295` and repository-group label sorting in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentSessionsViewer.ts:1442`. Any label starting with `[`, `^`, `_`, or backtick sorts after plain alphabetic labels instead of before them:

```
sorted by compareIgnoreCase: ["apple", "banana", "Cherry", "[brackets]", "^caret", "_config", "`tick`"]
expected (lowercase order):  ["[brackets]", "^caret", "_config", "`tick`", "apple", "banana", "Cherry"]
```

The existing tests (48 passing) miss this because none of the `compareIgnoreCase` cases pair a letter with a character in the 91-96 range. Mapping uppercase to lowercase (`code += 32`) instead would match the oracle; equality results are unaffected either way.

Seen on main at `51c141f0` (2026-09-25).

issues.title: Agents - keep chat git state when the git probe fails
issues.body:
Sessions could suddenly lose their Git-backed changesets (Branch, Uncommitted, Compare) mid-session, leaving only Session Changes and This Turn until a later Git refresh succeeded.

## Cause

Since #331792, `_computeSessionGitState` returns `undefined` when `git status` fails or times out (5 s default), with the contract that callers keep the last known state. The session-keyed refresh honors that. When changesets moved to chats (#337263, #337594), the chat-keyed refresh started clearing the chat's Git state on `undefined`. The default chat writes through to the session's persisted Git state, so one transient probe failure during a turn also wiped the session's Git state. `buildDefaultChangesetCatalog` then published a Git-less catalogue.

No Git service change makes `git status` fail more often; what changed is how a failure is handled.

## Fix

Keep the last known Git state when the Git probe returns nothing, matching the session-keyed behavior. Explicit clears (no resolvable working directory, chat removal) are unchanged.

## Validation

- Updated the peer-chat folder-scope test to expect retained state after a failed probe.
- Added a default-chat regression test.
- All agentHost node tests pass.

issues.title: Agent sessions: built-in GitHub MCP server is locked to a read-only 19-tool subset and its toolset cannot be configured
issues.body:
### Summary

Agent sessions in VS Code get a built-in GitHub MCP server that exposes only 19 tools, all marked `readOnlyHint: true`. There is no supported way to request additional toolsets (e.g. `projects`, `labels`), so the project-board write tools (`projects_write`, `label_write`, `issue_write`, `create_pull_request`) are unreachable from an agent session even when the user has the required OAuth scopes.

The remote endpoint supports these toolsets. The problem is that the agent host never sends `X-MCP-Toolsets` and offers no setting to add it.

Even when installing the github mcp and editing it's settings to all tools, the agents view still overwrites this and only claims 19 tools available to the agent.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| VS Code version | 1.139.1 |
| Copilot Chat extension | 0.67.0 |
| OS | macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83), arm64 |
| MCP server | `github-mcp-server` (built-in, agent host) |
| GitHub account scopes | `repo`, `read:org`, `read:user`, `user:email`, `read:packages`, `write:packages`, `read:project`, `project`, `gist`, `notifications` |

### Steps to reproduce

1. Ensure `chat.agentHost.githubMcpServer.enabled` is `true` (the default, even setting this to false didn't work for me, it still clinged to only 19 tools by default completely ignoring the github MCP i had downloaded and set up myself.).
2. Start an agent session and inspect the available GitHub MCP tools.
3. Note the tool list is 19 entries, every one annotated `readOnlyHint: true`.
4. Attempt to find a setting that configures the built-in server's toolsets.

### Actual behaviour

The agent session receives exactly these 19 tools:

```
actions_get, actions_list, get_commit, get_copilot_space, get_file_contents,
get_job_logs, issue_read, list_branches, list_commits, list_copilot_spaces,
list_issues, list_pull_requests, pull_request_read, search_code, search_issues,
search_pull_requests, search_repositories, search_users, web_search
```

All have `readOnlyHint: true`. `projects_write`, `projects_get`, `projects_list`, `issue_write`, `label_write`, and `create_pull_request` are all absent.

The only related setting, `chat.agentHost.githubMcpServer.enabled`, is a boolean that can only disable the server entirely. It cannot configure the toolset.

### Expected behaviour

The user should be able to select which toolsets the built-in GitHub MCP server exposes — for example via a setting, or by supplying a server definition that the agent host honours — so that accounts with the `project` scope can use project-board tools from agent sessions.

### Evidence

**1. The remote endpoint supports the extra toolsets.**

Calling `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` directly with a token that has the scopes above:

| Request | Tools returned | `projects_write` | `label_write` |
|---|---|---|---|
| No `X-MCP-Toolsets` header | 48 | ❌ | ❌ |
| `X-MCP-Toolsets: all` | 99 | ✅ | ✅ |

So the capability exists server-side; it is purely a client-side header issue.

**2. The built-in server's headers are hardcoded.**

In `out/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostMain.js`:

```js
var sr = "github-mcp-server",
    Hle = "X-MCP-Features",
    Ule = "remote_mcp_ui_apps,mcp_apps_disable_form_deferral",
    Nle = "X-MCP-Tools",
    dz = ["get_file_contents", "search_code", "get_copilot_space", "list_copilot_spaces", "web_search", "search_users"],
    Fle = ["search_repositories", "list_branches", "list_commits", "get_commit", "issue_read", "list_issues", ...];

function Ble(r, n = false) {
  let e = dS(r);
  if (!e) throw new Error("Unable to resolve the GitHub MCP server URL");
  let t = { [Hle]: Ule, [Nle]: Wle(n).join(",") };
  return { type: "http", url: e, headers: t };
}
```

Only `X-MCP-Features` and `X-MCP-Tools` are sent. `X-MCP-Toolsets` does not appear anywhere in the VS Code application bundle. The tool allowlists are hardcoded arrays in the source, not read from configuration.

**3. Agent sessions do not consume the user-level `mcp.json`.**

MCP discovery for agent sessions reads only:

```js
function Ipe(r, n) {                 // r = workingDirectory, n = userHome
  let e = [];
  r && (e.push(v.joinPath(r, ".claude", "settings.json")),
        e.push(v.joinPath(r, ".mcp.json")));
  e.push(v.joinPath(n, ".claude", "settings.json"));
  return e;
}
```

`~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/mcp.json` is not in this list. A server defined there is visible to the workbench/chat surface (its tool cache shows the server with 99 tools) but never reaches an agent session. This produces a confusing split where the same server appears configured in one place and absent in another.

**4. Supplying a server with a matching URL does not restore the toolsets.**

Because dedupe compares normalized URLs:

```js
_isGitHubMcpServer(e, t) {
  let i = this._gitHubMcpServerConfiguration?.type === "http"
    ? da(this._gitHubMcpServerConfiguration.url) : void 0;
  return e === sr || (i !== undefined && t.url !== undefined && da(t.url) === i);
}
```

a user-supplied `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` (with `X-MCP-Toolsets: all`) collides with the built-in identity. The result in practice was not the 99-tool set but the 48-tool default, i.e. the header was not applied to the session's server.

### Impact

Any workflow that needs project-board mutations, labels, or issue/PR creation from an agent session cannot be completed. In this case an issue-to-PR automation had to fall back to the `gh` CLI, because `projects_write` and friends were unreachable — despite the token holding the `project` scope and the remote server supporting them.

### Suggested fix

Either:

- add a setting (e.g. `chat.agentHost.githubMcpServer.toolsets`, mirroring the existing `github.copilot.chat.githubMcpServer.toolsets`) that is translated into an `X-MCP-Toolsets` header on the built-in server, or
- honour a user-supplied GitHub MCP server definition for agent sessions, including its `headers`, instead of collapsing it into the built-in identity.

It would also help to document that `User/mcp.json` is not read by agent sessions, since the current behaviour is hard to diagnose.

issues.title: workbench: Align macOS window-facing card corners
issues.body: ## Summary Make the inset card corners next to the native macOS window frame concentric in the Agents window and the editor's Modern UI floating layout. - Share the existing macOS frame radius and subtract the outer gutter for exposed card corners. - Account for UI zoom so the native frame stays fixed in screen coordinates. - Keep zoom values local to each workbench so detached editors can use independent zoom levels. - Follow the exposed edge when the panel, editor, or sidebars change; preserve internal seams and the existing fullscreen, compact, web, and non-macOS treatments. - Limit portaled webview rounding to anchors that actually touch the frame, including split editors and view panes. - Add regression coverage for corner ownership, older macOS/Tahoe, zoom, high contrast, and unaffected layouts. On macOS Tahoe at default zoom, this gives the exposed card corner a 12px radius inside the existing 4px gutter, rather than using the independent 8px card radius. ## Validation - `npm run typecheck-client` - Targeted ESLint and CSS stylelint - Eleven focused Electron regression tests covering both windows, compact layouts, independent auxiliary zoom, and split webviews - Native Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev on macOS 26.7: panel hidden/shown, zoom in, and zoom reset in both windows - Native split Markdown previews and independent main/auxiliary zoom through the native window zoom API - Matched native-window before/after captures using the baseline styles and the updated styles at the same window size and zoom The detached-window validation captured two separate raw recordings; the runner cannot combine them into one captioned timeline. ## Manual verification 1. On macOS, enable Modern UI and hide the status bar in the editor window. 2. Inspect the bottom corners next to the native frame; the gutter should follow the curve evenly. 3. Toggle the panel and sidebars, then zoom in/out. 4. Repeat in the Agents window. 5. Check that fullscreen, compact layout, and internal card corners retain their existing treatment. 6. Open Markdown previews in stacked editor groups and verify that only the bottom preview's exposed corner changes. 7. Give a detached editor a different zoom level, then zoom the main window and verify that the detached window's frame keeps its own scale.

issues.title: Agents Window uses incorrect base branch for Branch Changes with existing Git worktree
issues.body:
Type: Bug When starting an agent session in the VS Code Agents window using an existing Git worktree, the **Branch Changes** view uses `main` as the base branch instead of the branch that the feature branch was created from / tracks. In my repository: - The repository's default branch on GitHub is `dev`. - I create Git worktrees outside of VS Code. - The feature branch is created from `dev`. - The feature branch's upstream is `origin/dev`. - I open the existing worktree/folder in VS Code and use it for an Agents window session. - The Agents window nevertheless displays the comparison as: ```text feat/agency-office-types → main ``` I expect it to display: ```text feat/agency-office-types → dev ``` This results in **Branch Changes showing an incorrect and much larger diff**, because it includes differences between `dev` and `main` that have nothing to do with the feature branch. ## Steps to Reproduce Given a repository whose default branch is `dev`: ```bash git fetch origin git worktree add \ -b feat/test \ ../test-worktree \ origin/dev cd ../test-worktree git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/dev feat/test ``` Then: 1. Open the existing `test-worktree` folder in VS Code. 2. Open the **Agents** window. 3. Start an agent session using the existing folder/worktree. Do not ask VS Code to create a new worktree. 4. Make the session active. 5. Open **Changes**. 6. Select **Branch Changes**. ## Actual Behavior The Agents window compares the feature branch against `main`: ```text feat/test → main ``` As a result, Branch Changes includes unrelated changes between `main` and `dev`. ## Expected Behavior The Agents window should compare against `dev`: ```text feat/test → dev ``` For an existing worktree/folder, VS Code should determine the appropriate base branch from the existing Git repository rather than silently falling back to `main`, or allow user to change the base for comparison in the Changes pane. issues.title: TPI: Continue a ChatGPT Codex chat in VS Code
issues.body:
Refs: #337659

- [ ] windows (origin) -> linux (remote), worktree isolation
- [ ] macos (origin) -> windows (remote), folder isolation

Complexity: 3

Authors: @Giuspepe 

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23337969%0A%0A&assignees=Giuspepe)

---


# TPI: Continue a ChatGPT Codex chat in VS Code

## Context

Codex chats created or updated in ChatGPT should appear in the VS Code Agents window within a few seconds. You should not need to reload the window or restart anything.

If ChatGPT still has control of a chat, VS Code should keep it readable and explain why you cannot continue it yet. You should be able to retry after quitting ChatGPT.

**You need a ChatGPT account and the ChatGPT app to test this TPI.**

## Test steps

1. Open the Agents window in VS Code. Make sure Codex and external sessions are enabled.
2. Create a Codex chat in ChatGPT and exchange a few messages. Watch for the chat in the Agents window. It should appear within a few seconds without a reload or restart.
3. Open the chat in VS Code while ChatGPT still has it open. Check that the transcript is current and that VS Code shows a lock banner above the input before you try to send.
5. Try sending a message from VS Code and use Retry while ChatGPT is still running. VS Code should not start a turn or add duplicate messages.
6. Fully quit ChatGPT, then use Retry again. The banner should disappear, your draft should remain, and VS Code should not send it automatically.
7. Send the draft yourself and check that the chat continues normally in VS Code.
8. Try continuing the chat in ChatGPT again

issues.title: macOS 27: "Path does not exist" when opening folders with Portuguese (pt-BR) accented names on SMB share via File > Open Folder
issues.body:
Type: Bug After updating to macOS 27.0, I can no longer open folders or files located in folders with accented names (Portuguese, pt-BR — e.g. "Usuários", "Diário") on an SMB network share using File > Open Folder. This worked fine before the macOS update. Environment: - macOS 27.0, Apple Silicon (M1 Pro) - VS Code 1.137.0 (arm64) - Folder is on an SMB share mounted under /Volumes Steps to reproduce: 1. Connect to an SMB share containing folders with accented names (e.g. /Volumes//Usuários///Diário). 2. In VS Code, use File > Open Folder and select the folder through the dialog. Expected: the folder opens. Actual: error dialog "Path does not exist — The path '/Volumes//Usuários///Diário' does not exist on this computer." Diagnosis: The server stores the folder names in Unicode decomposed form (NFD). Checking the bytes: $ ls /Volumes/ | grep -i usu | xxd 00000000: 5573 7561 cc81 7269 6f73 0a Usua..rios. "á" is stored as "a" + U+0301 combining accent (61 cc81) instead of the precomposed form (c3a1). The path returned by the Open Folder dialog seems to use the precomposed (NFC) form, which does not match the name on the server, so the path is not found. Evidence that VS Code itself can handle the folder: - Passing the exact on-disk (NFD) path via the CLI works: `code -n ""` opens the folder normally. - Opening via File > Open Recent (after the folder was opened once via CLI) also works. - Other apps (e.g. Microsoft Excel) open files from the same folder through their own open dialogs without problems. So the issue appears to be in how the path returned by the native Open Folder dialog is handled (possibly NFC normalization) before it is used to access the file system. Workaround: open folders via the CLI or a Finder Quick Action that passes the exact path. Renaming the folders is not an option, since they are on a shared server used by other people. issues.title: [Feature Request] Allow chatSessionResource and telemetry badges to parse external Gateway consumption headers (e.g., Vercel AI Gateway)
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
### Feature Description

Following the implementation of milestone **1.126.0** (Issue #317977), VS Code introduced excellent per-message token usage and cost metrics badges. However, this telemetry metric framework is currently tightly coupled to internal GitHub Copilot billing schemas. 

As the **VS Code Agents** environment scales to allow developers to bring their own model endpoints and provider-agnostic infrastructure, there is currently no way to bubble up per-session cost tracking from third-party AI gateways like **Vercel AI Gateway**. Alternative tools like OpenCode already process this by default by remaining completely provider-agnostic while still tracking session spend.

When routing model traffic through a custom gateway, providers inject metadata headers directly into the stream payload (for instance, Vercel’s `x-vercel-ai-gateway-spend` or standard token counters). VS Code currently strips or discards these custom header footprints from the UI layer.

### Proposed Solution

1. **Expose an Extensible Metadata Parser Hook:** Allow the core chat and agent UI components to intercept response headers from the active language model provider stream.
2. **Support Dynamic Cost Badge Mapping:** Introduce a configuration setting or API hook where users or extensions can map arbitrary header keys (like `x-vercel-ai-gateway-spend` or custom token parameters) directly into the native UI session badge footer.
3. **Preserve Session Mapping:** Ensure that `chatSessionResource` contexts pass downstream response parameters accurately so extensions can reliably track session budgets without requiring brittle, backward-scanning hacks.

### Alternative Solutions Considered

- Using third-party extensions, but these cannot cleanly hook into the newly implemented native agent/chat session footer badges because the core framework discards custom provider telemetry headers.
- Constantly running `vercel ai-gateway api-keys inspect` in a side terminal, which breaks the flow of development inside the agent workspace.

### Additional Context

Giving developers real-time feedback on their chosen agnostic gateway's spending directly inside the active editor pane ensures proper budget boundaries and model optimization during long multi-agent loops.

Ref: #317977

issues.title: SCM - Update activeRepositoryName logic to use repository name for worktrees
issues.body:
This pull request modifies the logic for computing the `activeRepositoryName` variable in the context of Git worktrees. The changes ensure that the window title reflects the canonical repository name instead of the worktree name.

Key changes include:

- Updated the `SCMActiveRepositoryController` to prefer the `parentRootUri` when the `contextValue` is `'worktree'`, allowing the title to display the repository name.
- Introduced a new optional `SourceControl.repositoryName` metadata field to facilitate this change without disrupting existing functionality for other SCM providers.
- Added focused tests to validate the new behavior and ensure that the propagation of the `parentRootUri` is functioning correctly.
- Adjusted the `ExtHostSourceControl` to properly update the observable when `parentRootUri` is assigned after the source control creation.

These modifications aim to enhance the user experience by providing a more accurate representation of the active repository in the title bar when working with Git worktrees.

- **Dynamic Class Application:**

issues.title: agentHost: mark external sessions in ~/.copilot/chats as workspace-less
issues.body:
## Problem

Sessions that the GitHub Copilot app creates without a workspace run in a folder under `~/.copilot/chats`, nested by date (e.g. `~/.copilot/chats/2026-09-23/congenial-happiness-c052778d`). When Agent Host discovered these as external sessions, it reported that folder as a regular working directory without the workspace-less marker. The Agents window therefore showed the internal chats folder as the session's workspace instead of treating the session as a workspace-less (quick) chat.

## Changes

- **Copilot discovery and `getChatMetadata`** mark a chat workspace-less when its working directory is inside `~/.copilot/chats` (case-insensitive on Windows and macOS). `getChatMetadata` does this only when the host has not recorded its own `agentHost.workspaceless` marker, so host-created sessions keep their persisted value. Covering `getChatMetadata` keeps the marker when the session is restored or its catalog entry is rebuilt.
- **`workspacelessChatsRoot`** defines the `~/.copilot/chats` path in one place; `workspacelessScratchDir` builds on it.
- **Catalog resolver** no longer persists the `agentHost.workspaceless` marker for external sessions. That marker also identifies host-created sessions (`_readSessionRegistrationFacts`), so persisting it made a pruned-then-rediscovered external session register as internal. `_buildImportedCatalogSyncRequest` now passes the external flag so the resolver can tell.

## Notes for reviewers

- Detection is one path comparison per chat, with no extra file-system, database, or Git access.
- Like `workspacelessScratchDir`, detection uses `~/.copilot/chats` and ignores `COPILOT_HOME`.
- External sessions discovered before this change get the marker when they are next opened or their catalog entry is rebuilt.
- No Agents window changes: it already hides the workspace for sessions marked workspace-less.

## Tests

- `copilotAgent.test.ts`: discovery marks a `github/autopilot` chat under the chats folder as workspace-less but not a chat in a regular folder; `getChatMetadata` infers the marker only when the host recorded none.
- `agentService.test.ts`: a workspace-less external session stays external after it is pruned and rediscovered, and the host marker is not persisted.
- The discovery and rediscovery tests fail without the fix. The Copilot agent, Agent Service, and catalog resolver suites pass (1,047 tests).

issues.title: Copilot Chat agent mode: rename tool reports success but does not modify the file
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In agent/chat mode, when Copilot Chat invokes its built-in `rename` tool to perform a semantic symbol rename, the tool call returns a success message with a specific edit count (e.g. `Renamed <symbol> to <newName> - N edits across M files`), but the workspace files are **not actually modified**. There is no error, warning, or partial-failure indicator anywhere in the response.

This creates a silent divergence between what the agent believes happened and the actual state of the workspace, which is risky in an autonomous/agentic workflow: any commit, build, or further edit that follows may fail unexpectedly or produce misleading assumptions, since the model has no built-in signal that the rename did not apply.

### Exact tool call and response observed

Tool call (as exposed to the model in agent mode):
```
rename(filePath: "<file>", symbol: "<OldName>", lineContent: "<line containing the symbol>", newName: "<NewName>")
```

Response returned by the tool:
```
Renamed `<OldName>` to `<NewName>` - N edits across M files.
```

No `applied`/`ok`/error fields are present in the response — just this human-readable success string, with no indication of whether it reflects a verified or merely attempted change.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In an agent-mode Copilot Chat session, ask the agent to rename a symbol (class/method/etc.) that is referenced in several files.
2. The agent calls the built-in `rename` tool; the tool returns the success message above with a non-zero edit/file count.
3. Immediately after, inspect the workspace independently of the tool (open the files, run `git diff`, or `grep` for the new name across the repo).
4. Result: the old name is still present everywhere; the new name does not appear anywhere in the workspace. `git diff` shows no changes from this call.
5. Repeating the exact same `rename` call with identical parameters reproduces the same false-positive "success" result — no changes are applied on the second attempt either.

### Expected behavior

- If no edits were actually applied, the tool result should reflect that (e.g. an `applied: false` field, an error, or a clear "no changes made" status) rather than reporting a specific non-zero edit/file count.
- The reported edit/file counts should correspond to changes that are verifiably present in the workspace after the call returns.

### Actual behavior

The tool call returns a confident success message with specific counts ("N edits across M files"), but a subsequent inspection of the workspace shows zero actual changes. The failure is silent — no exception, warning, or degraded-result marker is surfaced to the model or the user.

### Environment

- VS Code: latest
- GitHub Copilot Chat extension: latest
- Mode: Agent/Chat mode, using the built-in semantic `rename` tool
- Model: various (reproduced at least with a Claude-based model, e.g. claude-sonnet-5)
- OS: Windows

### Additional context

This was reproduced across multiple sessions/models in the same workspace, including retrying the identical call, which still resulted in the same false-positive success message with no actual file changes. It would be valuable if the built-in rename tool's result schema always reflected verified, not merely attempted/intended, changes.

issues.title: Sweeper skills v7: split sweeper-fix into sweeper-plan and sweeper-implement
issues.body:
**TL;DR:** the vcodesweeper has now support for both **implementing** and **planning** an implementation for a reviewed issue. The PR adds the corresponding skills.

Replaces `.github/skills/sweeper-fix` (v6, #336827) with two skills.

**`sweeper-plan <n>`** — for a *plan first* agent-ready record, asks the review's open decisions in chat, writes `.sweeper/plans/issue-<n>.md` (git-excluded via `.git/info/exclude`, never committed). It writes no code; the maintainer edits the plan in their editor.

**`sweeper-implement <n>`** — implements. On an *implement* record it works straight from the review's brief; on a *plan first* record it reads the plan file as the maintainer left it. Tests are written first (fail before, pass after), the diff is validated against the brief or plan. After the maintainer's go-ahead it opens a **draft PR** under their identity, via `--body-file`, and keeps it a draft.

Tested end to end on the sweeper sandbox in VS Code chat and in the Agents window (plan-first and implement, plus the plan-record-without-a-plan refusal) before this PR.

I use vscode to connect to a remote Linux server using SSH. Over time, my remote folder `${HOME}/.vscode-server/cli/servers` slowly fills up. `code tunnel prune` claims to clean this, but a case mismatch means not.

Stable-2242ebbb...

the split produces:

quality = "Stable"

But Quality::try_from() accepts only:

stable

exploration

issues.title: Update git extension to use gitignore syntax for worktreeIncludeFiles
issues.body:
This pull request updates the git extension to align with the recent improvements made in the agent host regarding the handling of `git.worktreeIncludeFiles`. The key changes include:

- **Selection Logic**: The logic for selecting files to include in the worktree has been moved to a new file, `worktreeInclude.ts`, which closely follows the agent host's implementation.
- **Pattern Matching**: The extension now uses `.gitignore` syntax instead of globs for matching files. This change allows for more accurate file selection based on git's ignore rules.
- **Repository Methods**: The `_getWorktreeIncludePaths` method in `repository.ts` has been updated to execute `git ls-files` commands, ensuring that only the appropriate files are copied to the new worktree.
- **Removed Unused Code**: The old `findFiles2` API proposal has been removed from `package.json` and `tsconfig.json`, as it was only relevant to the previous glob-based logic.
- **Updated Setting Description**: The description for the `git.worktreeIncludeFiles` setting has been revised in `package.nls.json` to reflect the new gitignore syntax and clarify that files must be ignored by git.
- **Unit Tests**: New unit tests have been added in `worktreeInclude.test.ts` to validate the new selection logic.

These changes ensure that the git extension's behavior is consistent with the agent host, improving the reliability of file inclusion in worktrees. The new implementation has been tested against a real repository, confirming that it behaves as expected.

issues.title: Allow Run/Debug configuration picker and extension status items (e.g. device selector) in the Command Center / title bar
issues.body: ### Problem When working on Flutter projects with multiple flavors (dev / staging / production), I constantly switch between three controls that live in three different places: 1. **Run button** – in the Run and Debug view 2. **Launch configuration picker** – in the Run and Debug view header (only visible when that view is open) 3. **Target device selector** – in the status bar (contributed by the Dart/Flutter extension) To start the app with the right flavor on the right device, I have to open the Run and Debug view, pick a configuration, then look at the bottom-right corner to check or change the device. In JetBrains IDEs (Android Studio), all of these sit together in the top toolbar next to the search box, so the whole "what am I running, and where" state is visible and controllable in one place. `debug.toolBarLocation: "commandCenter"` moves the debug toolbar to the top, but only **during** an active session. It doesn't help with choosing the configuration or device **before** launching. ### Proposal 1. Add an option to show the **Run button + launch configuration picker** in the title bar next to the Command Center, visible at all times (not only during a debug session). For example: `debug.configurationPickerLocation: "commandCenter" | "debugView"`. 2. Provide an **extension contribution point** for the title bar / Command Center area, so extensions can place compact status items there (e.g. the Dart extension's device selector, or similar target pickers in other ecosystems like React Native, .NET MAUI, or embedded tooling). Both should be opt-in so the default layout stays unchanged. ### Screenshots - Current Run and Debug picker: - Current device selector in status bar: - Command Center area where these could live: ### Why this matters This isn't Flutter-specific. Any workflow with "configuration × target" (flavors, build variants, emulators, remote hosts) benefits from having that state visible at the top of the window instead of split between a sidebar view and the status bar.

issues.title: Terminal: Sanitize trailing/leading newlines when mutating environment variables
issues.body:
Fixes #337937

### Summary
When extensions contribute to environment variables (such as `PATH`) using `EnvironmentVariableMutatorType.Append` or `Prepend`, the existing environment variable value is concatenated directly via string addition (`+`).

If the existing environment variable happens to have a trailing carriage return (`\r`) or newline (`\n`)—which can happen via manual environment variable configuration, batch files, or external tools/installers—appending an extension path produces a string with an embedded `\r`. 

On Windows integrated terminals:
1. Printing `$env:Path` causes the cursor to return to the beginning of the line upon hitting `\r`, overwriting earlier characters with the appended path and visually truncating the line.
2. The path entry containing the trailing `\r` becomes an invalid filesystem path on Windows, breaking command resolution.

### Proposed Changes
- In `MergedEnvironmentVariableCollection.applyToProcessEnvironment`:
  - `EnvironmentVariableMutatorType.Append`: Trim trailing `[\r\n]+$` from `env[actualVariable]` before appending.
  - `EnvironmentVariableMutatorType.Prepend`: Trim leading `^[\r\n]+` from `env[actualVariable]` before prepending.
- Restricted the sanitization strictly to `[\r\n]` so that full-width Unicode characters (e.g., Japanese directory paths with full-width spaces `\u3000`) and standard spaces/symbols remain completely intact.
- Added comprehensive unit test cases to `environmentVariableCollection.test.ts` covering CR/LF sanitization and full-width multi-byte paths.

### Verification Done
- Verified with unit tests covering trailing `\r`, `\r\n`, `\n`, multiple newlines, and Japanese characters with ideographic spaces.
- Verified that trailing newlines are safely stripped while paths and full-width spaces remain intact.

issues.title: Terminal: Environment variable corruption and display overwrite when PATH contains carriage return

labels.name: terminal
labels.description: General terminal issues that don't fall under another label

issues.body:
### VS Code Version
1.139.0

### Operating System
Windows 10 / 11 (x64)

### Steps to Reproduce
1. In Windows PowerShell, append a carriage return (`\r`) to the user or process `PATH`:
   ```powershell
   $env:Path += "`r"
   ```
2. Open VS Code and open an integrated PowerShell terminal.
3. When an extension (such as Python's `ms-python.debugpy` or Copilot) mutates `PATH` via `EnvironmentVariableMutatorType.Append`, it directly appends its directory path using `(env[actualVariable] || '') + value`.
4. Run `$env:Path` in the integrated terminal.

### Expected Behavior
Environment variables should concatenate cleanly without display glitches or broken path resolution.

### Actual Behavior
- Because `\r` is embedded right before the extension's appended path, printing `$env:Path` hits the carriage return and moves the terminal cursor back to the line start, overwriting earlier characters with the appended path. Visually, the PATH looks like it got truncated right before the end.
- The path entry containing the trailing `\r` becomes invalid on Windows, causing commands in that directory to fail to resolve.
- *Note*: Splitting by semicolon (`$env:Path -split ';'`) outputs each entry on a separate line, which prevents the carriage return overwrite and makes all paths visible, making this issue particularly confusing to diagnose.

### Proposed Solution / PR
In `MergedEnvironmentVariableCollection.applyToProcessEnvironment` ([`environmentVariableCollection.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/environmentVariableCollection.ts#L88-L98)), defensively trim trailing/leading newlines (`[\r\n]+`) from the existing environment variable before applying `Append` or `Prepend`.
A PR with unit tests covering this fix and multi-byte / full-width paths is ready to submit.

issues.title: sessions: Make sessions list component fixtures data-driven
issues.body:
Sessions list component fixtures are now declared as data and rendered through the real list services. A new list feature or state can be covered by describing it, without writing new mocks.

## What changed

- **Declarative harness** — `sessionsListFixtureUtils.ts`. A fixture is a state object:
  - `sessions`, with chats, status, pins and CI state
  - custom `groups`
  - `view`: grouping, sorting, compact or phone layout, and which rows are collapsed or expanded
  - `interaction`: which rows are `selected`, `focused`, `hovered` or being `renamed`
  - `header`: New button style, Automations, navigation shortcuts, Customizations count
  - `settings`

  State is seeded into the real `SessionGroupsService`, `SessionsListModelService`, `SessionSectionOrderService`, `ContextKeyService` and `MenuService`. Row toolbars show real actions, and rename or archive update the rendered list.
- **Hover without a pointer** — `DefaultStyleController` and `sessionsList.css` pair every row `:hover` rule with a `.hovered` class, using `:is(:hover, .hovered)` to keep specificity. Hover-only actions and backgrounds now render in fixtures. `sessionsList.css` documents the convention.
- **Test-only list operations** — the new `TestSessionsList` subclass (under `test/`) focuses, selects, collapses, reveals and locates rows by model identity. `SessionsList` only gains a `protected tree` and a `protected findItem`, so product code can't reach these operations.
- **Shared test data** — `buildTestSession` in `services/sessions/test/common`.
- **Fixture location** — the fixtures moved to `src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.fixture.ts`. Fixture IDs (`sessions/sessionsList/...`) are unchanged.
- **18 new fixtures**, covering:
  - custom groups: default, collapsed, empty, empty hidden, create, rename, pinned precedence, date grouping
  - hovered, focused and selected rows: sessions, chats, group and workspace headers, multi-selection
  - the Customizations migrations indicator
- **Guidance** — the component-fixtures skill now explains how to make hover and focus states renderable, and to keep test-only operations out of production APIs.

## Why

The old fixture file combined a long list of boolean options with partial mocks that throw, empty toolbars, and DOM patching for hover and selection. It had no coverage for custom groups or group rename. More features are coming to the sessions list, and each new state should only need data.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Regression found (not fixed here):** since #337858, custom group header actions (New Session, Archive All, Delete Group) are no longer right-aligned like workspace section actions. `.session-section-label` stopped growing, and group rows don't use the new `.session-section-label-container`. `SessionsList_Groups_HoveredHeader`, `SessionsList_Groups_FocusedHeader` and `SessionsList_Groups_EmptyHoveredHeader` currently show this. Their expected visual descriptions describe the intended right-aligned layout.
- **Screenshot baselines:** rows now render real toolbar actions, so these blocks-ci fixtures change intentionally: `SessionsList_NarrowHoverToolbar`, `SessionsList_SelectedKeyboardFocus`, `SessionsList_CompactSessionRename` and `SessionsList_NestedChatHierarchyGuides`. I'll update their hashes once CI renders them. The new fixtures are screenshot-only and don't block CI.
- **Playwright:** `sessionsListTwistie.spec.ts` now moves the pointer away before its Tab/Shift+Tab check. A hovered row shows real toolbar actions, and those join the Shift+Tab order. That is existing product behavior, not changed here.

## Validation

- Unit tests: `sessionsList.test.ts` and `listWidget.test.ts` (180 passing)
- Component explorer: all 149 `sessions/sessionsList` renders succeed (59 fixtures across themes)
- Playwright: `sessionsListTwistie.spec.ts` (32 passed)
- `tsc`, ESLint and hygiene: clean for the changed files

## Use case

In my setup, installing Codex and Claude Code makes their tabs available alongside Chat. I want the same experience for my Gemini workflow, using the `google.google-antigravity` extension: a Gemini tab in the same strip, so I can switch assistants while keeping the editor and primary sidebar available.

Ideally, installing a compatible extension would make its tab available there automatically. Users should also be able to choose and retain that placement through supported VS Code UI or configuration.

## Current workaround and problem

I created a working customization:

https://github.com/arviphd/codex-customizations/tree/main/vscode/antigravity-gemini-sidebar

The script currently:

- Changes the extension manifest's view container from `activitybar` to `secondarySidebar`, assigns a new container ID, and labels it Gemini.
- Changes the extension's internal `viewLocation` from `sidebar` to `auxiliarybar` so its focus/close commands target the intended region.
- Updates VS Code's saved layout entries and clears stale extension scan caches, followed by a full restart.

I have observed losing this customization after updates. The repository documents one concrete cause: updating or reinstalling the extension replaces its installation directory and overwrites the patched files. I have not isolated a separate VS Code-update-only persistence bug.

Editing installed extension code and VS Code's layout database is a fragile way to maintain a preferred UI layout.

## Requested behavior

1. Make extension view containers discoverable as selectable tabs beside Chat in the Secondary Side Bar, through a supported extension contribution and/or a user placement action.
2. Preserve user-selected location, pinning, and order across restarts and normal VS Code/extension updates when extension and view identifiers remain stable.
3. Ensure supported view reveal/focus commands respect the selected location; document how extension authors should handle location-dependent behavior.
4. Allow this workflow without editing installed extension files, manipulating `state.vscdb`, or clearing extension scan caches.

## Scope and routing

The requested outcome is consistent placement of an extension's own UI as a sibling tab beside Chat. The example uses Google Antigravity, locally relabeled Gemini by my script.

The workaround already uses `contributes.viewsContainers.secondarySidebar`, so this is not a claim that VS Code has no Secondary Side Bar contribution mechanism. The gap I want addressed is achieving and retaining this experience through supported configuration and extension behavior.

If existing VS Code APIs and layout controls already cover the full scenario, please point to the supported approach and clarify which remaining changes belong with Google's extension. I recognize that VS Code cannot fix arbitrary location assumptions inside third-party extension code.

issues.title: sessions: rebind agent feedback to the provider's current connection
issues.body:
## Problem

On a remote agent host (dev tunnel), a feedback comment submitted via **Submit Feedback** was not visible to the agent: `listComments` and `viewUnreviewedComments` returned `[]` even though the turn attachment referenced the comment id.

From the server-side AHP wire logs and the client window log:

- The agents window reconnected to the tunnel host as a **new client** (fresh `initialize`, new client id), so the remote provider's `IAgentConnection` was replaced via `setConnection`.
- `AnnotationsAgentFeedbackItemsBackend` caches one channel per session and kept returning the one bound to the **old, closed** connection.
- The comment was added to the local cache (so it rendered in the editor) and dispatched on the dead connection, where `_sendNotificationMessage` silently drops it. The new connection never subscribed to `<session>/annotations`, and the server never received an `annotations/set`.

## Fix

`_ensureChannel` now remembers the provider/session it resolved the channel from and, on reuse, checks that the provider still reports the same connection. If the connection changed, the stale channel is released and re-subscribed on the current connection. If the provider has no connection (offline), the existing channel is kept so cached comments stay visible.

The check is a cheap provider cache lookup; it deliberately avoids `ISessionsManagementService.getSession` (linear scan) on the hot path. After a rebind, the new subscription's first snapshot fires the existing "loaded" change event, so consumers (editor comments, PR review seeder) refresh on their own.

## Notes for reviewers

- Comments that were already dropped on a dead connection are not replayed; the server stays the source of truth.
- The rebind happens lazily on the next read/write (every feedback access goes through `_ensureChannel`), since the provider has no public connection-change event.

## Testing

- Added `moves to the provider's new connection after a reconnect` to `agentFeedbackItemsBackend.test.ts` (fails without the fix).
- `agentFeedbackItemsBackend`, `agentFeedbackService` and `agentFeedbackPRReviewSeeder` suites pass (71 tests).

issues.title: agentHost: gate create_session chat folders on the provider's multi-root setting
issues.body:
`create_session` lets a current-session chat work in its own folder or worktree. That needs a provider that supports multiple working directories, but the tool offered it regardless and then failed with "Provider does not support chat working directories".

The tool now follows each provider's own multi-root setting — `chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.multiRootEnabled`, `chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.multiRootEnabled`, `chat.agentHost.codexAgent.multiRootEnabled` — through the provider's `multipleWorkingDirectories` capability:

- **Enabled:** unchanged. `relationship` is optional and defaults to `currentSession`; a current-session chat may take `workspace` and `worktree` to work in its own folder.
- **Disabled:** the session is offered the shared-workspace `create_session` from before #337544. `relationship` is required, current-session chats share the session's workspace, and `workspace`/`worktree` are rejected for `currentSession` and valid only for `independent` sessions.

A unified experiment-controlled setting (`chat.agentHost.multiRootEnabled`) was prototyped earlier and deliberately dropped; it is not part of this PR.

### Changes
- `sessionServerTools.ts`: shared-workspace definition selected per session, and matching validation.
- `agentService.ts`, `agentServiceFoundation.ts`: `supportsChatWorkingDirectories`, read from the provider's capability.
- `AGENTS.md`: documents both behaviors.
- Copilot prompt snapshots: the E2E suite runs Copilot with multi-root disabled, so each `create_session` block shows the shared-workspace definition.

### Validation
- agentHost node/common unit tests pass, including new tests for the definition switch and shared-workspace validation.
- Copilot prompt snapshots and `create_session` E2E tests pass in strict replay.
- ESLint clean; no type errors in changed files.

issues.title: Agents - Switch agent host to use gitignore for worktreeIncludeFiles matching
issues.body:
This pull request updates the agent host's implementation of the `worktreeIncludeFiles` setting to utilize Git's `.gitignore` matching instead of the previous glob parsing method. This change aims to ensure consistency with Git's behavior and improve the handling of ignored files.

### Changes made:
- Replaced the glob parsing logic in `agentHostGitService.ts` with a call to `git ls-files`, using a temporary exclude file for patterns.
- Updated the API to include a session ID for temporary file creation, ensuring safe file handling.
- Modified the integration tests to cover new behaviors, including handling of `.gitignore` syntax, negations, and line breaks.
- Adjusted workspace settings in `.vscode/settings.json` to reflect the new matching behavior.

- Aligns the agent host's file inclusion logic with Git's established `.gitignore` semantics.
- Reduces complexity by leveraging Git's built-in capabilities for file matching.
- Ensures that existing integration tests continue to pass while adding new tests for the updated functionality.

issues.title: chat: Keep incremental rendering stable when inline references stream in
issues.body:
Fixes #336883

## Problem

With incremental rendering enabled, every inline file reference that streams into the main response replays the entrance animation for the whole response.

`ChatMarkdownContentPart.tryIncrementalUpdate` rejected any update whose `inlineReferences` differed from the previous one. A streamed reference appends `[label](http://_vscodecontentref_/N)` to the markdown and adds key `N` to `inlineReferences`. That failed the equality check, so the renderer disposed the part and created a new one. The new part seeds the morpher with `animateInitial: true`, which re-animates every block.

## Fix

Accept the update when the new `inlineReferences` keeps every existing entry unchanged and only adds entries. A changed existing entry, such as a reference resolving to a symbol, still forces a full re-render. The morpher's render callback reads the updated `this.markdown`, so appended references resolve in place.

## How to test

1. Set:
   - `chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.enabled`: `true`
   - `chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.animationStyle`: `blur`
   - `chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.buffering`: `off`
2. Open a workspace and ask for a response that mentions existing workspace files (for example `` `src/example.ts` ``) and keeps streaming after each one.
3. Before: earlier paragraphs animate again each time a reference appears. After: only new content animates.

I checked this with the chat simulation mock server driving the in-repo Copilot extension. The response streamed two existing file paths; the control run named missing files so they stayed plain text.

| Run | Markdown parts created | Earlier paragraph animated again |
|---|---|---|
| Before, with references | 3 (one per reference) | Yes, when each reference arrived |
| Before, control | 1 | No |
| After, with references | 1 | No; animation counts match the control |

Both reference widgets still render after the fix. The existing tests in `chatMarkdownContentPart.test.ts`, `chatListRenderer.test.ts`, and `annotations.test.ts` pass.

issues.title: sessions: leave peer-discovered recorded pull requests to their folder
issues.body:
Follow-up to #337694. In a multi-folder Agents Window session, a pull request created with the Create PR button from a peer chat on its own worktree showed on the session row and on every session-folder chat.

## Cause

Create PR saves the new pull request in two places: the session's recorded artifacts, which carry no folder, and the GitHub state of the folder it was created from. #337694 promotes every recorded pull request of the repository into the session folder's GitHub info. So a peer worktree's pull request also counted as a session-folder pull request. An open pull request's icon outranks merged ones, so the session row and the session-folder chats showed it.

## Change

In `toGitHubInfo`, the session folder skips a recorded pull request that another folder discovered for its own working directory (`githubData`), unless the session folder discovered it too.
- Recorded pull requests that no folder discovered still go to the session folder, as with #337694.
- Folders other than the session folder are unchanged: they report only their own discovered pull requests.
- The lookup reads `githubData` directly rather than the host-published working-directory keys, which list metadata can lack.

## For reviewers

- A pull request that a peer chat's agent records with `add_artifact_or_reference` isn't discovered for the peer's folder, so it still goes to the session folder. Placing it correctly would require recording the folder on the artifact, which this change deliberately avoids.
- Some sessions contain peer folders whose GitHub state holds the session folder's pull request and branch. That was a separate agent host bug, already fixed in #337608. This change keeps such a pull request with the session folder, because the session folder discovered it too.

## Validation

- New test in `localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts`: a peer's recorded and discovered pull request goes only to its own folder, while a pull request both folders discovered, and one no folder discovered, stay with the session folder. The test fails without the fix, and it runs without host-published folder keys.
- Replayed a real affected session's GitHub state and artifacts through the provider: before, the session folder got the peer's open pull request; with the fix, only the peer's folder does.

issues.title: Agents: cached tunnels trigger repeated GitHub sign-in loop
issues.body:
## Summary

Opening/reloading the Agents window can queue one interactive GitHub sign-in per cached remote Agent Host tunnel. Completing a sign-in immediately opens the next queued flow, creating an apparently endless sign-in cycle that only stops when VS Code exits.

## Observed behavior

On VS Code Insiders 1.140.0-insider on Windows:

- The Agents window restored 9 cached Dev Tunnels.
- No cached GitHub session initially satisfied the configured tunnel scopes (`read:org user:email`).
- 10 identical scope requests were made within one millisecond (9 tunnels plus the Agents setup flow).
- The GitHub authentication provider serialized the interactive requests.
- Successful sign-ins replaced the same account session (`added=1, removed=1`) and then the next queued request opened another browser flow.
- Exiting VS Code canceled the queue. After restart, the newly created scoped session was reused and the loop stopped.

The repeated browser callbacks also created several empty timestamped log-run directories. Those were callback processes, not crashes.

## Root cause

Automatic entry reconciliation starts connections with `userInitiated: false`:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/remoteAgentHostServiceImpl.ts

For gateway-capable tunnels with no saved location preference, the tunnel factory then changes the connection to user-initiated:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/electron-browser/tunnelAgentHostServiceImpl.ts

```ts
const connectOptions = this.getAutoConnectMode(tunnel) === 'prompt'
    ? { ...options, userInitiated: true }
    : options;
```

`!connectOptions.userInitiated` is subsequently passed as the `silent` argument to `_getToken*`. Each cached prompt-mode tunnel therefore performs interactive authentication during automatic startup reconciliation and calls `createSession` when no matching token exists.

The browser tunnel implementation has the same pattern:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/browser/browserTunnelAgentHostService.ts

## Expected behavior

Automatic reconciliation of cached tunnels must never trigger interactive authentication. Only an explicit user connect action or the Agents setup flow should open sign-in.

Gateway endpoint selection may require interaction, but that should not convert background authentication into interactive authentication. Equivalent authentication requests should ideally also be coalesced or canceled after the first succeeds.

## Suggested fix

Separate the authentication interaction policy from the gateway-selection interaction policy:

- Preserve `userInitiated: false` for authentication during automatic reconciliation.
- Independently allow or defer gateway endpoint selection when a location preference is missing.
- Consider coalescing equivalent in-flight authentication requests as defense in depth.

## Additional notes

The GitHub `429` for optional EDU details and failures connecting to stale/local remote hosts occurred during the incident but were not causal.
