Fixes #337861.

The Codex Sandbox tests create their fixtures under `os.tmpdir()`. On Azure macOS that resolves to shared system temp, which Codex intentionally permits command processes to read and write. The tests therefore put their supposedly protected files inside an allowed area.

Use `AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY`, then `RUNNER_TEMP`, then the local temp fallback, matching the correction already made to the neighboring permission suite in #337826. Remove the Azure-only quarantine and its known-issues entry so all five tests run normally again. Every test assertion and the production permission profiles remain unchanged.

### Validation

- **RED:** current main with `TF_BUILD=1`, `TMPDIR=/tmp`, a private `AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY`, and the quarantine opt-in reproduces all five assertion failures.
- **GREEN:** changing only fixture placement makes the same five tests pass under the identical environment.
- After removing the quarantine, the Azure-like environment passes all **19 Codex sandbox, permissions, and customization cases**, plus the clean-state guard, with `AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES` unset.
- The GitHub temp-root fallback also passes all **13 sandbox and permissions cases**, plus the guard, with `TMPDIR=/tmp`.
- `npm run compile-client`, targeted ESLint/hygiene, and `git diff --check` pass.
- [GitHub macOS Electron](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36108322851/job/107985845794) passed; its job log confirms all five sandbox and eight permission cases execute and pass.
- [Azure build 477196](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477196) passed the macOS Electron integration-test task. Log 1594 confirms all five sandbox and eight permission cases execute and pass, including the disabled-plugin assertion from the reported failure.
- A second Azure macOS run, [477200](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477200), is in progress on the same commit. This PR remains a draft.

### Reproduce locally on macOS

With the normal macOS private `TMPDIR` available, preserve it as the CI-owned directory while making the system temp fallback point at shared temp:

```sh
env -u AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES \
  TF_BUILD=1 AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY="$TMPDIR" TMPDIR=/tmp \
  ./scripts/test-integration.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/codexSandbox.integrationTest.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/codexPermissions.integrationTest.ts
```

All five sandbox and eight permission cases must execute and pass; skipped tests do not establish recovery.

issues.title: Auto indent on paste when the first line is already indented
issues.body:
Fixes #285222

### The problem

With `editor.autoIndentOnPaste` enabled, pasting several lines at a position that is already correctly indented leaves every line but the first flush left:

```ts
{
	const a = 4;
const b = 4;
const c = 4;
const d = 4;
}
```

Breaking the indentation of the first line first makes it work, which is the clue: the adjustment is being skipped precisely when the first line needs no adjustment.

### The cause

`AutoIndentOnPaste.trigger` computes the indent for the first pasted line. When that indent already matches and the line matches no indentation rule, it returns from the whole method — which also skips the block below it that re-indents the remaining pasted lines.

### Why the guard cannot simply be removed

The early return was added in e77b196c269 for #38833. The remaining lines are shifted by the difference between the good indent of the second line and its actual indent, and the good indent does not account for continuation lines. Without the guard, blocks like these are outdented:

```ts
type T =
	| number
	| string;

const x = foo
	.bar()
	.baz();
```

Limiting the guard to pastes that start at column 1 is not enough either. A continuation block copied from its first non-whitespace character and pasted at an indented position is outdented the same way.

### The change

In the case the guard covers — the first line is already correctly indented and matches no indentation rule:

- **The paste starts at column 1:** return early, as before. The pasted block carries its own indentation.
- **The paste starts after existing indentation:** that indentation belongs to the document, and the following lines did not get it. Indent them to match, but never outdent them.

Every other path is unchanged: when that case does not apply, the new condition reduces to the previous `!==`.

### Tests

- `issue #285222` reproduces the bug. It fails without the change.
- `issue #38833: preserve the internal indentation of a pasted block` covers the original case at column 1. The nearest existing test (`issue #167299`) starts with a blank line, which leaves the second line unindented and hides the regression, so this behaviour was effectively uncovered.
- `issue #38833: preserve continuation lines when pasting at an indented position` pastes a method chain inside a function. It fails if the guard is only limited to column 1.

Removing the guard outright fails both `#38833` tests and the existing `issue #29753: incorrect indentation of header comment`.

### Behaviour change to be aware of

A multi-line template literal pasted at an indented position now has its second line indented, which changes the string. The same text pasted at column 1 of an empty line in a block is already indented this way today, so this makes the two cases consistent rather than introducing new behaviour for the feature. `editor.autoIndentOnPasteWithinString` does not apply because the pasted range starts and ends outside the string.

### Verification

- `vs/editor/contrib/indentation/test/**` — 63 passing
- `vs/editor/**` — 5429 passing, 0 failing

issues.title: fix(glob): keep path separator in negated bracket ranges
issues.body:
## What this fixes

Fixes #322331

A `files.exclude` pattern like `"Source[^M/]*": true` was excluding far more than it should: everything under `Source/` disappeared from the Explorer, even though `/` was explicitly listed in the negated character class.

## Root cause

In `src/vs/base/common/glob.ts`, `parseRegExp` silently dropped any `/` found inside a bracket expression when compiling the glob to a regular expression. So `Source[^M/]*` compiled to `Source[^M]*`, and the negated class happily matched `/` too. I confirmed this against current `main` with a small repro before changing anything:

- `Source[^M/]*` matched `Source/` and `Source/sub` (wrong, both)
- after the fix it matches neither, while `SourceX` / `SourceXyz` still match and `SourceM` still doesn't

## The change

In a *negated* bracket range the separator is now kept as a literal, so it stays excluded from matching (`[^/]` no longer matches `/`). Positive ranges are untouched: `foo[/]bar` still does not match `foo/bar`, which the existing test suite asserts.

## Tests

- Added regression cases to the `brackets` test in `src/vs/base/test/common/glob.test.ts` covering the exact pattern from the issue.
- Ran the full `src/vs/base/test/common/glob.test.ts` suite standalone on Linux (node, no display needed): **51 passing, 0 failing** with the fix; with the fix reverted the new assertions fail as expected (`Source[^M/]* should not match Source/`), so the test genuinely guards the regression.

Only the two files above are touched. Nothing else in the repo depends on the old drop-the-slash behavior; I checked the existing suite for any `/`-in-bracket expectations and the only one is the positive-range case, which still passes.

issues.title: Ensure the database directory exists before opening the database.
issues.body:
Fixes issue#337873

### Problem

`ExternalIngestIndex` opens its local index DB at `joinPath(context.storageUri, 'codebase-external.sqlite')`. `vscode.d.ts` guarantees only that storageUri's parent exists , and nothing creates the extension's own folder. So on a fresh workspace the folder is missing, `new DatabaseSync(path)` throws `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` (errcode 14), and the code falls back to `:memory:`. But an in-memory index can never be reused, so the whole workspace is re-ingested on every extension-host start. On a large workspace that pinned the extension host for minutes per reload — all other extensions in the process unresponsive — with nothing surfaced in the UI; the only trace is `Failed to create database. Falling back to in memory db` in the Copilot Chat output channel.

### Fix

Create the folder (recursively) immediately before opening the DB — the same pattern `_ensureDb()` /
`openDb()` already use elsewhere in this extension, and the placement suggested in the issue thread.

```diff
 import * as fs from 'node:fs';
+import * as path from 'node:path';
 import sql from 'node:sqlite';
@@
 			return this.createFreshDatabase(dbPath);
 		}
 
+		// VS Code only guarantees that storageUri's parent exists, this folder is created by the extension.
+		// node:sqlite cannot create a file inside a folder that does not exist.
+		fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(dbPath), { recursive: true });
+
 		// Try to open existing database and check cache version
```

Placed after the `:memory:` early-return, so no extra guard is needed, and it covers both the "open existing" and "create fresh" paths.
Failure behaviour is unchanged: if this still fails (read-only mount, permissions, …), the existing `catch` still falls back exactly as before.

### Test plan

- Field-verified on a Remote-SSH setup: with the folder missing, `codebase-external.sqlite` was never created and the ingest re-ran on every reload (extension host pinned ~1 core for minutes). After creating the folder by hand, the DB is created once (2,789,376 B), kept current, and reloads no longer re-ingest.
- Independent standalone reproduction (in the issue thread): the real directory layout plus the twofunctions mirrored from the bundle, on Node 24 / SQLite 3.53 — without the mkdir every start throws errcode 14 and re-ingests; with it, the second open reuses the existing rows and skips the ingest.
- No new test added: I'm contributing from the browser without a local checkout, so I can't iterate against the Vitest harness.
### Notes

- Deliberately out of scope: 
  (1) the fallback semantics — retrying once and then marking the codebase index unavailable instead of picking `:memory:` would be better
  (2) the synchronous ingest holding the extension host — need tracked separately.
- Credit: the `vscode.d.ts` / `extHostStoragePaths` reading that makes the root cause airtight, and the standalone reproduction, come from @aron-intframe in issue#337873.

issues.title: CLI spawns itself in an unbounded chain when more than one copy is on PATH
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.136.1 (commit a44adf7f53e00964ab890f9f8758a334f1fc15bc)
- OS Version: Linux aarch64 (openEuler 22.03 SP2, kernel 5.10.0), container

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Make two copies of the CLI binary:
   ```sh
   cp /path/to/code /tmp/a/bin1/code
   cp /path/to/code /tmp/a/bin2/code
   ```
2. Run a legacy editor command through one of them, with both on `PATH`:
   ```sh
   PATH=/tmp/a/bin1:/tmp/a/bin2 /tmp/a/bin1/code --list-extensions
   ```

Both copies are byte-identical plain binaries — no wrapper scripts, no symlinks.

**Actual**

The CLI spawns itself in an unbounded chain — one child per generation, linear, never
stops:

```
   PID    PPID  COMMAND
 53836       -  /tmp/a/bin1/code --list-extensions
 54002   53836  /tmp/a/bin2/code --list-extensions     <- first hop
 54168   54002  /tmp/a/bin2/code --list-extensions     <- self-spawn from here on
 54334   54168  /tmp/a/bin2/code --list-extensions
 54500   54334  /tmp/a/bin2/code --list-extensions
 ...    one child per generation, nothing exits
```

85 processes after 5 seconds, each holding 161 threads. In the environment where we hit
this, the chain ran for hours and reached **2,774 processes / 446,786 threads**, exhausting
the PID space (`kernel.pid_max = 600000`, `pids.current` reached 595,293). Once PIDs run
out, `fork()` fails process-wide and unrelated software in the same container starts
failing.

The original invocation never returns and never prints an error.

**Expected**

With a single copy of the CLI on PATH this works correctly — the CLI exits cleanly:

```
No installation of Visual Studio Code stable was found.
Install it from your system's package manager or https://code.visualstudio.com, ...
(exit 1)
```

The two-copy case should do the same, not loop.

**Analysis**

`--list-extensions` is parsed as a legacy editor command (`cli/src/bin/code/legacy_args.rs`)
and dispatched to `start_code()` (`cli/src/bin/code/main.rs`), which resolves a "desktop
Code" install and spawns it with the reconstructed argv:

```rust
let binary = match version_manager.try_get_entrypoint(&version).await {
    Some(ep) => ep,
    None => { desktop::prompt_to_install(&version); return Ok(1); }   // graceful exit
};
let code = Command::new(&binary).args(args).status()
```

The resolution skips a `PATH` candidate that resolves to the running binary itself
(`cli/src/desktop/version_manager.rs`):

```rust
match std::fs::canonicalize(&target) {
    Ok(m) if m == current_exe => continue,
    ...
};
```

That check is correct, but it only ever skips *the file that is running*. With two copies
on PATH, each one treats the other as a desktop install:

- `bin1/code` skips `bin1`, picks `bin2` — and **persists it** to
  `<cli-data-dir>/versions.json` under `RequestedVersion::Default`
- `bin2/code` resolves its entrypoint from that cache **before** scanning PATH, so it
  never reaches the guard again — it just spawns `bin2` again, forever

The cache written by that run:

```jsonc
{"versions":[[{"t":"Default"},{"Unix":[... "/tmp/a/bin2/code" ...]}]],"current":0}
```

The two things that turn this into an unbounded loop rather than a one-generation
mistake:

1. **The guard is only consulted on a cache miss.** `try_get_entrypoint()` checks the
   persisted cache first and returns on a hit, so the entrypoint is decided once and
   re-used by every generation.
2. **`start_code()` has no depth limit, no attempt cap, and no terminal error state.**

Having two copies of the CLI on `PATH` is not a contrived setup — `code version use
<x.y.z>` installs additional ones. The same loop also occurs when `code` on `PATH` is a
wrapper script rather than the binary, which is how we first hit it.

**Suggested fix**

A depth guard in `start_code()` — an env var checked before spawning and set on the child —
would bound this regardless of how the respawn happens. Re-validating a cached path (and
refusing to persist one that resolves back to `current_exe()`) would also close the cache
path.

Happy to open a PR for the depth guard if that direction is acceptable.

issues.title: Release inline request edit input and listeners when editing finishes

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

issues.body:
Related to #146841

With the default `chat.editRequests: inline`, clicking a request creates an inline `ChatInputPart` through `ChatWidget.createInput`. `createInput` registers about 10 listeners and autoruns on the widget's own store (`onDidLoadInputState`, `onDidFocus`, `onDidAcceptFollowup`, `inputEditor.onDidChangeModelContent`, `chatAgentService.onDidChangeAgents`, `input.onDidChangeCurrentChatMode`, `contextKeyService.onDidChangeContext`, two autoruns, and the scoped instantiation service), and `clickedRequest` adds 3 more listeners. They were only released when the whole widget was disposed, so every edit left them behind:

- the autoruns read the inline input's `selectedToolsModel.entriesMap` / `selectedLanguageModel`, keeping them subscribed to the global `LanguageModelToolsService.toolSets`, and through them the disposed input part, its `CodeEditorWidget`, `TextModel` and DOM;
- listeners accumulated on global emitters (`chatAgentService.onDidChangeAgents`, `contextKeyService.onDidChangeContext`);
- the edit listeners captured the edited request view model, so the replaced `ChatRequestModel`/`ChatResponseModel` stayed alive too.

Edit-only disposables now go into a per-edit `DisposableStore` (`_editingDisposables`), which `createInput` receives for the inline input and which is cleared in `finishedEditing`. The main input keeps using the widget's store. `createInput` subscribes to the input part it created rather than the active one (`this.input`), so the main input's autoruns can't switch to the inline input while an edit is open. `finishedEditing` clears the inline input and paste-target holders instead of only disposing the input, and only the main input gets the getting-started tip presenter (the tip only applies to the empty state; previously an edit replaced the main input's presenter and left it bound to the disposed inline input).

Retainer path (heap snapshot):
`LanguageModelToolsService.toolSets._observers → Derived (ChatSelectedTools.entriesMap) → AutorunObserver (ChatWidget._store)`, and `ObservableValue (owner ChatInputModelSelectionController) → ChatInputPart.container → <div class="chat-edit-input-container">`

### Measurement

| Per inline edit (send + edit) | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| CodeEditorWidget / TextModel | **+1 / +1** | flat |
| ChatRequestModel / ChatResponseModel | **+2 / +2** (replaced request kept) | +1 / +1 (the new request) |
| Detached DOM | **+36 nodes**, +19 roots | flat |
| Emitter / DisposableStore instances | **~+265 / ~+260** | +4 / +5 (the new request) |
| Heap after GC | ~+1 MB | ~+0.1 MB |

### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) with the mock LLM server from `scripts/chat-simulation` (no sign-in), driven over CDP with Playwright. After a warm-up round and after each of 4 rounds: 4× forced GC, live instance counts via `Runtime.queryObjects` on the class prototypes, and `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (descendants of every detached root, queried from a throwaway CDP session). "Without this change" means only this fix reverted. The retainers were identified from heap snapshot retainer paths.

Added a `ChatWidget` test for the inline edit path: it creates the main input, starts and finishes an inline edit, and checks that the inline input, its scoped instantiation service, listeners and autoruns are released, and that the main input keeps its tip presenter (fails without this change).

issues.title: Release previous chat models when the chat view switches sessions

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

issues.body:
Related to #146841

`ChatViewPane.showModel` defers marking the previous session as read with `this._register(disposableTimeout(..., 0))`. That adds one disposable to the view pane's store on every model switch (New Chat, picking another session), and it is only removed when the view is disposed. The timeout closure shares the `showModel` scope, which holds `model`, so every previous `ChatModel` stayed alive.

The timeout now gets the store as its third argument, so it removes itself from the store once it fired (and is still cleared if the view is disposed first).

Retainer path (heap snapshot):
`ChatViewPane._store → FunctionDisposable._fn → closure → Context(showModel) → model → ChatModel`

### Measurement

| Scenario (per round) | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| New chat + 4 messages (text, markdown, code blocks) | **+1 ChatModel**, +3 Emitters | flat |
| Switch between 3 sessions in the sessions list | **+3 ChatModels**, +9 Emitters | flat |

One retained `ChatModel` per session switch for the lifetime of the Chat view.

### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) with the mock LLM server from `scripts/chat-simulation` (no sign-in), driven over CDP with Playwright. After a warm-up round and after each of 4 rounds: 4× forced GC, live instance counts via `Runtime.queryObjects` on the class prototypes, and `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (descendants of every detached root). "Without this change" means only this fix reverted. The retainer was identified from a heap snapshot retainer path.

No new test: the change relies on the `disposableTimeout(handler, timeout, store)` contract that is covered in `async.test.ts`, and `ChatViewPane` has no unit test harness.

Type: Feature Request ## Summary Improve the UX for configuring plugins in 'Agents Customization' window by separating plugin configuration into two distinct groups: **Global configuration** and **Workspace configuration**. ## Motivation Currently there's no clear separation between settings that apply globally and settings that apply only to a specific workspace. This makes it hard to understand which configuration is actually in effect for a given plugin, and makes it cumbersome to override a plugin's behavior on a per-workspace basis. Additionally, there's no indication of *why* a plugin is disabled — whether it was disabled globally or just for the current workspace, both cases are shown identically. This makes it hard to tell at a glance where to go to re-enable it. ## Proposal ### 1. Two configuration groups - **Global configuration** — applies to all workspaces by default - **Workspace configuration** — applies only to the current workspace Both groups list **all installed plugins**. ### 2. Workspace configuration behavior - Each plugin in the Workspace configuration group has a checkbox, **unchecked by default** - Checking the box indicates that *"This plugin has a workspace configuration overriding the global one"* - Once checked, the plugin can be toggled **enabled/disabled** the same way as in the Global configuration group ### 3. Benefits - Clear visual distinction between global defaults and workspace-level overrides - Easier to spot which plugins have a workspace-specific override active - Consistent enable/disable interaction pattern across both scopes VS Code version: Code 1.139.0 (2242ebbb54efeeb0129e08e919e7e8d43033cd83, 2026-09-22T15:13:34Z) OS version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200 Modes:

issues.title: sessions: fix renderer OOM from workspace file count telemetry

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

labels.name: telemetry
labels.description: Telemetry system issues

issues.body:
Fixes #325919

## Problem

`SessionsTelemetryContribution` computes the `workspaceFileCount` telemetry measurement with `ISearchService.fileSearch({ filePattern: '' })` and no `maxResults`. The extension host streams every matching file URI to the renderer, and `SearchOperation` in `mainThreadSearch.ts` keeps all of them until the search completes. The scan was also restarted on every send: the `onWillSendRequest` prewarm bypassed the per-session cache, and the in-flight entry was deleted once the scan finished. It ran even with telemetry turned off.

When a session's workspace is a very large folder, such as the home directory, the renderer V8 heap runs out. This matches nine crash dumps from 1.140 Insiders (`eb1f2bba`):
- **Heap:** every dump is a renderer V8 OOM at the 4 GB pointer-compression cage limit.
- **Running JS:** crash keys name `$handleFileMatch` / `SearchOperation.addMatch`, and most main-thread stacks are parsing extension host search results.
- **Timing:** every crash came 1–5 minutes after a send to a session whose workspace was the home folder.
- **Crash loop:** the last four crashes repeated the cycle reopen → send → OOM.

This was introduced in #318435 and moved to its current location in #319019. The Copilot review on #318435 flagged the per-session caching, but it wasn't addressed.

## Fix

- **Bounded count:** the count is capped at 20,000 files. Folders are searched one at a time with the remaining budget, because providers apply `maxResults` per scheme or per folder. Only one bounded result list is in memory at a time.
- **One scan per folder set:** a single cache keyed by workspace URI plus folder roots holds the pending or completed count. The prewarm and the logging paths share it, so each set of folders is scanned at most once per window. A session that gains folders under the same URI gets a fresh scan.
- **No scan without usage telemetry:** the scan is skipped when the telemetry level is below usage, since the event wouldn't be sent.
- **Field descriptions:** the `workspaceFileCount` descriptions now state the cap.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Telemetry meaning:** a `workspaceFileCount` of 20000 now means "20,000 or more files".
- **Staleness:** counts are computed once per window for each folder set, so they can go stale if a workspace's file count changes a lot.
- **Not addressed here (pre-existing):**
  - Remote agent host sessions (`vscode-agent-host:`) have no file search provider, so their count likely never resolves and their `requestSent` / session action events never fire.
  - Command telemetry is dropped when a command runs without arguments, for example from the title-bar button bar (flagged in the #319019 review).

## Testing

- Two new unit tests:
  - The scan is bounded and runs once per folder set, including the same URI with different folders.
  - No scan runs without usage telemetry.
  - Both fail without the fix.
- `scripts/test.bat --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsTelemetry.contribution.test.ts`: 12 passing.
- `npm run typecheck-client` and eslint on the changed files pass.

issues.title: Claude agent host: keep WebSearch available on the native transport
issues.body:
Fixes #337886

## What

`buildOptions` passed `disallowedTools: ['WebSearch']` for every Claude session. The reason, per `roadmap.md`, is that CAPI doesn't support WebSearch, which only applies when the SDK is routed through the Copilot proxy. Native (Anthropic-auth) sessions talk to Anthropic directly, where WebSearch works, so they were losing web search for no reason.

The block now applies only when `transport.kind === 'proxy'`, using the `isProxy` flag `buildOptions` already computes for the other transport-specific options. The two roadmap lines describing the setting are updated to match.

## How to test

- Unit tests added in `claudeSdkOptions.test.ts`: the proxy transport still sets `disallowedTools: ['WebSearch']`; the native transport leaves it unset.
- Manually: in a Claude session authenticated with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, ask for a web search. Before the change the model has no WebSearch tool; after it, the search runs and returns results. Copilot-routed sessions are unchanged.

I tested the native behaviour by applying the same change to the built 1.139.0 `agentHostMain.js`; I haven't run the unit tests locally.

issues.title: Claude agent host: native (Anthropic-auth) sessions have WebSearch disabled by the CAPI-only disallowedTools block

labels.name: claude-agent
labels.description: Integration with the Claude Agent SDK

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
- VS Code Version: 1.139.0
- OS Version: macOS 27.0 (arm64)
- Harness: Claude agent host, native Anthropic auth (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`)

## Problem

`buildOptions` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/claudeSdkOptions.ts` always passes `disallowedTools: ['WebSearch']` to the Claude Agent SDK, for both transports.

The reason is documented in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/roadmap.md`: "CAPI does not yet support the WebSearch tool. Without this the SDK may invoke it and the upstream CAPI call will fail mid-session." That applies to the Copilot proxy transport. On the native transport the SDK talks to Anthropic directly, where WebSearch works, so native sessions lose web search for a reason that doesn't apply to them.

## Evidence

- In native Claude sessions before any change, the transcripts show zero web searches over a day of use; the model could only fetch URLs it already knew.
- With the `disallowedTools` entry removed for native sessions, the model called `WebSearch` and received results normally.

## Proposed fix

Keep the block for `transport.kind === 'proxy'` and omit it for `'native'`. `buildOptions` already computes `isProxy` for the same kind of transport-specific setting (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, subprocess env). I'll open a PR with the change and tests.

issues.title: Stop chat progress signals once the request settles

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

labels.name: accessibility
labels.description: Keyboard, mouse, ARIA, vision, screen readers (non-specific) issues

issues.body:
Related to #146841

## Leak

`ChatAccessibilityService.acceptRequest()` stores an `AccessibilityProgressSignalScheduler` in `_pendingSignalMap`. It was removed only by `acceptResponse()` or `disposeRequest()`. Some callers never report a response. For example, the `ChatWidget.viewModel` setter calls `acceptRequest(uri, true)` when it attaches to a request that is already in progress. That happens for every session created from the Agents window new-session composer. Each such session left a scheduler behind, and its `playSignalLoop` setTimeout chain ran every 5 s forever. The map was also keyed by URI object identity, so `acceptResponse` with an equal but different URI instance never removed the entry.

Retainer: `ChatAccessibilityService._pendingSignalMap` → `Map` → `AccessibilityProgressSignalScheduler` (+ the signal loop timer).

## Fix

- Key the map with `ResourceMap`.
- Each entry now lasts until the chat model's `hasActiveRequest` settles as false or the model is disposed. The scheduler pauses while `requestInProgress` is false (tool confirmation or elicitation) and restarts when processing resumes.
- Reruns call `acceptRequest` and then `resendRequest`, which synchronously cancels the active request and adds its replacement. So the entry is only removed once `hasActiveRequest` is still false after that call (a 0 ms `RunOnceScheduler`).
- `ChatWidget` passes the model it displays. Models that aren't registered with `IChatService` still clean up when disposed, such as the Agents window preparation transcript (`sessions/contrib/chat/browser/chatView.ts`).

## Measurement

Code OSS `--agents` against the local mock agent host (`--enable-mock-agent`). 6 rounds of "new session → send prompt", with live instance counts from heap snapshots after forced GC. Leave-one-out: only this change was reverted.

| | AccessibilityProgressSignalScheduler | RunOnceScheduler |
|---|---|---|
| before | 5 → 11 (+1 per session) | 165 → 184 |
| after | 0 → 0 | 160 → 173 (unchanged after each review revision) |

## Tests

New `chatAccessibilityService.test.ts`. Covers: settling without a reported response, pausing and resuming around a confirmation (true → false → true), a rerun that cancels the active request before its replacement, model disposal (registered and unregistered models), and matching of equal URIs.






## Known pre-existing issue (out of scope)

On `main` too, "rerun without" (participant detection) while the original request is still streaming loses the rerun's progress sound. The original request's `ChatWidget` chain later calls `acceptResponse` for the same session, which deletes the rerun's entry. That stale call also plays "response received" and announces the rerun's partial text. This isn't a leak and this PR doesn't change it, so I'm leaving it for a separate fix.

issues.title: Agents Window: Figma Sign In action targets slack-github

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
cc @connor4312

## Summary

In Agents Window → Customizations → MCP Servers, clicking the **Sign In** control visually associated with a Figma row briefly shows progress and then resets without opening Figma authentication.

Agent Host debug logs show that the control targets a different MCP server: every click sends a Start request for `slack-github`. No Figma authentication request is made.

## Reproduction

1. Open the Agents Window using the local Agent Host / Copilot CLI harness.
2. Open Customizations → MCP Servers.
3. Locate a Figma MCP row showing **Sign In**.
4. Click **Sign In** repeatedly.

### Actual

The control briefly shows progress and resets. No Figma sign-in flow opens.

### Expected

The action authenticates the Figma server represented by the row. An action displayed on one server must never operate on another server.

## Log evidence

The reporter confirmed the clicked control was the Figma row's Sign In button. The corresponding AHP traffic contains six client-to-host requests, all targeting `slack-github`:

```text
03:09:40.301 c2s session/mcpServerStartRequested
  id=mcp-top-level:copilotcli:<session>:slack-github
03:09:43.107 c2s session/mcpServerStartRequested
  id=mcp-top-level:copilotcli:<session>:slack-github
03:09:44.637 c2s session/mcpServerStartRequested
  id=mcp-top-level:copilotcli:<session>:slack-github
03:09:46.075 c2s session/mcpServerStartRequested
  id=mcp-top-level:copilotcli:<session>:slack-github
03:09:49.724 c2s session/mcpServerStartRequested
  id=mcp-top-level:copilotcli:<session>:slack-github
03:09:59.091 c2s session/mcpServerStartRequested
  id=mcp-top-level:copilotcli:<session>:slack-github
```

There is no request for either Figma customization ID and no request for `https://mcp.figma.com`.

Each misrouted request causes this loop:

1. `slack-github` transitions to `starting`.
2. Existing Slack credentials are forwarded silently; renderer logs report `MCP authentication succeeded for slack-github`.
3. The SDK rejects the restart with `MCP server "slack-github" still requires authentication`.
4. Slack returns to `authRequired`, explaining the visible progress/reset behavior.

The Agent Host executes the exact Slack customization ID sent by the renderer, so the wrong-target association occurs client-side before the AHP boundary.

## Code-path discrepancy

The rendered Sign In path in `McpServerItemRenderer.updateStatus()` should call:

```ts
authenticateMcpServer(this.agentHostCustomizationService, activeSessionResource, activeSessionServer.id)
```

The captured traffic instead corresponds to the lifecycle callback from `getActiveSessionServerLifecycleAction()`:

```ts
() => server.start()
```

This indicates that a stale or incorrectly associated Start Server action is attached to the visible Figma control. Likely areas include virtualized row recycling, row reordering, active-session matching, or retained action nodes.

## Suggested validation

Add a renderer-level regression test that:

1. Renders at least two active-session rows, Figma and Slack.
2. Transitions/reorders/recycles rows through `stopped`, `starting`, and `authRequired` states.
3. Clicks the Sign In button in the row whose visible label is Figma.
4. Asserts that authentication receives the Figma ID.
5. Asserts that neither Slack authentication nor `slack-github.start()` is invoked.

Related details/source-provenance issue: #337874.

issues.title: Agent Host model configuration resets during draft-to-running handoff
issues.body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Reproduction

1. Open the Agents window and create a local Copilot Agent Host session.
2. Select a configurable model such as GPT-6 Sol.
3. Choose non-default model configuration, for example Extra High reasoning and the 872K context window.
4. Send a request that remains active long enough for the draft session to become a committed/running session.
5. Observe the model configuration shown by the committed chat input, or queue another message while the first request is active.

## Actual behavior

The first request receives the selected configuration, but the committed chat input can restore an older per-model configuration bucket. A queued or subsequent request then uses those stale values.

A local pre-fix reproduction produced:

| Model | Initial turn | After handoff / queued message |
|---|---|---|
| GPT-6 Sol | Extra High / 872K | Low / 272K |
| GPT-5.6 Sol | Extra High / 922K | Medium / 272K |

The issue appears model-specific because the committed chat configuration is persisted per model. For example, a stored empty object is an authoritative reset to that model's schema defaults, while another model may already have the desired non-default values stored.

## Expected behavior

The model configuration selected in the new-session composer should survive the draft-to-running transition and be used by queued and subsequent requests.

## Cause

The Agent Host provider has a provider-owned `AutomationModelConfiguration` for each draft/running session, and request dispatch uses that scoped configuration. The ordinary `NewChatInputWidget` creates `SessionModelSelection` without enabling its existing model-configuration adapter, so the visible picker writes through its global fallback instead of the provider-owned session configuration.

When the draft becomes committed, `ChatInputPart` restores its separate `(location, sessionType)` model-configuration bucket. Because the selected configuration was not explicitly carried through the provider-owned store, that older bucket can replace what the user selected.

The split originated with the per-editor model configuration work in #321011. The provider-scoped configuration path was added in #334521, but only the Automation dialog opted into it. #335498 added most of the draft-to-running preservation but did not connect the ordinary Agents composer to the scoped adapter.

## Proposed fix

Construct the normal Agents `SessionModelSelection` with `modelConfiguration: true`. This routes picker reads and writes through the provider-owned session configuration already used by request dispatch and handoff.

A local fixed-build validation retained GPT-6 Sol Max / 872K after materialization and sent both the initial turn and an active-turn queued message with `{ thinkingLevel: "max", contextSize: 872000 }`.

(Written by Copilot)

issues.title: Agents Window: MCP details lose source provenance or remain stuck loading

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
cc @vritant24

## Summary

In the Agents Window, opening MCP server details from the Agent Host harness can produce two broken states:

1. Plugin-provided servers with a real `.mcp.json` source (for example Figma) remain on **Loading MCP server definition...** indefinitely.
2. User-configured Copilot CLI servers (for example `slack-github` from `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`) show **No definition is available for this MCP server.**

These look similar in the UI but have separate causes.

## Reproduction

1. Open the Agents Window using the local Agent Host / Copilot CLI harness.
2. Open Customizations → MCP Servers.
3. Select a plugin-provided Figma server.
   - The details page remains on `Loading MCP server definition...`.
4. Select a server loaded by Copilot CLI from its user MCP configuration, such as `slack-github`.
   - The details page reports that no definition is available.

## Agent Host log evidence

An exported Agent Host debug bundle shows:

- The two Figma entries are distinct plugin installations and are published with real copied `.mcp.json` file URIs.
- `slack-github` is published as a synthetic customization:
  `mcp-top-level:copilotcli:<session-id>:slack-github`.
- Copilot session inventory records for `slack-github` contain name/status/state, but no `mcpSource` or source path.
- Figma inventory records include `mcpSource: "plugin"` and plugin metadata.

## Root cause 1: source-backed details discard a successful read

`EmbeddedMcpServerDetail.renderItem()` starts `loadSourceDefinition()` and captures the current input object. Immediately afterward, `AICustomizationManagementEditor.refreshMcpDetailMigrationState()` calls `setMigratable()`.

`setMigratable()` replaces the current input with a clone:

```ts
this.current = { ...this.current, migratable };
```

When the file read completes, `loadSourceDefinition()` rejects the result because it checks object identity:

```ts
if (this.current !== server || this.renderGeneration !== renderGeneration) {
    return;
}
```

No error is raised and the loading message is never replaced. This appears to have been introduced by `82bef1ccc83a` (`mcp: link migratable servers to review`).

## Root cause 2: top-level Agent Host MCP reflection drops provenance

This is specifically the Agent Host harness path; Local-harness MCP discovery is not authoritative here.

The Copilot SDK session inventory exposes an optional source classification, but no source path. In the captured inventory, the optional source was also absent for `slack-github`.

Agent Host then loses all provenance before publishing the customization:

1. `CopilotAgentSession._applyMcpServerList()` reduces inventory entries to name/status/error.
2. `ISdkMcpServer` has no source or source-path field.
3. `McpCustomizationController._buildTopLevel()` assigns a synthetic `mcp-top-level:` URI to servers without a known plugin/directory child.
4. `AbstractAgentHostCustomizationService.getMcpServers()` deliberately suppresses `sourceUri` for the synthetic scheme.
5. The details input consequently has neither `config` nor `source` and renders the unavailable message.

The synthetic top-level behavior dates to `74c45d448154` (`agentHost: initial implementation of mcp reflection on the agent host side`).

## Expected

- A source-backed MCP definition finishes loading even if diagnostic or migration metadata changes while the read is pending.
- MCP servers loaded by the Agent Host retain authoritative source provenance so Agents Window details can show/open their definition.
- Provenance must come from the host/SDK path and support `COPILOT_HOME` and remote Agent Hosts; the client should not guess `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` or rely on Local-harness discovery.

## Suggested validation

- Add a detail-view regression test with a pending source read followed by `setMigratable(false)`.
- Extend the SDK/Agent Host inventory path to carry authoritative source-path metadata into the published MCP customization.
- Cover user, workspace, plugin, source-less runtime, and remote-host URI mapping cases.

issues.title: Copilot Chat codebase index re-indexes on every reload and freezes the extension host
issues.body:
# Copilot Chat codebase index re-indexes on every reload and freezes the extension host

**Filed against: `microsoft/vscode`** (the extension's own `package.json` declares `"bugs": {"url": "https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues"}` and `"repository": "https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat"`).

Attribution, verified on the affected machine:

- Copilot Chat is a **built-in VS Code extension** here (it lives in `<server>/extensions/copilot/`, i.e. it ships with VS Code 1.138.0; it is *not* a marketplace install.
- The whole failure path below — the log line, `openOrCreateDatabase`, `createFreshDatabase`, and the `codebase-external.sqlite` path — is in **the VS Code-shipped bundle** `<server>/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js`, and it runs **inside the VS Code extension host**(which is why the freeze takes every other extension down with it). The V8 profile quoted below was taken from the extension-host process.

---

## Title

Copilot Chat codebase index re-indexes on every reload and freezes the extension host

## Environment

- VS Code: **1.138.0** (commit `7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda`, 2026-09-15)
- Built-in extension: **Copilot Chat 0.66.0** (`publisher: GitHub`, `engines.vscode: ^1.138.0`)
  — bundle at `<server>/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js`
- Setup: **Remote-SSH** (VS Code client on Windows, extension host on a Linux server, RHEL 9 / XFS).
  Reported symptom is server-side (extension host), so a plain local Linux/macOS/Windows setup with a missing storage folder should reproduce as well.

## Summary

If the per-workspace storage folder for the built-in Copilot Chat extension does not exist, the codebase index SQLite DB cannot be created. Copilot logs the failure and silently falls back to an **in-memory** DB — so the codebase index is rebuilt from scratch on **every** extension-host restart. That re-ingest pins ~1 CPU core for several minutes **on the shared extension-host process**, which starves the event loop: the whole window becomes unresponsive (webview panels won't open, command palette / status-bar commands appear to do nothing.

The user-visible report was *"the VS Code window freezes for ~5 minutes after every window reloading, and clicks do nothing"* with no error surfaced in the UI.

## Impact

- Extension host pinned at **100–175 % CPU for ~6 minutes** (measured four consecutive reloads: `00:27:24→00:33`, `00:41:55→00:48:20`, `00:52:28→00:59:15`, plus one short one).
- During that window the extension host's event loop is **frozen**, not merely slow. Measured with a 5-second `setInterval` heartbeat inside another extension: one tick reported **`lag=325099 ms`** (≈5 m 25 s) — i.e. no timer callback ran for the entire re-ingest.
- Every command/webview message from other extensions is queued behind it; VS Code shows "activating extension…" and then appears to do nothing.
- Failure is silent: the error only goes to the *GitHub Copilot Chat* output channel.

## Steps to reproduce

Prereq: VS Code 1.138 with built-in Copilot Chat 0.66.0, workspace opened, extension host running.

1. Close the window.
2. Delete the extension's per-workspace storage folder on the machine running the extension host
   (Remote-SSH: the *server*):

   ```
   rm -rf ~/.vscode-server/data/User/workspaceStorage/<hash>/GitHub.copilot-chat
   ```

   **(Equivalently: use a workspace whose hash folder has never had a `GitHub.copilot-chat` subfolder.
   The folder is missing because nothing else creates it — see root cause.)**
3. Reload the window (`Developer: Reload Window`).

   - *GitHub Copilot Chat* output channel shows:
     `Failed to create database. Falling back to in-memory db: Error: unable to open database file`
   - The extension-host process burns ~1 core for minutes; other extensions are unresponsive.
4. Reload again **without** creating the folder → same error, **full re-ingest again** (this is the bug:an in-memory DB can never be reused).
5. Now create the folder and reload:

   ```
   mkdir -p ~/.vscode-server/data/User/workspaceStorage/<hash>/GitHub.copilot-chat
   ```

   - `codebase-external.sqlite` is created there (2.7 MB for our workspace) and keeps being written.
   - The error is gone, startup is normal, and subsequent reloads are fast(heartbeat back to `lag=0 ms`).


## Root cause (code)

File: `extensions/copilot/src/platform/workspaceChunkSearch/node/codeSearch/externalIngestIndex.ts`
(class `ExternalIngestIndex`; upstream mirror: `src/platform/workspaceChunkSearch/node/codeSearch/externalIngestIndex.ts`).

The codebase-index DB path is built directly from `context.storageUri` and opened **without ensuring the parent directory exists**:

```js
let A;
Oqo || !ctx.storageUri || ctx.storageUri.scheme !== file
  ? A = ":memory:"
  : A = joinPath(ctx.storageUri, "codebase-external.sqlite").fsPath;
try { this._db = this.openOrCreateDatabase(A) }
catch (g) {
  logService.error("Failed to create database. Falling back to in-memory db", g);
  this._db = this.createFreshDatabase(":memory:");
}
```

```js
openOrCreateDatabase(n) {
  if (n === ":memory:") return this.createFreshDatabase(n);
  if (existsSync(n)) { /* open + cacheVersion check, maybe unlink */ }
  return this.createFreshDatabase(n);          // ← no mkdir anywhere
}
createFreshDatabase(n) {
  ...
  let r = new DatabaseSync(n, { open: true, ... });   // ← SQLITE_CANTOPEN if dirname(n) is missing
}
```

Notably, **other SQLite paths in the very same bundle do it correctly** — so the pattern exists, it was just not applied here:

```js
_ensureDb(){ ... mkdirSync(dirname(this._dbPath), {recursive:true}); new DatabaseSync(this._dbPath); ... }
openDb(){    ... mkdirSync(dirname(this.dbPath),  {recursive:true}); ...
             } catch(e){ if (this.dbPath!==":memory:" && isCantOpen(e)) { this.deleteDbFiles(); this.openDb(); } }
```

`context.storageUri`'s directory is not guaranteed to pre-exist (VSCode creates per-extension workspace storage lazily, on demand) — so opening a file inside it is a race that a fresh workspace loses.

Happy to send a PR if you'd like

issues.title: [1.139] Skip known scratch-directory cleanup race test
issues.body:
## Summary

Temporarily skip `workspaceless session uses and cleans up a provider scratch directory` in the Copilot Agent Host E2E suite on `release/1.139`. Windows already skips this test.

The test failed four Linux Electron integration attempts in [build 477081](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477081&view=results) because a catalog metadata persistence race can leave the scratch directory behind after session disposal.

The defect exists in the already-shipped 1.139 version. This release-only test skip keeps the 1.139.1 patch free of unrelated product changes. It does not fix the cleanup defect; the fix and test coverage remain on `main` in #337566.

Only the test registration and explanatory comment change. The test body, other tests, and product code remain unchanged.

## Validation

- Diff checks and pre-commit hygiene passed.

issues.title: [1.139] Backport scratch-directory cleanup ordering fix
issues.body:
## Summary

Backport the scratch-directory cleanup ordering fix from #337566 to `release/1.139`.

Session disposal could reach Copilot before the host had persisted the workspace-less marker. Copilot would then skip scratch-directory cleanup even though `disposeSession` succeeded. This caused four Linux Electron integration failures in [build 477081](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477081&view=results).

- Drain pending catalog metadata writes before provider disposal.
- Extend the regression test to verify that the workspace-less marker is visible during disposal.

This is a focused partial backport of `2e112d9dca581653747117dddd511e38b764f706`; the unrelated test-server shutdown changes are omitted.

## Validation

- The two-file patch matches the corresponding upstream changes.
- Diff checks and pre-commit hygiene passed.
- Local unit/E2E tests were not completed; release-branch CI provides validation.

issues.title: agents: Let Toggle Block Comment keep Ctrl+Shift+A on Linux

labels.name: linux
labels.description: Issues with VS Code on Linux

issues.body:
Fixes #321321

## What

On Linux, `Ctrl+Shift+A` is the default keybinding for **Toggle Block Comment** (`editor.action.blockComment`), but **Open Agents Window** (`workbench.action.openAgentsWindow`) registered the same key at a higher weight (`WorkbenchContrib` vs `EditorContrib`), so pressing it in the editor opened the Agents window instead of commenting.

Both `Ctrl+Shift+A` window-switching keybindings now defer to the editor on Linux when a writable editor in the editor area has focus:

- `OpenAgentsWindowAction` (VS Code → Agents window)
- `OpenVSCodeWindowAction` (Agents window → VS Code), for consistency

New `when` clause component: `!isLinux || !editorAreaFocus || editorReadonly`

## Notes for reviewers

- **Linux only.** On Windows/macOS, Toggle Block Comment is `Shift+Alt+A` / `⇧⌥A` and Toggle Line Comment is `Ctrl+/` / `⌘/`, so there is no default conflict there; behavior is unchanged on those platforms. The issue says "All OS", but all duplicates (#326962, #328272, #333341) were reported on Linux.
- **Read-only editors** still get the Agents shortcut, since Toggle Block Comment's keybinding requires `!editorReadonly` and would not fire anyway.
- Non-text editors in the editor area (e.g. image preview, settings editor) don't set `editorReadonly`, so on Linux the shortcut is inert while one of those has focus. The Command Palette entry still works.
- The screen-reader variant (`Ctrl+Shift+Alt+A`) is unchanged.

issues.title: Release canceled Delayer tasks to avoid retaining detached DOM

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

issues.body:
Related to #146841

## Leak

`Delayer.cancel()` cleared the timeout and rejected the pending promise, but it kept `this.task`. `dispose()` calls `cancel()`, so it had the same problem. The last task closure stayed on the delayer until the next `trigger()`. `ThrottledDelayer` wraps a `Delayer`, so it kept the closure too.

`QuickInputList._registerHoverListeners` uses a `ThrottledDelayer`. Its `onMouseOver` task closes over the tree mouse event `e`. When the mouse leaves, `onMouseOut` calls `delayer.cancel()`, but the task and its `MouseEvent` stay alive. When the pointer moves from editor text into a Quick Open row, the event's `relatedTarget` is an editor token span. After the editor view is detached, for example by switching tabs, the canceled task keeps that old view DOM alive. At most one view is retained this way, and only until the next hover.

Retainer path seen in a heap snapshot:

```
QuickInputService._controller → QuickInputController.ui.list → QuickInputList._store → DisposableStore
  → ThrottledDelayer.delayer → Delayer.task → closure (promiseFactory) → closure scope { e }
  → Object.browserEvent → MouseEvent → <span class="mtk22"> → … → <div class="monaco-editor">
```

## Fix

- `Delayer.cancel()` (and so `dispose()`) now clears `task`. A canceled trigger still rejects with `CancellationError` and doesn't run its task, and a later `trigger()` works as before.
- A `cancel()` can happen after the delay has elapsed but before the queued `.then` runs the task. Before this change, the task still ran in that case. Now it rejects with `CancellationError`, which matches a normal cancel.
- Each round's `.then` now checks that it still owns `completionPromise`. Before, a `cancel()` in that window followed immediately by `trigger()` let the stale round run the new task as the canceled promise's result and clear the new round's promise, so the new promise never settled. This was already the case before this PR (found in review); the stale round now rejects with `CancellationError` and leaves the new round alone.
- `Throttler.dispose()` now clears `queuedPromiseFactory`. After dispose, the queued factory never runs, but the throttler used to keep a reference to it.
- `ThrottledDelayer` needs no separate change because it uses these two classes. `Throttler` already clears finished tasks: `activePromise` holds only the promise, and `queuedPromiseFactory` is cleared once it has been queued.

## Tests

New tests in `src/vs/base/test/common/async.test.ts`:

- Delayer: `cancel` / `dispose` release the pending task. The pending promise rejects with `CancellationError`, the task doesn't run, and a later trigger works.
- Delayer: a cancel after the delay elapsed doesn't run the task.
- Delayer: a cancel and retrigger after the delay elapsed rejects the canceled promise and settles the new one with its own task.
- ThrottledDelayer: `cancel` releases the pending task.
- Throttler: disposal releases the queued factory.

The unit test runner doesn't expose `gc()`, so a `WeakRef` or `FinalizationRegistry` check isn't reliable here. The tests read the private field directly instead. All 6 new tests fail without the fix and pass with it. The full async suite passes.

## Measurement (Code OSS, Windows)

Scenario, driven with Playwright over CDP (`--remote-debugging-port`):

1. Open two files and press Ctrl+P.
2. Move the mouse onto an editor token span below the widget, then straight onto a Quick Open row, then back to the span within the hover delay. This makes `mouseover` fire with `relatedTarget` = the editor span, followed by `mouseout` → `cancel()`.
3. Press Escape, then Ctrl+PageDown to switch tabs so the previous editor view is detached.
4. Run `HeapProfiler.collectGarbage` 5 times, then `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes`. Count detached roots whose subtree contains `view-lines` / `overflow-guard`.

Each variant got 3 fresh launches with 5 iterations each. The build was the same apart from `out/vs/base/common/async.js`:

| | detached editor views after each iteration | nodes in those roots (`retainedNodeIds`) | total detached nodes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 1 in 15/15 iterations | 154 | ~260–275 |
| After | 0 in 15/15 iterations | 0 | ~106–111 |

The retained view is bounded (always exactly 1), as expected, because the delayer holds only the latest task. `retainedNodeIds` counts are smaller than the ~1,057 nodes seen in the original heap snapshot. The count depends on file contents and window size, and CDP only reports nodes that JS retains.

issues.title: Agent Host: chat URIs encode the owning session, contrary to AHP

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

issues.body:
## Summary

VS Code's Agent Host generates chat URIs by encoding the owning session URI into the path. This conflicts with AHP's documented chat identity model: a chat has a server-allocated identifier, and its relationship to a session is represented in protocol state rather than encoded in its address.

The shared parsing helpers also require this VS Code-specific encoding, so they reject chat URIs that follow the documented AHP form.

This report is based on public source inspection at VS Code commit [`e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c), not a new end-to-end runtime reproduction.

## AHP contract

The [Chat Channel specification, URI section](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/296b25e7b698a4a84a0ee5a28d9573e70048a0bf/docs/specification/chat-channel.md#uri) documents `ahp-chat:/<uuid>` and states:

> The path is a server-unique identifier (typically a UUID) allocated by the server when the chat is created. The owning session URI is **not** encoded in the chat URI — the relationship is expressed via the session's `chats` catalog and each chat's `origin`.

The same specification describes `defaultChat` as an optional, advisory routing hint. It does not define a default chat address that clients can calculate from the session URI.

## Current implementation

### 1. Chat identity embeds session identity

[**sessionState.ts — `buildChatUri`**](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/sessionState.ts#L1171):

```ts
export function buildChatUri(sessionUri: ProtocolURI | ResourceURI, chatId: string): string {
	const session = typeof sessionUri === 'string' ? sessionUri : sessionUri.toString();
	const encoded = encodeBase64(VSBuffer.fromString(session), false, true);
	return `${AHP_CHAT_SCHEME}://${chatId}/${encoded}`;
}
```

This produces `ahp-chat://<chatId>/<base64url(sessionUri)>`. The chat ID is placed in the authority, while the path contains the encoded session URI.

[**sessionState.ts — `buildDefaultChatUri`**](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/sessionState.ts#L1186):

```ts
export function buildDefaultChatUri(sessionUri: ProtocolURI | ResourceURI): string {
	return buildChatUri(sessionUri, DEFAULT_CHAT_ID);
}
```

[**`AgentHostStateManager._ensureDefaultChat` in agentHostStateManager.ts**](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts#L1194) uses that builder, registers the chat, and publishes the resulting address in `SessionState.chats` and `SessionState.defaultChat`.

**Those discovery fields are already populated. The problem is the identity construction, not missing advertisement.**

### 2. Parsing treats the encoding as a requirement

[**`parseChatUri` in sessionState.ts**](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/sessionState.ts#L1208) requires a nonempty authority and decodes the path to recover the owning session. Consequently, an illustrative AHP-shaped URI such as `ahp-chat:/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111` is rejected because it has no authority.

[**`parseRequiredSessionUriFromChatUri` in sessionState.ts**](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/sessionState.ts#L1247) then reports it as `Malformed AHP chat URI`.

## Why this matters

- Host and client code using the same builder can agree with each other while still relying on a convention that AHP explicitly does not define.
- Consumers that reconstruct chat addresses or decode them to discover ownership cannot handle independently allocated chat identities through those paths.
- Changing only the host's URI generator would leave those consumers and restoration paths dependent on the old encoding.

## Expected behavior / proposed scope

- Allocate server-unique chat identifiers without embedding the owning session URI. Apply the same identity model to default, additional, and subagent chats.
- Keep ownership explicit in host state and the protocol's catalog/origin relationships. Consumers should use advertised chat resources, `defaultChat` when present, and chat-creation results rather than inventing addresses.
- Replace ownership lookups that depend on decoding the URI; do not classify a protocol-conforming URI as malformed solely because it lacks the legacy encoding.
- Plan compatibility for existing persisted sessions, restored chats, and older clients before changing established identities.
- Add coverage for opaque identifiers across creation, default/additional chat selection, ownership lookup, restoration, and reconnect. Include fixtures whose chat addresses cannot be calculated from the session address.

The goal is to align the local Agent Host and its consumers with the published AHP contract, not to introduce another URI convention.
