issues.title: Release accessible view listeners per show instead of on dispose

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

labels.name: accessibility
labels.description: Keyboard, mouse, ARIA, vision, screen readers (non-specific) issues

labels.name: terminal
labels.description: General terminal issues that don't fall under another label

issues.body:
Related to #146841 (replaces the `AccessibilityHelpWidget` item of the issue, which became `AccessibleView`)

`AccessibleView` is a long-lived singleton, but `show()` registered per-provider listeners into its own `_store` on every call:
- `provider.onDidChangeContent` listener
- `provider.onDidRequestClearLastProvider` listener
- a code block context provider registration (chat)

and `_render()` returned a new listener store on every content refresh, which was dropped when refreshing an already visible view. So every provider ever shown was retained for the lifetime of the window — for the terminal that is the whole `TerminalInstance`, xterm and DOM of every terminal whose accessible view was ever opened, even after the terminal was killed.

Now listeners of a `show()` are released when the view hides, render listeners replace the previous set, the clear-last-provider listener lives as long as that provider is remembered, and the code block context provider is registered once.

Retainer path (heap snapshot, before):
`AccessibleViewService → AccessibleView._store → FunctionDisposable → listener closure → TerminalAccessibleBufferProvider._instance → TerminalInstance._wrapperElement → <div class="terminal-wrapper">`

The clear-last-provider listener now uses the structural provider contract, so providers implementing `IAccessibleViewContentProvider` directly (like `TerminalAccessibleBufferProvider`) are honored. The terminal provider's clear notification is tied to the terminal instance instead of the provider, because the accessible view disposes the provider on hide while it may still remember it. Copies of the provider made for Accessibility Help (and restored when it closes) forward the clear request too.

### Measurement

| Scenario | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| 5× (create terminal, `echo hello`, *Open Accessible View*, Escape, kill terminal) | **5** `TerminalInstance`, **5** `XtermTerminal`, **5** `TerminalAccessibleBufferProvider`, **5** `BufferContentTracker` alive; 5 detached terminal DOM trees (+26 detached roots / +96 nodes) | **0** of each |

This is unbounded: it grows by one terminal per terminal whose accessible view was opened (live object counts from heap snapshots after GC).
### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) driven over CDP with Playwright. After each scenario: 4× forced GC, then `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (the data behind Edge's *Detached Elements* tool), counting the descendants of every detached root. "Without this change" means all other fixes from this series applied and only this one reverted, so the number shows what this retainer alone keeps alive. Each scenario was run 3 times with identical results. The retainer was identified from a heap snapshot retainer path.

Added a unit test that provider listeners don't accumulate across show() calls and are released when the view hides.

issues.title: Release the input focus tracker once the input blurs

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

issues.body:
Related to #146841

`ContextKeyService.updateInputContextKeys` creates a focus tracker for the focused input on every `focusin`. When the input blurred, the tracker was disposed, but the disposed tracker and the `Event.once` listener stayed in the per-focus `DisposableStore` until the next `focusin`. The tracker's `_refreshStateHandler` closure references the element, so the last focused input stayed alive — e.g. the `native-edit-context` of an editor view that was disposed while focused, when focus didn't move to another element.

The store is now cleared once the input blurs.

Retainer path (heap snapshot):
`ContextKeyService … onFocusDisposables (MutableDisposable) → DisposableStore → FocusTracker._refreshStateHandler → element → <div class="native-edit-context">`

### Measurement

| Scenario | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| Focus an editor and close all editors of the group (Ctrl+K W) | **1 detached node** (`native-edit-context`) + the disposed `FocusTracker` | 0 |

Small: the edit context element is removed from the view on dispose, so only the element itself is retained, not the view. Included for completeness of the #146841 cleanup.
### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) driven over CDP with Playwright. After each scenario: 4× forced GC, then `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (the data behind Edge's *Detached Elements* tool), counting the descendants of every detached root. "Without this change" means all other fixes from this series applied and only this one reverted, so the number shows what this retainer alone keeps alive. Each scenario was run 3 times with identical results. The retainer was identified from a heap snapshot retainer path.

issues.title: Only remember sticky scroll mouse targets inside the widget

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

issues.body:
Related to #146841

Every `StickyScrollController` (one per code editor) listened to `mousemove` on the main window and stored `mouseEvent.target` in `_mouseTarget` — for any element in the window. When the element under the mouse was part of an editor view that got detached afterwards (e.g. the tab was switched with the keyboard), every sticky scroll controller kept that span and, through its parent chain, the complete detached view alive until the mouse moved again.

`_mouseTarget` is only used to find the hovered sticky line, so only targets inside the sticky scroll widget are remembered now.

Retainer path (heap snapshot):
`StickyScrollController._mouseTarget → <span class="mtk21"> → <span> → view-line → view-lines → … → <div class="monaco-editor">`

### Measurement

| Scenario | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| Rest the mouse over editor text, switch tabs with Ctrl+PageUp | 1 detached editor view, **1,059 DOM nodes** | 0 |

Bounded (one tree, released on the next mouse move), but independent of which editor had the controller: every open editor's controller retained it.
### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) driven over CDP with Playwright. After each scenario: 4× forced GC, then `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (the data behind Edge's *Detached Elements* tool), counting the descendants of every detached root. "Without this change" means all other fixes from this series applied and only this one reverted, so the number shows what this retainer alone keeps alive. Each scenario was run 3 times with identical results. The retainer was identified from a heap snapshot retainer path.

issues.title: Don't retain the faded out editor message widget

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

labels.name: editor-contrib
labels.description: Editor collection of extras

issues.body:
Related to #146841

`MessageController` kept the last message widget in `_messageWidget` after it faded out, and the fade-out disposable kept referencing it too, so the widget and its DOM stayed alive until the next message was shown in that editor.

The widget is now handed over to the fade out (`clearAndLeak`), and the fade out keeps all references in a store that is emptied once the animation completes.

### Measurement

| Scenario | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| Show an editor message (F12 where there's no definition → "No definition found"), let it close | **4 detached DOM nodes** (`monaco-editor-overlaymessage`) + the `MessageWidget` | 0 |

Small and bounded (one widget per editor that showed a message); included for completeness of the #146841 cleanup since it shows up in every detached elements listing after using Go to Definition.
### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) driven over CDP with Playwright. After each scenario: 4× forced GC, then `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (the data behind Edge's *Detached Elements* tool), counting the descendants of every detached root. "Without this change" means all other fixes from this series applied and only this one reverted, so the number shows what this retainer alone keeps alive. Each scenario was run 3 times with identical results. The retainer was identified from a heap snapshot retainer path.

issues.title: Release widget DOM nodes when an editor view is disposed

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

labels.name: editor-window
labels.description: Issues around editor window UI

issues.body:
Related to #146841

Content, overlay and glyph margin widgets outlive the editor `View`: `CodeEditorWidget` keeps them and re-adds them to the next view once a model is attached. When a model is detached without a new one (e.g. all editors of a group are closed, the editor stays around without a model), the widgets' DOM nodes stayed parented in the disposed view — or in its `overflowingContentWidgets`/`overflowingOverlayWidgets` containers, which live outside the view's DOM. Since the widgets are referenced by live contributions (rename, suggest, hover, sticky scroll, …), the entire previous view DOM stayed alive.

`ViewContentWidgets`, `ViewOverlayWidgets` and `GlyphMarginWidgets` now remove the DOM nodes of their widgets on dispose. Attaching a new model adds them to the new view as before.

Retainer path (heap snapshot):
`StickyScrollController → StickyScrollWidget._rootDomNode → <div class="sticky-widget"> → overlayWidgets → overflow-guard → <div class="monaco-editor">` (same for `RenameWidget`, `SuggestWidget`, `HoverWidget` via the overflowing containers)

### Measurement

| Scenario | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| Open a file, show rename (F2) and suggest widgets, run *Close All Editors* | 1 detached editor view, **1,402 DOM nodes** + **95 nodes** of overflowing widget containers | 0 |
| Same, closing the group's editors with Ctrl+K W | **1,443 + 95 nodes** | 0 |

One retained view per editor control that is left without a model (e.g. per empty editor group), until a model is attached again.
### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) driven over CDP with Playwright. After each scenario: 4× forced GC, then `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (the data behind Edge's *Detached Elements* tool), counting the descendants of every detached root. "Without this change" means all other fixes from this series applied and only this one reverted, so the number shows what this retainer alone keeps alive. Each scenario was run 3 times with identical results. The retainer was identified from a heap snapshot retainer path.

Added a CodeEditorWidget test with a real view: widget nodes (incl. an overflowing content widget) are released on setModel(null) and reattached on the next setModel.

issues.title: Don't retain the last KeyboardEvent in ModifierKeyEmitter

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

issues.body:
Related to #146841

`ModifierKeyEmitter` stored the last modifier `KeyboardEvent` in its (singleton) key status. A `KeyboardEvent` references its target and event path, so the DOM that received the last Ctrl/Alt/Shift/Meta key stayed alive until the next modifier key press — e.g. the complete view DOM of an editor whose model changed or which was closed, or a killed terminal.

The event is now only exposed while listeners are notified. Its only consumer (menubar Alt handling) reads it synchronously in the listener.

Retainer path (heap snapshot):
`ModifierKeyEmitter.instance → _keyStatus.event → KeyboardEvent → EventPath → <div class="native-edit-context"> → … → <div class="monaco-editor">`

### Measurement

| Scenario | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| Focus an editor, press and release Ctrl, click another editor tab | 1 detached editor view, **1,058 DOM nodes** | 0 |
| Show rename + suggest widgets (Ctrl+Space), close all editors of the group | 1 detached editor view, **1,385 nodes** | 0 |
| Close all editors of the group with Ctrl+K W | 1 detached editor view, **1,426 nodes** | 0 |

Bounded to one retained tree at a time (replaced on the next modifier key press), but it's the most common way an old editor view stays alive — any keyboard-driven tab switch or close.
### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) driven over CDP with Playwright. After each scenario: 4× forced GC, then `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (the data behind Edge's *Detached Elements* tool), counting the descendants of every detached root. "Without this change" means all other fixes from this series applied and only this one reverted, so the number shows what this retainer alone keeps alive. Each scenario was run 3 times with identical results. The retainer was identified from a heap snapshot retainer path.

Added a unit test that the event is only available while listeners run.

issues.title: agentHost: keep refreshed sandbox credentials bound to the host
issues.body:
## Summary

Prevent a sandbox credential refresh from combining new host-key metadata with a cached token encrypted for a different key.

Previously, a refresh that omitted the sealed token also replaced any newly reported host key with the cached key. That could hide a host-key change while accepting the new relay credentials.

- Check that the sealed token names the refreshed host key, and that cached key metadata has not changed when reusing a sealed token.
- Keep the entire previous credential bundle on mismatch, log a warning without credential contents, and retry using the existing 30-second schedule and 10-consecutive-failure cap.
- Install matching credentials together while preserving the existing optional-key behavior and leaving the current socket untouched.

This is a defensive correctness fix for host/key changes, not a measured performance improvement. It does not add recovery-time admission refresh or change connection retry policy.

## Validation

- Reproduced the host-key mixing regressions before the fix.
- Focused TypeScript check passed after rebasing onto main.
- All 22 focused credential-refresh and scheduling unit tests passed.
- Targeted ESLint, whitespace checks, and pre-commit hygiene passed.

Coverage includes key changes, matching replacement credentials, omitted key metadata, preservation of the complete previous bundle, and exact retry timing and limits.

Focused unit-test command after compiling the test output:

```sh
npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxCredentialRefresh.test.ts
```

Live sandbox and end-to-end validation have not been established. No application was launched as part of these checks.

issues.title: Fix Agent Host sandbox path normalization on Windows
issues.body:
## Summary

Fixes #337171.

- Resolve sandbox configuration in a shared, provider-neutral Agent Host accessor before SDK or host-terminal policy mapping.
- Normalize Windows filesystem path separators using the executing Agent Host's OS, independently of whether its client is local or remote.
- Apply the resolver at session launch/resume, per-turn SDK updates, and host-terminal settings reads.
- Preserve stored configuration, client forwarding, POSIX paths, and session/managed-policy overrides.
- Reuse the platform normalization helper in the existing Windows MXC terminal path.

## Validation

- 74 targeted sandbox, session, launcher, and Windows terminal tests passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- ESLint passed for all 11 changed files.
- `npm run compile` completed with zero errors.
- Pre-commit hygiene passed.
- Launched Code OSS and attached the Agent Host debugger with a breakpoint after normalization. End-to-end access-denial enforcement has not been verified.

## Compatibility / follow-up

No persisted schema or wire-format migration is required. Existing sessions receive normalized policy on resume or the next policy application. Windows paths that previously failed to match may now enforce their intended restrictions.

The runtime filesystem schema still accepts generic objects; this change assumes the documented string-array fields. Malformed persisted configuration is not covered by the new normalization tests and may throw earlier during resolution, including with sandboxing disabled.

issues.title: Test: Remote session delegation across agent hosts
issues.body:
Refs: #336690, #336682

- [ ] windows (origin) -> linux (remote), worktree isolation
- [ ] macos (origin) -> windows (remote), folder isolation

Complexity: 5

Authors: @dmitrivMS

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23337849%0A%0A&assignees=dmitrivMS)

---

NOTE: Windows to Windows is also ok, and more than 2 machines is better than 2.

Validate picker-free remote-session creation and two-way messaging in the Agents window. Aim for about 45-60 minutes with machines already available. Claim one row above; each tester runs the four scenarios below, not every OS/model/transport combination.

## Setup

- **Every tester must use at least two distinct machines:** machine A hosts the coordinating Agents window and originating session; machine B runs the remote session. VMs count as machines; two windows or multiple sessions on one machine do not satisfy this requirement. Both testers must exercise a real cross-machine round trip.
- Use 1.140 Insiders or development builds containing the merged #336690 on the coordinating client and agent hosts. Do not assume an older Insiders/remote-host installation has the feature yet.
- On A, start a Copilot Agent Host conversation, not the Local harness. Enable `chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled` and connect B through either SSH or an authenticated dev tunnel. One transport and one advertised Copilot model per tester are sufficient.
- Have Git and a disposable, trusted repository on B. Record its current branch and use the isolation mode assigned above. Do not use production repositories or broaden approval settings for this test.

## 1. Opt-in, discovery, and matching

- Start with `chat.remoteSessions.tools.enabled` explicitly `false`: the agent must not have the four remote-session tools. Set it to `true` and ask the agent to list remote hosts with `list_agent_hosts`. Verify B's identity, connection status, OS, memory capacity, CPU count, and advertised models match the machine.
- Request a session with an impossible requirement, such as more memory than any connected host has. Expect a clear failure and no session creation or fallback to a nonmatching machine.

## 2. Cross-OS creation, replies, and follow-up

Use a **non-default chat within the originating session** for this scenario. For example, adapt this prompt to B's OS and known resources:

> Start one remote session on a connected Linux host with at least 8 GiB of memory and two logical CPUs. Report the actual OS and the marker `remote-tpi-1` back to this originating chat. Do not modify any files.

- Verify `create_remote_session` selects B without a host picker, creates exactly one workspace-less session, and actually runs on B. Use one model advertised by B and confirm it is selected. The original chat remains usable while the task runs.
- Confirm the remote agent uses `send_remote_message` to report back to the **same originating chat**, not a different chat or only the remote transcript. During one round trip, give the origin another task so a returning message queues if it is busy. Expect one delivered reply and no acknowledgement loop or repeated polling.
- Send a short follow-up to that existing remote session and receive a second distinct marker. Use `get_remote_session` to verify its status/latest response without starting another turn or session.
- **Optional, only if already available:** with a second eligible remote host connected, try two short tasks and check that automatic placement accounts for running sessions and pending creations. Do not provision a third machine just for this check.

## 3. Explicit target workspace

Ask for one small edit in B's trusted test repository, explicitly using the assigned isolation mode and the target's existing path.

- **Windows -> Linux tester:** use a new worktree from an existing target-local branch. Verify the edit is in the new worktree and the source checkout/branch is unchanged.
- **macOS -> Windows tester:** use folder isolation. Verify the edit is in the specified folder, with no unexpected worktree or branch switch.

In both cases, verify nothing is cloned/copied from A, normal approvals still apply, and the remote session can report the result back.

## 4. Disconnection and disabling

- Disconnect B before requesting a session explicitly on B. Expect a clear unavailable-host failure, no duplicate session, and no silent local/other-host fallback. Reconnect B and send a new follow-up to the existing remote session; messaging should work again.
- Disable `chat.remoteSessions.tools.enabled` while a harmless remote task is running. The tools become unavailable, but B stays connected and the task is not canceled. Observe completion in the remote session rather than expecting tool-based replies after disabling.

## Report and cleanup

Record both OSes, client/host builds, transport, model, isolation mode, and any failed or blocked steps. Restore settings and remove only test-created files/worktrees. No need to exhaust creation/depth limits, create hundreds of sessions, or run an exhaustive provider/transport matrix; boundary behavior has automated coverage.

issues.title: SDK hangs due to spamming listSessions
issues.body:
A couple times a day, the SDK uses 800% CPU for awhile and AH sessions hang. Seems that refreshing sessions is misbehaving somehow. Can provide logs

```
Yes. The logs provide a strong smoking gun, and it is **not primarily thousands of `getSessionMetadata` calls**.

## What happened

### 1. Repeated bulk `listSessions` prewarming

`agenthost.log` recorded:

- **111** “Listing prewarm session metadata” passes
- Each pass enumerated approximately **4,854–4,858 SDK sessions**
- Total session records enumerated: **538,958**
- Median pass: **1.42 seconds**
- Slowest pass: **84.4 seconds**
- Since 16:50, four passes enumerated **19,432 session records**

Immediately before this recurrence:

- 16:53:47: enumerated 4,858 sessions
- 16:53:49: enumerated the same 4,858 sessions again

The regular Agent Service list only had **47 provider-fallback sessions**, but the Copilot prewarm enumerated the entire 4,858-session SDK store to provide metadata for those fallbacks.

### 2. Not direct metadata RPC spam

The retained AHP JSONL logs contain:

- `listSessions`: **31 actual requests**
- `getSessionMetadata`: **0**
- `sessions.getMetadata`: **0**

The current provider code deliberately performs one bulk `client.listSessions()` in `prewarmSessionMetadata`, specifically to avoid one `getSessionMetadata` RPC per session.

`AgentService` invokes that prewarm whenever even one Copilot session needs provider fallback metadata. The cache is short-lived and is cleared when that list computation finishes, so another `listSessions` call repeats the full runtime enumeration.

This is amplification rather than raw client spam: a relatively modest number of AHP list requests repeatedly caused full scans of nearly 5,000 runtime sessions.

### 3. The immediate 16:55 window also had lifecycle churn

Between 16:55 and 16:56, the logs show:

- 8 session resumes
- 8 restored sessions
- 8 disconnects
- 10 failed subscriptions to resources that had disappeared
- 20 customization-discovery failures across 16:55–16:56

So this particular recurrence appears to be:

1. Two back-to-back bulk catalog scans around 16:53:47
2. Followed by substantial resume/restore/disconnect churn around 16:55

## Live sample

The stock runtime sample captured the tail of the event:

- **126 native threads**
- **99 `copilot-cabi` threads**
- 31 `copilot-cabi` threads created or retired during the ten-second sample
- About **1.16 GB** resident memory
- CPU dropped from roughly 19% to 1% while thread count fell from 126 to 80

The sample was mostly waiting by then, with little active filesystem I/O. That is consistent with the worker pool retiring after a filesystem-heavy burst rather than an endless main-thread loop.

Raw capture: `copilot-runtime-42514-20260924-sample.txt`

## Likely fix

The most promising VS Code-side fixes are:

1. Keep the bulk SDK session metadata cache alive briefly across list computations, rather than disposing it after each pass.
2. Coalesce concurrent and trailing prewarm requests.
3. Avoid enumerating all 4,858 SDK sessions when only 47 fallback session IDs need metadata.
4. Reduce redundant local `listSessions` refreshes, especially the back-to-back pairs.

Historical context: the bulk prewarm optimization was introduced by Vijay Upadya on September 1 in [#333896](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/333896), then integrated with centralized fallback metadata by Sandeep Somavarapu in [#332410](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/332410).

## tl;dr

VS Code was not visibly spamming individual `getMetadata` RPCs. It was repeatedly issuing `listSessions`, and each list amplified into a full scan of roughly **4,858 Copilot sessions**. This run performed **111 full prewarm scans**, plus session resume/disconnect churn. That is the strongest explanation for the CPU and `copilot-cabi` thread explosion.
```

issues.title: mcp: make assisted setup destination-aware
issues.body:
## Summary

- Choose the destination before package-assisted MCP setup, including Copilot Global.
- Preserve the server's stdio, HTTP, or SSE configuration and use package manifests when available.
- Keep collected values out of generated files and require explicit approval before falling back to VS Code configuration.

Stacked on #337838. The base is `agents/p3-copilot-global-manual`; main integration is intentionally deferred.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Package setup previously generated a stdio-shaped configuration before choosing its destination. That prevented the prompt and input handling from matching the destination, excluded Copilot Global, and overwrote remote transport intent.

### Implementation

Core selects the destination using the existing install-target service, global picker, and workspace-file defaults. It supplies a destination schema to the extension. The extension validates and extracts exactly one named server without partially converting its dialect; core then normalizes through the shared converters, and the existing scanner owns the final file representation and safe write.

Usable package manifests still bypass the model. Their inputs and unsupported fields remain intact so core can offer a safe destination instead of stripping metadata. Workspace-root generation can retain required VS Code fields or SSE intent, but those configurations require explicit approval to use the legacy workspace file.

### Behavior and constraints

- Manual setup retains its question order and the existing global labels and path descriptions.
- VS Code input answers become opaque references before reaching the model, including when embedded inside URLs, arguments, or headers. Values go through the existing saved-input path rather than the configuration file.
- Copilot Global prompts request uppercase environment-variable names, not values. Generated references are retained, and the completion notification explains that variables must be set on the agent-host machine before a new session.
- Validation rejects malformed or ambiguous output, missing or altered input references, and mismatched command output formats without logging sensitive payloads. Older callers without a destination format retain the VS Code default; incompatible extension output produces an explicit error.
- Explicit file targets are never silently redirected. Cancellation and policy rejection occur without writes, and package configurations requiring unresolved inputs cannot be handed to the current agent session.
- Existing Copilot-home lookup, authority-scoped discovery behavior, shared workspace eligibility, and scanner concurrency protections remain unchanged. No agent-host protocol or general destination framework is added.

</details>

### Type of issue

Bug

### Description

Opening **Agent Customizations** for a remote agent host/dev box hides the **MCP Servers** section entirely.

The baseline behavior should be to show the section and explain why it is unavailable if the active target cannot support it. Silently hiding the section makes it look like MCP is not part of the remote target and gives the user no path forward.

The **MCP Servers** section is absent for the remote target.

### Expected behavior

- **MCP Servers** is visible for remote targets.
- The section lists and manages the MCP servers used by that remote agent host.
- If a particular remote target cannot support MCP management, keep the section visible and show a clear explanation and remediation instead of hiding it.

The remote harness currently opts out of the section explicitly:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/browser/remoteAgentHostCustomizationHarness.ts#L146-L149

issues.title: Agent Host user MCP servers are grouped as Built-In in Customizations

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Description

In the **Copilot CLI / Agent Host harness**, MCP servers discovered from the user's `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` are running and available to Copilot CLI, but **Chat: Open Customizations > MCP Servers > User** is empty.

The servers are instead classified as **Built-In** by the customization UI.

This is not related to `chat.mcp.discovery.enabled`. That setting controls VS Code's **Local harness** discovery. In this case, Copilot CLI discovers its own user configuration and Agent Host reflects the SDK-reported MCP inventory.

## Reproduction

1. Add MCP servers to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, for example:

   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "perplexity": {
         "type": "http",
         "url": "https://api.perplexity.ai/mcp"
       },
       "slack-github": {
         "type": "http",
         "url": "https://mcp.slack.com/mcp"
       }
     }
   }
   ```

2. Start or select the Copilot CLI Agent Host harness.
3. Confirm that Copilot CLI reports the servers as connected by sending a message.
4. Open **Chat: Open Customizations**.
5. Select **MCP Servers > User**.

## Actual behavior

The User group is empty. SDK/runtime-discovered servers are represented as `session-server-item` entries and grouped under Built-In.

## Expected behavior

MCP servers originating from the Copilot CLI user configuration should appear under **User**. Genuine provider-built-in MCP servers should remain under **Built-In**.

## Root cause

Agent Host's `McpCustomizationController` publishes globally configured SDK servers as bare top-level `McpServerCustomization` entries. These entries carry a synthetic `mcp-top-level:...` URI, name, state, channel, and enablement, but no source classification or original configuration URI.

The workbench receives these as `session-server-item` entries. The grouping introduced in #337399 (`b2ecc9b331104f38e3594217c5fe59a78293fc7e`) classifies:

- local installed servers by User/Workspace scope;
- plugin and extension entries by their known source;
- every remaining entry, including every `session-server-item`, as Built-In.

Before #337399, runtime and session entries appeared together in the flat **Installed** section, masking the missing provenance. Splitting Installed into source groups exposed the regression as an empty User group.

Relevant code:

- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.ts` (`_buildTopLevel`)
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostCustomizationService.ts` (`getMcpServers`)
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/mcpListWidget.ts` (`getMcpEntryGroup`)

## Suggested direction

Preserve a bounded source classification for top-level Agent Host MCP customizations and carry it through `IAgentHostMcpServer` into `getMcpEntryGroup`.

A UI-only rule that classifies every session server as User would be incorrect because genuine provider-built-in servers also use top-level session entries.

## Regression

Confirmed after #337399 / commit `b2ecc9b331104f38e3594217c5fe59a78293fc7e` (September 24, 2026).

issues.title: Close the promo hover when Try is clicked
issues.body:
Follow-up to #331588.

### Problem
When a user clicks the Copilot status entry, the closed-chat promo tooltip is pinned. Clicking **Try <model>** in that tooltip leaves the hover open, and it switches to the Copilot usage dashboard.

Here's why: the Try command opens Chat synchronously. This withdraws the offer, so `ChatStatusBarEntry` swaps the tooltip back to the dashboard. The status bar item then calls `hover.update(...)`, and the pinned managed hover re-renders in place with the new content, keeping its focus, before the hover action gets a chance to dispose it.

### Fix
In `ChatStatusPromo`, the `_chat.tryPromoModel` command now calls `hoverService.hideHover(true)` before it opens Chat.

### Testing
- New regression test in `chatStatusPromo.test.ts`: "Try closes the pinned offer instead of swapping in the dashboard". It drives a real `StatusbarEntryItem` and `HoverService`: it pins the offer, clicks Try, and asserts that no hover remains.
  - It fails without the fix (the hover shows `Dashboard`) and passes with it. All 37 tests in the file pass.
- `npm run typecheck-client` is clean.
- I checked it manually in Code OSS with a GPT-5.5 sale fixture. After clicking Try, no hover is left and Chat opens.

### Proof
Both clips use Code OSS with a GPT-5.5 sale fixture and the `copilotIconPopup` treatment, with Chat collapsed. The mouse moves to the status bar pip, clicks it to pin the offer, then clicks **Try GPT-5.5**.

**Before** (`a6e06b5`, main): Chat opens, but the pinned hover stays open and switches to the Copilot dashboard.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fb0abd4-b2f2-4da2-8194-8ff004f53d54

**After** (`1c1477e`, this PR): the hover closes and Chat opens with the input focused.

issues.title: mcp: add manual Copilot Global setup
issues.body:
## Summary

- Add a persistent Copilot Global destination for manual Command/stdio and HTTP server setup.
- Resolve the configuration on the window's agent-host machine and preserve existing Copilot CLI entries when adding a server.
- Keep VS Code Global and existing destinations available; package-assisted setup remains unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Manual Add Server previously wrote to VS Code configuration or added a server through the current agent-host session. Persistent Copilot configuration is a separate destination, consumed natively by the Copilot runtime.

### Implementation

After a manual server's type, details, ID, and Global target are selected, a second picker offers Copilot Global or VS Code Global. Copilot Global resolves `COPILOT_HOME/mcp-config.json`, falling back to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, using `INativeMcpDiscoveryHelperService.load()` through the existing remote or main-process channel. Lookup respects agent-host enablement, times out after five seconds, and logs failures before falling back to VS Code configuration. Browser windows without a remote host do not offer this destination.

Copilot file conversion is shared with SDK forwarding. The scanner validates new entries, edits only the named entry, preserves unknown neighboring CLI entries and document properties, and rejects malformed documents. A canonical-resource queue serializes same-service edits; a content reread plus etag/mtime checks protect existing files, and creation uses overwrite:false. Reads and removals of missing files do not create them.

### Behavior and constraints

- Installation policy is checked before the Copilot write. Unsupported properties and interactive input references fail explicitly.
- Successful additions open the configuration and explain that referenced environment variables must be set on the agent-host machine before a new Copilot session starts.
- Explicit file targets, cancellation, VS Code user configuration, Remote/workspace targets, and current agent-session additions retain their existing behavior. Current agent-session additions remain host-wide, not session-exclusive.
- No package-assisted generation changes, generation schemas, gallery/manifest/URL-handler expansion, configuration migration, or new settings are included.

### Review context

Based on main, including merged #337775. The locator reuses that PR's shell-aligned COPILOT_HOME discovery rather than resolving environment variables independently. Its provider/authority-specific no-forwarding behavior is unchanged.

Related to open #337781 at `227a48acaf37570191b124fb3a5ee69d8a221b8d`, but does not depend on or include its implementation. Production hunks compose cleanly with that head. The overlapping entry-point test file requires combining imports and preserving both quick-input recorders (`prompts` and `questionOrder`); no production conflict was found. ## Summary

Reject refreshed sandbox relay credentials when their `client_id` differs from the logical client that requested the refresh.

Previously, a refresh for `client-1` could accept credentials for `client-2`, while the protocol connection still used `client-1`. The mismatch now fails explicitly before the credential refresher replaces the existing credentials. Matching responses, initial connections, scoped request parameters, and waking responses remain unchanged.

This PR contains only the client-identity guard and its regression tests. It does not change recovery timing, host-key handling, account lifetimes, or retry policy.

## Validation

- Confirmed the mismatched-client regression failed before the production fix.
- Focused TypeScript check passed.
- All 49 sandbox API unit tests passed, including five new connection-credential tests.
- Targeted ESLint, whitespace checks, and pre-commit hygiene passed.

issues.title: sessions: keep new-session controls opaque over dark chat backgrounds
issues.body:
Fixes #337721

With a chat background configured, the new-session composer's bottom-row controls, including the combined Mode + Permissions picker, were transparent in the default dark themes, so the background showed through them. Light themes were unaffected.

### Root cause

`chatView.css` repeated the `chatWidget.css` surface rule for `.new-chat-bottom-container .action-label` with higher specificity (it adds `.chat-view`), so it always won. Its base color is `var(--vscode-chat-list-background, var(--vscode-button-secondaryBackground))`:

- The new-session view has no chat list, so `--vscode-chat-list-background` is never set there and the fallback always applies.
- `button.secondaryBackground` is transparent (`#00000000`) in 2026 Dark and Dark Modern and opaque in the light themes, hence dark-only.

The in-session toolbar isn't affected because `ChatWidget` sets `--vscode-chat-list-background`.

### Fix

Remove the duplicate new-session selectors (resting, hover, and open) from `chatView.css`, so the existing `chatWidget.css` rule, which falls back to the opaque `--session-view-background`, applies. A short comment explains why they shouldn't come back. The in-session rules are unchanged.

The issue calls out the combined picker, but every bottom-row control used this rule; the Worktree | Branch group only looked right because its action bar paints its own surface. The other session controls and status actions are now opaque in dark themes too.

### Testing

- `keeps background-image composer controls on complete opaque surfaces` (`chatView.test.ts`) never exercised the winning rule because its new-session DOM was missing `.chat-view`. It now uses the real ancestry, a transparent `button.secondaryBackground` like the dark themes, and a combined picker. It fails on `main` with `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` and passes with this change.
- The chat view, new-chat widget, and agent host picker suites pass; `typecheck-client`, eslint, and stylelint are clean.

### Screenshots

The real `AgentHostModePicker` in the new-session bottom row, rendered in the Component Explorer over a gradient standing in for the chat background. Captions come from the picker's computed styles. The Light Modern crops are byte-identical before and after.

![Before and after: the combined picker is transparent over the chat background in 2026 Dark and Dark Modern before the fix, and opaque after it; Light Modern is unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16b41e67-bfde-44d6-a4c0-da3cbc97efad)

### Notes for reviewers

- This PR updates the `NewSessionChatBackground/Dark` blocks-ci baseline. The only pixels that change are inside its bottom-row status controls, which now hide the part of a faint wallpaper icon that used to show through the Status control (70 pixels, max delta 9/255). That fixture's expected description already says these controls have opaque surfaces.
- The `chat/scrollAnchoring` entries in the bot's screenshot diff report are unrelated. They're workbench chat fixtures, which none of the removed selectors can match, and the two Light entries just trade hashes with each other, which points to timing-dependent rendering (they run with virtual time disabled) rather than a real change.

issues.title: agentHost: attribute model responses to client window
issues.body:
## What

Copilot SDK model-response telemetry can now be segmented directly by the VS Code window that initiated the owning turn.

`agentHost.turnCompleted` already carries `initiatorClientType` at the turn level. Before this change, analyzing individual `copilotSdk/response.success` or `copilotSdk/response.error` rows required joining through their host-remapped turn, and incomplete or uncorrelated responses could not always participate. These response events now include `initiatorClientType` with `agents_window`, `editor_window`, or `unknown`. The `agentHost.modelCallTurnCorrelated` join event carries the same field.

## How

- Capture the initiating client type from exact root and subagent turn context.
- Carry it alongside the model-call-to-turn correlation so delayed responses remain attributed to their original window even after the active turn changes.
- Retain a bounded turn-to-client mapping for correlations recorded after turn completion.
- Leave SDK cancellation, todo-state, and generic tool events unchanged because they do not have equivalent exact host-turn attribution.

issues.title: terminal: dispose auto responders when a persistent process is reattached

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

labels.name: terminal
labels.description: General terminal issues that don't fall under another label

issues.body:
## What

`AutoRepliesPtyServiceContribution.handleProcessReady` now disposes any existing `TerminalAutoResponder`s for a persistent process id before installing fresh ones.

## Why

`handleProcessReady` runs again for the same persistent process id whenever the workbench reattaches to it (e.g. on window reload): `attachToProcess` → `start()` takes the already-started path in `PersistentTerminalProcess`, which calls `triggerReplay()` → `onPersistentProcessReady` → `handleProcessReady`. The old responder map was replaced without disposing its entries, so each responder kept its `onProcessData` listener on the long-lived child process. After N reloads with one configured auto reply, a terminal held N+1 responders and a matched prompt was answered N+1 times (the throttle is per responder).

Disposal is done in place rather than via `handleProcessDispose`, so `_terminalProcesses` is never briefly missing the process. On first start there is no existing map, so behaviour is unchanged.

## Validation

- New unit test `AutoRepliesPtyServiceContribution` in `src/vs/platform/terminal/test/node/autoRepliesContribController.test.ts`: calls `handleProcessReady` twice and asserts one reply. Fails without the fix (`['reply', 'reply']`), passes with it.
- UI scenario against a Code OSS dev build on Windows (PowerShell, persistent sessions): an interactive program prints a prompt matched by `terminal.integrated.autoReplies` and echoes every line it receives.

| Step | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| New terminal: prompt answered once | ✅ | ✅ |
| Reload window, terminal reattached | ✅ | ✅ |
| After 1 reload: prompt answered once | ❌ answered twice | ✅ |
| After 2nd reload: prompt answered once | – | ✅ |
| Change the reply setting: reattached terminal uses the new reply once | – | ✅ |
| New terminal after reloads: prompt answered once | – | ✅ |

**Before fix** (fails at step 4 with 3 replies for 2 prompts):

**After fix** (all 7 steps pass):

issues.title: agentHost: keep Codex permission tests out of /tmp
issues.body:
## What changed

- Create Codex permission-boundary fixtures under the CI runner's private temp root instead of relying on `os.tmpdir()`.
- Keep the fixture-local `TMPDIR` used to verify Codex's private temporary-directory access.
- Make Azure DevOps validation a non-negotiable requirement for every new Agent Host E2E or real-provider integration test.

## Why

[Azure build 476995](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=476995&view=logs&j=e352877c-ff47-5dec-32e2-b206099d9704&t=b83513b4-f303-5ddc-d18a-1b47c02d8dad) failed six macOS Codex permission integration tests because that worker resolved `os.tmpdir()` to `/tmp`. Codex intentionally grants macOS processes access to system scratch roots, so the test's supposedly external fixtures were actually allowed.

The same test passed in PR CI because the GitHub runner provided a private temp directory. The initial fix placed fixtures under `.build`, but GitHub's macOS Electron job then exposed a second invalid assumption: Codex discovered repository-level `AGENTS.md` instructions outside the test workspace and correctly denied access while materializing the session. Preferring `AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY` on Azure and `RUNNER_TEMP` on GitHub keeps fixtures outside both system scratch roots and the source tree.

## Validation

- Reproduced the original six failures with `TMPDIR=/tmp`.
- Reproduced and diagnosed the GitHub macOS `CodexMaterializeFailed` failure from the completed job log.
- Azure-like environment (`TMPDIR=/tmp` plus private `AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY`): 9 passing.
- Focused [Azure DevOps build 477038](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477038): succeeded, including Electron integration tests on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- Earlier forced-temp verification of the sandbox-boundary fix: 36/36 cases passing.
- `npm run compile-client`
- Targeted ESLint
- Pre-commit hygiene
- `git diff --check`

(Written by Copilot)

issues.title: agentHost: handle relay publish acknowledgement failures
issues.body:
## Summary

Relay publish acknowledgements were requested but ignored. A rejected or unacknowledged publish could leave a request pending even while unrelated traffic kept the connection looking healthy.

- Track acknowledgement IDs for every published chunk. Accept successful and `Duplicate` acknowledgements; fail through the existing handshake or transport-close path on rejection.
- Give each publish a 30-second acknowledgement deadline, sharing the existing handshake timeout constant. Use one scheduler per transport, preserve older deadlines when newer traffic arrives, and clear tracking and timers on settlement or close.
- Preserve chunk ordering and do not automatically resend publishes. Relay acceptance is not a guarantee that the host executed the request.

Follow-up to #337778.

## Validation

- Targeted TypeScript check passed.
- All 58 focused relay transport, framing, and chunking unit tests passed.
- Targeted ESLint and whitespace checks passed.

Regression coverage includes rejected and missing acknowledgements, out-of-order and `Duplicate` acknowledgements, chunked publishes, exact timeout boundaries, handshake transitions, failed socket writes, and timer cleanup.

Focused unit-test command (after compiling the test output):

```sh
npm run test-node -- \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/browser/webPubSubRelayTransport.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/webPubSub/framing.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/webPubSub/chunking.test.ts
```

Live relay and end-to-end testing have not been run and remain pending manual validation. This PR does not claim measured production reliability or performance improvements.

issues.title: Test: Enterprise managed settings and Local OTel
issues.body:
# Test: Enterprise managed settings and Local OTel

Refs: [#336814](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/336814), [#336968](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/336968), [#337151](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337151), [#337177](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337177), [#337486](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337486), [#337583](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337583)

- [ ] anyOS @jruales 

Complexity: 3

Authors: @rwoll

---

Basic smoke coverage for one tester, approximately 30-45 minutes including setup. Based on [last week's TPI](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/336872). OTel testing is **Local only**; Agent Host OTel remains a [separate follow-up](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337413).

## Setup

1. Use 1.140 Insiders containing the PRs above, a disposable workspace, and a test profile signed into Copilot. Close unrelated VS Code windows. Use a device without conflicting machine policy; do not change production policy.
2. Enable `"chat.editor.localAgent.enabled": true`. Remove personal OTel overrides and launch without inherited `COPILOT_OTEL_*` / `OTEL_*` variables.
3. Run `npm run mock-policy-server` from a current VS Code checkout. Follow its [proxy setup](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/scripts/mock-policy-server/README.md). Leave endpoints other than **Managed Settings** on passthrough initially.
4. Start the collector below. Set the Managed Settings response to HTTP 200 with this body:

   ```json
   {
     "autoTier": "intelligence",
     "telemetry": {
       "enabled": true,
       "endpoint": "http://localhost:4318",
       "protocol": "http/json",
       "captureContent": false,
       "capture": { "identity": true }
     }
   }
   ```

5. Run **Developer: Sync Account Policy**, confirm a client request in the mock server's **Live Requests**, then reload VS Code. Sync after each subsequent mock change.

## Test

### 1. Local identity capture

- [ ] Select **Local**, start a conversation, and send a unique harmless prompt. Verify the response succeeds and the collector receives `copilot-chat` telemetry: `user.name` on `invoke_agent` spans, and `process.user.name` / `host.name` on resources. The prompt content should not be exported because `captureContent` is false.
- [ ] Change `capture.identity` to `false`, sync, reload, and send another prompt. Telemetry still arrives, but the three identity keys are absent from the **new** records. Keep collector output private.

### 2. Managed Auto default

- [ ] In a fresh Local conversation without an explicit/saved tier preference, select **Auto** and confirm **Intelligence** is the default. Select another tier and verify it remains editable.
- [ ] Run **Developer: Restart Local Agent Host** and repeat in a fresh same-machine Copilot Agent Host conversation using the same account. Send a harmless prompt successfully. If cached policy prevents the default appearing, follow the mock server's cache troubleshooting instructions.

### 3. Policy survives a failed refresh

- [ ] Change Managed Settings to **Server error (500)** and sync. Confirm the failed request in Live Requests. Previously applied policy remains, Local telemetry continues, and no spurious OTel reload notification appears.
- [ ] Restore the successful HTTP 200 policy and sync. Normal operation continues.

This is a quick retention/recovery check, not the hour-old-cache regression test.

### 4. Minimum-version notice

- [ ] Select **Client update required (466)**. Set `client_version` to your tested version and `minimum_client_version` to a higher version (for example `1.141.0`), then sync.
- [ ] Editor Chat explains that an update is required; closing Chat leaves the update banner visible. The Agents window shows one blocking overlay without a duplicate banner. **Open Editor Window** opens a fresh editor window.
- [ ] Return Managed Settings to HTTP 200 `{}` and sync in both windows. The restriction clears.

### 5. Agents disabled by account policy

- [ ] Temporarily mock the **Token** endpoint with `{"token":"agent_mode=0;editor_preview_features=0;mcp=0"}` and sync. The normal Agents entry point and Welcome invitation disappear.
- [ ] Launch the same test profile directly with `code-insiders --agents` (include its `--user-data-dir`). Verify **Agents Disabled** rather than a usable Agents window. Do not send model requests with this synthetic token.
- [ ] Restore Token passthrough and sync. Normal permitted behavior returns.

## Cleanup

Restore the original proxy/settings/mock configuration, sync, and reload. Stop the collector and test server; remove private trace output and disposable test data. Report the build/OS and any failed or blocked checks; do not attach raw identity data or tokens.

## Collector

Use a trusted local OTLP/HTTP JSON collector, or run the official Collector with Docker. Unlike last week's byte-count-only script, this displays the attributes needed for the identity check.

Save as `otel-tpi.yaml` in a disposable directory:

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318
exporters:
  debug:
    verbosity: detailed
service:
  pipelines:
    traces: { receivers: [otlp], exporters: [debug] }
    metrics: { receivers: [otlp], exporters: [debug] }
    logs: { receivers: [otlp], exporters: [debug] }
```

Run outside VS Code:

```sh
docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:4318:4318 --mount "type=bind,source=$PWD/otel-tpi.yaml,target=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml,readonly" otel/opentelemetry-collector:latest
```

For PowerShell, replace `$PWD/otel-tpi.yaml` with `$($PWD.Path)/otel-tpi.yaml`. Keep output local and stop with Ctrl+C.

issues.title: Track customization marketplace installation records
issues.body:
## Summary

Follow up to #337110 by separating marketplace installation provenance from local-item discovery.

- Persist machine-local profile installation records after successful marketplace installs. Each record keeps the source/identifier/version identity, validated installation descriptor, and exact installed URI or MCP server ID.
- Derive `checking`, `installed`, and `missing` state by reconciling records with the owning skill, plugin, or MCP implementation. Same-name and same-repository local items no longer imply marketplace installation or hide an available entry.
- Add **Repair** for missing recorded installations. Skill repair restores only recorded files that are missing, preserving edited and additional files.
- Route skill uninstall through the existing confirmed deletion/Trash flow. Cancelling keeps both the target and its record; already-absent targets can drop their record cleanly.
- Keep exact association and repair state available to keyboard and screen-reader users, including Accessibility Help and Accessible View.

## Model

This follows the extension installation model: durable profile metadata owns marketplace identity/version/location while reconciliation observes the local installation. Customization records use the same record-versus-local separation. One deliberate difference is that customization resource identity still includes version because this marketplace does not yet expose an update flow.


## Production hardening review

A line-by-line architecture, correctness, lifecycle, accessibility, and test review found and resolved 12 initial issues before this draft is ready for review. Five additional inline review findings were also fixed and resolved:

- Split persistence/validation and complete skill package operations into focused internal modules; the public install service now owns orchestration and reconciliation.
- Store each deterministic SHA-256 installation slot independently, avoiding cross-window lost updates and bounding record count, individual/aggregate bytes, fields, and skill manifests.
- Persist immutable skill and plugin Git revisions. Repair uses the existing commit-aware source adapter and rechecks revisions before restoring content.
- Reconcile only relevant owner records and affected skill files; unrelated plugin/MCP events no longer rescan every skill manifest.
- Distinguish missing files from verification errors, keep uninstall available, and make Repair eligibility respect source enablement, AI disablement, and plugin policy.
- Preserve destination-group identity, rebase exact targets when provider URIs move, and expose recorded resources even when a catalog entry disappears.
- Fix stale target notifications, plugin uninstall races, incomplete-repair success, accessible state announcements, picker documentation, and the prior formatter CI failure.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- full repository hygiene
- changed-file ESLint
- Discover CSS Stylelint
- 131 focused marketplace installation and Discover tests
- Dev-build UI scenario on macOS arm64 covering public-feed search, exact install, same-name separation, missing-file detection, non-destructive repair, and confirmed uninstall

## Video evidence

Captioned Dev-build scenario (VS Code 1.140.0, macOS arm64): 5/5 steps passed.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ad1837e-d415-4d7e-890b-c6932c5ee92a

The recording demonstrates public-feed search, independent same-name entries, exact install association, missing-file detection through VS Code’s Explorer deletion path, immutable repair preserving an extra local file, and confirmed uninstall.

## Follow-ups addressed

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337110#discussion_r4089215563
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337110#discussion_r4089215561

issues.title: Chat: onboarding spotlight tour for the chat input
issues.body:
Adds an onboarding spotlight tour to the Chat view. It reuses the onboarding engine and spotlight primitives that power the Agents window tours (`workbench/contrib/onboarding`).

## Behavior
When `chat.onboarding.experience` is `spotlight`, a user who has never sent an editor chat message sees a two-step tour the first time the Chat view opens:
1. **Mode picker.** Explains Agent, Ask, and Plan, and when to switch between them.
2. **Model picker.** Explains that you can change models at any time.

The tour only highlights the pickers and never opens them. It runs at most once per user. It is hidden when AI features are disabled (`ChatContextKeys.enabled`) and while a modal editor is open.

## Implementation
- `chat/browser/onboarding/chatInputTour.contribution.ts`:
  - Registers the scenario and target providers.
  - Registers `ChatInputTourTrigger`, which waits for a visible Chat view whose pickers have rendered before it triggers.
  - Registers the `chat.onboarding.experience` setting (`none` | `spotlight`, default `none`). The setting uses `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }` so an ExP treatment can drive it later.
- `ChatInputPart` exposes `modePickerElement` and `modelPickerElement`. Target providers use these getters, so the tour does not query the DOM.
- `EditorChatUsage.getMessageCount()` reuses the existing cross-profile editor chat message counter (`chat.editorUsage.messages`) as the "has never chatted" signal.
- `onboarding.developerMode["chat.onboarding.chatInput"]` bypasses the message-count gate for previews.

### Caveat on the "never chatted" signal
`chat.editorUsage.messages` has only been recorded since #336792 (about Sept 18). Users who chatted before then look new until they send their next message. Other options are worth considering before an ExP rollout.

### ExP follow-up
The ExP wiring is not done yet. The setting can already be targeted by a `config.chat.onboarding.experience` treatment. For clean scorecards, a follow-up could add an `IOnboardingExperiment` (with an `onb-` assignment-context id) to the scenario so exposure is gated at the onboarding moment.

## Validation
- Unit tests: `chatInputTour.test.ts` (6 tests) and the existing `editorChatUsage.test.ts` pass.
- `typecheck-client`, eslint, and `valid-layers-check` pass.
- Proof in the real Code OSS Electron window under Xvfb in a Codespace, 1600x1000 H.264 video:
  - `spotlight`: step 1 highlights the mode picker, and step 2 highlights the model picker. Neither picker opens. Telemetry recorded one `onboarding.scenarioShown` and one `onboarding.scenarioOutcome` (`completed`, `lastStepIndex=1`, `stepCount=2`). The tour did not repeat after a window reload.
  - `none`: no tour is shown, and no chat tour telemetry is emitted.
  - Not run: the "messages already sent" state needs a signed-in account to reach honestly. Unit tests cover it.

issues.title: Run hooks from SDK-installed plugins
issues.body:
## Summary

- forward hooks from SDK/runtime-installed plugins through the Copilot SDK callback bridge
- keep agents, skills, instructions, and MCP servers runtime-owned to avoid duplicate registration
- extend the runtime-native plugin integration test with a `SessionStart` hook and assert exactly one invocation

## Root cause

VS Code 1.138's Copilot runtime executed hooks from runtime-installed plugins natively. Starting with the SDK-owned runtime in 1.139, the plugin and its hook are still discovered, but the native hook is not invoked.

Agent Host already projects hooks explicitly for client- and host-supplied plugins. Runtime-native plugin containers were intentionally omitted from that projection because the runtime loads their other contributions itself. This change projects only their parsed hook commands.

The stricter `allowManagedHooksOnly` runtime case is tracked separately in [github/copilot-sdk#2769](https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/issues/2769), because the runtime must preserve managed provenance there.

## Validation

issues.title: chat: Gate Discover separately and default the GitHub Feed on
issues.body:
## Summary

Provide the small shared base for the MCP Gallery, Plugin marketplace, and Copilot Connectors PRs.

- Add default-off `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled` to control whether Agent Customizations shows Discover instead of the original Overview. Toggling it replaces the visible home surface and cancels stale discovery; Marketplace installation is unavailable while it is off.
- Default `chat.customizations.marketplace.sources.publicFeed.enabled` **on**, independently of Marketplace visibility. The GitHub Feed can still be disabled. With Marketplace visibility off, this change preserves Overview and existing management-page catalogs rather than starting Discover requests.
- Hard-gate the GitHub Feed itself on **both** switches: when Marketplace or the Feed is disabled, no public-feed query or installation can start, and toggling either cancels in-flight work. Other feeds with existing management-page catalogs can still serve those legacy pages while Marketplace is hidden.
- Provide an internal adapter-assigned priority for Marketplace entries. Browse shows higher-priority custom entries first and interleaves equal-priority entries round-robin across pages; search keeps global relevance order and uses priority (then round-robin) to break equal scores. Priority never appears as a quality or trust rating.

## Verification

- 141 focused source-gating, ranking, and installation tests passed, including Marketplace-off cancellation and rejection of direct GitHub Feed queries even when its own setting is on.
- Client typecheck, changed-file ESLint/formatter, layer check, and diff check passed.
- Overview with the enabled GitHub Feed but Marketplace visibility off, Overview with no source, and Discover with another source only all rendered in dark and light component fixtures without errors.

## Manual test

1. With neither setting explicitly configured, open Agent Customizations: Overview and the existing MCP/Plugin Available sections remain; no Discover catalog is queried.
2. Enable `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled`: Discover appears and the default-enabled GitHub Feed can be browsed without signing in.
3. Disable the GitHub Feed: Discover returns to Overview when no other feed is enabled. Re-enable it and verify the catalog loads afresh.
4. Turn Marketplace visibility off during a GitHub Feed query or skill import and verify cancellation, no new feed calls (including direct catalog IPC), and the original Overview. Legacy MCP/Plugin management catalogs remain usable.
5. With independently enabled test feeds, verify higher-priority custom entries precede default entries in browsing and equal-priority feeds round-robin across page boundaries; search still orders by relevance before priority.

issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not recorded
- VS Code Version: Regression introduced by #330896; fixed on main by #337583 and backported to release/1.139 by #337739
- OS Version: Not recorded
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Enterprise managed settings / Copilot OpenTelemetry configuration
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): N/A
- Logs: Not attached; diagnosis and validation are documented in #337583.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Sign in with an enterprise account that supplies server-managed settings, such as an OpenTelemetry endpoint, and allow a successful settings fetch.
2. Allow the cached response to become older than one hour, then encounter a failed refresh (no response, transient 401/403, 429, 5xx, or malformed response).
3. Observe that the previously applied policy is dropped. A subsequent successful fetch restores it.

**Actual behavior:** Managed settings alternate between the enterprise policy and defaults during refresh failures. For an OTel endpoint, affected users see recurring notifications such as "Copilot OTel endpoint will change to http://localhost:4318 after reload.", especially after idle. Other server-managed restrictions are also temporarily lifted.

**Expected behavior:** A failed refresh is not evidence that policy was withdrawn. Keep the last successful settings, even when stale, without renewing their original fetch timestamp so subsequent polls or focus events retry. Successful responses, explicit withdrawal, sign-out/account changes, and forced-refresh behavior retain their existing semantics.

**Fix and release tracking**

- Main fix: #337583 (merged).
- Cherry-pick: #337739 (merged into `release/1.139`).

This issue tracks the stale-policy retention regression addressed by those PRs. The separate session-lookup-error and `managedSettingsActive` lifecycle problems described in #337583 are outside this issue's scope.

issues.title: sessions: list each pull request once in the multi-folder session hover
issues.body:
In a multi-folder session, the session hover showed the same pull requests twice. The top section lists the main chat's pull requests. The "Session summary" section then listed every pull request of every folder and chat, including the main chat's again.

## Change
`getSessionSummaryHoverData` (`sessionHoverContent.ts`) now leaves out of the Session summary any pull request already listed in the top section. It compares by PR URI, the key the existing pull request collection already uses. When nothing is left, the summary sends no pull request list, so the widget renders no empty block.

These are unchanged: the summary's workspaces and changes rows, single-folder sessions, and the peer chat hover (`getChatSummaryHoverData`). The helpers are split into `getPullRequestRefs` (collect, keyed by URI) and `toHoverPullRequests` (map to hover items) so both sections share one identity.

## Tests
New suite "session hover pull requests" in `sessionsList.test.ts`:
- **Overlapping PRs:** the main folder has #1 and #2, a peer folder has #2 and #3. The summary shows only #3.
- **All PRs in the main folder:** the summary has no pull request list.
- **Single-folder session:** unchanged.

I also updated the existing rendered test "shows the rich chat-scoped hover for peer chats": its Session summary now lists only the peer's pull request. Without the fix, the two multi-folder tests and the rendered test fail.

The `sessionHover` component fixture uses only single-folder sessions, so its screenshots are unaffected.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck-client`: clean.
- `vs/sessions/**` unit tests: 4514 passing.
- `vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/**` unit tests: 1735 passing.
- eslint and hygiene: clean on both changed files.

issues.title: test: cover managed sandbox enforcement in Agent Host smoke tests
issues.body:
## Summary

Add macOS/Linux/Windows Agent Host regression smoke tests for managed sandbox enforcement.

- Enforce `sandbox.enabled: true` and `sandbox.allowBypass: false` through the real device managed-settings file.
- Start separate fresh processes with local sandboxing off and on; leave local `allowUnsandboxedCommands: true` in both cases.
- Require the SDK shell to complete without a policy conflict, reject a controlled out-of-sandbox write, and leave the disposable probe file unchanged. A locked UI toggle or configuration log is not sufficient, and no bypass confirmation is accepted.
- Windows uses `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows`, the Windows filesystem configuration, and the SDK PowerShell tool. macOS/Linux use Bash.

Related: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9646

## Stack / draft gate

**Stacked on #337795**, which provides the shared managed-policy fixture, Agent Host harness hooks, existing policy-test opt-in, and desktop CI provisioning/cleanup. This PR's diff contains only sandbox coverage and registration/documentation.

Keep draft until the sandbox startup fix lands and the full smoke cases pass 10 times per platform, with acceptable duration. No production fix, local enablement workaround, or expected-failure skip is included.

## Validation

- Smoke/automation TypeScript compile and targeted ESLint: passed, including Windows coverage.
- Shared managed-file fixture safety checks in a disposable Linux container: passed in the base PR.

Add desktop smoke coverage for real Agent Host managed OTel export, using the existing `VSCODE_SMOKE_TEST_POLICY=1` opt-in from #335107.

issues.title: Support trusted “Try This” experiences in release notes and documentation

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Release notes and documentation can explain a feature, but users still have to leave the content, find the relevant UI, and reconstruct the example themselves. This makes newly announced or unfamiliar functionality harder to discover and evaluate.

VS Code should support trusted **Try This** links that connect release notes and documentation to locally registered product experiences. Depending on the feature, an example could:

- open an existing view or command;
- prepare an isolated, read-only sample;
- open the relevant UI and guide the user through its controls;
- explain missing prerequisites and offer an explicit setup action; or
- hand off to the correct VS Code window, including the Agents window.

The fetched Markdown should contain only a stable tryout identifier. Installed VS Code code should own all titles, descriptions, commands, arguments, samples, availability checks, and guided steps. Unknown, malformed, unavailable, or stale identifiers should remain inert.

The experience should preserve normal product safeguards and accessibility. It must not automatically trust a workspace, enable settings, install extensions, accept confirmations, select a model or provider, submit Chat input, or modify user resources. External documentation links should require confirmation before launching an installed example.

Reference implementation: #337713

issues.title: Customizations view does not identify signed-out MCP server
issues.body:
## Type of Issue

Bug

## Description

When an MCP server is signed out, the Customizations view shows a large generic **Sign In** button without identifying which server requires authentication. This makes it unclear what account or server the action applies to, especially when multiple MCP servers are configured.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the Slack MCP server.
2. Sign out of the Slack MCP server (or let its authentication expire).
3. Open the Customizations view.
4. Observe the authentication prompt.

## Actual Behavior

The view shows a prominent **Sign In** button, but does not identify Slack or otherwise indicate which MCP server is signed out.

## Expected Behavior

The authentication prompt should name the affected MCP server (for example, **Sign in to Slack**) or otherwise clearly associate the action with that server.

issues.title: agentHost: resolve native OTLP trace endpoints
issues.body:
## Summary

Addresses the trace-routing portion of #337413.

Agent Host copied a bare collector URL such as `http://localhost:4318` into the native trace-specific endpoint. Unlike a base OTLP endpoint, that value is used verbatim, so Copilot's native runtime posted traces to `/` instead of `/v1/traces`.

- Reuse `resolveOtlpTracesEndpoint` when constructing native HTTP trace configuration.
- Preserve explicit/custom paths, query parameters, gRPC endpoints, headers, and the external/base destination used by other signals.
