issues.title: mcp: unify destinations and validate workspace install targets
issues.body:
## Summary

**MCP: Add Server** now shows the eligible agent-host session, Global, Remote, and workspace destinations in one picker, instead of asking users to choose between an agent session and a local installation first.

The picker uses the focused agent-host session, or the sole distinct open agent-host session when none is focused. Multiple widgets for the same session count as one; ambiguous sessions are not guessed.

This also fixes a misleading **Workspace** destination in the Agents window. That entry pointed to the window's internal settings workspace, not the user's project. Project folders are now shown as **Workspace (folder-name)**, while normal editor workspaces retain their workspace-level destination.

## Before and after

Workspace-related choices are shown below, assuming `chat.mcp.workspaceRootConfig.enabled` is enabled. Global, Remote, and eligible agent-session destinations remain available.

| Context | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Agents window, no project folders | **Workspace**, pointing to internal window configuration | No workspace destination |
| Agents window, one project folder | **Workspace** + bare folder name | **Workspace (folder-name)** only |
| Agents window, multiple project folders | **Workspace** + each bare folder name | **Workspace (folder-name)** for each folder |
| Editor, single folder opened directly | **Workspace**, representing that folder | Unchanged |
| Editor, workspace containing one folder | **Workspace** + bare folder name | **Workspace** + **Workspace (folder-name)** |
| Editor, multi-folder workspace | **Workspace** + each bare folder name | **Workspace** + **Workspace (folder-name)** for each folder |
| Editor, empty window | No workspace destination | Unchanged |
| Editor, workspace configuration file does not exist yet | Workspace-level destination available | Still available; eligibility does not depend on file existence |

**Add Server**, **Install in Workspace**, and installation validation share the same destination rules. In the Agents window, Install in Workspace offers only project folders, skips scope selection for a sole folder, and is unavailable when there are no folders. Programmatic attempts to install into the internal workspace configuration are rejected before writing.

Explicit configuration-file destinations still skip scope selection. Question ordering, cancellation, configuration-format gates, and policy checks are preserved. Existing configuration is not migrated or deleted, and the Agents window's internal settings remain writable for their existing uses. Adding through an agent session still updates host-level configuration; it does not create session-exclusive configuration.

## Validation

- Client and built-in extension compilation: passed with zero errors.
- **180 passing tests in Electron and 179 each in Chromium and WebKit** covering destination pickers, session selection, cancellation, explicit targets, installation guards, and changing project folders.
- Client type-check, ESLint, hygiene, and layer checks: passed.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, run **MCP: Add Server** with an agent-host chat and a project folder open. Confirm the destinations appear together and the project is labeled **Workspace (folder-name)**, with no separate internal Workspace entry.
2. Try **Install in Workspace** with zero, one, and multiple project folders, then confirm a normal editor workspace still offers its workspace-level destination.
3. Confirm explicit configuration-file additions skip scope selection, and cancelling a destination/file picker does not install a server.

issues.title: sessions: feat: add Copilot canvas support
issues.body:
## Summary

Adds the smallest Copilot-only canvas vertical slice for saved chats in the Agents window.

- enables released Copilot SDK extensions and canvas rendering during normal trusted create/resume
- projects live model-opened canvases through a minimal chat-owned AHP contract
- projects canvas-extension `session.send()` requests as visible turns in the owning chat
- keeps source URLs private and resolves them only for the exact live chat, instance, and revision
- exposes provider-neutral Sessions canvas state, initially only for the local Copilot Agent Host provider
- automatically presents canvases beside their owning chat in a non-restorable Sessions editor
- embeds pages in unlisted, ephemeral BrowserViews that are excluded from browser discovery and agent audiences
- ships behind the default-off `sessions.experimental.canvases.enabled` preview setting

Canonical protocol counterpart: microsoft/agent-host-protocol#472 at `12e86060451722c699ac2e8d1314be6673ce1b9f`.

microsoft/vscode#335951 and its branch were used only as read-only reference evidence. This branch was built from `origin/main`; no broad commits were cherry-picked.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Trust["Workspace Trust admission"]
    Agent["Copilot Agent"]
    Runtime["Released Copilot runtime + SDK"]
    Extension["Project canvas extension"]
    Tools["Native canvas model tools"]
    Projection["Live chat-owned projection"]
    AHP["AHP canvasesChanged + resolveCanvasSource"]
    Provider["Provider-neutral ISessionCanvas"]
    Service["SessionCanvasService"]
    Editor["SessionCanvasEditor"]
    Browser["Unlisted ephemeral BrowserView"]
    CanvasRequest["Canvas-originated model request"]

    Trust --> Agent
    Agent -->|normal create/resume with extensions| Runtime
    Runtime --> Extension
    Runtime --> Tools
    Tools -->|open_canvas| Extension
    Extension --> Projection
    Projection --> AHP
    AHP --> Provider
    Provider --> Service
    Service --> Editor
    Editor -->|revision-fenced source resolution| Projection
    Editor --> Browser
    Browser -->|user requests agent work| CanvasRequest
    CanvasRequest -->|extension session.send| Runtime
    Runtime -->|correlated root turn| Projection
```

### Runtime lifecycle and trust

Durable Copilot create/resume requests extensions and the canvas renderer directly through the released SDK. `CopilotAgent` launches the packaged extension bootstrap only for canonical project entrypoints beneath a ref-counted live session root; symlink escapes and session-scoped extension launches are rejected. Each admitted extension receives a stable absolute `VSCODE_CANVAS_DATA_DIR`.

Extension readiness is subscribed before querying current extension state, so the first relevant model turn cannot miss the loaded event. The released runtime's native `<canvases>` catalog and `list_canvas_capabilities`, `open_canvas`, and `invoke_canvas_action` tools are used without SDK/runtime source changes.

### Projection and resource limits

`CopilotAgentSession` maps live SDK canvas events into revisioned, metadata-only chat state. URLs remain private in the live Copilot session, are restricted to HTTP(S), omitted from synchronized state/editor identity, and fail-closed redacted from AHP logs.

Identical duplicate opens are ignored. Each chat retains at most eight projected instances, evicting the oldest projection. Resume-restored canvases are ignored until a new user turn, and all projection is lost when runtime residency ends.

When a canvas extension calls the public SDK's `session.send()` without a host-started turn, a correlated root SDK message now creates a provider-started AHP turn first. Its generated prompt, tool calls, approvals, usage, response, errors, cancellation, and completion are visible in the owning chat. Injected or uncorrelated SDK messages remain hidden, and extension-authored prompt text is excluded from human-message telemetry.

### Sessions presentation and rollout

`BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider` maps AHP state into provider-neutral `ISessionCanvas` objects. Canvas capability is advertised only for the local Agent Host provider; remote, Claude, and Codex presentation remain unsupported.

`SessionCanvasService` requires all of:

- `sessions.experimental.canvases.enabled`
- visible AI features
- canvas capability
- an active owning session/chat
- a ready live revision

A new revision automatically opens a non-serializable `SessionCanvasInput` with focus. User dismissal suppresses only that revision. Disabling the setting, removing the canvas, or removing the owning session closes and cleans up presentation state.

### Browser privacy and accessibility

`createExternalBrowserView` creates a user-owned, ephemeral `Unlisted` BrowserView with no agent audience or associated browser resource. Renderer subscriptions are installed before initial navigation, preventing the main/renderer URL race observed in real Code OSS validation. Unlisted views are excluded from browser events, hydration, quick open, and tools, and their `window.open()` popup requests are denied.

`WebContentsViewHost` contains the reusable native overlay, focus, screenshot, keybinding, and layout behavior extracted from the regular browser renderer. Accessibility Help and Accessible View use incremental bounded Chromium AX retrieval: at most 2,000 nodes and 32 KiB of formatted text.

## Released runtime proof

A tokenless executable trace and committed bundled-runtime integration exercised the repository's released `@github/copilot-sdk` `1.0.15-preview.3` and runtime `1.0.89-3`.

Create and cold resume both proved that:

- the project extension was running before the model turn
- the model received all native canvas tools
- `open_canvas` emitted a model-opened canvas with an HTTP source
- `invoke_canvas_action` reached the extension handler
- a request started by the extension appeared as a complete visible AHP chat turn

No runtime or SDK source changes are included.

## Real Code OSS Chess validation

A fresh isolated authenticated Code OSS Dev run with the Chess canvas under `~/Downloads` passed end to end:

- extension bootstrap was running before `sendMessage`
- native capability discovery returned the Chess canvas and its four actions
- the model opened `chess-e2e`
- AHP projected the canvas with status `White to move`
- `Chess — e2e` automatically became the selected editor beside its owning chat, with no click
- the native page rendered the heading, status, controls, move history, and all 64 board cells
- integrated-browser quick open contained only `New Integrated Browser Tab`

![Rendered Chess canvas in the Agents window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6222db7f-00b1-4b13-95f9-f3385ef1b0d0)

OS-composited verification video: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25c73180-42b8-4944-9d37-3df4e2a13bf5

## Validation

- canonical AHP: TypeScript, Go, Rust, Swift, Kotlin, and .NET checks pass
- Copilot Agent and session suites, including the current 712-test `CopilotAgentSession` suite
- Sessions/provider suites: 317 passing, 11 pending
- BrowserView/accessibility suite: 16 passing
- deterministic Copilot prompt replay: 23 passing
- bundled runtime/model integration covering model-opened canvas and extension-started visible turn: 1 passing
- AHP JSONL logger: 13 passing
- AgentHostPty: 33 passing
- AgentSideEffects: 246 passing
- changed-file ESLint, import layers, stylelint, hygiene, and `git diff --check`
- full client typecheck
- post-rebase canvas service/capability regressions: 5 passing

The deterministic prompt fixtures intentionally changed because durable Copilot requests now include the released extension and canvas tool catalog. The E2E harness clears ambient Copilot feature flags so local app experiments cannot change committed prompt baselines.

Broad local Agent Host E2E encountered unrelated machine constraints in Codex `sandbox-exec` and macOS `/var` path normalization, not canvas failures.

## Review commits

1. `78cbc843fec` — extract the reusable native WebContentsView host
2. `9e6a1b89495` — launch/project Copilot canvases, canonical AHP, and provider-started visible turns
3. `7d53fd6c548` — add private unlisted external BrowserViews
4. `fa17bb7df7e` — add Sessions-owned automatic canvas presentation

Follow-up fixes and canvas-originated chat visibility are folded into the feature commits that own their behavior, keeping the review stack at four semantic commits.

## Remaining merge gates

- microsoft/vscode#337780 needs one collaborator approval
- microsoft/agent-host-protocol#472 needs one collaborator approval
- focused owner review is requested across Agent Host, Sessions, BrowserView, accessibility, and security/privacy

All automated checks are green on the rebased signed head across Linux, macOS, Windows, compile/hygiene, CodeQL, screenshots, Copilot tests, and Electron suites. The external `VS Code PR Check` remains the collaborator-approval gate.

## Explicitly deferred

- creating sessions without extensions and attaching resident extensions later
- provider initialization/restart UI
- canvas-first and zero-turn chats
- manual picker or UI-originated open/action calls
- restoration across VS Code/runtime restart
- remote Agent Host, Claude, and Codex support
- built-in Office, browser, or terminal canvas providers

issues.title: chat: allow skipping agent-host MCP startup
issues.body:
## Summary

Add an inline **Skip** action while MCP startup blocks an agent-host turn, and keep passive inventory/enablement reconciliation from starting MCP servers before the turn exists.

- Adopt the corresponding agent-host protocol action and `blocking` startup state, forwarding the idempotent request to the provider.
- Use the Copilot SDK's session-wide backgrounding operation, and only clear blocking state when the SDK reports that loading actually moved to the background.
- Wire the action through workbench and Agents Window providers, with an accessible text link, component fixtures, and regression tests.
- Use `mcp.list({ startServers: false })` for passive inventory and a fresh authoritative pre-turn enablement query. Re-read desired enablement after the query, await required mutations, and fail closed if the inventory query or required disablement fails.

## SDK compatibility

Companion runtime work: github/copilot-agent-runtime#22835 (tracking github/copilot-agent-runtime#22817).

A narrow compatibility cast allows this PR to compile with the currently published SDK, so the SDK bump is no longer a merge prerequisite. The older generated SDK ignores the additional list options and retains its existing materializing behavior; non-starting inventory takes effect after the SDK/runtime update. No dependency pins or local package paths are changed.

## Validation

- Follow-up 331320e7f76: **43 browser/accessibility tests** and **687 Copilot session tests** passed, plus targeted ESLint and full client typecheck against the original published SDK declarations (without changing local links).
- Verified keyboard Skip in the shared Component Explorer: the startup message disappears immediately and focus returns to the chat input. Tests cover newly starting/restarted servers and failure retries.

- Merged current main and resolved the provider import conflict.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed with the linked SDK.
- Fresh transpilation plus the Copilot agent session and local agent-host provider suites: **977 passing, 11 pending**.
- Runtime companion: native build and focused regression tests passed; linked-SDK POC passed all **44 assertions** across uncached, warm-cache, broken, and disabled MCP scenarios.
- Manual Agent Host logs confirm Skip made the server non-blocking within 5 ms and allowed the reply to complete before a deliberately broken sleeping process exited. This does not claim to resolve cold-resume latency or every reconnect path.

## Manual test

1. Configure a slow-starting MCP and start a new agent-host session.
2. Send a message and select **Skip** in the MCP startup progress row.
3. Verify the startup row disappears immediately, stays hidden for those servers, and shows only new server startups. The response should proceed while startup continues.
4. With a healthy slow MCP, verify its tools become usable after it finishes, and test a warm-cache new session without Skip.
5. Disable/re-enable individual MCP servers and their containing plugins, checking both existing and new sessions.

issues.title: Improve connection reliability with acknowledgements and tests
issues.body:
This pull request implements critical changes to enhance connection reliability in the VS Code transport layer by adding acknowledgment handling for received messages. The following updates were made:

- **Transport Layer Changes**:
  - Implemented acknowledgment of receipt before processing messages and added duplicate delivery filtering to prevent issues during chunk reassembly.
  - If an acknowledgment cannot be sent, the connection will now fail explicitly, addressing a significant gap in the previous implementation.

- **Testing Enhancements**:
  - Added comprehensive regression tests covering handshake traffic, duplicate handling, connection lifetimes, and scenarios involving large message streams (up to 10,000 messages and over 16 MB).
  
These changes aim to improve the robustness of the connection handling mechanism, addressing previously identified gaps and ensuring better performance and reliability in future interactions. Validation has been completed successfully, and the changes are ready for further review and testing.

issues.body:
### What happened?

Prow tests failing with "no image found". The image has newline in it:

ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-scalability-1-34: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-scalability-1-34/2102246705830301696
ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-scalability-1-35: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-scalability-1-35/2102246706027433984

### What did you expect to happen?

Tests to pass through the image download stage

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run a test as a specific point in time :(

More seriously, though - running any test will let us see that the fix is at least not breaking

### Anything else we need to know?

## ---- chatty LLM output below: ---- 


### Title
```text
cluster/gce/util.sh: `gcloud compute images list` without `--limit=1` (or `describe-from-family`) breaks cluster bringup when multiple images exist in `family:cos-*-lts`
```

---

### What happened?
```markdown
When bringing up a GCE cluster via `kubetest` / `cluster/gce/util.sh` without an explicit `KUBE_GCE_MASTER_IMAGE` / `KUBE_GCE_NODE_IMAGE` (relying on `MASTER_IMAGE_FAMILY` / `NODE_IMAGE_FAMILY`, e.g. `cos-121-lts`), `cluster/gce/util.sh` resolves the image name using `gcloud compute images list` without `--limit=1` (or `gcloud compute images describe-from-family`):

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/gce/util.sh#L68
```bash
kube_master_image=$(gcloud compute images list --project="${MASTER_IMAGE_PROJECT}" --no-standard-images --filter="family:${MASTER_IMAGE_FAMILY}" --format 'value(name)')
```
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/gce/util.sh#L99
```bash
kube_node_image=$(gcloud compute images list --project="${NODE_IMAGE_PROJECT}" --no-standard-images --filter="family:${NODE_IMAGE_FAMILY}" --format 'value(name)')
```

Normally, `cos-cloud` has only 1 non-deprecated image per family. However, when a new COS image (`cos-121-18867-584-32`, created `2026-09-21T22:30:25Z`) was published to `family:cos-121-lts` before the previous image (`cos-121-18867-584-23`) was marked `DEPRECATED`, `gcloud compute images list ... --format 'value(name)'` returned **two lines**.

Because `"${MASTER_IMAGE}"` is passed in double quotes to `gcloud compute instances create` in `cluster/gce/gci/master-helper.sh`, the literal newline was concatenated into the `sourceImage` URL, causing `e2e-up.sh` (`kubetest.Up`) to fail across `sig-release-1.34-blocking` and `sig-release-1.35-blocking`:

```text
Using image: cos-121-18867-584-23
cos-121-18867-584-32 from project: cos-cloud as master image
Using image: cos-121-18867-584-23
cos-121-18867-584-32 from project: cos-cloud as node image
...
ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) Could not fetch resource:
 - Invalid value for field 'resource.disks[0].initializeParams.sourceImage': 'https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/cos-cloud/global/images/cos-121-18867-584-23
cos-121-18867-584-32'. The referenced image resource cannot be found.
Failed to create master instance due to non-retryable error
```

Public Prow logs showing the failure:
- `ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-scalability-1-34`: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-scalability-1-34/2102246705830301696
- `ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-scalability-1-35`: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-scalability-1-35/2102246706027433984
```

---

### What did you expect to happen?
```markdown
`cluster/gce/util.sh` should deterministically resolve a single image (the newest non-deprecated image in `MASTER_IMAGE_FAMILY` / `NODE_IMAGE_FAMILY`) even if multiple non-deprecated images temporarily coexist in the same GCE image family.
```

---

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?
```markdown
Simulate multiple active images in `family:cos-121-lts` (or run during a `cos-cloud` image rollout before deprecation of the prior image):

```bash
# Current command in cluster/gce/util.sh (when >1 image in the family is active):
gcloud compute images list --project="cos-cloud" --no-standard-images --show-deprecated --filter="family:cos-121-lts" --format 'value(name)'
# Outputs multiple lines:
# cos-121-18867-584-23
# cos-121-18867-584-3
# cos-121-18867-584-32
# cos-121-18867-584-7
```

---

### Anything else we need to know?

### Proposed Fix
Replace `gcloud compute images list ... --filter="family:..."` in `cluster/gce/util.sh` (lines 68 and 99) with `gcloud compute images describe-from-family` (which uses GCE's `images.getFromFamily` API to atomically return the single newest non-deprecated image in the family), or add `--sort-by="~creationTimestamp" --limit=1`:

```diff
--- a/cluster/gce/util.sh
+++ b/cluster/gce/util.sh
@@ -65,7 +65,7 @@ if [[ "${MASTER_OS_DISTRIBUTION}" == "gci" ]]; then
     # family.
     kube_master_image="${KUBE_GCE_MASTER_IMAGE:-${GCI_VERSION}}"
     if [[ -z "${kube_master_image}" ]]; then
-      kube_master_image=$(gcloud compute images list --project="${MASTER_IMAGE_PROJECT}" --no-standard-images --filter="family:${MASTER_IMAGE_FAMILY}" --format 'value(name)')
+      kube_master_image=$(gcloud compute images describe-from-family "${MASTER_IMAGE_FAMILY}" --project="${MASTER_IMAGE_PROJECT}" --format 'value(name)')
     fi
 
     echo "Using image: ${kube_master_image} from project: ${MASTER_IMAGE_PROJECT} as master image" >&2
@@ -96,7 +96,7 @@ function set-linux-node-image() {
 
     kube_node_image="${KUBE_GCE_NODE_IMAGE:-${GCI_VERSION}}"
     if [[ -z "${kube_node_image}" ]]; then
-      kube_node_image=$(gcloud compute images list --project="${NODE_IMAGE_PROJECT}" --no-standard-images --filter="family:${NODE_IMAGE_FAMILY}" --format 'value(name)')
+      kube_node_image=$(gcloud compute images describe-from-family "${NODE_IMAGE_FAMILY}" --project="${NODE_IMAGE_PROJECT}" --format 'value(name)')
     fi
 
     echo "Using image: ${kube_node_image} from project: ${NODE_IMAGE_PROJECT} as node image" >&2
```

﻿## What happened
Split out from kubernetes/kubernetes#142147 — this flake predates the Aug-16 regression (10 failures pre-regression) and got worse after, but it's a real, independent bug, not just timeout pressure.

**Spec:** "MirrorPod when kubelet restarts should not change container status"

kubelet.log shows the post-restart kubelet's first mirror-pod status write landing before its own readiness probe completes, so Ready genuinely flaps False->True over a short window (~254ms observed) during every restart while the kubelet races to recreate the mirror pod against the still-existing pre-restart one ("already exists").

This looks like a test assertion that's too strict for how kubelet actually reports status post-restart.

issues.title: e2e_node: make ImageGCPeriod (and other e2e_node wait budgets) configurable for tests

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

issues.body:
﻿## What happened
While removing duplicated `[Slow]` spec execution between `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial` and `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-slow` (kubernetes/test-infra#37903), we looked into why the `[Slow]`-tagged ImageGC/GarbageCollect/MirrorPod specs in `test/e2e_node` cost ~30 minutes per host.

It's not image size or pull time — these use the standard few-MB e2e-test-images (pause, busybox, nginx-slim/agnhost). The time comes from wait/poll budgets hardcoded in the tests themselves, bound to production defaults:

- `image_gc_test.go`: two `[Slow]` specs poll for up to `checkGCUntil = 6 * time.Minute`, gated by kubelet's `ImageGCPeriod` (hardcoded to 5 minutes).
- `garbage_collector_test.go`: `setupDuration = 10 * time.Minute`, `garbageCollectDuration = 3 * time.Minute`.
- `mirror_pod_test.go`: several `2 * time.Minute` `Eventually` polls, plus a couple `5 * time.Minute` waits.

Polling more frequently doesn't help — these tests aren't slow because they check infrequently, they're waiting on a real kubelet-side event gated by a fixed period.

## What we'd like
Make `ImageGCPeriod` (and whatever governs the GC/mirror-pod wait windows above) configurable for e2e_node tests, so these specs aren't bound to the 5-minute production default and can run with a much shorter period in test.

## Context
- kubernetes/test-infra#37903 (merged) — removed duplicate execution of these specs as a stopgap
- kubernetes/kubernetes#142147 — the investigation that led here
- Requested by @kannon92 during review of #37903

/sig node
/kind feature

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

kube-proxy links the whole generic apiserver and the CEL stack for two accidental reasons. `pkg/cluster/ports` imports `k8s.io/cloud-provider/options` for one constant, which brings `k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options`, admission and the etcd client. `responsewriters` imports `k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/registry/rest` for one interface, and `registry/rest` imports `admission`, which imports cel-go.

This PR makes the port constant a literal (a test keeps it equal to the cloud-provider value) and declares an identical `ResourceStreamer` interface in `responsewriters` so it no longer imports `registry/rest`.

Measured on linux/amd64 with a plain `go build`: the kube-proxy package graph goes from 1452 to 1102 packages (`k8s.io/apiserver` packages from 182 to 35), cel-go, antlr and the etcd client are no longer linked, and the binary shrinks from 111,514,088 to 100,053,388 bytes. kubelet loses only the cloud-provider packages; it keeps CEL through the authorizer factory and the scheduler's DRA plugin.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The `ResourceStreamer` interface is duplicated on purpose, not moved: `registry/rest` keeps its definition for its own API, and `responsewriters` gets a structurally identical copy. `writers_test.go` has compile-time assertions that the two interfaces stay assignable in both directions, so the type assertion in `WriteObjectNegotiated` matches the same objects as before. `StreamObject` has no callers outside the package; only the static type of its `stream` parameter changes. `pkg/cluster/ports/ports_test.go` fails if the port value drifts from `k8s.io/cloud-provider/options`.

issues.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind flake
/sig node

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The two-plugin test "must call NodeUnprepareResources again if it's in progress for one plugin when Kubelet restarts" restarts the kubelet right after both NodePrepareResources calls succeed. Nothing checks that the kubelet is actually inside plugin2's blocked NodeUnprepareResources at that point. In the four failures on ci-node-crio-dra listed in #142404 the restart landed while the old kubelet's CreateContainer was still in flight, and the rest follows from that: CRI-O logs `CreateCtr: context was either canceled or the deadline was exceeded`, the new kubelet creates the container again, the pod finishes, and StopPodSandbox then takes 118 to 119 s because the sandbox still holds the container that was created but never started (`Using stop timeout: 119`, then `Stopping container ... with stop signal(15) timed out. Killing...`). The kubelet calls NodeUnprepareResources only after that stop, which is later than the 120 s the test waits. In passing runs the restart happens after the container has exited and the sandbox stop takes 0.3 s. The same early restart showed up once on ci-node-e2e-containerd-2-0-dra-1-34 (run 2098416805084139520, 2026-09-11) with a different outcome: NodeUnprepareResources succeeded, but the pod ended up Failed.

The test now waits for plugin2's NodeUnprepareResources call to be recorded before it restarts the kubelet, so the restart always interrupts the call the test is named after. After the restart it requires a NodeUnprepareResources call recorded after the restart to succeed, instead of accepting the pre-restart call that completes once the block is lifted.

Two matchers are added for that: `NodeUnprepareResourcesInProgress` (call received, no response yet) and `NodeUnprepareResourcesSucceededAfter(n)` (a successful call recorded after the first n calls). Both come with unit tests.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Related to #142404. @dharmjit is assigned there; this is the fix I mentioned in my comment, so we don't end up doing it twice.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
The barrier relies on the test driver recording a call before its handler runs (`recordGRPCCall` appends the entry, then calls the handler, then writes the result back at the same index), so a blocked call shows up with a nil response.

I could not run the node e2e suite locally against CRI-O. Evidence is the kubelet.log and crio.log of the four failing runs (2101223445017661440, 2101857630149414912, 2102673018894422016, 2103308210961125376) and of the passing run 2103398808246292480. `go vet` and the matcher unit tests pass; the e2e change compiles.

The two-minute sandbox stop after a cancelled CreateContainer looks like something for CRI-O to look at separately; it is not caused by the DRA code.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
NONE
```

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind dependency

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Bumps `google.golang.org/grpc` from v1.82.2 to v1.84.0 and removes the pin added in #142036.

v1.82.2 does not contain the fix for CVE-2026-84304 (HTTP/2 DATA frame heap exhaustion, GHSA-vp52-pcj8-j9qc). The fix, grpc/grpc-go#9331, shipped only in v1.83.1 and later, and there is no v1.82.x backport. The kubelet gRPC probe client dials servers that pod authors control, so the client side of this bug is reachable from any pod. v1.84.0 also carries the CVE-2026-84303 fix (xDS, which we do not vendor).

grpc v1.83.0+ requires `cloud.google.com/go/auth`, which adds four modules from the unwanted list to the module graph: `s2a-go`, `enterprise-certificate-proxy`, `gax-go/v2` and `google.golang.org/api`. Only `grpc/credentials/google` imports them and we do not vendor that package, so none of them reaches the build list or `vendor/`. This takes option 1 of #142005 and records them in `status.unwantedReferences` with grpc as the only referencer, next to the existing `protoc-gen-validate` and `vtprotobuf` entries. The upstream removal (grpc/grpc-go#9385) is approved but targets grpc 1.86.

The second commit takes what the pin was holding back: the etcd modules to v3.7.2 (they require grpc v1.83.2), `otelgrpc` to v0.71.0 and `otlptracegrpc` to v1.45.0. `otlptracegrpc` v1.46.0 is not taken because it requires `grpc-gateway/v2` v2.30.0, which stays pinned. MVS also moves otel core to v1.46.0, `proto/otlp` to v1.11.0, `golang.org/x/net` to v0.58.0 and `go-logr/logr` to v1.4.4. Five otel modules no longer require `go-spew` or `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` and leave those status lists.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #141798
xref #142005

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

`hack/lint-dependencies.sh` passes after each commit. The four unwanted modules appear only in `go mod graph` with grpc as the importer and have no directory under `vendor/`. The fix is present in the vendored code: `grep -c compactBacklogLocked vendor/google.golang.org/grpc/internal/transport/transport.go` prints 2.

Correction to #141798: the 2026-09-09 comment there says v1.82.2 has the same fix. It does not; v1.82.2 only has the grpc/grpc-go#9365 and #9346 cherry-picks.

issues.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind failing-test
/sig node
/cc @natasha41575

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
`VerifyContainerCgroupValues` execs into the container once per cgroup file: memory limit, CPU limit, CPU weight. This PR reads the first line of each of the three files with a single exec and checks them together. Retry semantics are unchanged: a failed read is retried, a wrong value is final.

In `ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master` the 63 `[Feature:InPlacePodVerticalScaling]` specs spend most of their time in exec calls into the test pods (#142262): 1104 execs per run, of which 729 come from this helper (243 calls, three files each). The test pods use CPU limits of a few tens of millicores, so the shell spawned by each exec is CFS throttled and one exec takes seconds.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Related to #142262

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
I measured this with the same 63 specs, run serially, on a local kind cluster (rootless podman, cgroup v2), each binary twice in ABBA order:

| pair | binary | specs | wall | execs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pair 1 | base | 63 passed, 0 failed | 3810 s | 1034 |
| pair 1 | batched | 63 passed, 0 failed | 2976 s | 548 |
| pair 2 | batched | 63 passed, 0 failed | 2677 s | 548 |
| pair 2 | base | 63 passed, 0 failed | 2913 s | 1034 |

The exec count is the deterministic part: 243 verification calls per run in both binaries, two execs fewer per call. The wall times are from my own machines, not from GCE. The kind rig cannot set a negative `oom_score_adj` under rootless podman, so the oom check was skipped there in both binaries; that is the only difference from the job's exec sequence (547 cpu.weight, 243 memory.max, 243 cpu.max, 70 oom_score_adj).

I also ran both binaries once on a single-node kubeadm cluster (kubelet 1.37.0, containerd 2.4.0, cgroup v2), where the `oom_score_adj` check runs unchanged: 55 specs passed with both. The same 8 failed with both binaries while waiting for the resize: that node has swap enabled and the kubelet reports an in-place resize of a container with swap as infeasible. Execs there: 1026 with the base binary, 572 with this change. The e2e binary is built from master, so I treat that cluster as a pass/fail and exec-count check, not a timing reference.

`VerifyPodCgroups` still reads its files one exec at a time. The failing job never calls it, so I left it for a separate change.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
NONE
```

issues.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/sig node

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR adds support to enable Quantum Crypto within the hack/local-up-cluster.sh script.

- Add ENABLE_QUANTUM_CRYPTO flag to hack/local-up-cluster.sh that stands up a fully post-quantum local Kubernetes cluster using ML-DSA (FIPS 204) certificates
- Add hack/tools/quantum-cert-gen/ — a standalone Go tool that generates a complete ML-DSA certificate chain (CAs, serving certs, and client certs for all control plane components)
- When enabled, every TLS endpoint in the cluster uses ML-DSA-65 keys and signatures — apiserver serving cert, kubelet serving cert, and all client certificates used for mutual TLS between components

Note: cfssl is not used if PQC is enabled, since cfssl does not support it.

Usage:

```bash
# Full quantum cluster (ML-DSA-65, the default)
ENABLE_QUANTUM_CRYPTO=true hack/local-up-cluster.sh
```

```bash
# With a specific variant
ENABLE_QUANTUM_CRYPTO=true QUANTUM_CRYPTO_ALGORITHM=ML-DSA-87 hack/local-up-cluster.sh
```

```bash
# Traditional cluster (unchanged behavior)
hack/local-up-cluster.sh
```

Verification:

With quantum enabled, both the apiserver and kubelet serve ML-DSA certificates:

```bash
$ openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:6443 </dev/null 2>&1 | grep 'PKEY\|sigalg'
  a:PKEY: ML-DSA-65, 15616 (bit); sigalg: ML-DSA-65
```

```bash
$ openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:10250 </dev/null 2>&1 | grep 'PKEY\|sigalg'
   a:PKEY: ML-DSA-65, 15616 (bit); sigalg: ML-DSA-65
```

Related to #141838

issues.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

#141203 started rejecting a decimal exponent that does not fit the int32 scale. A <=1.37 apiserver accepted those spellings, narrowed the exponent to an int32 and stored the object with the text it was given, so master cannot read them back: `ParseQuantity` fails, and per #141166 the etcd3 store fails an entire LIST on the first object it cannot decode.

Following the recipe in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/141166#issuecomment-5817729514:

**What v1.37.1 actually does**, measured against the release branch:

| input | v1.37.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `1e4294967296` | parses, `AsInt64` = `(1, true)`, `String()` = `1e4294967296` |
| `1e4294967297` | parses, `AsInt64` = `(10, true)`, `String()` = `10` |
| `-1e4294967296` | parses, `AsInt64` = `(-1, true)` |
| `1e-4294967296` | parses, `AsInt64` = `(1, true)` |
| `1e8589934592` | parses, `AsInt64` = `(1, true)` |
| `1e9223372036854775807` | parses, narrows to `-1`, `String()` = `100e-3` |
| `1e9223372036854775808` | parse error, on 1.37 and on master |
| `1e2147483648`, `1e-2147483648` | parse, then hang while canonicalizing |

So the stored contract is narrowing, not clamping: `1e4294967296` means **1**. Clamping the exponent to `MaxInt32` would decode those objects as astronomically large values instead of the values they hold.

**The tests** in `quantity_compat_test.go` pin the decode path, the re-encode path and the protobuf round trip for the four spellings that 1.37 both accepted and could write. They pass unchanged on `release-1.37` (v1.37.1) and fail on master with `unable to parse quantity's suffix`, which is the regression.

**The fix** narrows the exponent the way 1.37 did. A scale of `math.MinInt32` stays rejected: negating it overflows int32, and 1.37 hung while canonicalizing such a quantity rather than writing it, so no stored object can carry one. That also keeps those two spellings out of the compatibility set, since a test for them could not pass on 1.37.

`TestInterpretExponentInt32Bounds` and the parse error baseline move back to describing the narrowing.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Part of #141166

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Two things deliberately left out, both wanting your call:

- **Rejecting these on write.** With this change `cpu: 1e4294967296` is accepted again and silently means 1. Rejecting it at admission needs the parser to report that it narrowed, which is the strict entry point below rather than something validation can see today.
- **The opt-in strict mode.** Per your note about not shipping a variant that fixes 1 of N, I did not add one here. `1e2147483648` still hangs, and `Add`/`Sub`/`String` still wrap or blow up at extreme scales, so a "strict" `ParseQuantity` today would still hand callers a quantity that hangs later. Happy to add it in a follow-up once those land, or in this PR if you would rather have it now.

/assign @jpbetz
/sig api-machinery

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a regression in 1.38 where resource quantities written by a 1.37 or older apiserver with a decimal exponent outside the int32 range, such as `1e4294967296`, could not be decoded, which failed reads of the whole collection.
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES. Claude Code was used to measure the v1.37.1 behaviour, draft the tests and the fix, and run the verification described above. I reviewed every line and am responsible for the result.

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This is a follow-up to #141932. This PR adds a way to customize whether a victim is a valid candidate for reprieval.

This is needed for Kueue integration with WAS through the scheduler-library, as Kueue needs to keep track of per-victim quota or fair-sharing and block reprieval if it would cause preemptor to violate the constraint.

Note that this is very similar to the current `PreFilterExtensions.AddPod/RemovePod` and `Filter`, however we need the functions to operate on group-level rather than pod-level. With a dedicated customization point, we can skip reprieval at a minimal cost, and we have more flexibility if we ever need to change it.

Fixes #128201

## Problem

UnstructuredExtractor fails with `duplicate entry for /v1, Kind=APIResourceList` when an aggregated API serves overlapping OpenAPI information.

## Root Cause

`NewGVKParser` in `staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/managedfields/gvkparser.go` returned an error when duplicate GVK entries were encountered.

## Fix

Keep the first occurrence of a GVK and skip subsequent duplicates, allowing parser construction to continue.

## Testing

Added regression tests covering:
- duplicate APIResourceList GVK
- duplicate ConfigMap GVK

issues.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind flake
/sig storage

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
`testForceDetachMetric` reads the force detach counter once, right after the
test sees the fake detacher called. But the reconciler increments the counter
only after `DetachVolume` returns, while the detach itself runs in a goroutine
started by the operation executor (`nestedpendingoperations`). If that goroutine
wins, the test sees the detach before the increment:

    reconciler_test.go:962: Expected desiredForceDetachMericCounter to be 1, got 0

The counter is global, so a late increment also leaks into the next test's
baseline and fails its "unchanged" check ("to be 78, got 79").

This makes `testForceDetachMetric` poll with the file's existing
`waitForCondition`, like the other assertions here. For "unchanged" checks it
returns on the first read, as before.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes #142349

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
Reproduced on an idle x86 host only under CPU contention: 150 processes pinned
to 4 cores, `GOMAXPROCS=1`, `-race`, 15,000 runs of each of the three affected
tests.

| | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| failures / 45,000 runs | 49 | 0 |

Failures on master were at lines 320, 962 and 1300 (missing increment) and
964 and 1280 (the leaked increment). With no contention, master passed all
15,000 runs, which fits CI hitting this mostly on s390x and loaded nodes.
`make test WHAT=./pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/...` with `-count=3`
passes.

The same helper exists on release branches (the issue also lists
ci-kubernetes-unit-1-34), so this may be worth cherry-picking.

stress harness and the fix, and draft this description. I reviewed the change
and ran the tests.

issues.title: Client-go: Add support for Connection Pool

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

I would like to propose adding a support to client-go library for creating multiple connections **to the same endpoint** and using some naive load balancing (such as round robin or power of 2) to send traffic.

The option cloud be set using one of the following mechanisms:
* In kubeconfig, via option similar to 'disableCompression' we have today
* In golang, by setting respective value, e.g. via rest.Config flag

Goal:
* In many environments, the endpoint specified in kubeconfig is an L4 load balancer that picks backend randomly. By opening multiple connections we can split the traffic from a single client / controller to multiple kube-apiserver replicas and avoid single kube-apiserver instance becoming overloaded while the other replicas are idle.
* Avoid single-replica pinning issue -- improve client experience in case of single kube-apiserver replica slowdown / unhealthiness. E.g. today kubelet sends traffic only to a single kcp replica. if the replica is slow or unhealthy (e.g. not able to process requests but alive), all connections are persistent and all kubelet's retries are still going to that replica, leading to marking the replica as unhealthy. By sending traffic to multiple replicas, we increase chances (both must be unhealthy).

Out of scope:
* Multiple endpoint support (we still want client-go to open connections to single endpoint -- we rely on L4 load balancer to assign connections to multiple backends)
* Endpoint discovery: Client-go somehow finds out what are the IPs for kube-apiserver instances.

### Why is this needed?

This is important use case for performance-heavy controllers / schedulers and similar technique is widely used by the components (see e.g. [transportHack](https://github.com/kubernetes/perf-tests/blob/1317eb81116835070beecdb2f6cb4eda3fd27b1c/clusterloader2/pkg/framework/config/client_config.go#L86) in clusterloader).

By moving this concept to core client-go library we can help the controllers to avoid this "transportHack" or similar technique. By standardising this pattern, we can make this opinionated and ensure that controllers are behaving in expected way and automatically benefit from potential improvements in this area.

issues.title: Some kube-apiserver histograms stay classic because ApplyFeatureGates() runs after informers and REST clients are built

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/instrumentation
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Instrumentation.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

issues.body:
### What happened?

First of all, thank you for landing native histogram support in v1.37 — it's been a really
welcome addition on my side.

While verifying it on a kind cluster, I noticed that within a **single kube-apiserver
process**, some histograms are exposed as native while others stay classic. The split does not
look intentional, so I wanted to report what I measured.

Scraping `kindest/node:v1.37.0` with Prometheus v3.13.2 and `scrape_native_histograms: true`
(`always_scrape_classic_histograms` left at its default of `false`):

| metric | native from | classic from |
|---|---|---|
| `apiserver_request_duration_seconds` | **kube-apiserver** | — |
| `workqueue_work_duration_seconds` | kubelet | **kube-apiserver** |
| `workqueue_queue_duration_seconds` | kubelet | **kube-apiserver** |
| `rest_client_request_duration_seconds` | kubelet | **kube-apiserver** |
| `informer_processing_latency_seconds` | — | **kube-apiserver** |
| `apiserver_admission_controller_admission_duration_seconds` | — | **kube-apiserver** |

The first row shows the feature gate is active for kube-apiserver
(`apiserver_request_duration_seconds` had 158 native series). So this isn't a gate or config
problem — only the metrics registered early stay classic.

The consequence is that **the same metric name is native from one component and classic from
another**. `workqueue_work_duration_seconds` had 4 native series from kubelet and 319 classic
series from kube-apiserver, and this query silently returns kubelet data only, with no warning:

```
sum(rate(workqueue_work_duration_seconds[10m]))
```

### Why it happens, as far as I can tell

`toPromHistogramOpts()` reads the gate when `Create()` runs, i.e. at registration time, so
`ApplyFeatureGates()` has to run first. The doc comment says as much:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/features/kube_features.go#L51-L53

```go
// ApplyFeatureGates propagates the current feature gate state to the metrics
// subsystem. It must be called after feature gates are finalised and before
// any histogram metrics are registered.
```

kubelet calls it before any client or informer is built:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/cmd/kubelet/app/server.go#L671-L673

kube-apiserver calls it inside `CreateConfig()`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/pkg/controlplane/apiserver/config.go#L303

but an informer is already instantiated nine lines earlier, at `server.go:230`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/server.go#L230

```go
endpointSliceGetter, err := proxy.NewEndpointSliceIndexerGetter(versionedInformers.Discovery().V1().EndpointSlices())
```

That calls `sliceInformer.Informer()`
([`endpointslice.go#L74-L76`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/proxy/endpointslice.go#L74-L76)),
which triggers the deferred registration in the fifo metrics provider. The REST clients behind
`versionedInformers` are built earlier still.

What makes me think this is unintended rather than a deliberate scoping decision is that the
workqueue and fifo providers already contain a workaround for exactly this ordering problem:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/prometheus/clientgo/fifo/metrics.go#L61-L66

```go
// init only installs the provider with cache. The actual metric
// registration with legacyregistry is deferred until the first factory
// method is called (which happens at runtime when the first informer is
// constructed). This ensures Create() — and therefore the read of the
// NativeHistograms feature gate inside toPromHistogramOpts — runs after
// ApplyFeatureGates has propagated the gate state.
```

The deferral works, but in kube-apiserver the first informer is still constructed before
`ApplyFeatureGates()`, so the workaround doesn't have the intended effect there.

### What did you expect to happen?

I'd expect a given metric name to be exposed in the same format regardless of which component
emits it, so that a query like `sum(rate(workqueue_work_duration_seconds[10m]))` covers every
component that reports it.

Moving the `ApplyFeatureGates()` call in kube-apiserver earlier — before the REST clients and
`SharedInformerFactory` are built — would line it up with what kubelet already does. I may well
be missing a constraint that forces the current placement, though.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?


1. Create a cluster:

```
kind create cluster --image kindest/node:v1.37.0
```

2. Run Prometheus v3.x with native-only scraping for both the apiserver and the kubelet:

```yaml
global:
  scrape_native_histograms: true
scrape_configs:
- job_name: kubernetes-apiservers
  # ... standard in-cluster apiserver scrape config
- job_name: kubernetes-nodes
  # ... standard in-cluster kubelet scrape config
```

3. Compare the native and classic forms of the same metric:

```
count by (job) (workqueue_work_duration_seconds)          # => kubernetes-nodes only
count by (job) (workqueue_work_duration_seconds_bucket)   # => kubernetes-apiservers only
```

4. Confirm the gate is actually on for the apiserver:

```
count(apiserver_request_duration_seconds{job="kubernetes-apiservers"})   # => 158
```


### Anything else we need to know?

- With `convert_classic_histograms_to_nhcb: true`, the split becomes an exponential/NHCB schema
  mix instead, and `sum(rate(workqueue_work_duration_seconds[10m]))` returns an empty vector
  with a PromQL warning rather than partial data.
- Two other groups of histograms stay classic for different reasons, which I assume are out of
  scope here: `TimingHistogramOpts` metrics (e.g. `apiserver_flowcontrol_*_utilization`) never
  receive native options, and the `go_*` runtime metrics come from client_golang's Go collector
  and don't go through `component-base` at all.
- I couldn't find this discussed in KEP-5808 or in an existing issue, so apologies if I've
  missed it.
- Possibly related: #142377 (on `NativeHistogramMinResetDuration` being unset).

Happy to send a PR moving the call site if that's the direction you'd want to take.

```

issues.title: Was leaving NativeHistogramMinResetDuration unset in component-base intentional?

issues.body:
First of all, thank you for landing native histogram support in v1.37 — it's been a really
welcome addition on my side. In my own testing on a kind cluster, scraping the control plane
metrics as native-only cut the number of stored series by roughly 75%, and no longer being
bounded by the classic bucket boundaries has already changed how I'm approaching SLI design.

While evaluating it, I ran into something I wasn't sure how to read. Apologies in advance if
this has already been discussed somewhere I've missed.

`component-base` sets two of the native histogram options:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/internal/nativehistograms.go#L33-L40

```go
var defaultNativeHistogramOptions = NativeHistogramOptions{
	BucketFactor:    1.1,
	MaxBucketNumber: 160,
}
```

`NativeHistogramMinResetDuration` is left at zero. As far as I can tell, that means once a
histogram exceeds `MaxBucketNumber`, `maybeReset()` is skipped and only `doubleBucketWidth()`
runs, so the reduced resolution stays in place for the lifetime of the process:

https://github.com/prometheus/client_golang/blob/v1.24.0/prometheus/histogram.go#L478-L480

```go
//  - Any increased zero threshold or reduced resolution is reset back
//    to their original values once NativeHistogramMinResetDuration has
//    passed (since the last reset or the creation of the histogram).
```

A few other projects in the ecosystem do set it to `1h`:

| repo | org | BucketFactor | MaxBucketNumber | MinResetDuration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| controller-runtime | kubernetes-sigs | 1.1 | 100 | `1h` |
| cluster-api | kubernetes-sigs | 1.1 | 100 | `1h` |
| Prometheus | prometheus | 1.1 | 100 | `1h` |

That said, I can imagine a reason not to: `maybeReset()` also clears `_sum`, `_count` and the
classic buckets, which may well be something you'd want to avoid for `STABLE` metrics.
KEP-5808 explains the reasoning behind `BucketFactor` and `MaxBucketNumber` but doesn't touch
on reset behaviour, so I couldn't tell whether this was weighed and set aside, or simply
hasn't come up yet.

Could you help me understand which it is? I'd be glad to open a PR if it turns out to be just
an oversight, though I wanted to ask first in case there's context I'm missing.

/sig instrumentation
/kind bug

issues.body:
### What happened?

I tried to take a backup of a pod's data using `kubectl exec`. When inspecting file sizes the files seemed not to be the same. After some testing and experiments, I found the issue to occur only when the client reads slower than the (in-pod) process writes (to stdout). Only the end of the stream was missing, the beginning was intact. `kubectl exec` often exited with 0, with nothing on stderr. So the truncated result could not be told apart from a complete one. `kubectl cp` fails the same way when the client is behind a slow link with `error: unexpected EOF` (copying to a fast local disk did not fail). The error occurred using the older SPDY transport as well as WebSockets.

**kind v1.37.0, two nodes, kubectl v1.37.0; pod writes 32 MiB, client reads at 1MiB/s**

path | truncated reads | # of those with exit 0 + empty stderr
-- | -- | --
kubectl exec, WebSocket (default) | 3/5 | 0
kubectl exec, SPDY | 5/5 | 5
crictl exec on the node, same reader | 5/5 | 5
crictl exec on the node, reader not throttled | 0/5 |  
kubectl exec, process sleeps 45 s after its last write | 0/1 |  

* crictl exec on the node, where only the CRI streaming server is involved, already truncates
* packet captures have shown the kubelet passes everything it received, so bytes are lost at the streaming server & apiserver -> client connection

### What did you expect to happen?

Everything the remote (in-pod) process wrote should have reached the client, or the client should exit with a non-zero exit code.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I let a coding agent reproduce the error in various ways (k3s, kind, crictl, k8s versions from 1.30 to 1.37), full measurements, per-hop packet captures and scripts: https://github.com/knoppiks/k8s-exec-truncation-repro

I ran the reproduction myself, on multiple nodes. With the folowing script
<details open>
<summary>Script to reproduce</summary>

```bash
cat <<'EOF' | kind create cluster --name trunc --config -
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes: [{role: control-plane}, {role: worker}]
EOF
kubectl run payload --image=alpine:3.22 --restart=Never \
  --overrides='{"spec":{"nodeName":"trunc-worker"}}' -- sleep infinity
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/payload --timeout=120s

# The container writes exactly 32 MiB (33554432 bytes) and exits 0.
PAYLOAD='head -c 33554432 /dev/zero'

# A reader that consumes 1 MiB per second and prints how many bytes it got.
slow_count() {
  total=0
  while n=$(head -c 1048576 | wc -c) && [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; do
    total=$((total + n)); sleep 1
  done
  echo "got=$total"
}

# 1) kubectl exec through the apiserver: WebSocket (default), then SPDY.
for ws in true false; do
  echo -n "kubectl exec, websockets=$ws: "
  KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS=$ws kubectl exec payload -- sh -c "$PAYLOAD" | slow_count
  echo "  kubectl exit code: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
done

# 2) The same reader on the node, reading crictl exec directly: only the CRI
#    streaming server is in the path. No kubelet, apiserver or network.
id=$(docker exec trunc-worker crictl ps --name payload -q)
echo -n "crictl exec on the node: "
docker exec trunc-worker bash -c "$(declare -f slow_count)
  crictl exec $id sh -c '$PAYLOAD' | slow_count
  echo \"  crictl exit code: \${PIPESTATUS[0]}\""

# Control: keep the process alive until the reader has caught up.
echo -n "kubectl exec, 'sleep 45' after the last write: "
kubectl exec payload -- sh -c "$PAYLOAD; sleep 45" | slow_count
```
</details>

**Sample output**
<details>
<summary>Setup</summary>

```console

E0924 09:31:18.537655  292110 v2.go:151] "Copying stdout failed" err="next reader: read tcp 127.0.0.1:54760->127.0.0.1:33907: read: connection reset by peer"

<details>
<summary>GitHub Actions</summary>
The reproduction repository also runs the same measurement on GitHub Actions:

run | what | result
---|---|---

### Anything else we need to know?

The issue seems related to
* #60140, which was closed as not reproducible, using local copies (I'd assume a fast reader, which didn't fail in my tests either).
* #124571, closed as stale

issues.title: kube-apiserver keep using a stale webhook configuration after an update

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: needs-sig
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `sig/foo` label and requires one.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

issues.body:
### What happened?

The kube-apiserver kept calling admission webhooks with an old version of `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration`, even though the object had been updated. It kept doing so until the object was updated again.

There is a recurring e2e flake in Cluster API, which most likely is related to this cache race. Right after the providers are installed, every webhook fails with:
```
failed calling webhook "validation.cluster.cluster.x-k8s.io": failed to call webhook: Post "https://capi-webhook-service.capi-system.svc:443/validate-cluster-x-k8s-io-v1beta2-cluster?timeout=10s": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

Following the time from one failing [run](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/periodic-cluster-api-e2e-main-v2/2100268237257183232) :
* (17:22:15) cert-manager issues the serving certificate (signle revision)
* (17:22:16) `clusterctl` creates the `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` without a `caBundle`. In the same time, cert0manager caininjector sets the `caBundle` on all webhooks. The object ends at `generation: 2` and it is never modified again.
* (17:22:19) the webhook server loads the serving certificate.
* (17:22:23 --> end of the test) every call from the kube-apiserver fails with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. The webhook server logs remote error: tls: bad certificate for the same connections.

A dump of the objects after the failure shows `caBundle` equal to `ca.crt` of the serving certificate Secret, meaning that the stored object was correct for the failing duration, but the kube-apiserver, probably, kept serving with the version that had no `caBundle`.

It seems that the race is in `configurationsCache`, `sync.Map`,  in the webhook managers code (validating/mutating). The cache is built with keys derived only by configuration name. The informer `UpdateFunc` runs `configurationsCache.Delete(name)` and then `lazy.Notify()`. `getValidatingWebhookConfigurations` builds accessors from a lister snapshot and runs `configurationsCache.Store(name, accessors)` without checking which version they were built from.



### What did you expect to happen?

After a webhook configuration is updated, the kube-apiserver uses the latest version. Accessors built from an older version are never cached in the way that they will outlive an update event.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

During the investigation for the kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api/issues/13300, we were trying to pinpoint if the source of flake was on the CAPI side or on the kube-apiserver side. I used the following unit test as way to reproduce it.

```go
package configuration

import (
	"context"
	"testing"
	"testing/synctest"

	v1 "k8s.io/api/admissionregistration/v1"
	metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
	"k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook"
	"k8s.io/client-go/informers"
	"k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/fake"
)

func TestValidatingWebhookConfigurationStaleCache(t *testing.T) {
	synctest.Test(t, func(t *testing.T) {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
		defer cancel()

		cfg := &v1.ValidatingWebhookConfiguration{
			ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{Name: "cfg", ResourceVersion: "1"},
			Webhooks:   []v1.ValidatingWebhook{{Name: "webhook.example.com"}},
		}
		client := fake.NewSimpleClientset(cfg)
		factory := informers.NewSharedInformerFactory(client, 0)
		m := NewValidatingWebhookConfigurationManager(factory, nil).(*validatingWebhookConfigurationManager)

		release := make(chan struct{})
		create := m.createValidatingWebhookAccessor
		m.createValidatingWebhookAccessor = func(uid, name string, h *v1.ValidatingWebhook) webhook.WebhookAccessor {
			if len(h.ClientConfig.CABundle) == 0 {
				<-release
			}
			return create(uid, name, h)
		}

		factory.Start(ctx.Done())
		factory.WaitForCacheSync(ctx.Done())
		synctest.Wait()

		// Hold the old evaluation across the configuration update.
		go m.Webhooks()
		synctest.Wait()

		updated := cfg.DeepCopy()
		updated.ResourceVersion = "2"
		updated.Webhooks[0].ClientConfig.CABundle = []byte("injected-ca")
		if _, err := client.AdmissionregistrationV1().ValidatingWebhookConfigurations().
			Update(ctx, updated, metav1.UpdateOptions{}); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		synctest.Wait()

		close(release)
		synctest.Wait()

		got := m.Webhooks()
		if len(got) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("expected 1 webhook, got %d", len(got))
		}
		if ca := string(got[0].GetClientConfig().CABundle); ca != "injected-ca" {
			t.Fatalf("caBundle = %q, want %q", ca, "injected-ca")
		}
	})
}
```
Using `k8s.io/apiserver` `v0.37.0` 
```
=== RUN   TestValidatingWebhookConfigurationStaleCache
    stale_cache_simplified_test.go:62: caBundle = "", want "injected-ca"
```
The idea was to replicate the cert-manager `inject-ca-from` create the configuration and then patch the `caBundle` immediately (cainjector)

### Anything else we need to know?

Testing a possible fix where we capture the `resourceVersion` next to the cached accessors and reuse them onky when it matches. That approach seems to fix the unit test above.

Another workaround was to trigger an update to the webhook configuration (eg. adding an annotation) clears the stale entry, without changing the current apiserver code. 

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
Server Version: v1.37.0
```
Seen since at least early 2026 in Cluster API CI across several Kubernetes versions.
</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
None
</details>

<details>

# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture

```

</details>

<details>

</details>

<details>

</details>


### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

<details>

</details>

/kind bug

`kubectl label -o yaml` on more than one object never writes `---`. A new printer is built for each object, and the yaml printer only emits the separator after it has already printed something. annotate keeps one printer, so the same list comes out as separate documents.

Name output still gets a printer per object, so "labeled" / "not labeled" does not change.

```release-note
kubectl label -o yaml prints a document separator between objects
```

Fixes kubernetes/kubectl#1265

issues.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
If the ID range available to the kubelet for user namespaces changes between
restarts (editing /etc/subuid, installing getsubids, or creating the `kubelet`
user), a pod's persisted mapping can fall outside the new range. The kubelet
then refuses to start, and all it says is:

    create user namespace manager: record pod mappings for existing pod "<uid>": id 1153695744 is out of range

This PR keeps the refusal (starting anyway could hand out overlapping
mappings, see #137930) but makes the error actionable: it names the mapping
file, the pod's ID range, and the range available to the kubelet, and points
at restoring the previous range:

    record pod mappings for existing pod "<uid>" from /var/lib/kubelet/pods/<uid>/userns:
    user namespace IDs [1815871488, 1815937024) are out of range [65536, 7274496)
    available to the kubelet; if the kubelet ID range changed, restore the previous one

Range bounds are computed in uint64 because the default range ends at 2^32.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Part of #141941. It covers only the diagnostics question raised there; whether
a single pod can be refused instead of the whole kubelet is left for SIG Node.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
- The hint only suggests restoring the previous range. It deliberately does not
  suggest deleting the pod directory, which would lose emptyDir data and is
  still an open question in the issue.
- Tested:
  - `make test WHAT=./pkg/kubelet/userns` and `./pkg/kubelet` with `-race` pass.
  - The new test fails on master with the original message.
  - End to end in a kind node (v1.36 control plane, kubelet built from this
    branch): allocated a `hostUsers: false` pod under the default range, moved
    the kubelet to a delegated range via /etc/subuid, and restarted the kubelet.
    The new error appeared. After restoring the range, the kubelet started with
    no restarts and kept the pod's original mapping.
  - The node image lacks `getsubids`, so a stand-in script printing the same
    format was used.
  - The sandbox cannot start in nested kind (sysfs mount in a userns), which
    does not affect the startup replay path.
- AI disclosure: an AI assistant (Claude) helped find the issue, write the
  reproduction and the test, and draft this description. I reviewed the change
  and ran all tests myself.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
kubelet: when a pod's persisted user namespace mapping is outside the kubelet's current ID range at startup, the error now names the mapping file, the pod's ID range and the available range, instead of only "id N is out of range".
```

#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Three documentation references in the tree point at things that no longer exist. This points each one at its current location.

`cluster/addons/dns/kube-dns/README.md` links its "Administrators guide" to `http://kubernetes.io/docs/admin/dns/`. That URL returns HTTP 404. It is easy to miss because kubernetes.io serves a styled "404 Page not found" page with full site navigation, so a browser appears to load something, just not the DNS documentation. Updated to `https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/dns-pod-service/`.

`test/e2e_node/garbage_collector_test.go` has the same problem in the comment above the `GarbageCollect` test, which cites the Kubelet garbage collection policy at `http://kubernetes.io/docs/admin/garbage-collection/`. Also HTTP 404. Updated to `https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/garbage-collection/`, which is the current page and covers the node-level container and image cleanup this test exercises.

`staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/docs/maintainers/MAINTAINERS.md` links the release planning template as `../template.md`. Relative to `docs/maintainers/`, that resolves to `docs/template.md`, which does not exist. The template is at `docs/roadmap/template.md`, so the link is off by one directory. Updated to `../roadmap/template.md`.

All three are comment and documentation changes only. No behavior changes and no code paths touched.

Fixes #142370

This touches three areas with different approvers, so it will need approval from sig-network for the DNS add-on README, sig-node for the e2e_node comment, and sig-cli for the kubectl maintainers doc. issues.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`NodeExpandVolume` passes `opts.newSize.Value()` as `CapacityRange.RequiredBytes`. `Value()` saturates at `math.MaxInt64` when the quantity does not fit an int64 and drops the `ok` bool from `AsScaledInt64`, so a size past int64 reaches the driver as `9223372036854775807` bytes, which is a byte count the request never named. The negative case was fixed in #141181 by switching to `Sign()`. This is the overflow end of the same check.

This reads the size through `AsScaledInt64(0)` and returns an error when `ok` is false, before the client is created and before the CSI call. `AsScaledInt64(0)` is what `Value()` already wraps, so the rounding and the result are unchanged for every size that fits. Only the overflow case changes, from a silently wrong request to an error.

`AsInt64()` would be the wrong accessor here. It returns `ok=false` for any `inf.Dec`-backed quantity, including representable ones, which would reject valid resizes.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Follow-up to #141181. Part of #141166.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The test case was already in tree from #142224, pinning the current behavior with `mustFail: false` and a `TODO(#141166)`. This flips it to `mustFail: true`. The neighbouring "with quantity of exactly MaxInt64 bytes" case stays `mustFail: false` and confirms the check does not reject sizes that do fit.

One thing worth a reviewer's opinion: the new error is a plain error, not a gRPC status, so `isInfeasibleError` in expander.go returns false for it and the resize is retried rather than being marked infeasible. That matches how the existing negative-size check directly above it behaves, so this PR keeps the two consistent, but a size past int64 can never succeed on retry. Happy to return an infeasible error for both checks in a follow-up if you would prefer that.

Verified locally with go1.27.1, matching .go-version:

* `go test ./pkg/volume/csi/...` passes.
* Reverting only the csi_client.go hunk makes `TestNodeExpandVolume` fail with "expected an error", so the test does exercise the change.
* `gofmt -l` and `go vet ./pkg/volume/csi/` are clean.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed an issue where resizing a CSI volume to a size too large to represent as an int64 number of bytes would send the driver a saturated byte count instead of failing.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs

```

Drafted with an AI coding assistant. I reviewed the change against the source before submitting, and the tests and linters were run locally.

/cc @jpbetz

issues.body:
Following the same pattern as #132312, for a different dependency.

`gopkg.in/inf.v0` is a **direct** dependency of `k8s.io/apimachinery`, where `inf.Dec` backs the arbitrary-precision path of `resource.Quantity`:

```go
type Quantity struct {
	// i is the quantity in int64 scaled form, if d.Dec == nil
	i int64Amount
	// d is the quantity in inf.Dec form if d.Dec != nil
	d infDecAmount
	...
}
```

It is also part of apimachinery's exported surface -- `func (q *Quantity) AsDec() *inf.Dec` and `func NewDecimalQuantity(b inf.Dec, format Format) *Quantity`, so it is compiled into essentially every Go program that talks to a Kubernetes API server, not only Kubernetes itself.

## What I am not claiming

There is no CVE (OSV reports zero for `gopkg.in/inf.v0`), no bug report, and no urgency. The package is 760 lines across `dec.go` and `rounder.go`, has **no external dependencies at all**, just `math/big`, `fmt`, `io`, `strings`, and uses neither `unsafe` nor `reflect`. Decimal arithmetic is a stable problem, and "no commits since 2018" is not by itself alarming for code of this shape. This is materially lower-risk than the json-iterator situation in #132312, and I do not think it should be treated with the same urgency.

I am also not proposing removal. `inf.Dec` is in a GA Go API on one of the most widely used types in the ecosystem, so removing it would need `k8s.io/apimachinery/v2`. That is not what this issue is asking for.

## What the actual concern is

It is bus factor, not code quality. As far as I can tell there is currently nobody able to publish a release under this import path:

- Last commit: **2018-03-27**. Last release: **v0.9.1, 2018-03-26**. Only two versions were ever tagged.
- Sole author is Péter Surányi (`@speter`, per the LICENSE copyright line); the only other commit in the repo's history is a one-line `gofmt` change from 2017. His last authored commit in any public repo is **2020-03-28**.
- The **`go-inf` organisation has zero public members**, no org email, and one repo. It was created in 2015 purely to back this vanity import path after Google Code shut down (see #26231). The original `speter.net` domain no longer resolves.
- [go-inf/inf#8](https://github.com/go-inf/inf/issues/8), "is it EOL ?", has been **open and unanswered since 2023-01-11**.
- [go-inf/inf#9](https://github.com/go-inf/inf/pull/9) was closed by its own author the day it was opened, unmerged, with no maintainer response.

So if a fix is ever genuinely needed under this path, a Go compatibility break, or an arithmetic bug found by the ongoing `Quantity` work, there is presently no mechanism to ship one, and downstream cannot route around it because the import path is in a public API.

I have tried the obvious things first: commented on go-inf/inf#8 on September, 05, 2026, and emailed the address in the repo's git history on September, 21, 2026. No response to either as of filing.

## The question

At what point, if any, is it worth acting on this proactively rather than waiting to need a fix we cannot ship? Roughly in increasing order of effort:

1. Someone with karma reaches Péter successfully and a maintainer gets added to `go-inf`, cheapest by far, and non-breaking, since the import path is unchanged.
2. Kubernetes adopts the package under an owned path, as was done for `google/gofuzz` → `sigs.k8s.io/randfill` and the `go-yaml` fork → `go.yaml.in/yaml`. The license is BSD-3, so this needs no one's permission, but note it is still a breaking Go API change, because `AsDec()` would return a different named type.
3. Deprecate `AsDec`/`NewDecimalQuantity` now and drop the dependency at a hypothetical apimachinery v2. Cleanest, slowest.

"The risk is acceptable, leave it alone" is a perfectly good answer too — I would just like it to be a decision on the record rather than something nobody has looked at. Happy to do the legwork on any of these if it is useful.

cc @thockin (you have both `dep-approvers` and `pkg/api/resource` hats, and may remember the 2016 `speter.net` migration) @dims (you filed #132312) @jpbetz (flagging so this does not surprise the `Quantity` burndown in #141166 — this issue is not a proposal to change that code)

/sig architecture
/sig api-machinery
/area dependency
/kind cleanup

issues.body:
IIUC, CPUs are assigned during the admission stage when allocating a pod resize. During upsize, this is not a problem, but when downsizing the unallocated CPUs are returned to the available pool before the runtime has actually updated the container. This could cause a race condition where those CPUs are assigned to a different pod before the previous pod has actually released them.

I think CPU manager needs to track not-yet-released CPUs separately from what's been allocated to ensure they aren't reassigned before they're released.

/sig node
/assign @esotsal 
/cc @ffromani @natasha41575

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

issues.body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140387 changed resize to happen before containers are started.

If resize fails, it adds the error to the sync result, but then proceeds with starting containers. This could cause resource oversubscription or OOMs if the resize was supposed to free up resources for the starting containers.

I'm not sure what the right way to handle this is. The simplest solution would be to simply return early and skip starting containers if the resize failed, but this could cause container start to be blocked indefinitely if, for example, a memory decrease was blocked by the usage > new limit check.

One possible solution is to look at the resource budget after the resize partial failure: actual pod-level limits - actual container requests (??), and only start the new containers that are budgeted for. But this approach breaks down in burstable pods, or burstable containers within a PLR envelope.

The solution requires more thought.

/kind bug
/area kubelet
/sig node
/assign @natasha41575
