issues.title: Pull images used in volumes with type=image
issues.body:
## Description
When running `docker compose pull`, images referenced in volume mounts with
`type=image` were not being pulled. Only the main service images (`service.Image`)
were considered.
The `pullRequiredImages()` function (used by `docker compose up`) already handled
this case by iterating through service volumes and creating fake `ServiceConfig`
entries for volume images. However, the `pull()` function (used by `docker compose pull`)
did not have this logic.
This adds the same volume image discovery to the `pull()` function so that
`docker compose pull` also pulls images referenced in `type=image` volume mounts.
## Changes
- **`pkg/compose/pull.go`**: Added a loop in `pull()` that iterates each service's
  volumes, checks for `type=image`, deduplicates against `imagesBeingPulled`, and
  queues them for pulling via `pullServiceImage()`.
## How to test
```yaml
services:
  nginx:
    image: "nginx:alpine"
    volumes:
      - type: image
        source: mattfly/obsidian:latest
        target: /srv/http/ObsidianIRC
        image:
          subpath: usr/share/nginx/html/
```
Fixes #13809

issues.title: fix: avoid JSON serialization error in res.status for BigInt values
issues.body:
When `res.status()` or `res.sendStatus()` received a BigInt (or other values that JSON.stringify cannot serialize), the error message construction would throw:
```
TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt
    at JSON.stringify (<anonymous>)
```

This obscured the actual intended error message about invalid status code. The fix replaces `JSON.stringify()` with `String()` in error messages to safely convert any value to a string representation.

**Before:**
```js
res.sendStatus(200n)
// throws: TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt
```

**After:**
```js
res.sendStatus(200n)
// throws: TypeError: Invalid status code: 200. Status code must be an integer.
```

Fixes #6756

issues.title: fix: preserve original Content-Type value when mime.contentType returns false
issues.body:
When `res.set('Content-Type', value)` is called with an unrecognized type (where `mime.contentType()` returns `false`), the header was being set to the literal string `'false'` instead of preserving the original value. This was inconsistent with `res.type()` which handles unknown types properly by defaulting to application/octet-stream.

**Before:**
```js
res.set('Content-Type', 'some-custom-type')
// Sets header: Content-Type: false
```

**After:**
```js
res.set('Content-Type', 'some-custom-type')
// Sets header: Content-Type: some-custom-type
```

Known types like `'html'` still get properly resolved to their full MIME type with charset when applicable.

Fixes #7034

issues.title: fix: handle view names ending in '.' without throwing opaque TypeError
issues.body:
When a view name ends with a dot (e.g., `'index.'`), `path.extname()` returns `'.'` which is truthy, causing the code to skip the default engine extension logic. This resulted in `require('')` being called, throwing an opaque `TypeError` synchronously instead of passing a proper lookup error to the callback.

**Changes:**
1. In `lib/view.js`: Treat extension `'.'` the same as no extension - fall back to using the default view engine
2. In `lib/application.js`: Wrap the `View` constructor call in try/catch to ensure all errors are passed to the callback instead of throwing synchronously

**Before:**
```js
app.render('index.', cb)
// throws synchronously: TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE]: The argument 'id' must be a non-empty string. Received ''
```

**After:**
```js
app.render('index.', cb)
// callback receives normal 'Failed to lookup view "index."' error
```

Fixes #7350

issues.title: fix: handle raw ArrayBuffer in res.send()
issues.body:
Raw ArrayBuffer instances were falling through to JSON serialization, sending an empty object `{}` instead of binary data. This adds an `instanceof ArrayBuffer` check alongside the existing `Buffer.isBuffer` and `ArrayBuffer.isView` checks to properly handle ArrayBuffer as binary with Content-Type application/octet-stream.

```js
res.send(new ArrayBuffer(10))
// Before: sends {} (Content-Type: application/json)
// After: sends 10 zero bytes (Content-Type: application/octet-stream)
```

ArrayBuffer is the standard binary type used by fetch, Web Crypto, WebSocket, FileReader, and similar web APIs.

Fixes #7362

issues.title: fix(res.send): add Content-Length only if Transfer-Encoding is not present
issues.body:
> **Context:** this is the 4.x branch missing what master already carries. #4893 stopped adding Content-Length next to Transfer-Encoding in june and #7459 kept the etag working while doing it, both merged on master, neither ever landed here

## What is the current behavior?

when res.send() runs with a Transfer-Encoding header already set it still adds Content-Length next to it. RFC 9110 section 8.6 says a server must not send Content-Length in a response with Transfer-Encoding, and node's own http client refuses to parse such a response

raw response from untouched 4.22.3 (origin/4.x 899b5249), Transfer-Encoding set by the app, body and etag untouched:

```
PROBE | HTTP/1.1 200 OK
PROBE | X-Powered-By: Express
PROBE | Transfer-Encoding: chunked
PROBE | Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
PROBE | Content-Length: 5
PROBE | ETag: W/"5-qvTGHdzF6KLavt4PO0gs2a6pQ00"
```

a node client on the same wire fails before the body is even read:

```
Error: Parse Error: Content-Length can't be present with Transfer-Encoding
    code: 'HPE_INVALID_CONTENT_LENGTH'
```

so any node client hitting an express 4.x app that sets Transfer-Encoding (a streaming proxy handler, a gateway mixin, anything forwarding the hop-by-hop header) gets a connection level error on every response

### Steps to reproduce

1. npx mocha test/res.send.js on 4.x with the fix reverted, the test in "when Transfer-Encoding is set"
2. Expected: no Content-Length on the wire, body and ETag exactly as before
3. Actual (raw output on untouched 4.x): 1 failing, Error: Parse Error: Content-Length can't be present with Transfer-Encoding

## What is the new behavior?

the body length is still calculated on every path because the automatic ETag depends on it, that is the exact regression #7459 fixed on master, so only the header write is guarded:

```js
// Because Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding can't be present in the response headers together,
// Content-Length should be added only if there is no Transfer-Encoding header
if (!this.get('Transfer-Encoding')) {
  this.set('Content-Length', len);
}
```

same wire probe on the fixed branch:

```
PROBE | HTTP/1.1 200 OK
PROBE | Transfer-Encoding: chunked
PROBE | Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
PROBE | ETag: W/"5-qvTGHdzF6KLavt4PO0gs2a6pQ00"
PROBE Transfer-Encoding present: true | Content-Length present: false
```

204, 205 and 304 paths are untouched (they manage their own headers), HEAD responses keep skipping the body, and the full test run passes with the one new test proving the guard

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

issues.title: perf: memoise the Content-Type resolution in res.set, res.type and setCharset
issues.body:
A response sets one of a handful of content types, and each of them goes through the mime database (`mime.contentType` in `res.set` and `res.type`) and, for a string body, through content-type's parse and format (`setCharset` in `res.send`). Profiled under load with autocannon, that is about 1.9 us per `res.json` and 0.9 us per `res.send` of a string, the largest cost in Express's own code after the prototype switch in `app.handle`.

This memoises both by their input, in maps capped at 100 entries. Same output for the same input, nothing observable changes. `setCharset` on the json type goes from 470 ns to 11. The cache for `setCharset` is a map per charset: a key made by joining the two strings measured 240 ns, since the joined string is hashed again on every call.

Self time per request, node 26, before and after: `res.json` route, mime.contentType 400 ns, content-type parse 280-315, parseParameters 255-303, format 218-291, skipValue 270, setCharset 233, charset 218, after only setCharset at 11 ns; `res.send("Hello World")`, mime.contentType 264-330, charset 190-207, lookup 154-159, res.type 314-384, after res.type at 132-178.

This is the same memoisation I did in [fulmine.js](https://github.com/nigrosimone/fulmine.js), an Express 5 replacement on uWebSockets.js that keeps the API, where `mime.contentType` measured 273 ns a response and 6 memoised. It applies here as it is, since `res.set` and `res.send` see the same handful of types.

issues.title: Open redirect regression in res.location() — reintroduces CVE-2024-29041 [Severity: Medium]
fix: acceptParams truncates quoted values containing a semicolon
issues.body:
`res.format()` normalizes its keys through `acceptParams()` in `lib/utils.js`, which parses each `;`-separated parameter by scanning for the next raw `;` to know where the value ends. That breaks when the value is a quoted string that legitimately contains a `;`, e.g.:

    text/plain; foo="a;b"; bar=baz

Right now this parses `foo` as `"a` and silently drops the rest (`b"`), because the parser has no idea it's inside quotes when it hits that semicolon. I ran into this while poking around `res.format()` and figured it was worth fixing properly rather than patching around it.

The fix adds a small helper, `indexOfUnquoted()`, that walks the string and ignores delimiters found inside a quoted span (also handles an escaped `\"` so it doesnt end the quote early), and swap it in for the one `indexOf(';')` call that needed it. Everything else about `acceptParams` is untouched — same behavior for plain types, missing `=`, malformed params, etc.

Added two tests in `test/utils.js` covering the quoted-semicolon case and the escaped-quote case. Ran the full suite locally (1263 passing) and lint is clean.

issues.title: deps: bump qs minimum to 6.16.0
issues.body:
## Summary

Raises the minimum `qs` version from `^6.15.2` to `^6.16.0` so installs can no longer resolve to a release affected by two recently published advisories, both patched in `qs@6.16.0`:

| Advisory | CVE | Severity | Affected range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) — Denial of Service via attacker-controlled `isBuffer` | CVE-2026-82417 | medium | `>= 2.2.5, < 6.16.0` |
| [GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx) — array-limit bypass via bracket-key comma parsing | CVE-2026-82562 | medium | `>= 6.14.2, <= 6.15.3` |

The existing `^6.15.2` range already permits 6.16.0, so fresh installs pick up the fix; this change guarantees it for consumers with older resolved versions, following the same approach as #7305 and #7057.

## Testing

- `npm ls qs` resolves to `qs@6.16.0` (deduped across `supertest`/`superagent`/`formidable`)
- `npm test`: 1261 passing
- `npm run lint`: clean

## What's included in the `History.md`

```markdown
5.3.0
=====

## 🐞 Bug fixes

- Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by [@YuryShkoda](https://github.com/YuryShkoda) in [#4893](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/4893)


    Fixed the behavior of `res.send()` to prevent conflicts between `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` HTTP headers in responses. The `Content-Length` header in `res.send()` is now only added when a `Transfer-Encoding` header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response

* Upgrade `qs` to `^6.15.2`, which fixes [CVE-2026-2391](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-2391) ([GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883](https://github.com/ljharb/qs/security/advisories/GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883)): an `arrayLimit` bypass in comma parsing allowed a denial of service via arbitrarily large arrays in the query string - by [@davetashner](https://github.com/davetashner) in [#7057](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7057) and [@cyphercodes](https://github.com/cyphercodes) in [#7305](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7305)

## 🚀 Improvements

* Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. `req.fresh` previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by [@Cherry](https://github.com/Cherry) in [#7366](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7366)

    ```js
    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
    app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
      res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
      res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
    });
    ```

* Improve HTML structure in `res.redirect()` responses when HTML format is accepted by adding `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<title>`, and `<body>` tags for better browser compatibility - by [@Bernice55231](https://github.com/Bernice55231) in [#5167](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/5167)

* When calling `app.render` with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by [AkaHarshit](https://github.com/AkaHarshit) in [#6903](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/6903)

    ```js
    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected
    ```

* Upgrade `content-type` to `^2.0.0`, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker `Content-Type` parsing/formatting in `res.send()`) along with a behavior change: `res.send()` now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a `Content-Type` that fails to parse. `type-is` is upgraded to `^2.1.0` as part of the same change - by [@blakeembrey](https://github.com/blakeembrey) in [#7234](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7234)

    ```js
    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
    // -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8
    ```

* The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as `Error.cause` and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's `parent`/`original`) are no longer swallowed - by [@Nitin-Mohapatra](https://github.com/Nitin-Mohapatra) in [#6464](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/6464)

* Upgrade `content-disposition` to `^2.0.0`, which changes the `Content-Disposition` header emitted by `res.download()`, `res.attachment()`, and `res.sendFile()`: file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by [@blakeembrey](https://github.com/blakeembrey) in [#7233](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7233)

    ```js
    res.attachment('user.html');
    // before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
    // after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html
    ```

* Upgrade `body-parser` to `^2.3.0`, which fixes [CVE-2026-12590](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12590) ([GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6](https://github.com/expressjs/body-parser/security/advisories/GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6)): an invalid `limit` option value caused request body size enforcement to be silently disabled (fail-open), allowing a denial of service via arbitrarily large payloads. Invalid `limit` values now throw at parser initialization instead of being ignored - by [@Mayvis](https://github.com/Mayvis) in [#7390](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7390)

## ⚡ Performance

* Avoid duplicate Content-Type header processing in `res.send()` when sending string responses without an explicit Content-Type header - by [@bjohansebas](https://github.com/bjohansebas) in [#6991](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/6991)

issues.title: fix(res.send): preserve bytes when sending DataView
issues.body:
`res.send(new DataView(buffer))` returned HTTP 200 with `Content-Length: 0` and an empty body. `res.send(new Uint8Array(buffer))` on the same bytes sent the payload.

`ArrayBuffer.isView` is true for DataView, so the value is treated as binary. The length path then uses `chunk.length` / `Buffer.from(chunk, encoding)`. DataView has no `.length` (only `.byteLength`), and `Buffer.from(dataView)` is an empty Buffer.

This copies non-Buffer views with `Buffer.from(view.buffer, view.byteOffset, view.byteLength)`. Existing `Buffer` and `Uint8Array` behavior is unchanged.

This does not change bare `ArrayBuffer` (still sent as `{}` JSON). That is covered by #7362.

Tests: `test/res.send.js` for a full DataView and a sliced DataView.

issues.body: ## Summary - allow the documented `null` overrides for `env.Request` and `env.Response` in ESM and CommonJS declarations - add strict type regressions for both module modes - document the fix in the pre-release changelog ## Testing - ESM fetch type regression: passed - CJS fetch type regression (TypeScript 4.9): passed - full ESM module suite: 9 passed - full CJS module suite: 7 passed with one unrelated timeout; the isolated timed-out test passed on rerun --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Fixes the `env.Request` and `env.Response` TypeScript declarations so they accept `null`, matching the documented runtime behavior that lets consumers disable those fetch environment constructors. Previously the types required a constructor, so passing `null` failed type checks even though it is supported at runtime. - Allow `null` overrides for both fetch environment constructors in the ESM (`index.d.ts`) and CommonJS (`index.d.cts`) declarations. - Add strict type regressions in both module test suites. - Record the fix in the pre-release changelog. ## Docs No documentation updates needed; this change brings the declarations in line with the existing documented `null` overrides. ## Testing Added type regressions covering `axios.create()` with `Request: null` and `Response: null` in the ESM and CommonJS fetch type helpers. ESM types, CommonJS types (TypeScript 4.9), and both full module suites passed; the single CJS failure was an unrelated timeout that passed on rerun. ## Semantic version impact Patch. The change only widens the existing optional env types to also accept `null`; it does not alter runtime behavior or break existing consumers. issues.title: fix(headers): honor function, string and RegExp rewrite matchers in set()
issues.body:
## Summary AxiosHeaders#set only looked at rewrite === true and rewrite === undefined, so a function, string or RegExp rewrite was treated like false and the header was never overwritten. this runs the matcher through matchHeaderValue, same as has() and delete(), and overwrites when it accepts the current value. true, false and undefined behave exactly like before, and every internal call in lib passes false or nothing so nothing inside axios changes. ## Linked issue Closes #11247 ## Changes - lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js: call the rewrite matcher in setHeader - tests/unit/axiosHeaders.test.js: function, RegExp, string and setContentType cases - PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md: bug fix entry #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (no change needed, README and index.d.ts already describe this) - [x] No breaking changes --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Fixes `AxiosHeaders#set` (and the `set
` accessors) so a function, string, or RegExp `rewrite` argument is honored as documented instead of being treated like `false`. Previously such a matcher meant the header was never overwritten; now the matcher runs through `matchHeaderValue` and the header is overwritten only when it accepts the current value. `true`, `false`, and `undefined` behave exactly as before, and no internal call passes anything but `false` or nothing, so nothing inside axios changes. Closes #11247. ## Docs No documentation changes needed — `README` and `index.d.ts` already describe this behavior. ## Testing Added tests covering function, RegExp, and string matchers plus the `setContentType` accessor case. ## Semantic version impact Patch change — bug fix with no breaking changes. Written for commit 51a27e3bc7f7cc6a800ff347258c8a911641e048. Summary will update on new commits.

fix(http): reject negative timeouts instead of crashing the process
issues.body:
## Summary

A negative `timeout` passes the Node HTTP adapter's NaN-only check and reaches `req.setTimeout()`, which Node rejects with `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`:

- With the default transport (follow-redirects), the `RangeError` is thrown from a socket callback, outside the request promise, as an **uncaught exception that crashes the process**.
- With `maxRedirects: 0`, it surfaces as a raw `RangeError` instead of an `AxiosError`.

This is easy to hit in practice, e.g. `timeout: deadline - Date.now()` after the deadline has already passed.

```js
await axios.get(url, { timeout: -1 });
// RangeError [ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE]: The value of "msecs" is out of range. It must be a non-negative finite number. Received -1
//     at RedirectableRequest.destroyOnTimeout (follow-redirects/index.js:222)
// -> uncaughtException, process exits
```

This PR validates the timeout before the request is created and rejects with `AxiosError` / `ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE`, next to the existing `httpVersion` option checks, so no connection is opened.

## Linked issue

No existing issue. Earlier attempts to validate timeouts globally (#7444, #7436, #7429) were closed as stale or targeted the wrong branch, and none covered the process crash. This change is intentionally scoped to the Node HTTP adapter, where the crash happens, so XHR/fetch behavior is unchanged.

## Changes

- `lib/adapters/http.js`: reject a negative `timeout`, including fractional values such as `-0.5` (checked with `parseFloat` so they are not truncated to `-0`), with `AxiosError` `ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE` before the request is created. The existing NaN check and non-negative timeout behavior are unchanged.
- `tests/unit/adapters/http.test.js`: regression test covering `-1`, `-0.5`, and `"-1"` on both the follow-redirects path and `maxRedirects: 0`. It also asserts that the server receives no request.
- `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`: Bug Fixes entry.

## Validation

Node v26.7.0, npm 11.19.0, macOS (darwin). Run with the existing `node_modules`, not a fresh `npm ci`.

- New test without the fix: fails with an uncaught `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` from `follow-redirects/index.js:222`, as expected.
- `npm run test:vitest:unit -- tests/unit/adapters/http.test.js`: 247/247 passed (re-run after f3f15393).
- `npm run lint`: passed.
- `npm run build`: passed.
- `npm run test:vitest:unit`: 58 files, 1076/1076 passed.
- Standalone repro against a local server: `-1`, `-0.5`, `"-0.5"`, and `"-5abc"` now reject with `AxiosError` `ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE`, with 0 open connections, on both transport paths.
- `npm run test:vitest:browser:headless`: not run. The change is confined to the Node-only HTTP adapter (`lib/adapters/http.js`), which browser builds do not load.
- Module/smoke suites: not applicable. There are no packaging, export, or type changes.

## Compatibility and documentation

- Semver: patch. A negative `timeout` used to crash the process or reject with a raw `RangeError`; it now rejects with `AxiosError`. Valid timeouts are unaffected.
- Environments: Node HTTP adapter only. XHR and fetch are unchanged.
- No public API or type changes, so no `index.d.ts`, `index.d.cts`, or `PRE_RELEASE_DOCS.md` update is needed.

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason)
- [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`): N/A, no public API change

Updates `multer` from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0
Release notes

Sourced from multer's releases.

v2.4.0

Highlights

multer finally supports Google Cloud Functions and Firebase 🎉

These platforms read the request body before your code runs, so multer's classic req.pipe(busboy) received nothing: empty req.body, empty req.files, and nearly a decade of duplicated issues.

The new streamHandler option closes that gap: you decide how the body reaches the parser, so the pre-read rawBody just works (see image).

const multer = require('multer')

const upload = multer({

storage: multer.memoryStorage(),

streamHandler: (req, busboy) => {

// Cloud Functions / Firebase expose the pre-read body here

if (req.rawBody) busboy.end(req.rawBody)

else req.pipe(busboy)

}

})


app.post('/upload', upload.single('file'), (req, res) => {

res.json({ name: req.file.originalname, size: req.file.size })

})

This landed thanks to community PRs going back to 2017; their authors are credited as co-authors in the release.

issues.title: fix: align request handling across runtimes (v0.x)

labels.name: commit::fix
labels.description: The PR is related to a bugfix

labels.name: v0x
labels.description: Version 0

issues.body:
### Summary

Align request option resolution, encoded body size accounting, and form serialization on v0.x. Streamed uploads honor the configured byte limit across transports, and data URL size checks follow the decoder's encoding rules, including bare `data:base64,...` metadata.

- Preserve live native agent options, pool controls, and custom connection/pool-name hooks when selecting or reusing a direct connection pool. Only the selected protocol's agent is adapted, including redirects; supported hooks retain their configured receiver, and the configured agent's `destroy()` cleans up its direct pool. Cached direct pools remain selected after public proxy options are removed or replaced.
- Validate enumerable custom-object parameter roots consistently before merging while retaining the existing treatment of nested custom values. Validation uses `WeakMap` or `Map` where available; legacy runtimes use bounded ancestry scans and a fixed-size cache without mutating caller objects. Array validation checks canonical numeric elements, including hidden and inherited slots, and ignores named metadata.
- Unwrap hidden and inherited array-like numeric indexes, including terminal null-prototype parents, preserve sparse arrays, and retain noncanonical numeric form field names through JSON serialization. Define collection outputs and traversal state as own properties so inherited read-only numeric slots do not block conversion or multipart serialization.
- Copy `FileList` values by index without relying on host-object property reflection, and convert direct file collections before multipart iteration. Conversion returns `null` for unavailable indexed values so incomplete collections follow the existing unconverted-value path instead of emitting a partial list.
- Keep affected browser helpers compatible with ES5 number/reflection APIs and independent of property enumeration order.
- Isolate and restore process proxy settings in native proxy tests.

Compatibility notes: params deeper than 100 levels reject with `ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE`; sparse or noncanonical numeric form indexes serialize as keyed objects. On runtimes with native environment proxy support, `proxy: false` uses a direct pool with the configured native options, current public pool controls, and supported connection/key hooks. Agents overriding native pool-management or TLS-session lifecycle hooks reject with `ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE`; use an agent constructed without `proxyEnv` for these configurations. Plain subclasses remain supported. Public type signatures are unchanged.

### Related issue

N/A.

### Testing

- Full-suite baseline at `d111e26a`: `npm run build` and `npm test` pass on Node 24.18.0: source lint, **490 Node tests**, **752 Chrome/Firefox tests**, and declaration checks.
- Latest test-helper update: 48 focused serialization cases pass on both Node 24.18.0 and Node 16.20.2. New cases verify preparation of externally created VM contexts and reuse without wrapping reflection APIs again. The new supplied-context case failed before the fix.
- Prior focused Node 16.20.2 checks pass: four custom-root cases including the generated `postForm` shortcut and seven routing/agent cases with 33 native-proxy capability skips.
- Forty focused Node 24 routing/agent cases pass with `NODE_OPTIONS` and `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` unset. Native-proxy cases explicitly configure `proxyEnv` on each agent, so the gate checks capability rather than startup enablement. The edited-options case explicitly checks that a direct pool was selected.
- Pool-key regressions verify separate sockets across custom keys and reuse within a matching key, including own and inherited hooks with private receiver state. Unsupported lifecycle hooks reject before dispatch and are checked again on cached selections.
- Legacy validation checks use frozen, wide, shared, and circular parameter graphs with bounded instrumentation; individual identity scans remain bounded as input width grows. Cache eviction can revisit shared subgraphs.
- File collection checks cover omitted/throwing host reflection, missing/null/undefined indexed values, single-read getters, empty collections, direct and default multipart transforms, and native browser `FileList` values.
- Array checks cover ignored named metadata, hidden/inherited numeric elements, shadowing, sparse arrays, and existing depth/cycle validation.
- Isolated legacy cases exercise read-only inherited numeric slots with utility and serializer code in the same realm, including file collections, mutable output descriptors, and nested metadata. Large-length cases distinguish incomplete coverage from unrepresentable lengths.
- Browser and isolated legacy cases cover null-prototype inheritance, ordinary intrinsic prototype exclusion, absent modern Number methods/identity maps, and ES5 reflection behavior.
- Changed source parses as ES5 and changed tests as ES2019; whitespace checks pass. Actual IE and Node 12 runtime checks were unavailable on this host.

labels.name: v1x

issues.body:
## Summary

Align request option resolution, body size accounting, and form serialization across Node and browser adapters. Configured limits use encoded byte counts, while uploads retain their routing, contents, explicit multipart boundaries, and progress behavior.

## Linked issue

N/A.

## Changes

- Count encoded stream bytes across HTTP transports and calculate multipart sizes from fields and Blob/File sizes before constructing the upload body. Honor configured `env.Blob` constructors, including custom runtimes without a global Blob, and keep adapter caches separate for distinct constructors. The generic multipart helper receives a boundary and Blob implementation; core selects the cryptographic random source and translates serialization failures into Axios errors.
- Align data URL size estimates with each adapter's decoding behavior, preserve unlimited stream chunking, and verify output across rate accounting windows.
- Normalize redirect/proxy routing and same-origin URL resolution. The HTTP adapter owns direct-agent creation, caching, and cleanup. Direct agents follow the selected protocol, preserve connection and pool-name hooks with their configured receiver, and close their pooled sockets when the configured agent is destroyed. Unsupported pool-management and TLS-session lifecycle overrides reject before dispatch, including when selecting a cached pool.
- Merge parameters iteratively, inspect only defaults that contribute to the result, and leave depth policy to the configured serializer, including custom serializers and `maxDepth: Infinity`. Core owns parameter validation and its Axios error behavior. String-keyed parameters and config merges remain supported without symbol-reflection APIs. Cycle checks inspect retained fields, including reserved data properties on shallow array elements, without evaluating reserved-name accessors.
- Preserve hidden and inherited array-like indexes, reject incomplete array-like shapes, and retain numeric form field names that cannot be array indexes.
- Keep shared test utilities, including the bounded child-process runner, in `tests/setup`. Failed child runs retain captured stdout/stderr on the original error, including partial output and termination metadata. Reuse the adapter runtime-support predicate in agent tests and verify generated multipart boundaries use the supplied random source and have valid output. Record user-visible behavior in the pre-release changelog.

Compatibility notes: circular parameters reject with `ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE`; sparse or non-index numeric form fields serialize as keyed objects. On runtimes with native environment proxy support, `proxy: false` uses a direct pool with the configured native options, connection hook, and pool-name hook. Unsupported pool-management or TLS-session lifecycle overrides reject with `ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE`; those agents must be constructed without `proxyEnv`. Fetch multipart uploads needing size accounting, progress tracking, or an explicit boundary use a sized Blob with a matching boundary. Generated boundaries require a cryptographic random source. Public type signatures are unchanged.

## Testing

- `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass on Node 24.18.0.
- Latest multipart/core separation: **160 focused unit tests pass** across Fetch, multipart body length, and parameter merging. The shared multipart suite also passes **147 checks across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit**, with three existing Node-only random-source skips.
- Node 16.20.2: **28 parameter-merge cases pass**; direct multipart checks confirm generated/explicit boundaries, exact size limits, caller error identity, and unchanged Axios error codes. The symbol-reflection test restores the builtin before any assertions; a forced failure retains its original AssertionError diagnostics.
- Full-suite baseline at `214305bf`: **1,285 unit tests** and **783 browser tests** passed, with three existing Node-only random-source skips.
- Existing coverage includes custom Blob selection and cache separation, missing global Blob, upload progress, symbol-reflection fallback, custom pool keys and receiver state, unsupported lifecycle hooks, and combined active/free socket accounting.
- Shared data URL checks compare supported whitespace processing with native Fetch and verify exact response limits across Node and all three browsers. Existing `postForm`, promise rejection, and inherited absolute-URL-default checks pass.
- New generic-helper cases verify serialization using supplied dependencies without runtime random sources, generic validation failures, core error translation, and caller-supplied size errors.
- Formatting and diff whitespace checks pass; files changed in the latest refactor parse as ES2019. Actual Node 12 runtime checks were unavailable locally.

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated.
- [x] Docs/types reviewed; pre-release changelog updated and no public type signature changes.
- [x] Compatibility changes called out above.

issues.title: fix(fetch): cancel ReadableStream body after response stream capability probe
issues.body: ## Summary The `supportsResponseStream` probe reads `new Response('').body` and never cancels it, so the stream's pull promise stays pending for the life of the realm. Same defect [#7515](https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/7515) fixed in the request probe; that shipped in 1.14.0 and left this one behind. Cancelling it takes a 256-file suite I run from 89 axios-attributed leaks down to 4 under Vitest's `--detect-async-leaks`. Repro: [bdcarr/axios-fetch-probe-leak](https://github.com/bdcarr/axios-fetch-probe-leak). ## Linked issue Closes https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/11240 ## Changes - cancel the response probe body once support has been read - both probes now share a `cancelProbeBody` helper that makes cleanup best-effort - tests in `tests/unit/adapters/fetch.test.js`, changelog entry The helper is the one part that goes past the issue as filed, so it's worth explaining. `isReadableStream` is a `toStringTag` check rather than a structural one, so a custom `env.Request`/`env.Response` can expose a stream-like body with no working `cancel`. On Node 22 a native body always fulfils, so this only bites injected implementations, but I'd rather the bare `cancel()` didn't reach them: - a `cancel()` that throws synchronously escapes into `test()`, which turns it into `false`, silently downgrading a capability that was previously detected as supported - a `cancel()` that rejects produces an unhandled rejection The existing request probe has both of these today, which is why the helper is shared rather than applied only to the new code. Happy to split that half out if you'd rather keep this PR to the response probe. On the tests: the response-probe one stubs `env.Response` rather than spying on `ReadableStream.prototype.cancel`, because the request probe already calls that method and a prototype spy passes with or without the fix. issues.title: fetch adapter: response-stream capability probe leaks an uncancelled ReadableStream
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

The fetch adapter's `supportsResponseStream` capability probe creates a `ReadableStream` and never cancels it, leaking one pending promise per module realm.

This is the sibling of #7515, which fixed the same defect in the `supportsRequestStream` probe. That fix shipped in 1.14.0; the response probe was not covered and still leaks in 1.20.0.

```js
// lib/adapters/fetch.js
const supportsResponseStream =
  isResponseSupported &&
  isReadableStreamSupported &&
  test(() => utils.isReadableStream(new Response('').body));   // never cancelled
```

`new Response('').body` creates a `ReadableStream` whose internal pull pipeline is set up but never consumed or cancelled, so its pull promise stays pending for the lifetime of the realm — the mechanism described in #7515.

## Reproduction

https://github.com/bdcarr/axios-fetch-probe-leak

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm test        # vitest run --detect-async-leaks
```

The readme has more details about how the repro works, and a script to test before/after the proposed fix.

## Impact at scale

One leak per module realm means one per test file. On the 256-file suite in which I encountered this issue, counting only leaks whose stack originates in axios:

| axios | axios-attributed leaks |
| --- | --- |
| 1.13.2 (before #7515) | 182 |
| 1.20.0 (after #7515) | 89 |
| 1.20.0 + the change below | 4 |

Roughly one per file in each case — 1.13.2 leaks both probes, 1.20.0 only this one.

## Proposed fix

Mirror #7515: keep a reference to the probe body and cancel it once the capability has been read. With this applied the repro reports no leaks and the 256-file suite drops from 89 axios-attributed leaks to 4.

Worth doing the cleanup as an explicitly best-effort helper shared with the request probe, rather than the bare `probeBody.cancel()` the request probe uses today:

```js
const cancelProbeBody = (body) => {
  if (body == null) {
    return;
  }

  try {
    const cancelled = body.cancel();

    if (cancelled && isFunction(cancelled.then)) {
      cancelled.then(undefined, () => {});
    }
  } catch (e) {
    // Ignored: an uncancellable probe body only leaks, it is still a valid body.
  }
};
```

`isReadableStream` is a `toStringTag` check rather than a structural one, so a custom `env.Request`/`env.Response` can expose a stream-like body with no working `cancel`. Two things fall out of that, and both apply to the existing request probe as well as this one:

- a `cancel()` that throws synchronously escapes into `test()`, which turns it into `false`. So the naive fix silently downgrades a capability that was previously detected as supported.
- a `cancel()` that rejects produces an unhandled rejection, since the returned promise is dropped.

I checked both against Node 22. A native `new Response('').body.cancel()` always fulfils, so this only bites custom or polyfilled implementations, but `env.Response` is a supported injection point so it seems worth guarding.

## Environment

```
axios     1.20.0 (present since the probe was introduced; 1.13.2 leaks both probes)
Adapter   fetch
Vitest    4.1.11
Node      v22.16.0
OS        macOS 26.6.2 arm64
```

Here is your AI disclosure: :surfer: :)

Cleanup runs without blocking the original rejection, and a cleanup rejection is handled without replacing the size-limit error. ## Linked issue No existing issue found. issues.title: feat(retry): add adaptive request retry mechanism with exponential backoff and jitter

labels.name: commit::fix
labels.description: The PR is related to a bugfix

labels.name: v1x
labels.description: Version 1

issues.body: ### Summary This PR adds a native **Adaptive Request Retry Engine** to Axios with: 1. **Exponential Backoff with Jitter**: Configurable `backoffFactor`, `retryDelay`, `maxDelay`, and `jitter` (to mitigate thundering herd on server outages). 2. **`Retry-After` Header Parsing**: Parses both integer delta-seconds and HTTP-date header values to respect rate limits (`429 Too Many Requests` / `503 Service Unavailable`). 3. **Idempotent Method & Status Code Filtering**: Default retries for transient HTTP errors (`408`, `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, `504`) and network connectivity drops (`ECONNRESET`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `ENOTFOUND`, etc.) on idempotent methods. 4. **Lifecycle Callbacks & Predicates**: `onRetry(retryCount, error, config, delay)` for monitoring / telemetry and custom `shouldRetry(error, retryCount)` predicate. 5. **TypeScript Declarations**: Fully typed `AxiosRetryConfig` interface in `index.d.ts`. --- ### Motivation Request retries with exponential backoff and rate-limit compliance are an essential requirement in modern microservices and distributed systems. Providing a lightweight, battle-tested native retry interceptor eliminates the need for unmaintained third-party packages and ensures consistent retry semantics across browser and Node.js environments. --- ### Usage Example ```javascript import axios, { attachRetry } from 'axios'; // Attach retry to an axios instance const api = axios.create({ baseURL: 'https://api.example.com' }); attachRetry(api, { retries: 3, retryDelay: 1000, backoffFactor: 2, jitter: true, respectRetryAfter: true, onRetry: (count, error, config, delay) => { console.warn(`Retry attempt #${count} after ${delay}ms due to: ${error.message}`); } }); // Or enable per-request await api.get('/data', { retry: { retries: 5, retryDelay: 500 } }); ``` --- ### Verification * Added [`tests/unit/helpers/retry.test.js`](file:///C:/Users/Vijay/open_source_projects/agent2_repo/tests/unit/helpers/retry.test.js) (14 unit tests): - `parseRetryAfter`: integer seconds and HTTP-date parsing - `calculateRetryDelay`: exponential backoff, jitter, maxDelay caps, custom functions - `isRetryableError`: 5xx/429 status classification, non-retryable POST preservation, network error recovery, cancellation exclusion - `attachRetry`: multi-attempt recovery, retry exhaustion, explicit disable (`retry: false`) * Ran full Vitest unit test suite (`npm run test:vitest:unit`) — **all 96 test suites passed**. --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Adds a native retry engine to Axios with exponential backoff, jitter, and `Retry-After` header support, opt-in per instance or request. - Retries idempotent methods (`GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) on transient status codes (408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504) and common network errors. - Configurable via `retries`, `retryDelay`, `backoffFactor`, `maxDelay`, `jitter`, `respectRetryAfter`, custom `shouldRetry`, and `onRetry` callback. - Attach with `axios.attachRetry(instance, options)` or per-request `retry` config; disable with `retry: false`; default is 3 retries. - Adds typed `AxiosRetryConfig` / `AxiosRetryHelper` to `index.d.ts` and exports `retry` / `attachRetry` from `lib/axios.js`. - Backoff waits are abortable via cancel token or signal; aborting during backoff preserves the original abort reason, including `AxiosError`, `Error`, and string reasons. - Requests with stream bodies are not retried. - Provides built-in retry semantics, removing the need for third-party packages. - `Retry-After` parses both integer delta-seconds and HTTP-date header values. ## Docs Update `/docs/` with the retry config options and usage examples. ## Testing Adds 14 unit tests in `tests/unit/helpers/retry.test.js` covering header parsing, delay calculation, retry classification, interceptor integration, stream-body exclusion, abort during backoff, and abort reason preservation; full unit suite passes. ## Semantic version impact Additive feature, no breaking changes; minor version bump. Written for commit ec21e45a496c582a09ab4c121d4123886a164921. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.body: ## Summary When `Object.prototype[Symbol.iterator]` is polluted, Node.js/undici's internal header dispatch creates a plain `{}` for merged request headers and iterates it with `for...of`. issues.title: fix(helpers): treat explicit port 0 as a real port in shouldBypassProxy

labels.name: commit::fix
labels.description: The PR is related to a bugfix

labels.name: v1x
labels.description: Version 1

issues.body: ## Summary `shouldBypassProxy` used `value || fallback` to compute ports on both sides of the `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` comparison, which treats an explicit port `0` the same as "no port given" because `0` is falsy in JavaScript. This produces two incorrect outcomes: - A request URL with an explicit `:0` (e.g. `http://example.com:0/`) had its port silently replaced with the protocol's default port (80 for `http`), so it could incorrectly match a `NO_PROXY` entry scoped to that default port. - A `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` entry with an explicit `:0` (e.g. `example.com:0`) had its port requirement dropped entirely, so it matched a request to `example.com` on *any* port instead of only port `0`. Both were verified with small repro scripts against the current source before and after the fix. ## Linked issue None — found via manual code review, no existing issue. ## Changes - `lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js`: compute the request port from `parsed.port !== ''` instead of `Number.parseInt(parsed.port, 10) || ...`, since the WHATWG `URL` parser reports port `0` as the string `"0"` (truthy as a string, falsy once parsed to a number) and an unset/default-matching port as `""`. - `lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js`: change `parseNoProxyEntry`'s "no port in this entry" sentinel from `0` to `null` so an explicit `:0` in a `NO_PROXY` entry is distinguishable from "no port restriction". - `tests/unit/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.test.js`: added two regression tests covering both directions of the bug. - `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`: added a Bug Fixes entry per `AGENTS.md`. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) — N/A, internal helper, no public API change - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) :surfer: --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Makes `shouldBypassProxy` treat an explicit port `0` as a real port instead of "unset" on both sides of the `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` comparison. - Summary of changes - Previously a request URL with `:0` silently fell back to the protocol's default port (e.g. 80 for `http`), so it could incorrectly match a `NO_PROXY` entry scoped to that default port. Now the request port is read directly from the URL string. - Previously a `NO_PROXY` entry with an explicit `:0` had its port requirement dropped and matched every port. Now it restricts the bypass to port 0 only. - The "no port in this entry" sentinel changed from `0` to `null` so an explicit `:0` is distinguishable from "no port restriction". - Reasoning - Found via manual code review; no linked issue. ## Docs No documentation update needed — internal helper only, no public API change. ## Testing Added two regression tests covering both directions: a request URL with `:0` no longer matches a `NO_PROXY` entry for the default port, and a `NO_PROXY` entry with `:0` only matches requests to port 0. ## Semantic version impact Patch release. Bug fix only, no breaking changes. Written for commit 67e8126f00d118d2afa9cbb3ce46f36dbbf5a97a. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.title: fix(buildURL): reject nullish url instead of coercing it to an empty string

labels.name: commit::fix
labels.description: The PR is related to a bugfix

labels.name: v1x
labels.description: Version 1

issues.body:
## Summary

#10959 added `url = url || ''` to `buildURL` to stop a `TypeError` when params were passed with an undefined url. That guard also changed what a nullish url means. `axios.get(null, { params })` used to blow up before any request went out; since 1.18.1 it builds `?foo=bar`, which the browser resolves against the current page, so the app silently fires a request at itself.

The empty string is a legitimate relative url and should keep working. `null` and `undefined` are not, and they should not quietly become one. This restores the fail-fast behavior without bringing back the raw `TypeError`: a non-string url with params now throws an `AxiosError` carrying `ERR_INVALID_URL`, the same code `buildFullPath` already uses for unusable urls. Values such as `0`, `false` and a `URL` instance previously reached `url.indexOf` and died with a bare `TypeError`, so they are covered by the same check. A url that comes from `baseURL` alone is unaffected, since `combineURLs` has already turned it into a string by then.

Scope is deliberately limited to the params path, which is the part #10959 changed. `axios.get(null)` without params returns early at `if (!params)` and behaves exactly as it did before 1.18.1.

## Linked issue

Closes #11160

## Changes

- `lib/helpers/buildURL.js`: throw `AxiosError` / `ERR_INVALID_URL` for a non-string url instead of coercing it to `''`.
- `tests/unit/helpers/buildURL.test.js`: cover the rejection and keep the empty-string case explicit.
- `tests/unit/helpers/resolveConfig.test.js`: regression test for the reported path, a null url plus params no longer resolves to the current page.
- `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`: note the fix.

## Testing

- `npx eslint lib/helpers/buildURL.js`
- `npm run test:vitest:unit` — 58 files, 1,064 tests passed

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] No public API type change
- [x] Behavior change is intentional and restores pre-1.18.1 semantics for nullish urls

issues.body: ## Summary - `Axios#_request()` wrote `url` directly onto the `config` object passed by the caller when using the `axios(url, config)` shorthand (e.g. `axios('example/url', config)`), silently mutating an object the library does not own. - This is easy to hit by accident: `const shared = {...}; axios('/first', shared); axios('/second', shared);` leaves `shared.url` set to `'/second'` afterwards, even though the caller never asked for that field to be added. - Fixed by building a shallow copy (`config = { ...config, url: configOrUrl }`) instead of mutating in place, consistent with the project's existing "do not mutate config objects" convention used elsewhere in `mergeConfig`/`utils.merge`. ## Test plan - [x] Added a regression test in `tests/unit/axios.test.js` asserting the original `config` object is unchanged (no `url` key added) after `axios.request(url, config)`. - [x] `npm run test:vitest:unit` — full unit suite passes (one pre-existing, unrelated failure in `tests/unit/adapters/fetch.test.js` reproduces identically on `v1.x` without this change). - [x] `npx eslint lib/core/Axios.js tests/unit/axios.test.js` — clean. - [x] Added a `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md` entry under Bug Fixes. :surfer: --- ## Summary by cubic Prevents `axios(url, config)` from mutating the caller’s config object or triggering unsafe getters. issues.title: fix: various runtime crashes and type definition mismatches

labels.name: commit::fix
labels.description: The PR is related to a bugfix

issues.body: This PR fixes 14 issues found while auditing the codebase for inconsistencies between the source and type declarations, null-safety gaps, and a couple of edge cases that crash requests. Runtime fixes - cookies.js: decodeURIComponent throws on plain cookie values (not everyone URL-encodes them). Wrapped in try/catch. - fromDataURI.js: Was running decodeURIComponent on base64 data URIs, which corrupts the payload. Only decode when it's not base64. - toFormData.js: Custom Blob constructor passed via options was being used for the capability check but ignored when actually creating the Blob, always fell back to the global one. Also guards Buffer.from against missing global in non-Node environments. - composeSignals.js: Abort listeners were never auto-removed after firing. Added { once: true } so long-lived signals don't accumulate dead listeners. - buildURL.js: Crashes with TypeError when called with params but an undefined URL. Added a guard. - resolveConfig.js: encodeURIComponent explodes on lone surrogates in auth passwords. Also guards Object.entries against null from getHeaders(). - mergeConfig.js: mergeConfig(null, config) throws because hasOwnProperty.call(null, ...) isn't valid. Added the same null guard config2 already had. - validator.js: typeof null === 'object' is a JS footgun transitional: null bypassed the type check and hit Object.keys(null). - adapters.js: Hardcoded 'ERR_NOT_SUPPORT' string instead of the constant. - xhr.js: Protocol rejection path returned early without calling done(), leaking cancel listeners. - http.js: Raw Error was being thrown from the buildURL catch block instead of AxiosError. Type fixes (index.d.ts + index.d.cts) - Added 6 missing HTTP status codes (521-526) that exist in the source - CanceledError had no explicit constructor signature and was missing __CANCEL__ - CancelToken was missing subscribe, unsubscribe, and toAbortSignal - AxiosHeaders.set() was missing the iterable overload - AxiosHeaders.toString() wasn't declared - SerializerOptions was missing maxDepth and Blob - axios.Cancel was typed as CancelStatic but at runtime it's just CanceledError --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes several runtime edge-case crashes and cleans up cancellation listeners, while updating TypeScript types to match runtime APIs. Improves stability across adapters and makes `axios` typings accurate, including new `CancelToken` methods, `AxiosHeaders` updates, and Cloudflare 52x status codes. **Description** - Summary of changes - Runtime hardening: safe cookie decoding; correct base64 handling in data URIs (and default empty mime to ""); respect custom `Blob` and guard `Buffer` in `toFormData`; once-only abort listeners in composed signals; ensure XHR protocol rejection calls `done()`; issues.title: fix(fetch): cancel ReadableStream body after request stream capability probe
issues.body:
## Problem

The module-level capability probe in the fetch adapter (`lib/adapters/fetch.js`) creates a `new ReadableStream()` as a `Request` body to test for streaming support, but never cancels it. The `Request` constructor sets up an internal pull pipeline on the stream body; since the stream is never consumed or cancelled, the `[[pullAlgorithm]]` Promise remains pending indefinitely, causing an async resource leak.

## How to reproduce

Run any test file that imports axios (with the default fetch adapter, which has been the default since v1.7) using Vitest with async leak detection:

```bash
vitest --detect-async-leaks
```

This reports 1 `PROMISE` leak per test file due to the uncancelled stream from the probe.

## Root cause

In the `factory()` function, the `supportsRequestStream` probe creates a `ReadableStream` inline:

```js
const hasContentType = new Request(platform.origin, {
  body: new ReadableStream(),  // ← never cancelled
  method: 'POST',
  // ...
}).headers.has('Content-Type');
```

The `Request` constructor enqueues an internal pull on the stream. Without cancellation, this pull promise persists for the lifetime of the process.

## Fix

Extract the `ReadableStream` to a variable and call `body.cancel()` after the probe completes:

```js
const body = new ReadableStream();

const hasContentType = new Request(platform.origin, {
  body,
  method: 'POST',
  // ...
}).headers.has('Content-Type');

body.cancel();
```

## Impact

Affects every project using the axios fetch adapter (default since v1.7) under test tooling with async leak detection (Vitest `--detect-async-leaks`, Jest `--detectOpenHandles`, Node.js `async_hooks`). The fix is a single `cancel()` call with no behavioral change to the probe logic.

## Test

Added a unit test that spies on `ReadableStream.prototype.cancel` during a fresh `getFetch()` call (via a unique env to bypass the seed cache) and asserts the cancel method is invoked.

<!-- This is an auto-generated description by cubic. -->
---
## Summary by cubic
Fixes an async resource leak in the fetch adapter by cancelling the `ReadableStream` used in the request-stream capability probe. Adds a unit test to verify the stream is cancelled.

**Bug Fixes**
- Cancel the probe `ReadableStream` in `lib/adapters/fetch.js` after creating the `Request`.
- Prevents a pending pull promise and async leaks seen in `vitest --detect-async-leaks`, Jest open handles, and Node `async_hooks`.
- No behavior change to request-stream support detection.

**Testing**
- Added a unit test that spies on `ReadableStream.prototype.cancel` during a fresh `getFetch()` run; asserts it is called.
- No other tests changed.

<sup>Written for commit 69588e8ba11e8955ba465106240ac1c0017a68be. Summary will update on new commits.</sup>

issues.title: Remint theme color pairings from --{name}-base
issues.body:
Stacked on #42929. Review and merge that first; this builds on it.

- Rebuild `$theme-colors` through a new `theme-color()` helper so each pairing (`fg`, `fg-emphasis`, `bg-subtle`, `bg-muted`, `border`, `focus-ring`) derives from `var(--{name}-base)` with `color-mix`, instead of referencing fixed palette stops like `--blue-600`.
- Add `color-stop()` and `theme-blend()` to `scss/_colors.scss` and `theme-pair()` to `scss/_theme.scss` to replay the palette tint/shade recipe against the base.
- `base` still anchors to the palette 500; `inverse` and `secondary` stay hand-authored. Default compiled colors are unchanged (exact parity).
- One `:root { --bs-primary-base: … }` override now re-mints the whole set. Add a **Root** option to the token playground to show this next to **Base** and **All**.
- Document the derivation, the `:root`-vs-subtree cascade limit, and single-token overrides in `customize/theme.mdx`.

Note: reminting from one variable works at `:root`. For a subtree, CSS resolves the derived tokens where they are declared, so users restate the tints/shades they need.

Supersedes the hardcoded pairings.

Updates `cspell` from 10.3.0 to 10.3.2
Release notes

Sourced from cspell's releases.

v10.3.2

Fixes

fix: Add Experimental Validation setting. (#9250)

This pull request introduces new experimental support for fine-grained validation control and refactors plugin support in the CSpell types package. The main changes add the ability to specify which segments of parsed text should be spell-checked using tag-based validation, and reorganize plugin configuration for future extensibility. The changes also update type definitions and exports to support these new features.

Validation Tag Support:

  • Introduced the CSpellSettingsValidation interface, allowing configuration of which tagged segments of text are spell-checked via the new validate property. This uses the new ValidationTags and TagPattern types to enable hierarchical and wildcard matching of tags. [1] [2]
  • Updated exports to include TagPattern and ValidationTags for external usage.

Plugin Configuration Refactor:

  • Added the CSpellSettingsPlugins interface to encapsulate plugin-related settings, including an experimental plugins array. [1] [2]
  • Refactored ExperimentalFileSettings to extend both CSpellSettingsPlugins and CSpellSettingsValidation, consolidating experimental settings. [1] [2]

API and Type Definition Updates:

  • Changed the defineConfig function and its type definition to accept AdvancedCSpellSettings instead of CSpellSettings, reflecting the expanded configuration options. [1] [2]
  • Updated imports and type usage throughout the codebase to align with the new structure for plugins and validation settings.

These changes lay the groundwork for more flexible and precise spell-checking configuration and future plugin extensibility.

fix: Plugin (#9244)

This pull request introduces support for a new DocumentParser interface alongside the existing Parser interface, modernizing the way documents are parsed throughout the codebase. It updates type definitions, internal APIs, and logic to handle both parser types, and refactors related code for improved clarity and flexibility.

Key changes include:

API and Type Definition Updates:

  • Added DocumentParser, TextDocument, and related types to @cspell/cspell-types, and updated the ParseResult interface to remove content and filename fields, making it compatible with both parser interfaces.
  • Deprecated the old Plugin interface in favor of the new CSpellPlugin interface, which now supports both Parser and DocumentParser instances.

Core Library Refactoring:

  • Updated parser handling in CSpellSettingsServer.ts to support both Parser and DocumentParser, including changes to caches, type signatures, and plugin mapping functions.
  • Refactored DocumentValidator in docValidator.ts to use a new parseDocumentWithParser helper, which abstracts over the two parser interfaces.

Updates `prettier-plugin-astro` from 0.14.1 to 1.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from prettier-plugin-astro's releases.

v1.0.0

Major Changes

  • a8bf1a3: Raises the minimum supported Node version to 22.12.0.

  • 595d47f: The plugin has been fully rewritten on top of Astro 7's new Rust compiler. This rewrite fixes many long-standing issues, such as certain elements not being handled properly inside expressions.

    Whitespace formatting now matches Astro’s whitespace handling, and a new astroCompressHTML option has been added to match Astro's compressHTML setting. If you set compressHTML in your Astro config, also set astroCompressHTML in your Prettier config to match.

    In addition, this rewrite has allowed us to more closely match Prettier's built-in JSX and HTML formatting, leading to less cosmetic differences between the different files in your repo.

v1.0.0-beta.2

Patch Changes

  • cc30d24: Fixes various formatting issues when using astroCompressHTML: 'html' or 'none':

    • Fixes a stray > being added after an empty or ignored element that is followed by a sibling.
    • Fixes closing tags being split from trailing void elements like <img>.
    • Fixes whitespace being added inside tables, lists, and captions under htmlWhitespaceSensitivity: 'strict'.
    • Fixes line breaks around inline elements being replaced by spaces.
    • Allows inline elements to wrap at the print width without adding rendered whitespace.
    • Keeps inline elements written on one line on that line.
    • Fixes components with dotted names like <Astro.self> losing their closing tags or failing to format.
    • Fixes whitespace around inline-block elements and reflowing markup written on one line.
    • Fixes quotes in style attribute values being written unescaped, corrupting the attribute and breaking the next format.
    • Fixes children hugging the closing bracket when an element's attributes span multiple lines.
    • Fixes whitespace being added around a lone <slot />, which stopped :empty from matching the container.
    • Fixes srcset values being mangled when a URL contains a comma, such as a data: URI or query string.
    • Lays out block-level elements like HTML.
    • Fixes whitespace being removed around a lone <slot />, which allowed :empty to start matching the container.
    • Fixes children hugging the closing bracket when an element's attributes wrap and allows a lone long attribute to wrap.
    • Formats style and srcset attributes.
    • Allows runs of adjacent inline elements to wrap at the print width without adding rendered whitespace.
    • Lays out graphical SVG contents one element per line.
    • Fixes nested markup being kept on one line.
    • Fixes spaces being removed from text directly inside <body>.
    • Fixes nested elements being collapsed onto a single line.
    • Fixes a blank line being left inside an opening tag whose attributes break.

v1.0.0-beta.1

Major Changes

  • a8bf1a3: Raises the minimum supported Node version to 22.12.0.

Patch Changes

  • b0ec799: Fixes <script> tags being formatted as JavaScript instead of TypeScript
  • 04ecfe2: Fixes a crash on parenthesized types in template expressions

Major Changes

issues.title: Rename datetime edit minute pseudo-element
issues.body:
### Description

Backport https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/pull/42140 from v6.

`::-webkit-datetime-edit-minute` doesn't match any element in Chromium or WebKit, which both name the minute field `::-webkit-datetime-edit-minute-field`. As a result, the minute field keeps the browser's default `padding: 1px`, while the hour, day, month and year fields get `padding: 0` (#42007, #42052).

On the Browserslist question raised in #42052: both names are non-functional `::-webkit-` pseudo-elements, which [Selectors 4, Appendix B](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors-4/#compat) requires browsers to treat as valid at parse time, so the rename shouldn't affect how the rest of this selector list is parsed. I've only measured the result in Chrome 152: in the built CSS, the minute field's computed padding goes from `1px` to `0`, the same as the hour field.

issues.title: Wire --spacer to $spacer in root tokens
issues.body:
### Description

`$root-tokens` hardcodes `--spacer: 1rem` instead of interpolating `#{$spacer}`. This changes it to `--spacer: #{$spacer}`, matching how neighboring tokens in the same map (e.g. `--border-width: #{$border-width}`) already work.

### Motivation & Context

`$spacer` is the base of the spacing scale and is meant to be overridable. Every `--spacer-N` token is generated from the `$spacers` map, which itself derives from `$spacer`, so overriding `$spacer` moves the whole scale. But `--spacer` itself stayed at `1rem` regardless, because it was never wired to the variable it's named after. Anyone reading `var(--spacer)` directly after overriding `$spacer` would silently get a stale value.

Found while auditing v6-dev's custom-property/Sass-variable philosophy against [julien-deramond/bootstrap-tokens#11](https://github.com/julien-deramond/bootstrap-tokens/issues/11).

issues.title: Add a manual workflow to deploy the docs to gh-pages
issues.body:
Deploying the docs meant building the site and pushing it to `gh-pages` by hand. This adds a manual workflow and retires release-drafter.

- Add `.github/workflows/docs-deploy.yml`, a `workflow_dispatch` job that runs `npm run dist` and `npm run docs-build`, then copies `_site/` over a `gh-pages` checkout with `rsync`.
- Omit `--delete` from the `rsync`, so every older `docs/<version>` directory survives while the root files and the current version get replaced. Each build holds one version only.
- Use no third-party actions. GitHub's own Pages actions (`actions/upload-pages-artifact` and `actions/deploy-pages`) replace the whole site on each deploy, so they cannot keep the version archive, and they need the Pages source moved off the branch.
- Skip the commit when the built site matches `gh-pages`.
- Delete `.github/workflows/release-notes.yml` and `.github/release-drafter.yml`. The release UI generates the notes now.
- Add `.github/release.yml` so the generated notes keep the same label categories the drafter used.
- Add `nojekyll` to `.cspell.json` for the new workflow.

Dispatch the workflow from the branch you want to publish, for example `gh workflow run docs-deploy.yml --ref v6-dev`.

issues.title: Fix .table-responsive causing unexpected body scrollbar with visually…
issues.body:
Fixes #41554

### Description

`.table-responsive` didn't establish its own positioning context. A `.visually-hidden` element (which is `position: absolute`) placed inside a scrolled `.table-responsive` wrapper (e.g. in a table header cell) had no positioned ancestor closer than the document, so its containing block effectively bubbled up past the wrapper. This caused Chrome to compute extra scrollable overflow on the document itself, producing an unexpected body-level scrollbar even though the table's own wrapper was already scrolling correctly.

This PR adds `position: relative` to `.table-responsive`, giving it its own containing block so absolutely positioned descendants (like `.visually-hidden` content) are contained by the wrapper instead of leaking into page-level layout.

### Motivation & Context

Reported in #41554: a horizontally scrolled, wide table with `.visually-hidden` text in the last column of the table head produces an unexpected body scrollbar in Chrome (not Firefox). Possibly related: #41790, where `.visually-hidden` on a `<table>` also takes up unexpected layout space in Safari/Chrome — likely the same underlying containing-block mechanism.

### Testing done

- Rebuilt the reporter's reduced test case locally, using Bootstrap's actual `.table-responsive` component, and confirmed the fix holds for the scenario described (wrapper scrolled fully, no document-level scrollbar).
- `npm run css-lint` passes.
- `npm run css-test` passes (46 specs, 0 failures).
- Manually checked the Tables documentation page for visual regressions — none found.
- Note for reviewers: I wasn't able to reproduce the original bug on the Chrome version available to me for local testing, so I could not directly confirm a before/after contrast myself. The fix is based on the containing-block mechanism described in the issue. Happy to have this verified against the original reporter's browser/version during review.

issues.title: Bump @floating-ui/dom from 1.7.6 to 1.8.0
issues.body:
## Summary
- Bumps `@floating-ui/dom` from `^1.7.6` to `^1.8.0` in `peerDependencies` and `devDependencies` (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`).
- Updates the pinned jsDelivr CDN URL for `@floating-ui/dom` in `config.yml`, used by the import-map examples in the docs.

## Impact
This is a semver-minor release ([1.8.0 release notes](https://github.com/floating-ui/floating-ui/releases/tag/%40floating-ui%2Fdom%401.8.0)). No breaking changes for Menu, Tooltip, Popover, or Combobox.

- **New (unused by us):** `rootBoundary: 'layoutViewport'` option — stays stable during pinch-zoom or when a mobile keyboard opens, unlike `'viewport'`. We don't expose this option today, so it has no effect on current behavior.
- **Bug fixes that improve our components:**
  - `autoUpdate` now refreshes immediately on reference movement instead of waiting for the 1s layout-shift throttle, and its layout-shift observer refreshes correctly on root resize. Benefits Tooltip, Popover, and Menu, which rely on `autoUpdate`.
  - Clipping-ancestor detection is fixed for fixed-position elements, and `scrollbar-gutter: stable` (including `both-edges`) is now accounted for in viewport/clipping calculations. Improves positioning accuracy for `boundary: 'clippingParents'`, our default.
  - `inline()` middleware no longer throws when a virtual element lacks `getClientRects`.
- **Perf:** smaller bundle size and less redundant per-call work in the core/dom positioning utilities.

Our `peerDependencies` range was already `^1.7.6`, so this bump doesn't change what consumers can install — it only updates our own dev/CI copy and the CDN-pinned version shown in docs examples.

## Verification
- `npm run js-lint` — passes (pre-existing warnings only)
- `npm run js-compile` — builds cleanly against 1.8.0
- Browser-mode unit tests could not run in this environment (missing Playwright browser binary); no code changes were needed beyond the version bumps.

issues.title: Fix TypeError when a component is disposed mid-transition
issues.body:
### Description

Skip a component's queued transition-completion callback if the instance was disposed before the transition finished.

`dispose()` nulls every property on the instance but cannot cancel a callback already queued via executeAfterTransition as that helper registers a transitionend listener plus a setTimeout fallback, and neither can be cancelled. The callback then runs against a gutted instance and throws.

This deliberately does not null-guard `Tooltip._isWithActiveTrigger()`, the fix proposed in #37474. As noted there, that is only a defensive patch, and it just relocates the crash two lines down to `this._element.removeAttribute('aria-describedby')`. Better the queued callback not run at all.

Since every component routes transition completion through `BaseComponent._queueCallback`, guarding that single method fixes it for all of them at once. `_element` is already nulled by `dispose()`, so it doubles as the disposed flag and no new state, and `executeAfterTransition`'s signature is untouched. Nothing leaks by skipping the callback: Modal and Offcanvas already dispose their backdrop and focustrap explicitly in their own `dispose()`.

### Motivation & Context

Fixes the long-standing `Uncaught TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object from Tooltip._isWithActiveTrigger()` when a component is disposed mid-transition. Reported repeatedly since 2022 and typically worked around with a setTimeout before `dispose()`.

`dispose()` is public API with no documented restriction against calling it during a transition, and the common trigger is not misuse: a MutationObserver disposing a tooltip whose trigger element was just removed from the DOM has no way to know a fade is still in flight.

issues.body:
### Description

Fixes a race condition in the `Collapse` plugin when used as an accordion. Rapidly clicking different accordion items in quick succession previously allowed multiple items to remain open simultaneously.

### Motivation & Context

When multiple active children exist within an accordion parent (such as one resting and another transitioning), checking only `activeChildren[0]._isTransitioning` failed if the transitioning element appeared later in DOM order. Additionally, `SELECTOR_ACTIVES` was previously requiring `.collapse.collapsing`, which did not match in-flight elements during transition since `.collapse` is removed.

Fixes:
1. Updated `SELECTOR_ACTIVES` to `'.collapse.show, .collapsing'`.
2. Filtered out co-targets sharing triggers so multi-target accordion controls continue to toggle together.
3. Tracked `_isExpanding` state to guard `show()` against in-flight sibling expansions.
4. Added comprehensive Jasmine unit and data-api integration tests to `js/tests/unit/collapse.spec.js`.
