issues.title: fix: chain upstream plugin sourcemaps whose sources contain full paths
issues.body:
Fixes #18778

## Summary

When a bundler plugin (e.g. a Vite plugin using `MagicString.generateMap({ source: id })` where `id` is the absolute module path, as Vite commonly does) passes a sourcemap to `compileOptions.sourcemap`, the source entry is a full or relative path (e.g. `/project/src/App.svelte`) rather than just the basename. The previous fix in #18518 only handled the empty `sources[0]` case (from `generateMap()` without a `source` option), but the full-path case was still failing: `@jridgewell/remapping` does strict string matching on source names, so a full path never equals the basename that Svelte uses in its own map, causing the upstream chain to be silently dropped and producing wrong devtools/stack-trace positions.

## Changes

- In `apply_preprocessor_sourcemap` (`packages/svelte/src/compiler/utils/mapped_code.js`): normalize every entry in the incoming map's `sources` array — not just an empty first entry — replacing any source whose basename matches `filename` (or is empty/null) with `filename` itself. This covers:
  - `sources: ['']` (already fixed in #18518)
  - `sources: ['/abs/path/to/App.svelte']` (the #18778 case, from `generateMap({ source: id })`)
  - `sources: ['relative/path/App.svelte']`
- In `preprocess/index.js`: added a matching `normalize_preprocessor_sources` helper that is applied to maps returned by script/style/markup preprocessors before source-index lookup and map combination. This ensures consistent behavior whether the upstream map arrives via `compileOptions.sourcemap` or from a `preprocess` group.
- Added test case `sourcemaps/samples/sourcemap-fullpath-source` that simulates a Vite plugin calling `generateMap({ source: '/fake/project/path/src/input.svelte' })` and asserts the chained map correctly maps positions back to the original source.
- Added a changeset.

### Root cause

`combine_sourcemaps` composes maps by matching source names. Svelte sets its own map's `sources[0]` to the basename of the file being compiled (`get_basename(options.filename)`). A MagicString-generated map with `{ source: id }` uses `id` verbatim as the source name. When `id` is anything other than the bare basename, the names don't match during remapping and the incoming map is treated as a leaf (original source) instead of a branch to continue chaining through — so every position that should resolve back through the plugin's transform ends up with `{ source: null, line: null, column: null }`.

Vite works around this in `pluginContainer._getCombinedSourcemap`; this PR applies the analogous normalization on Svelte's side so the documented contract (`compileOptions.sourcemap` accepts an upstream map and chains it) holds regardless of how the caller constructs their MagicString.

## Test plan

- New test `sourcemap-fullpath-source` reproduces the exact scenario from #18778 (full-path source in incoming map), fails without the fix (no matching segment in the composed map), passes with it.
- Existing sourcemap tests (including the `sourcemap-empty-source` test added in #18518) continue to cover the empty-source case.
- Preprocessor script/style/markup paths get the same normalization for consistency.

issues.title: fix: robustify async reactivity system (pt2)
issues.body:
Part two of the split of #18861 with the fork changes

## This branch tweaks behavior in one place

### Forks are always seen as the latest batch

Previously, creation of a `fork` did put it into the batch queue at that position and that position would not change. That meant a fork-batch could now be an earlier or later dependent batch on another one when you `commit` that fork. The end result is the same with regards to what you observe in the UI once everything settles, but it meant that there's a lot more cases to consider when forks enter the real world.

This branch changes that by treating forks as always being the latest batch in the queue. E.g. if you create batch A, then fork-batch B, then batch C, fork-batch B would move behind C in the queue. Implementation-wise this simplifies a lot of things.

## A few implementation details

Fork:
- if a real world change writes the same value as a fork did, that value is deleted from the fork (i.e. that part of the fork becomes obsolete). Once all sources of a fork are obsolete it's auto-discarded.
- forks can create branches that no real world batch sees yet - we need to make sure they ignore them in the real world unless a batch also "reveals" them. If another batch reveals that branch it also needs to treat it like discovering it for the first time, i.e. all the containing pre/render effects need to run again (they were likely have different values). A new `FORK_ONLY_BRANCH` that is toggled at the right times and enhancing the "skip this branch" logic solves this.

issues.title: fix: robustify async reactivity system (pt1)
issues.body:
This PR overhauls the async reactivity system to be more robust, reliable and predictable. It's part 1 of #18861, extracted into a separate PR with just the non-fork changes.

This supersedes #18558 which doesn't have any many tests passing, and the way entangling works on that PR enabled async starvation, which this one doesn't. This PR is also less lines of code.

- Fixes #18355
- Fixes #18761
- Fixes #18624
- Fixes #18503
- Fixes #18662
- Fixes #18675 (because the invariant is gone)
- Fixes https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/15067
- [this playground](https://svelte.dev/playground/hello-world?version=5.56.4#H4sIAAAAAAAACo1Sy47bMAz8FUJYIDbiJntObBe99dbeNwtEkumVUEVSJTpuYBjoR_QL-yWFLedx6KI9WRzNDIcWB2b5CdmOfUZjHPQumAYybDRhk7OCtdpgZLuXgdHFT7wJYMVV9cn7TTyjoQkTPOLfcOksoaXIdqyMMmhP9cEeyCABhwqeInHCbMVX-f6Ki3dwecefZ3TBLVTw_FB_77DDBip4eb1pWx0iQQUUOtxD4radlaSdBd9FlZ1zGCb0QLqFbObfkANd9S03MRnMcEDqgoXzPgFjMr7hFnv4GtxJR8yygNGZM-ZQ1XfflHUzJ8jmq4WWnfP86pqnhuOSe7uFXqEFDoKTVCAVt2_avsFRHEG600lTLICUjtAHTRjhKI_QdGHikOKUdKu4mLWmiwq84hHh989fQAqTEAy3TQQ9tWoDRmUuH2RATtgki8ngCdsWJS3pl8HEEn16svXazlUao9zet8CWvvYBYwQ-5UULYvl65yGgn1uZywa-WDhxbdNQOIXqNSngogDREUTlOtOAQBCi3Pr6YEvRETkLzkqj5bdqSPGmlVuJ1VjzcpsY73PFlSv-zV2eMSrdUpZ_3GT5WM_Ff0u981ehd_5BNv-lgY_LXL4exMOZ91xTWmAOaxD5w51czqxghD-I7ablH18LRlybXtuG7eZ1Hv8AoW0vUwgEAAA) which exists in one of my thousand tabs and I'm not sure which issue (if any) this is related to
- Closes #18363 (because we don't have the invariant anymore)
- Fixes https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/15083
- Fixes https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/16119
- ... (need to check more)

## This branch tweaks behavior in one place

### Changes that are in any way connected through the graph have to resolve in order

Previously, when you something like `await delay(a + '|' + b)` and you changed `a` first and `b` second, but the promise for `b` resolves first, we would show that result. With this change we now wait for the first result before showing the second. The idea is that related changes should resolve along their correct timeline, which avoids in-between-states that would never happen in a sync-only world. In the given example, if everything was sync, we would first see `1|0` and then `1|1` - if we were resolving `b` first we would see `0|1`, an impossible state.

An implementation-consequence is that when traversing the graph and executing if/each/etc blocks and async effects, we will do so with the latest value the current batch sees, which includes all the pending changes of earlier batches - only values updated in LATER batches will not be seen. In the above example this means we will not call `delay` with `a=1,b=0`, `a=0,b=1` and on resolve of the latter with `a=1,b=1` again; instead we only call it with `a=1,b=0` and then `a=1,b=1` which is arguably much more correct.

When flushing the (render)effects of a batch, we see the previous value of other pending (but unrelated) batches aswell - if the batch sees that it is dependent on another earlier batch (because they are connected through the reactivity graph) then it merges into that earlier batch like previously.

## A few implementation details

Roughly speaking the async reactivity system behavior is relatively easy to explain, but of course the devil's in the details. So I'm noting a few cases here and how they are solved.

When something gets a new value (source or derived), we store both the old value AND the old version. When two or more batches exist in parallel the logic then is:
- the `apply` method records all sources/deriveds of EARLIER batches in a "held" map
- the `apply` method records all sources/deriveds of its own and LATER batches in the batch_values/wv_values map
- the `apply` method records all sources/deriveds of LATER batches in the stale_sources map
- before flushing (render)effects we call `apply` again but this time we also add all sources/deriveds of EARLIER batches to batch_values/wv_values (this ensure we don't render newer values at this point)
- when a block effect or derived is executed in a later batch and it reads a signal that is in the "held" map (i.e. part of an earlier batch) then these two batches become entangled: the later batch now has to wait for the earlier batch to resolve first (or rather, it has to merge into it then). Same for writes.
- when is_dirty runs wv_values is used instead of the real wv, if available. Execution of a derived when multiple batches exist is always only reset to MAYBE_DIRTY. This ensures we always walk up the graph, together with wv_values this ensures we don't overfire. DIRTY/CLEAN are basically optimizations for the sync hot path.
- effects that saw at least one value that is not the latest don't set its wv, instead only in the context of its batch. Ensures their wv stays "early" and it can rerun in other batches.

Edge cases:
- when something in an earlier batch updates an async effect which writes to an async source that a later batch depends on, then those LATER entangled batches ALSO will get the same write applied to it once they read that value (in other words their async effects will rerun with the new value). 
- when an earlier batch creates a new branch (e.g. if block becomes truthy), it runs the pre/render effects right away. If this execution reads a value that is already outdated (i.e. later batch has newer value) we need to tell the later batch about it (i.e. reschedule these effects in that batch).

issues.title: fix: tolerate abort/reset of deferred transitions before initialization
issues.body:
Closes #18773.

### Problem

An out-only deferred transition (e.g. `out:send` from `crossfade`) crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'reset')` when its outro is aborted from an `$effect` during the same update that removed the branch.

### Root cause

In `animate()` (`packages/svelte/src/internal/client/dom/elements/transitions.js`), a deferred transition (transition function returning another function) creates its inner animation in a microtask and returns a facade in the meantime. The facade's `abort` was already null-safe (`a?.abort()`), but `deactivate`, `reset` and `t` dereferenced the not-yet-created inner animation directly. When the outro is aborted and reset before the microtask runs, e.g. the branch is restored from an `$effect` in the same update, so `resume_children` calls `transition.in()` → `outro.reset()`, the facade throws.

### Fix

Make the facade's `deactivate`, `reset` and `t` tolerate the uninitialized inner animation with optional chaining, matching `abort`. (`t()` callers already handle `undefined` via `??`.)

### Tests

- New regression test `transition-deferred-outro-abort` (runtime-runes): fails before the fix with the exact `TypeError` from the issue, passes after, the outro is aborted and the branch stays visible.
- All 64 transition-related runtime-runes tests pass; full `runtime-runes` + `signals` suites: 2814 passed, 0 failed.
- Changeset added.

issues.title: fix: deliver synchronous throws in async expressions to error boundaries
issues.body:
Closes #18824.

### Problem

With `experimental.async`, when an awaited expression throws **synchronously** (e.g. `{await load()}` where `load()` throws instead of returning a rejected promise), the original error never reaches the `<svelte:boundary>` `failed` snippet. Instead it surfaces as a cryptic `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'f')` and the boundary keeps showing stale content.

### Root cause

In `async_derived` (`packages/svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/deriveds.js`), the `catch` around `Promise.resolve(fn())` called `unset_context()` synchronously. The bookkeeping that runs after the `try`/`catch` (`increment_pending()`, `batch.async_deriveds.set(...)`) still needs the active context, on the non-throwing path it runs before the promise settles. Eagerly unsetting nulled `active_effect` and deactivated `current_batch`, so `increment_pending()` threw reading `.b` of `null`, and `handle_error` then threw reading `.f` of `null`, masking the original error.

### Fix

Defer the `unset_context()` until the rejection is handled (mirroring `.finally(unset_context)` on the non-throwing path), so the bookkeeping runs with the context intact and the original error flows through the signal's `ERROR_VALUE` to the boundary's `failed` snippet, exactly like an asynchronously rejected promise.

### Tests

- New regression test `async-boundary-sync-throw` (runtime-runes): fails before the fix (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`), passes after. Also verified the initial-mount sync-throw variant renders the `failed` snippet, consistent with async rejections.
- Full `runtime-runes` + `signals` suites: 2814 passed, 0 failed.
- Changeset added.

issues.title: fix: error when using `let:` directives on a component with a `children` snippet
issues.body:
Closes #13864

A `let:` directive on a component only applies to the default slot content. If the content is an explicit `{#snippet children()}` block, the value is never provided, so code like this compiles but fails at runtime with "value is not defined":

```svelte
<Child let:value>
	{#snippet children()}Value is: {value}{/snippet}
</Child>
```

This adds a compile error on the directive that points to snippet parameters instead (`{#snippet children({ value })}`, or `{ item: x }` for `let:item={x}`). Components with a `slot` attribute are not affected, since there the directive applies to the component itself. An unused `let:` next to a `children` snippet is also flagged now, but it never had any effect.

issues.title: fix: skip redundant attribute writes during hydration
issues.body:
Closes #18868. While hydrating, `set_attribute` fills its cache from `getAttribute()`, which returns a string, and then compares it with the client value. A number or boolean never equals that string, so `tabindex={-1}`, `aria-rowindex={i + 2}`, `` request their resource again. The other names weren't observed to refetch, but they are URLs, so they are excluded too. - SVG list attributes (`values`, `tableValues`, `kernelMatrix`, `transform`, `gradientTransform`, `patternTransform`, `points`, plus `x`, `y`, `dx`, `dy`, `rotate` on ``/``). Rewriting one detaches list items previously retrieved through `baseVal`. I checked every SVG element/property pair whose `baseVal` is an object in Chromium and WebKit, and only these lists behave this way, so `` or `` are still skipped. - Custom elements, because `attributeChangedCallback` observes the write. Autonomous ones are never skipped. For customized built-ins, an HTML element is only skipped when its prototype is that of `document.createElement(localName)`. This also holds after `is` is removed, and across realms and scoped registries. `localName`, `namespaceURI` and `createElement` are read from the prototypes, because form controls, `
` and own properties can shadow them. Known limitation: a customized built-in whose prototype was reset to the native one (`Object.setPrototypeOf(el, HTMLButtonElement.prototype)`) is treated as native, so it doesn't get callbacks for skipped numbers and booleans. `main` already treats unchanged strings on any customized built-in the same way. Nothing changes outside hydration. The spread path (`set_attributes`) is unchanged, and so is the `src`/`srcset`/`` early return. Attribute mutation records during hydration in Chromium, for a 29-row table with a mix of attributes (fixture below): | | `main` | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | numbers via `setAttribute` (`aria-rowindex`, `colspan`, `tabindex`, `svg width`/`height`/`stroke-width`) | 232 | 0 | | booleans via `setAttribute` (`data-selected={false}`, `aria-hidden={true}`) | 58 | 0 | | property setters (`translate`, `draggable`, canvas `width`/`height`, spread `disabled`/`required`, `disabled={on}`) | 203 | 203 | | total | 493 | 203 | The reproduction in the issue goes from 21 records to 3, which are the spread's `disabled` setters. With 300 rows, median hydration time went from 1.5–1.6 ms to 1.3–1.4 ms without an observer, and from 1.9–2.0 ms to 1.6–1.7 ms with one (Chromium headless, alternating runs; the numbers depend on the host).
Fixture ```svelte
{#each rows as row, i (row)} {/each}
t
``` The fixture is a `runtime-browser` sample with `mode: ['hydrate']`. A `MutationObserver` is attached in `before_test` and read in `test`. Tests: - `hydration/element-attribute-primitives`: a table of server/client values. Equal numbers, booleans, `NaN` and `1e21` aren't written, while `"1.0"`, `"-0"`, `"False"`, `""`, changed values and removals are. An object's `toString` runs once. Hydration resumes skipping after a mismatched `{#if}` branch. - `runtime-browser/hydration-attribute-unchanged`: what isn't written in Chromium. This covers `$effect.pre` versus `$effect`, updates after hydration, and elements whose `localName`, `namespaceURI` or `document.createElement` are shadowed, which hydrate without recovery. - `runtime-browser/hydration-attribute-written`: what is still written. This covers spread and own property setters, including setters wrapped or replaced mid-hydration, `translate`/`draggable`, canvas dimensions, SVG lists, ``, and customized built-ins (with or without `is`, with a shadowed `namespaceURI` or `localName`, upgraded after hydration, and the limitation above). - `runtime-browser/hydration-attribute-realms`: customized built-ins from a scoped registry and from another realm. - `runtime-browser/hydration-attribute-recover`: after a hydration error, updates are written normally, and a later hydration skips again. - `runtime-runes/async-hydration-attribute-unchanged`: skipping inside an `{#if await ...}` that resolves during hydration. ### Tests and linting

- [ ] Run the tests with `pnpm test` and lint the project with `pnpm lint` (full monorepo runs not done; the three affected runtime suites plus eslint on the changed file were run, see Validation)

Fixes #18070

**Problem**

With `{@attach}` + `on(node, 'click')` mutating state that an `$effect` turns into `disabled = true`, the browser flushes effects at the microtask checkpoint between listeners mid-dispatch. The button is therefore already `disabled` when the trusted click reaches the delegated `onclick` at the root, and `handle_event_propagation` skipped the handler (`disabled === true` while `event.target` is the inner `<span>`).

**Fix**

In `handle_event_propagation`, also invoke the delegated handler when `current_target === handled_at`: Svelte tracks the element the event was already observed reaching in `event[event_symbol]`, so when the delegated root processes the same event and reaches that same element, it proves the element was disabled mid-dispatch (by an earlier listener, e.g. the `{@attach}` handler's flushed `$effect`), the handler should still fire. This is narrower than checking `event.isTrusted`: a disabled element that Svelte never observed the event reaching keeps the previous behavior.

**Test**

New `runtime-browser` sample `delegated-onclick-mid-dispatch-disabled` reproduces the issue setup (attach throttle disabling the button via `$effect`) and performs a real mouse click via a new opt-in `real_click` harness option (`window.__real_click`), since only a real dispatch creates the microtask checkpoints where effects flush mid-dispatch. Verified red/green: fails on pristine code (`onclick: 0`) and passes with the fix (`onclick: 1`), in both `dom` and `hydrate` variants.

issues.title: fix: don't overwrite an unchanged spread `value`
issues.body:
Fixes #18862

When a `value` is applied through a spread (`<input {...props} />`), `set_attributes` always writes `element.value`, even if the element already has that value. Writing `value` on a number input clears any incomplete text: typing `250.` makes `input.value` `''` (the text is still visible, but `validity.badInput` is `true`). If the spread `value` then becomes `''` too, writing `''` erases what the user typed.

This is what happens with SvelteKit remote forms: `fields.quantity.as('number')` coerces `''` to `undefined`, the spread `value` becomes `''`, and Svelte writes it back to the input. When `.` is typed:

- Chromium clears the input in every locale, because `250.` is always incomplete input there.
- WebKit/Safari clears it in locales where `.` is not the decimal separator (e.g. `fr-CH`), which is where the reporter saw it.

A plain `<input type="number">` never clears. Neither does the same `value` in Svelte without a spread (`value={...}`), because `set_value` already skips writing when `element.value === value`. This PR adds the same check to the spread path. Svelte 3 had this check too (#3426, #3495); it was lost in Svelte 5.

The first write still always happens. Writing `value` sets the input's dirty value flag, and without that flag a `defaultValue` applied afterwards would change the current value (covered by `form-default-value-spread`).

This also likely affects sveltejs/kit#16270 (same symptom, plus a cursor jump caused by redundant writes). That issue is handled on the kit side in sveltejs/kit#16320; this PR is independent of it.

The test runs in a real browser (`runtime-browser`). It types with `document.execCommand('insertText')`, which goes through Chromium's own editing, so `250.` is real incomplete input. The locale is not mocked. The test fails without this change and passes with it.

issues.title: fix: guard against null batch in schedule_effect
issues.body:
### Before submitting the PR, please make sure you do the following

- [x] It's really useful if your PR references an issue where it is discussed ahead of time. In many cases, features are absent for a reason. For large changes, please create an RFC: https://github.com/sveltejs/rfcs
- [x] Prefix your PR title with `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, or `docs:`.
- [x] This message body should clearly illustrate what problems it solves.
- [x] Ideally, include a test that fails without this PR but passes with it.
- [x] If this PR changes code within `packages/svelte/src`, add a changeset (`npx changeset`).

Closes #18850

### What / why

`schedule_effect` dereferenced `current_batch` with an unsafe cast:

```js
export function schedule_effect(effect) {
	/** @type {Batch} */ (current_batch).schedule(effect);
}
```

`Batch.#process` deliberately nulls `current_batch` before flushing effects (and only repopulates it on the legacy-updates path). When an effect flushed there reaches the self-invalidation block in `update_reaction`, i.e. the effect wrote a source that first became one of its dependencies in that same run, and then called `flushSync()`, `schedule_possible_effect_self_invalidation` calls `schedule_effect` against the null and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'schedule')` (regression introduced by #17805 in 5.54.0).

The fix replaces the cast with `Batch.ensure().schedule(effect)`. This is the same pattern `#process` itself uses for legacy updates (`var batch = Batch.ensure();`), and it is safe here: a batch created during the flush is picked up afterwards (`var next_batch = current_batch; … next_batch.#process()`), so the scheduled effect still runs. All other `schedule_effect` call sites are unaffected, the only behavior change is "create a batch on demand" instead of "throw" when `current_batch` is null.

### Repro evidence

The issue's reproduction (`App.svelte` revealing a `Child` via state change; the child does `$effect(() => { if (x === 0) { x = 1; flushSync(); } })`) was ported to a `runtime-runes` sample (`effect-self-invalidation-null-batch`). Run locally with vitest:

- **Before the fix**: uncaught `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'schedule')` (both `hydrate` and default variants).
- **After the fix**: both variants pass, `x = 1` renders, no uncaught errors.

Targeted test results after the fix:
- new sample `effect-self-invalidation-null-batch`: 2/2 pass
- `signals` suite: 103 passed, 2 skipped
- flush-related `runtime-runes` samples: 8/8 pass

### Caveat on related issues

#18522, #18799 and #18546 describe the same null-`current_batch` invariant at other call sites. This PR is a guarded call-site fix for the `schedule_effect` path only; it does not change any of those other paths or attempt a shared upstream fix.

### Tests and linting

- [x] Run the tests with `pnpm test` and lint the project with `pnpm lint`

Note: ran the targeted suites (new regression sample, `signals`, flush-related runtime-runes samples) rather than the full workspace suite.

issues.title: fix: robustify async reactivity system
issues.body:
This PR overhauls the async reactivity system to be more robust, reliable and predictable.

This supersedes #18558 which doesn't have any many tests passing, and the way entangling works on that PR enabled async starvation, which this one doesn't. This PR is also less lines of code.

- Fixes #18355
- Fixes #18761
- Fixes #18624
- Fixes #18503
- Fixes #18662
- Fixes #18675 (because the invariant is gone)
- Fixes https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/15067
- [this playground](https://svelte.dev/playground/hello-world?version=5.56.4#H4sIAAAAAAAACo1Sy47bMAz8FUJYIDbiJntObBe99dbeNwtEkumVUEVSJTpuYBjoR_QL-yWFLedx6KI9WRzNDIcWB2b5CdmOfUZjHPQumAYybDRhk7OCtdpgZLuXgdHFT7wJYMVV9cn7TTyjoQkTPOLfcOksoaXIdqyMMmhP9cEeyCABhwqeInHCbMVX-f6Ki3dwecefZ3TBLVTw_FB_77DDBip4eb1pWx0iQQUUOtxD4radlaSdBd9FlZ1zGCb0QLqFbObfkANd9S03MRnMcEDqgoXzPgFjMr7hFnv4GtxJR8yygNGZM-ZQ1XfflHUzJ8jmq4WWnfP86pqnhuOSe7uFXqEFDoKTVCAVt2_avsFRHEG600lTLICUjtAHTRjhKI_QdGHikOKUdKu4mLWmiwq84hHh989fQAqTEAy3TQQ9tWoDRmUuH2RATtgki8ngCdsWJS3pl8HEEn16svXazlUao9zet8CWvvYBYwQ-5UULYvl65yGgn1uZywa-WDhxbdNQOIXqNSngogDREUTlOtOAQBCi3Pr6YEvRETkLzkqj5bdqSPGmlVuJ1VjzcpsY73PFlSv-zV2eMSrdUpZ_3GT5WM_Ff0u981ehd_5BNv-lgY_LXL4exMOZ91xTWmAOaxD5w51czqxghD-I7ablH18LRlybXtuG7eZ1Hv8AoW0vUwgEAAA) which exists in one of my thousand tabs and I'm not sure which issue (if any) this is related to
- Closes #18363 (because we don't have the invariant anymore)
- Fixes https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/15083
- Fixes https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/16119
- ... (need to check more)

## This branch tweaks behavior in two places

### Changes that are in any way connected through the graph have to resolve in order

Previously, when you something like `await delay(a + '|' + b)` and you changed `a` first and `b` second, but the promise for `b` resolves first, we would show that result. With this change we now wait for the first result before showing the second. The idea is that related changes should resolve along their correct timeline, which avoids in-between-states that would never happen in a sync-only world. In the given example, if everything was sync, we would first see `1|0` and then `1|1` - if we were resolving `b` first we would see `0|1`, an impossible state.

An implementation-consequence is that when traversing the graph and executing if/each/etc blocks and async effects, we will do so with the latest value the current batch sees, which includes all the pending changes of earlier batches - only values updated in LATER batches will not be seen. In the above example this means we will not call `delay` with `a=1,b=0`, `a=0,b=1` and on resolve of the latter with `a=1,b=1` again; instead we only call it with `a=1,b=0` and then `a=1,b=1` which is arguably much more correct.

When flushing the (render)effects of a batch, we see the previous value of other pending (but unrelated) batches aswell - if the batch sees that it is dependent on another earlier batch (because they are connected through the reactivity graph) then it merges into that earlier batch like previously.

### Forks are always seen as the latest batch

Previously, creation of a `fork` did put it into the batch queue at that position and that position would not change. That meant a fork-batch could now be an earlier or later dependent batch on another one when you `commit` that fork. The end result is the same with regards to what you observe in the UI once everything settles, but it meant that there's a lot more cases to consider when forks enter the real world.

This branch changes that by treating forks as always being the latest batch in the queue. E.g. if you create batch A, then fork-batch B, then batch C, fork-batch B would move behind C in the queue. Implementation-wise this simplifies a lot of things.

## A few implementation details

Roughly speaking the async reactivity system behavior is relatively easy to explain, but of course the devil's in the details. So I'm noting a few cases here and how they are solved.

When something gets a new value (source or derived), we store both the old value AND the old version. When two or more batches exist in parallel the logic then is:
- the `apply` method records all sources/deriveds of EARLIER batches in a "held" map
- the `apply` method records all sources/deriveds of its own and LATER batches in the batch_values/wv_values map
- the `apply` method records all sources/deriveds of LATER batches in the stale_sources map
- before flushing (render)effects we call `apply` again but this time we also add all sources/deriveds of EARLIER batches to batch_values/wv_values (this ensure we don't render newer values at this point)
- when a block effect or derived is executed in a later batch and it reads a signal that is in the "held" map (i.e. part of an earlier batch) then these two batches become entangled: the later batch now has to wait for the earlier batch to resolve first (or rather, it has to merge into it then). Same for writes.
- when is_dirty runs wv_values is used instead of the real wv, if available. Execution of a derived when multiple batches exist is always only reset to MAYBE_DIRTY. This ensures we always walk up the graph, together with wv_values this ensures we don't overfire. DIRTY/CLEAN are basically optimizations for the sync hot path.
- effects that saw at least one value that is not the latest don't set its wv, instead only in the context of its batch. Ensures their wv stays "early" and it can rerun in other batches.

Edge cases:
- when something in an earlier batch updates an async effect which writes to an async source that a later batch depends on, then those LATER entangled batches ALSO will get the same write applied to it once they read that value (in other words their async effects will rerun with the new value). 
- when an earlier batch creates a new branch (e.g. if block becomes truthy), it runs the pre/render effects right away. If this execution reads a value that is already outdated (i.e. later batch has newer value) we need to tell the later batch about it (i.e. reschedule these effects in that batch).

Fork:
- if a real world change writes the same value as a fork did, that value is deleted from the fork (i.e. that part of the fork becomes obsolete). Once all sources of a fork are obsolete it's auto-discarded.
- forks can create branches that no real world batch sees yet - we need to make sure they ignore them in the real world unless a batch also "reveals" them. If another batch reveals that branch it also needs to treat it like discovering it for the first time, i.e. all the containing pre/render effects need to run again (they were likely have different values). A new `FORK_ONLY_BRANCH` that is toggled at the right times and enhancing the "skip this branch" logic solves this.

issues.title: `schedule_effect` dereferences a null `current_batch` (regression in 5.54.0)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug `schedule_effect` casts away a null that `Batch.#process` sets deliberately: ```js // src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js export function schedule_effect(effect) { /** @type {Batch} */ (current_batch).schedule(effect); } ``` `#process()` nulls `current_batch` before it flushes effects, and only repopulates it on the legacy-updates path: ```js // any writes should take effect in a subsequent batch current_batch = null; if (updates.length > 0) { var batch = Batch.ensure(); … } … flush_queued_effects(render_effects); flush_queued_effects(effects); ``` If an effect flushed there reaches the self-invalidation block in `update_reaction`, it calls `schedule_effect` against that null and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'schedule')`. Three conditions have to line up: 1. **The effect runs inside `Batch.#process` → `flush_queued_effects`.** In the reproduction the child is mounted by a state change, so its first run happens during the microtask batch flush rather than at mount. 2. **The effect writes a source in the same run in which that source first becomes one of its dependencies.** `update_dependencies` attaches the reaction to `source.reactions` only *after* `fn()` returns, so at write time `mark_reactions` cannot mark the effect dirty. It stays `CLEAN` and the source lands in `untracked_writes` — the `$effect(() => x++)` case described in the comment in `sources.js`. 3. **`flushSync()` runs after that write, within the same effect run.** The write itself calls `Batch.ensure()`, which repopulates `current_batch`; `flushSync`'s `finally` then nulls it again. `update_reaction` then reaches: ```js if ( is_runes() && untracked_writes !== null && !untracking && deps !== null && (reaction.f & (DERIVED | MAYBE_DIRTY | DIRTY)) === 0 ) { for (…) schedule_possible_effect_self_invalidation(untracked_writes[i], reaction); } ``` The effect is `CLEAN` (condition 2) and is by now in `source.reactions` (attached by `update_dependencies` just above), so `schedule_possible_effect_self_invalidation` matches `effect === reaction` and calls `schedule_effect`. Removing any single condition avoids the throw, verified individually: - Drop the `flushSync()` call. - Read `x` unconditionally so it is an established dependency before the run that writes it. `mark_reactions` then marks the effect `DIRTY` and the `(reaction.f & (DERIVED | MAYBE_DIRTY | DIRTY)) === 0` guard fails. - Mount the child directly instead of revealing it via a state change, so its first run no longer happens inside `#process`. ### Affected versions | version | result | | --- | --- | | 5.53.0 | works | | 5.54.0 | **throws** | | 5.57.1 | **throws** | Introduced by #17805 (*chore: refactor scheduling*, merged 2026-03-08), which moved scheduling from the module-global `queued_root_effects` array onto `current_batch`. Before that, `schedule_effect` never touched `current_batch`. The function is unchanged on `main` as of today. We hit this in production on a SvelteKit app: ~120 events over 7 days, across several releases, Chrome 152/153. Independently hit by another app on 5.56 with the same diagnosis: intent-hq/cloudlands-fe#2547. ### Related, but not duplicates Several open issues look like the same underlying invariant at different call sites: #18522 (`batch.transfer_effects` null after a top-level `flushSync`), #18799 (`batch.increment` null during async component init), and #18546 (scheduling bails after a batch is dropped). #18758's `flushSync` guard does not cover this one, since it fires only for a `BRANCH_EFFECT`/`ROOT_EFFECT` mid-update, and here `flushSync` is called inside a plain user `$effect`. ### On a PR Happy to open one. `Batch.ensure().schedule(effect)` fixes the reproduction and leaves the effect tree reactive afterwards (I checked specifically, given #18546 describes a failure mode where the root goes permanently non-reactive). But since the four issues above may share a cause, you may prefer a single fix upstream of all of them rather than a guard at this call site. Say which direction you want and I'll put it together with a test. ### Reproduction https://github.com/ndri/svelte-repro-batch-schedule `pnpm install && pnpm dev`, then click **Mount the child**. The child renders (`x = 1`) and an uncaught `TypeError` is reported on the page and in the console. The essential part is two files: ```svelte {#if show}{/if} ``` ```svelte

x = {x}

``` Note the throw happens in the microtask that flushes the batch, so it does **not** propagate out of the click handler and a `try`/`catch` there will not catch it. The reproduction listens on `window.onerror` to display it. ### Logs ```shell TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'schedule') in $effect in Child.svelte in App.svelte Production build, symbolicated, from 5.57.0: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'schedule') at schedule_effect (svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js:1240:39) at schedule_possible_effect_self_invalidation (svelte/src/internal/client/runtime.js:220:4) at update_reaction (svelte/src/internal/client/runtime.js:274:5) at update_effect (svelte/src/internal/client/runtime.js:490:18) at flush_queued_effects (svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js:1100:4) at Batch.#process (svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js:389:3) at Batch.flush (svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js:619:9) at svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js:866:13 at run_all (svelte/src/internal/shared/utils.js:47:9) at svelte/src/internal/client/dom/task.js:10:2 ``` ### System Info ```shell System: OS: macOS 26.7 CPU: (12) arm64 Apple M2 Max Memory: 96.53 MB / 32.00 GB Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh Binaries: Node: 24.11.1 npm: 11.6.0 pnpm: 10.15.0 bun: 1.3.7 Browsers: Chrome: 153.0.8010.50 Firefox: 156.0 Safari: 27.0 npmPackages: svelte: 5.57.1 => 5.57.1 ``` ### Severity annoyance

issues.title: fix: hint at missing lang="ts" when snippet params look like type annotations
issues.body:
### Before submitting the PR, please make sure you do the following

- [x] It's really useful if your PR references an issue where it is discussed ahead of time. In many cases, features are absent for a reason. For large changes, please create an RFC: https://github.com/sveltejs/rfcs
- [x] Prefix your PR title with `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, or `docs:`.
- [x] This message body should clearly illustrate what problems it solves.
- [x] Ideally, include a test that fails without this PR but passes with it.
- [x] If this PR changes code within `packages/svelte/src`, add a changeset (`npx changeset`).

### Tests and linting

- [ ] Run the tests with `pnpm test` and lint the project with `pnpm lint`
  (full suites not run, ran targeted suites instead; see **Tests** below)

Closes #16835.

**Problem:** writing `{#snippet bar(text: string)}` without `lang="ts"` on the script tag fails with a bare `Unexpected token` error, which sends people hunting in the wrong direction.

**Fix:** when snippet parameter parsing fails as JavaScript, a conservative heuristic (`looks_like_type_annotation`) inspects the raw params text. If it looks like TypeScript type annotations and the component has no `lang="ts"`, the error is augmented with: *Did you forget to add `lang="ts"` to your `<script>` tag?*

The heuristic is deliberately conservative per the discussion in #16835 (no blind re-parse as TypeScript): string literals and comments are skipped, colons inside `{}`/`[]` (destructuring, object literals) don't count, and ternaries (`a ? b : c`) don't trigger the hint. The original error position is preserved.

**Tests:** new regression sample `tests/compiler-errors/samples/snippet-type-annotation-without-lang-ts` asserting the augmented message; full `compiler-errors` (148), `parser-modern` (29), `parser-legacy` (83) and `validator` (336) suites pass. Also verified an 11-case manual matrix (hint appears for `(text: string)`, `(text?: string)`, `({a,b}: Props)`, defaults, function types; no hint for valid JS, valid destructuring `({a: b})`, ternaries, or colon-less syntax errors; `lang="ts"` components compile cleanly). The single `snapshot` suite failure (`props-identifier`) also fails on clean upstream main in my environment and is unrelated.

Changeset added (patch).

issues.title: fix: a component `bind:` no longer copies the whole rendered page on every retry
issues.body:
Fixes #18845.

A component that uses `bind:` on a child renders in a retry loop: the child can write back
to the bound prop, so the parent body runs again. Every iteration starts from
`renderer.copy()`, and `copy()` duplicates everything the page has rendered so far, so a
page with N such components copies O(N²).

This is not a legacy-mode corner. `uses_component_bindings` is set by any `bind:` other than
`bind:this`, so plain runes components take the same path and pay more than legacy ones do.

A form of N rows, each row a runes component with `bind:value` on a child, Node 26.7.0,
`NODE_ENV=production`, ms per render, best of 15:

| rows | 5.38.10 | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 100 | 0.04 | 0.35 | **0.04** |
| 400 | 0.36 | 7.66 | **0.14** |
| 800 | 1.25 | 32.71 | **0.28** |

Doubling 400 to 800 multiplies `main` by 4.3 and this PR by 2.0.

In sync mode the retry loop is the only writer, so the copy does not need what was rendered
before the loop started. It keeps a reference to the renderer it continues (`#appends_to`)
and the offset its content will land at (`#offset`), starts empty, and `subsume` appends it
back. `get_path` follows `#appends_to`, so `<svelte:head>` ordering is unaffected. The async
path still copies, because there a suspended child can still be writing.

`copy()` also built the new renderer from `this.#parent`, so the constructor filled `local`
from the **parent's** `local` rather than from the renderer being copied.
`local.select_value` is how an `<option>` learns whether it is selected, so a `<select>` lost
its selection as soon as a component with a `bind:` rendered inside it. The same copy also
gives a `selected` to an `<option>` whose own value is `undefined`, since the child never
sees the real `select_value`:

```
- <option>in</option>
+ <option selected="">in</option>
- <option selected="" value="b">b</option>
+ <option value="b">b</option>
```

Tests: `select-value-after-legacy-bind` fails on `main` in both sync and async mode, and
`head-title-order-with-binding` pins the `<svelte:head>` ordering that `#offset` keeps.

`wrapper_bench` is unchanged (49.99 ms on `main`, 50.13 ms here, three interleaved rounds).

chore: bump typescript to version 6
issues.body:
We're currently using a version of TypeScript with a bug that prevents us from using `noUnusedLocals`. That bug was recently fixed: https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/60908. This PR bumps us to TypeScript 6 so that we can add that compiler option in a follow-up PR (not in this one, since it will make for quite a large diff).

Ideally we'd bump all the way to 7, but when I tried that it caused issues with ESLint that I couldn't be bothered to look into. Bumping from 6 to 7 (hi kids) should be fairly straightforward other than that.

No changeset because no user-observable changes.

issues.title: fix: error at compile time when a declaration in a snippet redeclares one of its parameters
issues.body:
`{const item = 1}` inside `{#snippet row(item)}` compiles, and the output declares `item` twice in one function, so it does not parse:

```js
const row = ($$anchor, item = $.noop) => {
	const item = 1;
```

`{let}`, `{@const}` and a nested snippet with the parameter's name do the same. In `phases/scope.js`, `EachBlock` visits its body's children in the item's own scope, so a tag that reuses the item name is a `declaration_duplicate`. `SnippetBlock` calls `context.next({ scope: child_scope })`, the `Fragment` visitor opens another scope for the body, and the tag never meets the parameter.

After visiting the body, `SnippetBlock` now reports any name in the body's scope that `child_scope` also declares. A declaration in a nested block or element still shadows the parameter.

[Playground](https://svelte.dev/playground/hello-world?version=5.57.0#H4sIAAAAAAAC_22OzQrCMAzHX6XEi4I4PHgZc-hzOA91y6DQxdBGp5S-u6nMm6eQX_4fSUB2QqghkmNGMWyDAsFgAg7Ye6sDtjA6jxHqSwJ5c9EXoHxxn5l38YleCrvZiP94fydBEo2BtPr1hfu8doLTJnfUSVJNFFOAOZr9lzXcpgJyU3HbUaoWazlSOgWkoXyrOYcSokWCL4FawgPzVTfr_OxogHq0PmL-AAetZf_zAAAA)

issues.title: Hydration mismatch recovery is intercepted by svelte:boundary
issues.body:
## Description

A recoverable hydration mismatch is intercepted by `<svelte:boundary>` when hydrating a SvelteKit 3 app. The boundary treats Svelte's internal hydration failure signal as an application render error, so SvelteKit renders its `+error.svelte` page instead of allowing top-level `hydrate()` recovery.

Originally reported in sveltejs/kit#17151.

## Proposed solution

In the client error-boundary dispatch, rethrow the private `HYDRATION_ERROR` sentinel before traversing boundaries or applying `transformError`, preserving its identity for the catch in `hydrate()`.

Add regression coverage asserting that malformed `{@html}` beneath a boundary warns and recovers without rendering the fallback, while genuine hydration-time component exceptions remain catchable.

issues.title: fix: remove incorrect special handling of :export pseudo-selectors
issues.body: #18793 added special handling for `:export` selectors, but this is incorrect. `:export` is (apparently) part of [Interoperable CSS](https://github.com/css-modules/icss) but Svelte doesn't (and shouldn't) know what that is. No changeset because #18793 is unreleased, and the changeset in that PR didn't mention ICSS

issues.title: fix: make Object.hasOwn reactive for state proxies
issues.body:
Fixes #18837

### What changed

State proxies now establish a per-property reactive dependency when `Object.hasOwn(proxy, prop)` invokes the `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` trap. Property additions and deletions therefore invalidate the expression, consistently with the `prop in proxy` operator.

The source creation uses the same eligibility constraints as the existing `has` trap so inherited properties retain their existing semantics.

A runtime-runes regression sample covers both adding and deleting the observed property in DOM and hydration modes.

### Tests and linting

issues.title: docs: note that `toStore` does not update for nested changes unless `get` reads them
issues.body:
Closes #17419

In #17419, @dummdidumm said the behavior is expected but surprising, and that the docs should add a note. This PR adds that note to the `toStore` JSDoc.

`toStore(() => state)` only reads the `state` variable. It does not read `state.nested`. So `state.nested = value` does not re-run `get`, and store subscribers are not notified. This includes `$store` in legacy `$:` statements. The template in the issue still updates, because it reads `.nested` directly from the proxy. A getter that reads the property, such as `() => state.nested` or `() => $state.snapshot(state)`, notifies subscribers.

I checked this with a temporary test that is not part of this PR. It used `proxy()` and `snapshot()` from the internals:

| getter | subscriber values after `state.nested = 'b'` |
|---|---|
| `() => state` | `["a"]` |
| `() => snapshot(state)` | `["a", "b"]` |
| `() => state.nested` | `["a", "b"]` |

### Where the note goes

`toStore` has `@overload` JSDoc blocks with no description. The description and example are only on the implementation signature, and that JSDoc does not reach `types/index.d.ts`. So editor hovers and the generated `svelte/store` reference show no text for `toStore` today. This PR adds the existing description, the example, and the new note to both overload blocks. `derived` already uses this pattern. The change is the same in `index-client.js` and `index-server.js`, and `types/index.d.ts` is regenerated with `pnpm generate:types`.

This PR changes only comments and the generated declarations, not runtime code. I added a `patch` changeset because the published types change. I can remove it if you want.

- [x] It's really useful if your PR references an issue where it is discussed ahead of time. In many cases, features are absent for a reason. For large changes, please create an RFC: https://github.com/sveltejs/rfcs

- [ ] Ideally, include a test that fails without this PR but passes with it.
- [x] If this PR changes code within `packages/svelte/src`, add a changeset (`npx changeset`).

This PR changes only documentation, so it adds no test.

issues.title: Regression: css_unused_selector false positive for global/:export rules in components whose only elements are inside <svelte:head> (#18160)
issues.body:
## Describe the bug Since **5.57.0**, `svelte-check` / the compiler reports `css_unused_selector` warnings for selectors that are not actually unused, in components that have **no scopable DOM elements of their own** — i.e. their only markup is inside `` (plus optionally components and `{@render ...}`). Two kinds of rule are wrongly flagged: - `:is(:global(...))` — a global selector wrapped in `:is()` (this is exactly what a CSS minifier such as LightningCSS produces from a `:global(a), :global(b)` list). - `:export { ... }` — the ICSS export block that `*.module.scss` files use to expose SCSS variables to JS. Both selectors are correct and functional at runtime; they are simply never marked "used". I bisected this to **#18160** ("fix: never apply class hash to elements inside ``"), the only CSS-analysis change between 5.56.10 and 5.57.0. In `css-prune.js` it adds: ```js !is_inside_svelte_head(element) && apply_selector(...) ``` `apply_selector` is what marks global/complex rules as used, and that marking is only reached by iterating the component's elements. When a component's *only* elements are inside ``, the iterable is now empty, `apply_selector` never runs, and those rules are reported as unused. Adding any non-head DOM element (e.g. a single `
`) makes the warnings disappear. Note: a plain `:global(a), :global(b)` list is **not** affected (it's recognised as global structurally); only the `:is(:global(...))` form is, which is why this surfaces in real projects only after a CSS minifier rewrites the selector list. ## Reproduction REPL (shows both warnings on 5.57.0+): https://svelte.dev/playground/f3d42eefdb154668bb1d2a49d348593b Minimal, no preprocessing required — compiling either component below emits a false `css_unused_selector` warning on 5.57.0 but not on 5.56.10: ```svelte ``` ```svelte ``` Adding `
` to the template of either makes the warning go away. | case | 5.56.10 | 5.57.0 | |---|---|---| | `A.svelte` (`:is(:global(td), :global(th))`) | no warning | `Unused CSS selector ":is(:global(td), :global(th))"` | | `B.svelte` (`:export`) | no warning | `Unused CSS selector ":export"` | | either + a `
` in the template | no warning | no warning | Real-world trigger: a SvelteKit `+layout.svelte` that only renders ``, a child component, and `{@render children()}`, with global `

issues.title: fix: avoid duplicate reaction when reconnecting a derived
issues.body:
Fixes #18781

## What's the problem

A component-owned `$derived` stays reachable after `unmount()` when this happens:

1. The component's derived is rendered inside an `{#if}` in its parent, so while visible the derived is "connected" to its dependencies.
2. The `{#if}` is hidden, the effect reading the derived is torn down, and once it has no more readers the derived gets disconnected.
3. While hidden, a nested reactive object the derived depends on is replaced (e.g. `shared.data = { value: 1 }`).
4. The `{#if}` is shown again, and `get()` reconnects the derived.

After step 4 the derived can no longer be collected, leaking the unmounted component.

## Why it leaks

In `runtime.js`, `reconnect()` pushes the derived into each dependency's `reactions` array without checking whether it's already there:

```js
for (const dep of derived.deps) {
	(dep.reactions ??= []).push(derived); // no dedup
	...
}
```

`remove_reaction()` removes only a single occurrence, so the leftover entry stays behind as a strong reference:

`source.reactions → derived → component closure → marker`

and the unmounted component is never garbage collected.

## Verified on the repository source

All evidence below was collected on this repository's `main` at `273e32a` (`svelte@5.57.0`), not on a published package.

### 1. `reconnect()` runs with the derived already registered

Breakpoint at `packages/svelte/src/internal/client/runtime.js:731` (the unguarded `push`), conditional on `dep.reactions.length > 1`:

![breakpoint, call stack, variables and watch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/svelte/72bb23b7630fe182f7a8af0d4ed1ed2fda9b753d/.github/evidence/18781/01-breakpoint-overview.webp)

The same frame shows:

| expression | value |
| --- | --- |
| `dep.reactions.length` | `2` |
| `dep.reactions.filter(r => r === derived).length` | `1` |
| `dep.reactions[1] === derived` | `true` |
| `derived.f` / `dep.reactions[1].f` | `34306` / `34306` |
| `derived.reactions` | `null` — no readers left |

So the derived is registered twice on the same dependency, while it has no readers of its own.

### 2. The trigger is the reconnect path

![call stack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/svelte/72bb23b7630fe182f7a8af0d4ed1ed2fda9b753d/.github/evidence/18781/02-call-stack.webp)

`reconnect` is reached from `get()` (`runtime.js:705`), which was entered from the component's template effect (`Retained.js:21` → `template_effect` → `consequent` → `BranchManager`) — i.e. from showing the `{#if}` again.

### 3. Consequence, and the exact trigger

![four-mode comparison and accumulation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/svelte/72bb23b7630fe182f7a8af0d4ed1ed2fda9b753d/.github/evidence/18781/03-modes-and-accumulation.webp)

30 component instances are mounted and unmounted; after `unmount()` the runner crosses task boundaries and forces GC ten times. Only the `replace` sequence leaks, which rules out "hiding" and "changing data" as the trigger — it is replacing that nested reactive object *while the reader is hidden*. Note `elements left in the DOM: 0` while all 30 markers are still retained, so this is a JS-side retention, not stale DOM.

### 4. The fix stops it

![patch effectiveness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/svelte/72bb23b7630fe182f7a8af0d4ed1ed2fda9b753d/.github/evidence/18781/04-patch-effectiveness.webp)

The identical reproduction is run three times, alternating between the unpatched and patched `reconnect()` — the only variable is the patch.

## The fix

Only push the derived if it isn't already in the dependency's `reactions` array:

```js
for (const dep of derived.deps) {
	var reactions = (dep.reactions ??= []);
	if (index_of.call(reactions, derived) === -1) {
		reactions.push(derived);
	}
	...
}
```

## Test plan

Two tests in `packages/svelte/tests/signals/test.ts`, both of which fail without the fix:

- `reconnecting a derived does not add a duplicate reaction` — asserts the graph invariant directly. Without the fix: `derived registered 3 times ... expected 1`.
- `reconnect() is idempotent` — the reverse check. It connects the derived, detaches it, then calls `reconnect()` three times and asserts the dependency registers it exactly once. This is the invariant that makes `remove_reaction()`'s single-removal semantics sufficient; without the fix the count becomes 3.

`reconnect()` is exported for these tests — it is not part of the public API, and no runtime behaviour changes.

- Existing suites: `tests/signals` 107 passed, `tests/runtime-runes` 2703 passed, `tests/runtime-legacy` 3304 passed.
- CI is green on all jobs (Tests on Linux/macOS/Windows, `TestNoAsync`, Lint, TSGo, Benchmarks).

A memory leak isn't observable through the jsdom-based unit harness (GC/WeakRef only), so the leak itself is verified with the WeakRef + `--expose-gc` repro; the regression test asserts the graph invariant directly.

A note on `async_mode_flag`: the reproduction does not need `experimental.async`. The component output used above does not import `svelte/internal/flags/async`, so the flag is `false` in this run.

issues.title: Discussion: Improving hydration performance for large lists
issues.body:
## Description

When working with large lists (1000+ items) in SvelteKit, hydration can be noticeably slow compared to the initial SSR render. This affects Time to Interactive (TTI) metrics significantly.

## Reproduction

Rendering a list of 2000 items with dynamic content shows a 300-500ms hydration delay on mid-range devices.

## Suggestion

Consider implementing virtual hydration or lazy hydration strategies:
1. Only hydrate visible items initially
2. Defer hydration of off-screen items until they enter the viewport
3. Provide a `lazy` directive for components that can be hydrated later

This would significantly improve TTI for content-heavy pages like e-commerce listings or social feeds.

issues.title: fix: don't crash when aborting a deferred out transition before it starts
issues.body:
### Before submitting the PR, please make sure you do the following

- [x] It's really useful if your PR references an issue where it is discussed ahead of time. In many cases, features are absent for a reason. For large changes, please create an RFC: https://github.com/sveltejs/rfcs
- [x] Prefix your PR title with `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, or `docs:`.
- [x] This message body should clearly illustrate what problems it solves.
- [x] Ideally, include a test that fails without this PR but passes with it.
- [x] If this PR changes code within `packages/svelte/src`, add a changeset (`npx changeset`).

### Tests and linting

- [x] Run the tests with `pnpm test` and lint the project with `pnpm lint`

Fixes #18773

This is the crash from that issue: an `{#if}` goes away, an out-only deferred transition starts (`out:fn` where `fn` returns another function, same idea as `crossfade`), and then an `$effect` turns the block back on in the same update.

The outro isn't a real animation yet — Svelte waits a microtask before creating it. When the branch comes back, `resume` calls `reset()` on that placeholder. `abort` already treated "not started" as fine; `reset` / `deactivate` / `t` did not, so you got:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'reset')
```

I made those three match `abort`. If the outro never started, cancelling it is a no-op, and the block stays on the page instead of throwing.

There's a runtime-runes sample that clicks hide while an `$effect` immediately sets the flag back to `true`. That used to throw; it doesn't now.

Local: `pnpm test runtime-runes -t transition-deferred-out-effect-resume`

docs: document CSS custom property spread limitation and workaround
issues.body:
Closes #15943

## Summary

CSS custom properties must be passed to components as explicit named attributes (e.g. `--track-color="black"`). They **cannot** be included in a spread object — Svelte detects `--`-prefixed attributes via static analysis at compile time, which cannot inspect the contents of a spread.

This PR adds a **Limitations** section to the CSS custom properties page that:
- States the constraint clearly with a ❌/✅ code example
- Provides the `style`-string-on-wrapper workaround for cases where the set of custom properties is dynamic or unknown at compile time

## Test plan

Documentation-only change; no code was modified.

- Verified that the existing docs don't already cover this case
- Confirmed the workaround (wrapper `<div style={themeStyle}>`) is correct per the maintainer's comment in #15943 ("to work we need to wrap the component in an element with display contents and the css variables as inline styles")

issues.title: perf: use Set for rest-prop exclude lists (server, legacy, exclude_from_object)
issues.body:
// markdown
Closes #18601
 
## What
 
Converts the remaining array-based exclude lists in `rest_props`, `legacy_rest_props`, and `exclude_from_object` to use `Set`, aligning them with the already-optimized client runes `rest_props` path.
 
## Changes
 
- **`shared/utils.js`** — `exclude_from_object` now accepts `Set<string | symbol>` and uses `.has()` instead of `.includes()`
- **`server/index.js`** — Server `rest_props` now accepts `Set<string>` and uses `.has()` instead of `.includes()`
- **`client/reactivity/props.js`** — `legacy_rest_props` handler uses `Set` with `.has()`/`.add()` instead of `.includes()`/`.push()`
- **Compiler** (`ast.js`, `transform-server.js`, `transform-client.js`) — Emits `new Set([...])` instead of plain arrays
 
## Why
 
Exclude lists are compile-time fixed but prop bags can grow; SSR multiplies across requests. `Set.has()` is O(1) vs `Array.includes()` which is O(n).
 
## Test plan
 
All existing tests pass: snapshot, compiler, runtime-runes (2707), runtime-legacy (3304), signals, ssr, lint.

Fixes #18623

### Description
In Svelte 5 reactivity runtime, \last_scheduled_effect\ held a reference to the last effect scheduled in module scope indefinitely until flushed. When component subtrees were destroyed/unmounted, this retained references to detached DOM nodes and component context, causing a memory leak.

### Fix
- Added \clear_last_scheduled_effect(effect)\ in \packages/svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js\.
- Called \clear_last_scheduled_effect(effect)\ in \destroy_effect()\ inside \packages/svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/effects.js\.
- Added test in \packages/svelte/tests/signals/test.ts\.
- Added changeset file.

issues.title: feat: entangle batches
issues.body:
This PR changes how the async reactivity system works when async work overlaps. Previously, we tried to record the current/previous values of each batch, so that each batch runs with the values it "can see" (meaning updates from other batches are held back in the context of that batch). On commit we "rebase" the other batches and rerun block/async effects where necessary.

While the idea is somewhat straightforward around batch values, the rebasing part was always a headache and bug magnet. We needed to find overlapping async/block effects to eagerly rerun them, and we also needed to keep track of new effects because we might need to rerun them once another batch commits. Additionally, we kept deriveds as (maybe)dirty while multiple batches existed so that we could always traverse the tree and get the correct value, which overfires.

This PR changes how it works. Instead, we now "entangle" (or merge) batches whenever we see that their reactive graphs overlap. This is straightforward by recording for each signal which batch has last touched it (render effects are exempt else too much would entangle). If there's already a batch on that signal that is not finished yet, these two batches will merge and become one unit, i.e. resolve together.

I was hoping that this would reduce the overall code size, and this change alone would, but there are two things making it bigger in the end (though a lot of it is comments):

First, we need to handle promise starvation: Async work could be repeatedly scheduled, always merging with an existing batch, and so the UI would never update. To battle this, there's a mechanism that after a certain amount of merges containing async work, we put any new work in a `waiter` property, which is only processed once the existing batch is done. Since stale UI could happen either way (see #18524) we could also be more pragmatic here and just flush at some point, even if it results in possibly weird UI - so that could get the code size down again if we agree on a simpler solution.

Second, we need to handle forking, which of course cannot entangle. So in addition to the merging logic we still need overlay logic to keep the world separate from each other. Since the "real world" always entangles now the overlay looks a bit different compared to main. It also fixes a lot of bugs that were discovered during working on this, so I assume that if we were to fix this in the existing system we would also have to add a bunch more code.

I also benchmarked this and it's either faster or only a tiny bit slower than main, depending on the benchmark. It's definitely faster than #18035.

What I didn't get to yet but would like to do (or someone else), is to check which of the existing issues in the Svelte repo are also fixed through this, so we know this is all worth it and not just shifting buggyness from one place to the other. Some I checked so far:
- Fixes #18355

issues.title: fix: properly handle interleaving renderers
issues.body:
This was a hell of a ride!

So after a discussion last maintainers meeting about what was the behaviour of custom rendered components on the server we concurred that they should just be a no-op.

I made the change, but I wanted to try in an actual project, so I've created a SvelteKit app, installed the custom version, tried it out and...nothing worked. Turns out, just adding `before` to a comment node doesn't allow for interleaving to happen.

There were a few problems:

1. The `insert_before` and `remove` operations were running with the `current_renderer` but they were also asking for the parent of the mounting node. During interleaving the parent is actually a DOM object so `getParent` failed (unless you accounted for it in the custom renderer).
2. In general, the API of "just tuck a `before` in the comment and handle the `getParent` case" was very ugly, error-prone and not nice to build upon.
3. That also didn't cover the opposite...when you want to mount a DOM component into a custom rendered one.

The main issue was that we needed a way to determine where a component was mounted and allow the developers to handle the different cases.

## Store the parent

Now `custom_renderer` is a global option, so every component (even the DOM ones) when the option is enabled will push their renderer (DOM components just push `null`). This means that, inside `push_renderer` we can store the `parent_renderer` and this allows us to determine where a component is being mounted by checking parent and current renderer:

- `null` and `null` means DOM into DOM
- `parent_renderer === current_renderer` means current in current
- `current_renderer` and `null` means DOM in renderer
- `parent_renderer !== current_renderer` means two different renderers

> [!NOTE]
> I also had to remove the optimization where a template is not created if there's a single node otherwise an anchor from a different renderer could go towards a different renderer component and that would've messed up the parent situation.

This leads to...

## The foreign object

Custom renderers can now declare an optional `foreign` property. If they don't declare that that custom renderer cannot interleave, and it will error out with a descriptive error when you try to mount in/from a custom renderer that's not the same. If they do declare it they have to provide a `insertForeign`, `removeForeign`, `insertIntoForeign` and `removeFromForeign` methods which are invoked respectively when:

- `insertForeign`: a component that uses a different custom renderer (or DOM) is inserted into a component that uses this custom renderer
- `removeForeign`: a component that uses a different custom renderer (or DOM) is removed from a component that uses this custom renderer
- `insertIntoForeign`: a component that uses this custom renderer is mounted into a different custom renderer (or DOM)
- `removeFromForeign`: a component that uses this custom renderer is removed from a different custom renderer (or DOM)

## Removing using segments

This is another kind of big change to the runtime, but luckily, it should only be in place when the renderer is meant to interleave (it has the `foreign` object defined).

The problem was that the current element removal when an effect is destroyed only stored `start` and `end` nodes and then invoked `getNextSibling` until we reached `end`. This works fine as long as all the nodes are in the same renderer...but if an effect (like an `if` or an `each` block) has nodes from two different custom renderers, this fails because `getNextSibling` will not return a node from a different renderer. This was pretty tough to figure out and the best solution me and Claude/Gpt 5.5 could come with is this `segments` array stored in the effects. This is more memory intensive, but I couldn't really figure out a way to transition the next siblings from one to the other without storing the boundaries inside this segment array so that the removal could re-apply the right parent/current renderer before running the removal.

## A few other fixes

I had to do a few other fixes like pushing the renderer before executing the snippets, pushing the same renderer when executing branches and then restoring the parent, wrapping the implicit snippet children into `renderer_snippet`.

## Updated test suite

I've also made a couple of changes to the test renderer so that it uses the foreign object AND it actually mounts a DOM element when interleaved so we could actually test this stuff. Furthermore, at one point I had all test passing but when used in the test SvelteKit app it was failing...so I've added an `hydrate` option that actually mount a DOM component and `hydrate` it instead of just mounting the components.

This is it! It was kind of exhausting, but happy to finally get this out.

P.s. this shouldn't have too many conflicts with #18317, but I'll try to solve them if it does.
